signals.title: [Feature][DSpark] Support Speculators-format checkpoints and ragged multimodal CUDA graphs
signals.text: <!-- Suggested title: [Feature][DSpark] Support native Speculators checkpoints and ragged multimodal CUDA graphs --> > **Status:** implementation, public-checkpoint compatibility, and paired > fixed-output performance tests are complete. Greedy target-output equivalence > remains unresolved, so this PR does not claim losslessness or quality parity. ## Motivation This PR extends SGLang's DSpark path to run native Speculators checkpoints end to end in eager mode, CUDA Graph replay, and ragged multimodal verification. It covers the checkpoint config and weight formats, both DSpark anchor layouts, independent draft vocabularies, and the runtime paths needed to verify them. Native Speculators checkpoints are not limited to the shared-vocabulary layout that DSpark originally supported in SGLang. They may contain an independent reduced-vocabulary LM head plus a draft-to-target (`d2t`) mapping. For example, the public [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark) checkpoint has: - target vocabulary: 248,320 tokens; - draft `lm_head`: 32,000 tokens; - `markov_w1`: target-vocabulary input; - `markov_w2`: draft-vocabulary output; - `d2t`: a 32,000-entry mapping from sampled draft IDs to target IDs. Treating these tensors as a shared-vocabulary model either fails during loading or feeds/scatters IDs in the wrong vocabulary space. Speculators checkpoints can also use either DSpark draft-block layout: - `sample_from_anchor=false`: the anchor is only a conditioning token. The draft forward has `gamma + 1` slots, and slot 0 is excluded from sampling and verification. - `sample_from_anchor=true`: the anchor is a trained prediction. The draft forward has `gamma` slots. Using the wrong width does not always crash; it can shift real draft positions and reduce the acceptance length toward 1. After checkpoint loading and draft geometry were working, mixed image/text validation exposed separate problems in ragged mRoPE and linear attention. The ragged-path changes make multimodal verification work under CUDA Graphs. During the same validation, I found a pre-existing interaction between `/flush_cache` and DSpark draft CUDA Graphs: emptying the allocator cache can invalidate addresses retained by a captured graph. This is included as a separate DSpark graph-lifecycle fix. ## Modifications - Normalize the native Speculators DSpark config format, whose backbone lives under `transformer_layer_config`, without importing checkpoint-side remote config code. This path is gated on `speculators_model_type=dspark` and reuses the existing config-dictionary fetch. - Load an independent tensor-parallel `ParallelLMHead` when `draft_vocab_size != target_vocab_size`; preserve the original shared-head path for full-vocabulary DSpark checkpoints. - Support the asymmetric Markov geometry: `markov_w1` consumes target IDs while `markov_w2` and the draft LM head produce draft-vocabulary logits. - Map sampled draft IDs through `d2t` before storing tokens or feeding the next Markov step. For probabilistic acceptance, scatter draft probabilities into target-vocabulary columns and leave unmapped target tokens at `-inf`. - Validate mapping shape/range and fail early for unsupported reduced-vocabulary checkpoints without `d2t`. Load `t2d` as checkpoint metadata without using it in the decode path. - Read authoritative `gamma` and `sample_from_anchor` metadata, reject inconsistent checkpoint geometry at startup, and propagate the same draft width through eager execution and CUDA Graph replay. - Keep verification, KV commit, and acceptance accounting at `gamma` real draft tokens. Only the draft forward width changes. - Build speculative mRoPE positions from each request's actual verify length; CUDA Graph padding uses zero-delta ghost positions. - Add packed-to-dense scatter/gather support for ragged linear attention and declare ragged CUDA Graph support per attention backend. - Preserve captured DSpark draft graph allocations across `/flush_cache` while still clearing logical request, KV, radix, grammar, and metrics state. - Use an 8-token SPS `M` bin for compact scheduling and recompute the simulated bonus token at the acceptance boundary. - Add regression coverage for full/reduced vocabularies, configuration normalization, tensor-parallel LM heads, Markov shapes, `d2t` mapping, corrected-logit scatter, both checkpoint layouts, CUDA Graphs, ragged mRoPE, linear attention, cache flushing, and SPS fitting. ## Status - [x] Bonus-anchor and dense anchor-first checkpoint layouts - [x] Full-vocabulary DSpark checkpoint regression - [x] Independent reduced-vocabulary LM head - [x] Draft-to-target vocabulary mapping and probabilistic corrected logits - [x] Eager and CUDA Graph draft-width propagation - [x] TP=1 and TP=2 public RedHat checkpoint inference - [x] Greedy and non-greedy sampling - [x] Ragged multimodal mRoPE and linear-attention layouts - [x] DSpark CUDA Graph behavior after `/flush_cache` - [ ] Greedy token-level equivalence with target-only decoding - [x] Same-GPU paired performance benchmark at concurrency 1 and 8 ## Accuracy and Correctness Tests On the PR branch rebased onto upstream `main` on 2026-08-13, the focused suite reports `212 passed, 54 subtests passed`; the reduced-vocabulary file reports `26 passed, 2 subtests passed`. Python compilation, formatting, focused Ruff checks, and `git diff --check` also pass. The public-checkpoint validation uses [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4) as the target and [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark) as the draft. The environment has PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, and FlashInfer 0.6.17. The official workloads are MT-Bench (80 two-turn conversations, 160 requests) and the MMSpec test split (600 conversations, 723 turns). Correctness runs compare target-only autoregressive (AR) decoding with DSpark under greedy decoding at concurrency 1. | Workload | AR repeat | DSpark completed | Exact first-turn AR/DSpark token sequences | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | MT-Bench | 160/160 | 160/160 | 8/80 | | MMSpec | 723/723 | 723/723 | 18/600 | The AR repeat is exact on both workloads, confirming a deterministic baseline. DSpark completes every request, but target-output equivalence is not established. A separate 20-prompt eager probe also mismatches on all 20 prompts, so disabling decode CUDA Graph does not remove the divergence; its cause remains unresolved. Acceptance is aggregated from raw server counters. The acceptance length below includes the target bonus token. | Workload | Draft acceptance rate | Acceptance length including bonus | | --- | ---: | ---: | | MT-Bench | 32.863% | 3.6257 | | MMSpec | 24.956% | 2.9925 | Separate focused lanes also pass TP=1 and TP=2 inference, greedy and non-greedy sampling, ragged multimodal CUDA Graph replay, and a post-`/flush_cache` request. ## Fixed-output Performance The formal fixed-output benchmark consists of three same-GPU paired repeats with service restart and unmeasured warm-up before each mode: - MT-Bench first turns with exactly 256 output tokens per request; - a deterministic 20-per-topic MMSpec subset with exactly 128 output tokens per request; - closed-loop concurrency 1 and 8; - pair order `target -> DSpark`, `DSpark -> target`, `target -> DSpark`. All 2,400 measured requests completed with the required output length. Values below are medians across the three runs; the interval is the range of the three paired throughput ratios. The raw service logs and result manifests bind these runs to the reported source commit and execution-environment freeze; strict reanalyzing after the provenance audit produced an identical summary. | Workload | C | Target tok/s | DSpark tok/s | Paired throughput | p50 E2E target -> DSpark | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | MT-Bench | 1 | 151.64 | 262.32 | 1.730x [1.726, 1.741] | 1.687s -> 1.008s | | MT-Bench | 8 | 715.30 | 942.30 | 1.317x [1.300, 1.327] | 2.853s -> 2.076s | | MMSpec | 1 | 132.89 | 178.49 | 1.343x [1.343, 1.346] | 0.937s -> 0.715s | | MMSpec | 8 | 467.98 | 519.74 | 1.111x [1.110, 1.124] | 2.086s -> 1.754s | The gain is not uniform across the latency distribution. MT-Bench C=8 p99 E2E regresses in all three repeats (paired target/DSpark ratios 0.906-0.920). MMSpec C=8 has about 9% higher p50 TPOT and mixed p99 E2E results (paired ratios 0.938-1.092, median 0.961). This supports a stable fixed-output throughput and p50 E2E improvement under the reported configuration, not a universal tail-latency improvement. SSE chunk gaps are not reported as token-level ITL because one speculative event can expose multiple tokens. TPOT is client-observed and amortized from the first to last token-bearing event. ## Validation caveat and follow-up The prior FlashInfer version caveat is resolved: the current environment uses FlashInfer 0.6.17. The remaining boundary is output equivalence. The results above establish native checkpoint loading, full request completion, and online acceptance, but the greedy target/DSpark mismatch persists in eager mode and under CUDA Graph replay. They therefore do not establish losslessness or downstream accuracy parity. The following remains a claim boundary rather than a merge blocker: - resolve the eager/graph numerical divergence and establish greedy token-level equivalence before making a lossless-output claim. ## Related work - Original SGLang DSpark implementation: [#30261](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30261) - Bonus-anchor checkpoint layout: [#30982](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30982) - vLLM Speculators checkpoint support: [vLLM #47093](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47093) Thanks to the authors and reviewers of these changes for the checkpoint-layout analysis and reference behavior. ## Contributors Engine Architecture Group 5, Engine Infrastructure Department, Xiaohongshu (RedNote): Su Zhan, Fei Ziyu, Hong Chenchen, Luo Zhaokai, Jin Huayi.

signals.title: [Diffusion] Unify component residency controls
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang-Diffusion currently exposes overlapping CPU-offload and layerwise-offload flags with different scopes. In particular, an explicit `--dit-layerwise-offload false` can still inherit automatic DiT component offload, even though callers use that spelling to request a resident DiT. The DiT/VAE booleans also implicitly control model-specific helper components, making placement difficult to reason about as pipelines add dynamic modules. ## Modifications - Add `--component-residency COMPONENT=MODE` with `resident`, `component-offload`, and `layerwise-offload`. Exact component keys override the `dit`, `text_encoder`, `image_encoder`, `vae`, and `all` groups. Omitted components retain their legacy or model defaults. - Map those mode names directly to runtime strategy classes; there is no duplicate policy/mode enum beside the strategy implementation. - Keep all legacy controls supported: `--dit-cpu-offload`, `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`, `--image-encoder-cpu-offload`, `--vae-cpu-offload`, `--cpu-offload-components`, and the existing layerwise flags. Legacy and canonical controls may be mixed; a canonical selector overrides only the components it matches. - Fix explicit `--dit-layerwise-offload false` to keep the DiT resident unless another explicit DiT offload control is selected. - Route loaders, stage lifecycle management, dynamic components, Diffusers pipeline-wide placement, quantization overrides, FSDP validation, disaggregation argument copies, and CI helpers through the resolved strategy. - Prepare and release single-component stages through the shared executor lifecycle. Multi-component stages declare their actual component-use intervals, and replacing or deleting a dynamic module clears stale active/cache/prefetch state. - Require explicitly selected components to implement layerwise offload. Explicit unsupported or FSDP-managed selections fail clearly; automatic selection warns and retains the component's previous placement instead of silently changing its mode. - Keep DiT/VAE groups limited to actual denoisers/VAEs. Model-specific helpers such as connectors, sound tokenizers, upsamplers, and vocoders remain independently addressable by exact component key. - Add focused coverage for precedence, every legacy flag, mixed controls, dynamic components, lifecycle behavior, strict layerwise validation, FSDP/quantization/LTX constraints, CPU platform behavior, disaggregation reconstruction, and Diffusers effective placement. - Update the multimodal-gen README and public SGLang-Diffusion CLI/deployment documentation. Deprecated `docs/diffusion` remains untouched. ## Accuracy Tests No model math, weights, scheduler behavior, or output contracts are intentionally changed. Existing diffusion CI exercises model execution and consistency paths. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No optimization claim. The selector chooses the existing resident, component-offload, or layerwise-offload execution behavior. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31921994130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921994130)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31921994040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921994040)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: refactor(hicache): flatten L2 transfer execution
signals.text: **Resolve device↔host work into flat `L2Transfer` commands so the executor and host-pool group no longer recursively dispatch pool transfers, without changing cache behavior.** ### Boundary ```python class L2Transfer(NamedTuple): host_pool: Any device_pool: Any host_indices: torch.Tensor device_indices: torch.Tensor layer_mapper: Optional[Callable[[int], Optional[int]]] = None is_draft: bool = False L2TransferEngine(io_backend).submit_device_to_host( transfers: list[L2Transfer], ) -> TransferCompletion L2TransferEngine(io_backend).submit_host_to_device( transfers: list[L2Transfer], *, layer_num: int, start_event=None, on_layer_done=None, ) -> TransferCompletion ``` ### Ownership - Controllers: allocation, queues, acknowledgements, layer mapping, and `PoolTransfer` resolution. - Engine: execute already-resolved device↔host commands and retain index tensors on its streams. - Host pools: move bytes for one concrete pool. - Storage/L3 and tree lifecycle: unchanged. ### Result - One flat execution boundary for base and hybrid caches. - No nested transfer dispatch in `L2TransferEngine` or `HostPoolGroup`. - Existing concatenated per-pool index tensors continue to feed the same C++/JIT kernels. ### Validation - 2,124 tests run: 1,092 passed, 1,032 skipped, 0 failures. - Compileall, diff check, and all applicable pre-commit hooks pass. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31927917622](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927917622)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31927917545](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927917545)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [PD] Preserve decode KV across retraction in HiCache
signals.text: ## Motivation PD decode retraction currently preserves KV in per-request CPU tensors. Reusing HiCache host pools avoids a second host-memory path and also lets speculative draft KV survive retraction. ## Modifications - Add explicit and inferred `cpu_tensor` / `host_pool` retraction backends behind `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup`. - Resolve the backend once the decode KV pool exists, since it cannot be decided in `ServerArgs.__post_init__`. The resolved value lands on the config bags via `get_context().override(...)`, and every reader goes through `get_disagg()` — `server_args` stays the pristine read-only record. - Make `--hicache-ratio` `Optional` and give it its default at that same point (`1.0` for host-pool retraction, `2.0` otherwise), so a decode server can size the host pool 1:1 with the device pool. The `hicache_ratio` reads in `hiradix_cache.py` and `hybrid_pool_assembler.py` move to `get_memory()` accordingly — that is the only reason those two files appear in the diff. - Reserve and validate HiCache capacity for compatible MHA and hybrid-SWA decode pools. - Back up, restore, and discard target plus speculative draft sidecar KV through the flattened L2 transfer path from #34793. - Force host-pool retraction in the PD EAGLE3 integration test and assert retracted requests retain speculative acceptance above the calibrated 1.3 gate. - Add a CUDA round-trip test that poisons both target and draft device KV before restoring them at different slots. ## Accuracy Tests Run on the current revision: - Python compilation for all changed files - All applicable pre-commit hooks on the changed files - The `_EXPOSED` / `_OVERRIDDEN_AND_READ` pin sets in `test_supplied_instance_exposure_ratchet.py` are unchanged by this PR, and the mutation / global-config-read ratchets stay at their zero baselines Run on an earlier revision of this branch, before the rebase onto post-#34793 main: - `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py` - `test_runtime_context_override.py` - `test_runtime_context_config_bags.py` The CUDA target/draft round-trip and the PD EAGLE3 integration test have not been executed locally (no GPU on the dev host). They are registered in CI. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. The new transfers execute only when decode requests are retracted; the steady-state decode path is unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit and integration tests. - [ ] Update documentation (no user-facing documentation change needed). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (GPU tests are delegated to CI; no steady-state performance change). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31984438697](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31984438697)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31984438611](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31984438611)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Speed up MiniMax-H3 VAE decode on 2×H100
signals.text: ## Summary - preserve the existing model-aware `auto` residency thresholds and `memory` mode's layerwise VAE default - make the measured MiniMax-H3 2×H100 CI recipe explicitly select `vae=resident` - tighten the H3 H100 performance baseline to the measured resident-VAE latency - keep canonical and legacy VAE placement overrides compatible and document the placement semantics ## Why - MiniMax-H3 VAE residency adds about 4.8 GiB/GPU, much less than full DiT and encoder residency, so it offers high performance return when that headroom exists. - Layerwise VAE offload repeats decoder transfers for every temporal chunk and spatial tile; residency reduces H3 decode latency from 14.72s to 2.15–2.22s (about 6.8×). - This remains an explicit H3 recipe choice rather than a global default because residency is not numerically interchangeable for every video VAE path; model-aware `auto` thresholds and the conservative `memory` default remain unchanged. ## H3 2×H100 measurement Same 1344×768, 4-second, 7-eval request, two steady-state runs per configuration: | Placement | Denoise | Decode | Pipeline E2E | Peak / GPU | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | DiT + encoder + VAE layerwise | 16.58s | 14.72s | 32.23s | 22.44 GiB | | DiT + encoder layerwise; VAE resident | 16.55s | 2.15–2.22s | 19.63–19.76s | 27.24 GiB | | Full resident | 13.99s | 2.16s | 19.01s | 69.18 GiB | All six generated MP4 files had the same SHA-256 (`f9ae69f5b08314ce5631978d83e4ed9a0a60ebc0286ff29c451941efe9da6faa`). VAE residency is therefore bit-exact for this path and reduces decode latency by about 6.8×, with about 4.8 GiB/GPU additional memory. Full residency provides only about 3% more E2E improvement while using about 42 GiB/GPU more than the selected recipe. A batched-tile experiment was also bit-exact but slower (2.35–2.43s decode), so it is not included. ## Validation - pre-commit hooks - extend server-args coverage for the `memory` VAE default and explicit canonical/legacy overrides - real 2×H100 H3 A/B through the normal `sglang serve` model-loading path <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31928950202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31928950202)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31928950135](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31928950135)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Store mamba prefix-cache checkpoints at the configured SSM state dtype
signals.text: The mamba radix track path snapshots the SSM state at the last chunk boundary of chunk-unaligned sequences so a later prefix-cache hit can restore it. That path read the per-chunk states `h`, which are always stored in the activation dtype (bf16) — so the checkpoint was pinned to bf16 regardless of `--mamba-ssm-dtype`. With the default fp32 pool (and likewise for fp16), a cache hit restored a lower-precision state than a cache miss keeps, making cached and uncached runs numerically diverge. The chunk-aligned path and the in-place final-state path already wrote at the pool dtype; only this intermediate-state path could not honor it. This PR snapshots the in-kernel fp32 accumulator and casts it once to the pool dtype, so checkpoints on this path faithfully follow `--mamba-ssm-dtype` (float32 / bfloat16 / float16): - Triton `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` gains `track_state`/`track_chunk_idx`: at the tracked chunk boundary it stores the fp32 accumulator into a per-sequence buffer, and `_track_mamba_state_extend` copies that buffer (instead of the rounded `h`) into the track slots, converting to `ssm_states.dtype` once. - The Helion prefill kernel gets native support for the same snapshot (separate varlen kernel configs so the tuned non-track configs are untouched). - New `LinearAttnKernelBase.supports_track_state_snapshot` capability flag; `KDAAttnBackend` asserts it before allocating the snapshot buffer, so a prefill kernel that cannot honor the snapshot fails loudly instead of silently caching unwritten state. FlashKDA's Triton fallback now forwards the track arguments (it previously dropped them, which would have written zeros into the checkpoint slots). - Tests: `test_kda_track_state.py` checks the snapshot matches an fp32 truncated-run reference and is strictly more precise than the bf16 `h` row, for both the Triton and Helion backends; a CPU bookkeeping test pins every KDA prefill kernel's declaration of the new capability flag.

signals.title: feat(moe): enable DeepGEMM MoE runner on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 6000D)
signals.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 (MXFP4 latent MoE) on SM120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 6000D / RTX 5090) currently cannot use the DeepGEMM MoE runner at all: `python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/configurer.py` hard-disables DeepGEMM on SM120, and even when bypassed, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` crashes inside DeepGEMM (`fp8_fp4_mega_moe` → "Unsupported architecture", since MegaMoE kernels exist only for SM90/SM100). With `sgl-deep-gemm >= 0.1.5` (the first release shipping arch-12 JIT kernels and the `transform_sf_into_required_layout` arch-12 scale-factor branches), the non-mega DeepGEMM path (m-grouped fp8/fp4/bf16 GEMMs) is functional on SM120 — this is the same support the upstream `deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM` `nv_dev` branch provides, which vLLM consumes via their vendored pin (vllm-project/vllm#52035, fixing vllm-project/vllm#51758). ## Changes 1. **`deep_gemm_wrapper/configurer.py`** - Remove the hard `sm_version == 120` gate. - Gate SM120 on the installed wheel's distribution metadata (`sgl-deep-gemm >= 0.1.5`); the library's internal `__version__` is frozen across releases so it cannot be used. Source installs without metadata log a warning and stay disabled. - Extend `DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL` / `DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0` to SM120: SM120 uses the same packed-UE8M0 (Blackwell-style) scale layout as SM100, and the runner's forward scale handling is keyed off these flags (`moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`), so they must agree with the unconditional `transform_sf_into_required_layout(recipe=(1, 32))` weight prep in `layers/quantization/mxfp4.py`. - Consequence (intended): with a capable wheel, `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM` and the FP8 dense UE8M0 path also become available on SM120, mirroring the vLLM Wall-1 fix. 2. **`server_args.py`** — `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` on SM120/SM121 now raises a clear `ValueError` at startup instead of aborting at load time inside the DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernel. MegaMoE remains SM90/SM100-only. 3. **Kimi-K3 cookbook** — documents the SM120 story (Marlin default; DeepGEMM runner opt-in with `sgl-deep-gemm>=0.1.5`; no megamoe). ## Usage ```bash # SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 6000D), MXFP4 models (e.g. Kimi-K3): sglang serve --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --moe-a2a-backend none \ ... ``` ## Testing - Static: python syntax; scale-layout consistency traced through `mxfp4.py` weight prep and `moe_runner/deep_gemm.py` forward paths. - On-cluster (4x RTX 6000D, sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post2): run `sglang serve` with the flags above and compare against the Marlin baseline. If the UE8M0 pack path still crashes, capture it with `DG_JIT_DEBUG=1` and report back — the DeepGEMM-side guard (sgl-project/DeepGEMM PR #75: CPU-tensor device assert + MXFP4 (1,32) SF regression test). ## Related - deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#372 / #403 — SM120 SF layout transform (NVFP4) - vllm-project/vllm#51758 / #52035 — same root cause in vLLM, fixed by pinning the nv_dev DeepGEMM tip - sgl-project/sglang#24692 — SM120 support work (DeepGEMM previously disabled) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31803855682](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31803855682)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31803855409](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31803855409)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Validate MiniMax-H3 quality=high on B300
signals.text: ## 0x0. What this PR does Video generation does not need distillation, a different solver, or model surgery to get fast. Keep the weights and the math untouched, be rigorous about *computing less*, and MiniMax-H3 goes from 41.19 s to 11.16 s for a 5-second 1344x768 clip with audio on 8x B300 — with the quality argument written down, gated, and byte-reproducible. Concretely, this PR: - admits the strict 8x B300 TP1/Ulysses8 deployment for MiniMax-H3 request-scoped `quality="high"` - gives each validated deployment its own audited Cache-DiT schedule: 4xH200 keeps the conservative `(4, 0.04, 1)`; **8xB300 ships `(4, 0.08, 3)`**, selected by a parameter sweep on the sglang-native prompt set and gated on LPIPS plus a consecutive-frame temporal review - makes Sol-Attn dense guard steps use the platform-selected FlashAttention implementation (FA4 on Blackwell) and preserves packed-document boundaries on sparse steps - lets the common BCG fail-closed path run before H3 arms Cache-DiT input preservation - documents the protocol, limitations, results, and comparison figure in the cookbook ![MiniMax-H3 B300 quality and latency comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16f604256169b1e9889a3ab4f297883f3f84c15d/docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/assets/minimax-h3-b300-quality-high.png) ## 0x1. Results first Hardware: 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (SM103). Workload: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA T2VA, 1344x768, 124 frames @24 fps, 50 sigma points, video/audio flow shifts 12/3, sglang-native prompts (cookbook example + two benchmark presets), seeds 0/1/2. Latency is the median of three requests after one warmup. This air-cooled node sits on its 1100 W power cap and its sustained-clock regime drifts intraday (~20% on step time), so only same-session ratios are comparable — every row below was measured back-to-back in one session: | Arm | Median latency | Speedup vs Diffusers | LPIPS mean / max vs SGLang lossless | Decision | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Diffusers BF16 dense + Ulysses8 | 41.19 s | 1.00x | 0.347 / 0.465 | baseline | | SGLang lossless | 23.03 s | 1.79x | 0.000 / 0.000 | exact default | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.04, 1) | 16.45 s | 2.50x | 0.101 / 0.129 | superseded on B300 | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.08, 3) | **11.16 s** | **3.69x** | 0.293 / 0.399 | **admitted** | The admitted path is 2.06x faster than SGLang lossless, and its LPIPS distance (0.293 / 0.399) sits below the distance that already separates the two reference implementations from each other (0.347 / 0.465). Side-by-side frames match the lossless output in content, staging, and lighting on all three prompts. ## 0x2. Where the speedup comes from The 0.08 residual threshold works as an adaptive brake: it sleeps on easy content and forces full computation the moment the trajectory drifts, leaving 21 of 49 full video-tower steps on this prompt set. The conservative 0.04 is too sensitive here (33 full steps on the same prompt, 16.45 s). The consecutive-cache cap barely binds at this threshold — cap 1 at the same threshold is strictly slower at equal quality (11.60 s, LPIPS 0.289 / 0.401) — so cap 3 is used. The schedule is deterministic: fresh server launches on the real `quality="high"` code path reproduce the audited sweep outputs byte-for-byte (md5-verified on all three prompts), so the quality gate transfers exactly to the shipped code. Measured on top of the admitted schedule but not enabled here: SubBlock sparse attention (#34148) composes with Cache-DiT and reaches 10.37 s, and passed a 6/6 production-style serving validation on six unseen prompts. Its blk64 kernel needed two separate fixes, both now proposed upstream in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4533 (open, not merged): a deterministic SM103 scheduling hang, and an intermittent CTA wedge — roughly 1 request in 25 — that turned out to be a named-barrier id collision in the kernel's correction warpgroup. With both applied, 100 consecutive requests ran clean and per-request output md5s became deterministic. That last result revises this arm's quality numbers rather than confirming them: the pre-fix kernel silently produced a differing output on roughly one request in six, so the LPIPS figures behind the 10.37 s arm were measured on a nondeterministic kernel and need re-taking before sparse can default. Latency is unaffected. NVFP4 was evaluated and rejected (LPIPS 0.53+ under the same-seed gate even MLP-only, for at most 6% latency). ## 0x3. Sweep and rejected candidates Every line below was measured, not guessed: - threshold 0.04 with cap 1 (the H200 schedule): 33 full steps, 16.45 s — superseded - wider thresholds: 0.24 never triggers the brake and reaches LPIPS max 0.596 — rejected - cache cap 4: LPIPS max 0.53+ — rejected - warmup 3: no end-to-end win, quality drops — rejected - cached audio tower: audio drift leaks into the video tower through the dual-tower bridge — rejected - TaylorSeer order 1: no measurable gain — rejected - `--minimax-h3-adaln-online` with Cache-DiT: corrupted outputs — disqualified - generic Sol-Attn on SM103: slower than dense cuDNN-SDPA — rejected - FA4 attention backend: 4-15% slower per kernel than cuDNN-SDPA at H3 shapes, end-to-end tie — not adopted ## 0x4. Quality protocol Two gates, both must pass. Gate one: frame-aligned LPIPS (AlexNet) at 1 fps against the bit-exact SGLang lossless output — LPIPS measures same-seed trajectory drift, not absolute quality, so the yardstick is stated explicitly: the two reference implementations already sit 0.347 / 0.465 apart, and drift below that line is treated as insignificant. Gate two: human review of consecutive 4 fps frames against a temporal-artifact taxonomy (flicker, coherence, boundaries, mosaic/static regions, ghosting, broken motion, major blur). ## 0x5. Reproducibility and validation - benchmark source rebased onto `41cd5a718`; Diffusers baseline `bb56997d4`, BF16 eager dense, lossless ContextParallel Ulysses8 only - `PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_admission.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sol_attn_backend.py` -> `25 passed, 1 skipped` on the current head - pre-commit hooks pass on every changed file - fresh-launch byte-exact smoke on 8x B300: three prompts, md5 match against the audited sweep outputs, no environment overrides ## 0x6. Risk and rollback The high-quality admission stays fail-closed to the exact B300 device name/capability, topology, task, shape, schedule, flow shifts, eager mode, and native dense attention. The per-deployment schedule map only distinguishes between already-admitted profiles; H200 behavior is unchanged. Removing the B300 deployment branch restores the previous H200-only admission without touching the lossless default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31934159311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934159311)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31934158406](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934158406)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix swa eviction frontier for bigram keys
signals.text: ## Motivation Root fix for the pool-accounting crash that #34823 gated off. On a hybrid SWA model with EAGLE speculative decoding and `SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1` (the default since #34653), every TP rank dies on `pool memory leak detected`. The leaf `cache_unfinished_req` inserts has to keep a full sliding window of live SWA, or the match that follows the insert refuses it. #29860 sized the eviction frontier for exactly that, against `page_floor(pre_len + 1)` as the insert boundary. That holds for a raw key, where `pre_len + 1` is the key length, but an EAGLE bigram key holds one entry less than the tokens it spans, so the leaf actually stops at `page_floor(seq_len - 1)`, and the call site was still passing the token count. Measured on an 8xH200 run with `sliding_window_size=127`, `page_size=64`, `seq_len=1024`: | key | insert boundary | frontier | live tail | vs window | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | raw | `page_floor(1024)` = 1024 | 896 | 128 | ok | | bigram | `page_floor(1023)` = 960 | 896 | 64 | short | ``` COMMIT node_len=960 swa_ev=896 split_pos=896 TOMB node=28 klen=896 VALID node=27 klen=64 acc=64 W=127 ok=False ``` Once the match stops short, `cache_protected_len` never advances, and the next insert treats the slice as a duplicate and frees KV the tree already owns. Passing the key length restores the boundary #29860 assumed, so the frontier moves to 832 and the leaf keeps its full 128-token tail. Swept over every page offset for the window sizes a model actually uses (15, 63, 127, 255, 511, 1023 against page 8, 16, 64, 128), the raw key never fell short before this change and the bigram key never falls short after it, so nothing about the raw path moves. ## Modifications - Build the `RadixKey` before the free call and hand `free_out_of_window_slots` its length rather than `effective_cache_len`. The key is page-aligned afterwards as before. - Drop the EAGLE gate from #34823, which is what that PR deferred to this one. - `TestSWAWindowUnderBigramKey` drives `cache_unfinished_req` on an EAGLE SWA cache and asserts the leaf keeps a full window and the match reaches it. ## Accuracy gpt-oss-120b, 8xH200, TP8, `--page-size 64 --chunked-prefill-size 16384`, EAGLE3 draft `lmsys/EAGLE3-gpt-oss-120b-bf16`, gsm8k 400 questions. | config | accuracy | invalid | leak | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | EAGLE3, OOW=1 (crashed before this fix) | 0.853 | 0.010 | 0 | | EAGLE3, OOW=0 | 0.845 | 0.015 | 0 | | no spec, OOW=1 | 0.840 | 0.020 | 0 | | HiCache, EAGLE3, OOW=1 | 0.855 | 0.013 | 0 | Instrumented on the same tree, the boundary case goes from `swa_ev=896, tail=64, ok=False` to `swa_ev=832, tail=128, ok=True`. The new test fails on main with `4 live SWA tokens against a 7 window` and passes with the fix. `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` and `test_swa_eviction_boundary.py` together: 1048 passed, 0 failed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31898996405](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31898996405)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31898996210](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31898996210)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: O(1) slot allocation in DecodeReqToTokenPool.alloc()
signals.text: ## Motivation `DecodeReqToTokenPool.alloc()` (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py`) has the same free-slot bookkeeping shape as `ReqToTokenPool.alloc()` (fixed in [#32208](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32208)), and the same drawback: it selects free request-slots from the **head** of `self.free_slots` and rebuilds the list from the remainder (`self.free_slots = self.free_slots[need_size:]`). CPython slicing always allocates a new list and copies the surviving `PyObject*` pointers, so this line is O(len(free_slots)) — proportional to how many free slots *remain*, not to how many are being allocated (`need_size`). This pool is decode-side-specific to PD disaggregation: unlike plain `ReqToTokenPool`, it also carries slots for requests that are pre-allocated or mid-transfer from the prefill side (`_alloc_size = size + pre_alloc_size + 1`), so at steady state under high concurrency `free_slots` is not just pool-sized but *larger* than the running-request cap, and stays long precisely in the regime PD disaggregation is meant to help (high concurrency headroom, trickle admission per scheduler step). `alloc()` runs once per scheduler step that admits new decode-side requests, on the single-threaded scheduler process that gates GPU dispatch — so this is wasted allocation-dominated CPU cost on every scheduler iteration, worse than the non-PD case because `pre_alloc_size` inflates the pool further. `free()` is already O(1) amortized (`self.free_slots.append(...)`) and is unaffected. ## Modifications - Pop from the **tail** of `free_slots` instead of the head (`select_index = self.free_slots[-need_size:]; del self.free_slots[-need_size:]`), which only touches the `need_size` removed elements — O(need_size) instead of O(len(free_slots)). - Allocation order has no semantic meaning (`req_pool_idx` is an opaque row index into `req_to_token`/`req_generation`; `req_generation` already tracks reuse separately), so this is a pure performance change, not a behavior change. - Added an explicit `need_size == 0` guard: `free_slots[-0:]` is the *entire* list, not `[]` (`-0 == 0`), so the naive tail-pop would silently drain/return the whole free pool whenever every request in a batch is reusing its slot (e.g. a chunked-prefill continuation batch on the decode side). The guard makes `select_index = []` in that case — same footgun and same fix as `ReqToTokenPool.alloc()`. - No change to `free()`, `available_size()`, `clear()`, `write()`, or the public `free_slots` attribute's type/semantics. - Scoped to `DecodeReqToTokenPool` only. It does not subclass `ReqToTokenPool` (it duplicates `alloc`/`free`/`clear` because of the pre-allocation semantics described above), so the `#32208` fix did not already cover it; `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool` inherits from `HybridReqToTokenPool` separately and is unaffected either way. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This is a pure Python-level bookkeeping change to which integer index is handed out from an interchangeable free-slot pool; it does not touch KV cache contents, tensor values, or model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Added `benchmark/scheduler/bench_decode_req_pool_alloc.py`, comparing the old head-pop implementation against the new tail-pop `pool.alloc()` across a sweep of pool sizes (256–16384) and free-slot ratios (10%/50%/90%), independent of batch size. Steady-state result (pool=16384, ~90% free / 14745 free slots, trickle admission batch of 1-4 — the regime a large `--max-running-requests` with PD pre-allocation headroom actually hits): ``` cell old mean old p50 old p99 new mean new p50 new p99 speedup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- pool=16384 free=14745 batch=1 28515 24625 56917 344 250 3707 82.9x pool=16384 free=14745 batch=4 28746 24833 59412 335 250 3374 85.8x ``` Full sweep (256–16384, 10/50/90% free, batch 1 and 4) shows the same monotonic trend as the non-PD fix: speedup grows with pool size and free ratio (1.1x at pool=256/free=10% up to ~86x at pool=16384/free=90%), because the old cost is dominated by `len(free_slots)`, not `need_size`. This is a scheduler-CPU-dispatch-overhead fix, not a GPU-kernel or network-transfer change, so no end-to-end `bench_serving.py` throughput/TTFT numbers are attached — the effect is real but only becomes visible relative to GPU compute / KV-transfer latency at very high concurrency on the decode side. ## Testing Added `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_decode_req_to_token_pool_alloc.py`: ``` test_alloc_exhausts_pool_then_returns_none ... ok test_alloc_free_alloc_roundtrip_no_duplicates ... ok test_alloc_with_all_reqs_reusing_is_noop_on_free_slots ... ok Ran 3 tests in 0.006s OK ``` `test_alloc_with_all_reqs_reusing_is_noop_on_free_slots` is the regression test for the `-0` slicing footgun — confirmed it fails (`available_size()` incorrectly drops from 4 to 0) against a naive tail-pop fix without the `need_size == 0` guard, and passes against the real fix. Confirmed all three tests pass unmodified against the pre-fix head-pop implementation too (it was correct, just slow), so the suite is purely a behavior-preservation + footgun guard, not a change-detector for the performance fix itself. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31834880961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31834880961)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31834880676](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31834880676)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Avoid deadlock when shared-memory node probe fails
signals.text: Fixes #34800 ## Summary - Keep every rank in `in_the_same_node_as()` on the same broadcast when the source shared-memory probe fails. - Add a two-rank Gloo regression that forces source shared-memory creation to raise `OSError`. ## Root cause `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` previously covered both local shared-memory operations and `broadcast_object_list()`. If source-rank creation failed, it skipped the broadcast while peers waited forever. ## Fix Limit the `OSError` suppression to local shared-memory creation/opening. The source broadcasts `None` on creation failure, reports itself as colocated, and peers report that they are not on the source node. Downstream readers therefore fall back to the remote path without a negative local-reader count. The macOS shared-memory name-length error is one trigger. The regression injects the same `OSError` and is registered in the Linux CPU CI lane to validate the platform-independent collective-safety invariant. Shared-memory name generation is intentionally unchanged. ## Validation - `PYTHONPATH=python python/.venv/bin/python -m pytest test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py::test_shm_creation_failure_keeps_all_ranks_in_the_collective -q` - `SKIP=no-commit-to-branch uvx pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py --show-diff-on-failure` - GitHub Lint: [Run #31923509772](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31923509772) - `git diff --check` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31893507153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893507153)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31893507005](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893507005)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Avoid padded Q for unified DSV4 prefill
signals.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 TP prefill currently allocates a decode-oriented 64-head padded Q tensor, then passes the local-head slice to the unified-KV attention backend. At TP=8 that slice has 16 heads and is noncontiguous, so the OPUS wrapper materializes it with `q.contiguous()` before launching the kernel. The 64-head layout is useful for the FlashMLA sparse decode specialization, but unified-KV extend/prefill does not require it. ## Modifications - evaluate the unified-KV gate once per `MQALayer.forward` call - skip TP head padding for unified-KV extend modes and write Q directly in contiguous local-head layout - retain the existing 64-head padded layout for decode - retain existing behavior for non-unified backends - add real `MQALayer.forward` control-flow tests for unified prefill, decode, fallback, multi-stream, and prefill-CP routing ## Accuracy Tests The focused test runs through the real `MQALayer.forward` control flow and verifies: - unified EXTEND, MIXED, TARGET_VERIFY, and SPLIT_PREFILL use contiguous local-head Q - unified DECODE retains 64-head padding - non-unified modes retain the previous layout - HIP multi-stream and prefill-CP paths preserve the intended decision Result: `4 tests passed` in the official ROCm MI355X image after rebasing onto current `main`. Static validation also passed: Ruff (`F401,F821,UP037`), `py_compile`, registered-test validation, and `git diff --check`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling At the production sparse-prefill shape, the OPUS wrapper-to-kernel delta was 43.5-44.7 us per call across three runs. That delta includes wrapper dispatch and argument handling, so it is an upper bound on the removable contiguous-copy cost, not a model-level or TTFT result. ## Model E2E (MI355X, TP8 / DP1) The branch was rebased onto current `main` (`ab9e7abad`; parent `c87a2ced1`) and tested in the pinned ROCm image on 8 x MI355X. Both arms used unified-KV DSV4 attention, TP8/DP1, chunked prefill 8,192, OSL=1, distinct uncached token sequences, one warmup, and repeated scored requests. - 8K: baseline median **318.23 ms**, candidate **315.29 ms** (**0.93%** improvement); all five output tokens matched. - 64K first sandwich: baseline median **2,790.31 ms**, candidate **2,771.56 ms** (**0.68%** improvement); all five output tokens matched. Candidate had one server-side **11.90 s** outlier, so the five-sample P90/mean regressed despite the steady-state median gain. - 64K candidate follow-up: ten fresh uncached prompts, median **2,772.25 ms**, P90 **2,782.55 ms**, range **2,765.25-2,808.13 ms**, zero retractions; the outlier did not reproduce. - 64K A2/B with the same ten fresh prompt indices: baseline median/P90/mean **2,793.65 / 2,795.65 / 2,793.33 ms**; candidate **2,772.25 / 2,782.55 / 2,775.21 ms**, improving **0.77% / 0.47% / 0.65%**. All ten output tokens matched; neither arm had an outlier above 2x its median. - Baseline A1 -> A2 drift on the original five prompt indices was **0.30%** at the median (A2 slower), below the candidate's steady-state improvement. The result is a small steady-state E2E win, not the larger wrapper-level upper bound. The isolated 11.90 s event is retained as a tail-risk observation; it did not reproduce in either ten-request arm and is not attributed to this Q-layout change. ## Checklist - [x] Add focused unit tests - [x] Preserve decode and non-unified behavior - [x] Provide accuracy and operator profiling evidence - [x] Complete model E2E and graph-capture validation - [ ] Documentation update (not needed for this internal layout change) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31890497031](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890497031)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31890496542](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890496542)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [MoE] Gather the cutlass MoE activation and its scales in one launch
signals.text: ## Motivation The fp8 blockwise CUTLASS MoE quantizes its activation once and then replicates rows per routed expert, so the gather it performs walks a `dst2src` map of `m * topk` entries. Until now it walked that map twice: one `shuffle_rows` launch for the fp8 values and a second one for the fp32 group scales. The second walk moves a thirty-second of the bytes the first one does — `k // 128` fp32 against `k` fp8 — so as a launch of its own it is almost entirely latency. That is exactly the cost that matters where this path spends its time: at low concurrency the whole gather is a few tens of KB, and the launch is the work. Where the gather sits, between quantizing the activation once and the first grouped GEMM: ## Modifications A triton kernel that walks the map once and writes both tensors, registered as a TRITON `KernelSpec` (`op="moe.shuffle_rows_with_scales"`) per RFC #29630. The grid is `(dst_row, k_tile)`; the tile that owns column 0 also carries that row's scales, which are 1/32 the width and do not deserve a launch of their own. The non-mxfp8 path calls it instead of the two `shuffle_rows`. The SM100 mxfp8 ES branch gathers a bf16 activation through a different kernel and is untouched. The two blue arrows are the point: `token 0` is read twice because it routes to two experts, which is why the gather moves `topk` times the rows the quantizer ever saw. The narrow cell trailing each row is that row's scales, and it travels under the same `a_map` — that shared map is the whole reason one kernel can produce both. Rows are copied as bytes rather than as fp8 — the values are never decoded — so the kernel works for any 1-byte dtype and cannot perturb them. Row bases are computed in int64, matching the CUDA `shuffle_rows` it replaces, since `rows * k` overflows int32 well inside the shapes this path serves. The kernel also masks its tails. The CUDA `shuffle_rows` takes its element count as `num_cols / elems_per_thread` with no remainder handling, so it only moves a whole fp32 scale row when `(k // 128) % 4 == 0`; every `k` that is a multiple of 512 is unaffected either way, which covers the shapes this path serves today. **mxfp8 MoE is not affected by this PR.** It will be addressed in the next PR. ## Accuracy Tests The result is **bit-identical** to the pair of calls it replaces, by construction rather than by tolerance. `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_shuffle_rows_with_scales.py` (new) checks that three ways, on B200: against plain torch advanced indexing as the oracle, against the two `shuffle_rows` calls for drop-in equivalence, and on the zero-row short circuit. Comparisons are made on integer views of both tensors — a random fp8 byte pattern is a NaN often enough that `torch.equal` on the float view would report a difference where the bytes agree, and bytes are what the kernel promises. The shape list includes `k = 896` (7 scale groups), which the CUDA reference cannot express because of the remainder above, so that case is checked against the torch oracle only. Maps are drawn with `randint` and therefore contain duplicate source rows, which is the normal case here: a token is replicated once per expert it routes to. ``` 22 passed, 6 warnings in 16.02s ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/moe/bench_shuffle_rows_with_scales.py` (new) benchmarks the fused kernel against the two launches it replaces. On B200 (sm100, torch 2.11.0+cu130, triton 3.6.0), topk 8: | k | tokens | rows | two launches | fused | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 7168 | 1 | 8 | 3.06 us | 1.31 us | 2.33x | | 2048 | 1 | 8 | 2.47 us | 1.42 us | 1.74x | | 7168 | 8 | 64 | 3.25 us | 1.60 us | 2.03x | | 7168 | 64 | 512 | 4.30 us | 2.10 us | 2.05x | | 7168 | 1024 | 8192 | 23.78 us | 11.14 us | 2.14x | ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31938972195](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31938972195) Latest PR Test (Extra): :no_entry_sign: [Run #31940619608](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31940619608)

signals.title: [Spec] Fix SWA eviction bookkeeping for DFLASH-family decode
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation DFLASH-family speculative decode, including DSPARK, reserves target KV headroom through `DFlashDraftInputV2.prepare_for_decode()`, but this path did not run SWA eviction bookkeeping or advance the per-request decode clock used by `ScheduleBatch.maybe_evict_swa()`. For hybrid-SWA models such as DeepSeek V4 Flash, SWA KV usage can then grow roughly linearly with full KV usage during long DSPARK decode, instead of reclaiming out-of-window SWA slots. This can fill the SWA pool and trigger repeated KV cache retractions/OOM behavior even when the model sliding window is small. Validated scenario: - Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (`sliding_window=128`) - Speculative decoding: `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5` - `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1` - Base commit: `8720a72` - Environment: H100 80G x 4, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.13 ## Modifications This PR updates `DFlashDraftInputV2.prepare_for_decode()` to run the decode bookkeeping expected by the SWA eviction path: - Call `batch.maybe_evict_swa()` before reserving new target KV headroom. - Increment `req.decode_batch_idx` once per decode iteration for each active request. `DSPARK` is routed through `SpeculativeAlgorithm.is_dflash_family()`, so it uses this DFLASH-family prepare path. ## Accuracy Tests Not run. This change only updates decode-time KV/SWA bookkeeping. It does not change model forward computation, sampling logits, attention kernels, or accepted token selection. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Functional validation and a lightweight serving benchmark were run on H100 x 4. Server command highlights: ```bash export SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact export SGLANG_DSV4_COMPRESS_STATE_DTYPE=bf16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --port 8000 \ --model-path ./models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --context-length 1048576 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ ``` Benchmark command: ```bash python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang-oai-chat \ --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 32 \ --random-input-len 1024 \ --random-output-len 32768 \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --request-rate inf \ --model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 ``` Results: | Metric | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | KV cache full / retractions | Yes, repeated `KV cache pool is full` | No | | Successful requests | 32 | 32 | | Benchmark duration | 468.00 s | 369.78 s | | Output token throughput | 2240.55 tok/s | 2835.66 tok/s | | Mean TPOT | 8.01 ms | 4.42 ms | | Mean ITL | 8.06 ms | 4.45 ms | | Max ITL | 129233.10 ms | 6761.81 ms | | Accept length | 5.22 | 5.25 | Log behavior: - Before the fix, single-request decode showed `#swa token` growing together with `#full token`. - After the fix, single-request decode kept SWA usage near the sliding-window footprint while full KV continued to grow. - Under the benchmark workload, the pre-fix run repeatedly triggered `KV cache pool is full`; the fixed run did not. signals.title: [diffusion][kernel] Accelerate Sana BCG with bit-exact conv post-processing
signals.text: ## Summary - fuse Sana GLUMB convolution bias + SiLU and bias + GLU post-processing into bit-exact Triton kernels during BCG capture/replay - reuse the shared bit-exact residual-gate-add kernel at the attention and MLP residual sites - materialize the patch-token layout once instead of making every downstream LayerNorm copy the same transposed view - verify each fused convolution path on first sight and permanently fall back to eager if the platform is not bit-exact ## Why The B300 profile showed that Sana BCG was launch-bound after the existing LayerNorm fusion. Repeated `add`, `copy`, `mul`, activation, and gating operations around the GLUMB convolutions accounted for most of the remaining gap to `torch.compile`. The new kernels preserve the BF16 materialization boundaries used by eager PyTorch, so `quality=lossless` output remains bit-exact. ## B300 performance Measured in the 2026-08-14 full sweep from #21 on one NVIDIA B300, Sana 1.5 1.6B at the preset's default 1024px workload: | Mode | Denoise | E2E | |---|---:|---:| | eager | 0.350 s | 0.476 s | | eager + BCG, before this optimization | ~0.333 s | — | | eager + BCG, this change | **0.233 s** | **0.363 s** | | `torch.compile` | 0.272 s | 0.388 s | The optimized BCG denoise latency is about 14.2% lower than `torch.compile` and about 30% lower than the profiled pre-optimization BCG path. ## Validation - added CUDA tests for BF16 channels-last bias-SiLU and bias-GLU; both require `torch.equal` against the eager chain - full pre-commit and CI registry validation pass on the rebased branch - Python syntax compilation passes - original isolated B300 candidate: `099844c2c`; this PR is rebuilt on current `main` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31933846130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933846130)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31943046331](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31943046331)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Enable breakable CUDA graphs for LTX-2.3
signals.text: ## Summary - register Lightricks/LTX-2.3 model IDs and `LTX23PipelineConfig` for breakable CUDA graphs - keep RoPE coordinate creation outside graph capture for legacy one-stage and two-stage paths - extract the existing coordinate preparation into a focused helper and add coverage for disabled, missing, and precomputed coordinates - add an explicit BCG registration test for both LTX-2 and LTX-2.3 ## Why LTX-2.3 uses the same capturable DiT path as LTX-2, but the support gate still rejected its model IDs and pipeline config. Its legacy path can also create RoPE coordinates from host data inside the model forward; doing that during capture causes an illegal unpinned host-to-device copy. Preparing the identical coordinates before entering BCG keeps the lossless eager values while making capture valid. ## B300 performance Measured in the 2026-08-14 full sweep from #21 on one NVIDIA B300: | Preset | eager + BCG denoise | `torch.compile` denoise | |---|---:|---:| | LTX-2.3 TI2V two-stage | 5.397 s | 6.283 s | | LTX-2.3 HQ two-stage | 33.977 s | 40.601 s | | LTX-2.3 one-stage | 23.875 s | 24.005 s | | LTX-2.3 two-stage | 15.095 s | 18.638 s | | LTX-2.3 two-stage CFG-parallel | 15.104 s | 18.638 s | All recorded BCG results were required to hit a real serving capture without capture failure, signature miss, or fallback. ## Validation - added unit coverage for BCG registration and RoPE coordinate preparation - full pre-commit and CI registry validation pass on the rebased branch - Python syntax compilation passes - original combined isolated candidate: `a40940428`; this PR contains only the BCG registration/capture part and is rebuilt on current `main` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31933843606](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933843606)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31936735386](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31936735386)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Reuse bit-exact modulation fast path for LTX-2.3
signals.text: ## Summary - reuse the existing self-verified bit-exact `_ltx2_modulate` fast path after the reference RMSNorm in `quality=lossless` - retain the fused RMSNorm + modulate path for request-scoped `quality=high` - keep the ordinary arithmetic expression visible to Inductor while compiling instead of routing compiled calls through an opaque custom op ## Why The lossless LTX-2.3 path already computes the reference RMSNorm and then launches separate broadcast scale/add operations. The shared modulation fast path preserves that RMSNorm result and its rounding while collapsing the two large pointwise launches. This is independent of enabling BCG for LTX-2.3. ## B300 validation In the 2026-08-14 full sweep from #21, the rebuilt lossless path kept the LTX-2.3 one-stage eager result within measurement noise of `torch.compile` (24.019 s versus 24.005 s denoise), while the two-stage presets remained faster than compile. These are end-to-end sweep results, not an isolated microbenchmark attribution. ## Tests - require `torch.equal` between the lossless fast path and the eager RMSNorm/modulate expression for both video and audio hidden sizes - verify that the compile path never calls the opaque modulation custom op - full pre-commit and CI registry validation pass on the rebased branch - Python syntax compilation passes - original combined isolated candidate: `a40940428`; this PR contains only the lossless modulation part and is rebuilt on current `main` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31933841193](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933841193)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31958334875](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31958334875)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Accelerate lossless Ideogram norm post-processing
signals.text: ## Summary - reuse the bit-exact modulation kernel for lossless Ideogram RMSNorm + scale post-processing - reuse the shared residual-gate-add kernel after materializing RMSNorm and `tanh(gate)` - preserve the existing `quality=high`, compile, and CUDA graph capture paths - cache the zero-shift row used by the scale-only modulation fast path per device, dtype, and hidden size ## Why Ideogram's lossless eager path performs the correct RMSNorm but then launches separate broadcast multiply/add kernels for scale and residual gating. The shared diffusion kernels remove those pointwise launches without changing model parameters or the reference CPU/compile behavior. ## B300 performance Measured in the 2026-08-14 full sweep from #21 on one NVIDIA B300: | Mode | Denoise | E2E | |---|---:|---:| | lossless eager | **2.015 s** | **2.121 s** | | `torch.compile` | 2.120 s | 2.235 s | | `quality=high` | 1.931 s | 2.035 s | Lossless eager is about 5.0% faster than compile on the measured denoise workload. ## Validation - added a CPU reference test for both lossless norm post-processing expressions and state-dict stability - full pre-commit and CI registry validation pass on the rebased branch - Python syntax compilation passes - original isolated candidate: `47338951d`; this PR is rebuilt on current `main` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31933839343](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933839343)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31936303764](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31936303764)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Accelerate Cosmos3 T2I QKNorm+RoPE
signals.text: ## Summary - enable the fused QKNorm + RoPE + KV-pack path for the Cosmos3 image case (`T == 1`) - preserve the eager split path's BF16 rounding boundary before RoPE so lossless output remains bit-exact - store the rounded RoPE cache in the activation dtype once instead of casting in every GEN layer - explicitly keep regional `torch.compile` GEN layers on their existing compile-safe path ## Why Cosmos3 video already uses fused QKNorm + RoPE, but T2I stayed on separate QKNorm, RoPE, and KV concatenation operations because the image path needs an intermediate BF16 round. The shared fused kernel now supports that rounding mode. This change wires Cosmos3 T2I into it and avoids repeated per-layer cache casts and KV packing launches. ## B300 performance Measured with the `cosmos3-nano-t2i` preset in the 2026-08-14 full sweep from #21 on one NVIDIA B300: | Mode | Denoise | E2E | |---|---:|---:| | lossless eager | **0.863 s** | **0.908 s** | | `torch.compile` | 0.997 s | 1.041 s | | `quality=high` | 0.867 s | 0.912 s | Lossless eager is about 13.4% faster than compile on the measured denoise workload. ## Validation - added a CUDA regression test that requires exact equality with separate BF16 QKNorm, RoPE, and KV packing - full pre-commit and CI registry validation pass on the rebased branch - Python syntax compilation passes - original isolated candidate: `dafa75ce5`; this PR is rebuilt on current `main` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31933836637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933836637)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31946430843](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31946430843)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Perf] Fuse prefill norm/act quantization for NVFP4 W4A4 hybrid models (Qwen3.5 family)
signals.text: > **Stacked on #34859 (Qwen3.8-27B Model Support).** This branch includes #34859 plus its main-conflict resolution; the net diff of this PR is the last two commits. Once #34859 merges, this PR rebases to a clean two-commit diff. ## Motivation For Qwen3.5-family hybrid (GDN + attention) models served with a mixed ModelOpt NVFP4(W4A4)+FP8 checkpoint, prefill spends a measurable share of GPU time in standalone norm / activation / quantization glue kernels: every projection input is normalized, written to HBM in bf16, then re-read and quantized by a separate kernel. Kernel-level tracing against vLLM 0.27.1 on the same model showed the GEMM/attention/GDN families at parity while SGLang lost time exclusively in this glue (vLLM fuses norm+quant and act+quant via torch.compile). This PR removes the extra round-trips with three targeted fusions (all bit-equivalent up to FP4/FP8 rounding ties, each with a kill switch): 1. **SiLU+mul + NVFP4 quant** for dense MLPs: replaces `act_and_mul` + the standalone per-block FP4 quantize with FlashInfer's `silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize` (single-group form), handing `down_proj` a prequantized `(fp4, swizzled_scale)` tuple through the existing `_accepts_prequantized_fp4` path. Enabled for both GDN-layer and attention-layer MLPs. 2. **Post-attention GemmaRMSNorm + NVFP4 quant**: FlashInfer `add_rmsnorm_fp4quant` fuses the residual-add, the norm, and the `gate_up` input quant into one kernel. Gemma's `(1 + w)` scaling is folded into a precomputed weight; the swizzled block-scale is exposed as the 2D `(m_padded, K/16)` view so the cuDNN mm_fp4 backend's shape validation also passes. 3. **GDN gated RMSNorm + static-FP8 quant**: adds an fp8-store epilogue to the `fla` `layernorm_gated` Triton kernel (skips the bf16 intermediate write entirely) and teaches `ModelOptFp8LinearMethod` to accept a prequantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple for `out_proj` (explicit opt-in attribute, mirroring the fp4 path). Kill switches: `SGLANG_DISABLE_SILU_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_POST_LN_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GATED_NORM_FP8_QUANT_FUSION=1`. ## Benchmark RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), Qwen3.5-family 27B hybrid GDN model, mixed ModelOpt NVFP4(W4A4)+FP8 checkpoint, TP1, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --disable-radix-cache`, flashinfer 0.6.17. Workload: `bench_serving`, random 8192-in / 1024-out, bs=1, 5 prompts, seed 1234, warmup pass then measured pass; both lanes in one session on the same GPU, base commit 5c9ee86d90. ### TTFT (8k prefill) | | main | main + this PR | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | TTFT mean | 674.8 ms | **640.1 ms** | **−34.7 ms (−5.1%)** | | TTFT median | 665.3 ms | **631.3 ms** | **−34.0 ms (−5.1%)** | ### Decode (unchanged, sanity check) | | main | main + this PR | |---|---|---| | output tok/s (bs=1) | 68.7 | 69.1 | | ITL median | 13.92 ms | 13.86 ms | Per-kernel effect at the 8k prefill step (torch profiler, per forward): the standalone `act_and_mul` (~8.6 ms), the gate_up-input `quantize_with_block_size` pass (~6.7 ms), the down-input `cvt_fp16_to_fp4` pass, and the out_proj `static_quant_fp8` launches (128/forward) are removed or absorbed into the producing kernel; the gated-norm epilogue also skips its 100 MB bf16 intermediate write per layer. The fusions auto-enable only when the touched projections use the matching ModelOpt linear method (NVFP4 W4A4 for 1–2, per-tensor static FP8 for 3), so other checkpoints and quant modes keep their current control flow. ### Accuracy GSM8K via `sglang.test.run_eval` (full test set, 1319 examples, same server flags as above): | | score | |---|---| | fusions **off** (all kill switches set) | 0.9635 | | fusions **on** (this PR default) | 0.9658 | Also verified layer-count wiring at startup (64/64 layers log each fusion) and bit-exact residual propagation (fused kernels update the residual identically to `fused_add_rmsnorm`). ### Data provenance The RTX PRO 6000 tables above were measured with **all three fusions of this PR** applied directly on `main` @ 5c9ee86d90 (commit a452f1ef8c, fusion content byte-equivalent to this branch's net diff), before stacking on #34859. The full stacked branch (#34859 + conflict resolution + these fusions, i.e. this PR's head) was additionally validated end-to-end on an H200 with the FP8 checkpoint (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, dynamic activation), where these fusions by design stay inactive (`fused_lines=0` in server logs) — confirming zero intrusion on non-W4A4 deployments: **H200, full stacked branch vs `main` @ 8922bb98e2, 4096-in/1024-out, seed 1234, same GPU back-to-back** | bs | main (tok/s) | stacked (tok/s) | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 95.9 | 95.8 | ±0 | | 8 | 607.1 | 623.0 | +2.6% | | 16 | 988.3 | 1013.4 | +2.5% | | 64 | 1468.5 | 1486.6 | +1.2% | (gains here come from #34859's model-side changes; this PR's fusions are inactive on FP8-dynamic) | accuracy | main | stacked | |---|---|---| | GSM8K (1319) | 0.9665 | 0.9642 | | AIME25 (30) | 25/30 | 25/30 | A matching bs-sweep + GSM8K + AIME25 matrix for the NVFP4 checkpoint on SM120 is queued (blocked on machine availability) and will be posted in a comment. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [NPU]Ensure tensors allocated by empty_like are contiguous
signals.text: ## Motivation `torch.empty_like(q)` inherits the memory format of `q` by default. If `q` is non-contiguous, `attn_output` may also become non-contiguous, which may lead to failures in downstream NPU operations requiring contiguous tensors. ## Modifications - Allocate `attn_output` with `memory_format=torch.contiguous_format` in attention forward paths. - Ensure `attn_output` has a contiguous memory layout for both extend and decode. ## Accuracy Tests gemma-3-4b-it ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1.
