signals.title: feat: support return_logprob under DSPARK speculative decoding
signals.text: ## Motivation `return_logprob` is rejected under DSPARK, both at admission in the scheduler and again at the top of `DSparkWorkerV2.forward_batch_speculative_generation`. That rejection is scope, not a technical blocker. #33459 added logprob support for DFLASH: it dropped the `return_logprob` check from `validate_dflash_request` (which covered the whole dflash family) and, because only the DFLASH path had been validated, added a DSPARK-only guard in the scheduler to keep DSPARK where it was. The `raise` inside the DSPARK worker predates that and dates back to the original DSPARK PR (#30261). The work #33459 did carries over as-is. DFLASH and DSPARK both verify a linear chain, so row `j` of the verify block is the distribution `out_tokens[:, j]` came from, and the tree accept-index gather that `compute_spec_v2_logprobs` expects degenerates to `arange`. DSPARK's `AcceptOuts.out_tokens` has the same `(bs, chain_len)` shape and the same semantics as DFLASH's — rows past the commit length carry unemitted drafts and are sliced off downstream by the accept lengths. ## Modifications - Extract the chain mapping DFLASH had inline into `compute_spec_v2_chain_logprobs(batch, logits_output, out_tokens)` in `logprob_processor.py`, and call it from both `DFlashWorkerV2` and `DSparkWorkerV2`. DFLASH behavior is unchanged. - Drop the two DSPARK guards: the `raise ValueError` in the worker, and the scheduler's admission branch (which now falls through to the shared `validate_dflash_request`). - Mix `SpecLogprobKit` into `TestBasicSanityDSpark` and remove the `@unittest.skip` that stood in for it. Bumped `est_time` 180 → 300. - Add `test/registered/unit/layers/test_spec_chain_logprobs.py`. The server kits leave one gap: `test_logprob_decode_match_prefill` sends one request at a time, so every request in a batch has the same `top_logprobs_num`, and `test_token_ids_logprob_ragged` only asserts the server does not 500. Nothing checks that heterogeneous per-request logprob params expand in step with the chain row layout — a drift there would silently pair one request's top-k with another request's distribution. The unit test covers that on CPU in ~10s. ## Accuracy Tests On 1x H200 (`fa3` target + draft backend, Qwen3-14B + `dspark_qwen3_14b_block7`, `block_size=7` / 8 draft tokens, overlap scheduling on, accept length 2.9–3.5): **DSPARK vs. no-spec baseline.** Same prompt set through both servers, dumping output token ids, per-token logprobs, top-k lists and token-ids logprobs. Cases were 5 x 64-token completions with per-request `top_logprobs_num` of `[5, 0, 3, 5, 1]` and probe id lists of varying length, plus `max_new_tokens` of 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 13 so completions end mid-chain and the trailing unemitted draft rows have to be sliced off. The two dumps are byte-identical: ``` $ cmp probe_dspark.json probe_baseline.json (no output) DSPARK spec vs no-spec baseline worst max|d| = 0.0000; cases with token divergence = 0 ``` The decode-vs-prefill self-consistency tables for the two servers also match cell for cell (worst `max|d|` 0.1213, 8 top-1 ties flipped), i.e. the residual is the usual bf16 gap between the decode and prefill paths and is present in the baseline too. **Test suites.** - `test_basic_sanity_dspark.py -k logprob` → 6 passed (`test_logprob_decode_match_prefill` reports `max_diff=0.0873 / 0.0792` against a 0.5 threshold). - `test_basic_sanity_dspark.py` (full) → 28 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_basic_math`, which reproduces byte-for-byte on unmodified `main`: Qwen3-14B enters reasoning mode and gets truncated by `max_new_tokens` before emitting `391`. Pre-existing, unrelated to this change. - `test_dflash.py::TestDFlashServerBase` and `::TestDFlashServerOverlap` `-k logprob` → 12 passed. Regression check for the helper extraction. - `test_spec_chain_logprobs.py` → 1 passed. Also checked it fails when the row layout is transposed against the param expansion, so it does guard what it claims to. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No change on the non-logprob path — `compute_spec_v2_chain_logprobs` only runs when `batch.return_logprob` is set, and the DFLASH call site is a straight move of existing code. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31879765400](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31879765400)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31879765275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31879765275)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Fix H3 swap PEFT SwiGLU lora_B halves when loading FFN Lora
signals.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3 fuses SwiGLU `gate` / `up` into one `(28672, 5376)` matrix. The two official layouts store that fused tensor with opposite row order: - diffusers / LightX2V: `ff.net.0.proj` = `[up; gate]` - sglang native: `mlp.fc1` = `[gate; up]` Loading a LightX2V LoRA already renames `ff.net.0.proj` → `mlp.fc1`, but does not swap `lora_B` rows. Shapes match and nothing errors, so the FFN adapter is applied with the two halves reversed. Attention LoRA is unaffected. The two layouts are defined by the `forward` implementations: diffusers [`SwiGLU`](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/v0.37.0/src/diffusers/models/activations.py#L143-L146) (`ff.net.0.proj`): ```python hidden_states, gate = hidden_states.chunk(2, dim=-1) return hidden_states * self.activation(gate) # [up; gate] ``` sglang [`_silu_mul`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py#L271-L272) (`mlp.fc1`): ```python gate, up = hidden.chunk(2, dim=-1) return F.silu(gate) * up # [gate; up] ``` The MiniMax-H3 repo ships the same DiT twice, which confirms the row-order mismatch is in the official weights, not a sglang-only convention: - `FL2VA/transformer/` → `blocks.N.mlp.fc1.weight` (what sglang loads) - `transformer/` → `transformer_blocks.N.ff.net.0.proj.weight` (what LightX2V trains against) | tensor | as-is | after swapping the two 14336-row halves | |---|---|---| | fused FFN `fc1` / `ff.net.0.proj` (52 / 52 blocks) | 0 exact | **52 / 52 exact** | | `fc2` / `ff.net.2` | exact | n/a | They are the same model: native fused `qkv_proj` is bit-identical to diffusers `to_q/to_k/to_v` after the documented per-head `[q,k,v]` pack. LightX2V's own two exports of the same adapter repeat the same signature: | | as-is | swapped | |---|---|---| | `fc1` `lora_A` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a | | `fc1` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | 0 exact | **50 / 50 exact** | | `fc2` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a | `lora_A` lives on the input side, so it does not need a row swap. ## Modifications Swap the two 14336-row halves of `lora_B` only on the `ff.net.0.proj.lora_B` → `mlp.fc1.lora_B` path in `load_lora_adapter`. Leave `lora_A` and `fc2` unchanged. Native fused `mlp.fc1` keys and other models' `ff.net.0.proj` (e.g. Flux) do not match both sides of the guard, so they are not rewritten. ## Accuracy Tests Prompt: `A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves.` Config: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA + `lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo` (`minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_4step_v0.1.safetensors`), 1344×768 / 5 s, `seed=1101`, `lora_scale=0.0625`, `flow_shift=12`, `audio_flow_shift=3`, one H200. Same LoRA, 4-step and 8-step, before vs after this change. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37ee7943-0d37-462a-96c3-fc2be88fca26 Before the fix the fur is smeared; after the fix hair, face, and eyes resolve. Audio RMS also rises (4-step 0.0063 → 0.0097, 8-step 0.0067 → 0.0129). Latency and peak memory are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31880164198](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880164198)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31880164099](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880164099)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU]fix(dspark): preserve parity in folded NPU paths
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. --> This PR fixes numerical and graph-replay parity issues in DSpark's folded NPU paths, then optimizes the enabled paths so they preserve acceptance quality while outperforming the previous all-disabled fallback. ## Modifications - Replace folded sampling based on `softmax(logits / temperature) / Exp(1)` with the equivalent log-space exponential race: - stochastic: `argmax(logits - temperature * log(Exp(1)))` - greedy: direct `argmax(logits)` - Stage exponential noise immediately before graph replay only for stochastic requests. All-greedy requests avoid full-vocabulary RNG and corrected-logit stores. - Keep the dense Vanilla Markov W2 projection aligned with the target LM-head TP vocabulary shard: - compute only the local vocabulary slice; - reduce each local slice to one `(value, token_id)` candidate; - all-gather only the small candidate tensor and select the global top-1 with an NPU Triton kernel; - preserve the eager full-logit path for stochastic sampling. - Add contiguous KDA conv-snapshot and strided temporal-state commit kernels for Ascend, with the existing generic kernels retained as layout fallbacks. - Reshape flattened K tensors to `[tokens, heads, head_dim]` before the Ascend RoPE kernel and apply the same 3-D contract to stacked context KV. - Add NPU and NPUGraph regression tests for proposal parity, near ties, stochastic replay, TP-sharded top-1, production-size vocabulary reductions, and production KDA state layouts. The proposal changes are gated by `is_npu()` and the new state kernels live in the Ascend backend, so GPU execution paths are unchanged. ## Correctness | Check | Result | |---|---:| | Folded proposal vs. eager proposal with actual weights | Draft tokens exactly identical | | Corrected logits maximum absolute error | `0` | | Greedy near-tie case | Matches direct-logit `argmax` | | Mixed sampling with identical exponential noise | Token-by-token identical | | Stacked context K maximum absolute error | `<= 4.88e-4` | | Stacked context V maximum absolute error | `<= 2.44e-4` | | KDA conv/temporal state commits, ordinary + NPUGraph | Bitwise exact | The near-tie regression came from converting logits to softmax probabilities before greedy selection: distinct logits can round to equal probabilities and change tie-breaking. Direct-logit argmax preserves their ordering. ## Performance Tested on four Ascend nodes with Kimi K3 W4A8, TP64/DP4, exact 8,000 input / 1,000 output tokens, one request, four warm-up requests, and seeds 42-46. ### Group A reference: parent code, all four paths disabled ```text SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=0 SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=0 SGLANG_DSPARK_STACKED_CTX_KV=0 SGLANG_DSPARK_EMBED_IN_GRAPH=0 ``` | Metric | Five-run mean | |---|---:| | TTFT | `7609.13 ms` | | TPoT | `15.6189 ms` | | ITL | `15.6189 ms` | | Acceptance length | `~7.392` | ### Final code: optimized paths enabled (`1111`) ```text SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=1 SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=1 # AUTO selects greedy folded sampling; stochastic requests stay eager SGLANG_DSPARK_STACKED_CTX_KV=1 SGLANG_DSPARK_EMBED_IN_GRAPH=1 ``` | Seed | TTFT (ms) | TPoT (ms) | Acceptance length | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 42 | 7731.116 | 15.806716 | 7.1667 | | 43 | 7767.762 | 14.556558 | 7.4667 | | 44 | 7758.790 | 15.001659 | 7.3667 | | 45 | 7789.845 | 15.106276 | 7.3500 | | 46 | 7533.141 | 14.453775 | 7.6633 | | **Mean** | **7716.131** | **14.984997** | **7.4027** | Compared with Group A, mean TPoT improves by `0.6339 ms/token` (`4.1%`) while mean acceptance length remains above 7.4 and mean TTFT remains below 7.8 seconds. ### State-commit microbenchmarks | NPU Event mean | Generic | Optimized | |---|---:|---:| | Conv snapshot, ordinary | 3.0991 ms | 0.0903 ms | | Conv snapshot, NPUGraph replay | 3.1370 ms | 0.0451 ms | | Temporal snapshot, ordinary | 0.6749 ms | 0.1334 ms | | Temporal snapshot, NPUGraph replay | 0.6800 ms | 0.0760 ms | ## Accuracy | Benchmark | Result | Notes | |---|---:|---| | GSM8K-200 | `96.5%` | Initial parity implementation; invalid `0.5%` | | GSM8K-1319 | `94.5%` | Final code; invalid `0.1%`; 1319/1319 complete; no request errors | | GPQA-Diamond | `92.42%` (`183/198`) | Final code; 198 predictions and reviews; no request errors | GPQA uses `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, and `reasoning_effort=max`. The final score is within the existing same-model run range observed on this machine (`91.41%` to `94.44%`). ## Validation - Full pre-commit suite: passed. - Python compileall: passed. - Final NPU/NPUGraph gate: `10 passed`. - Five random 8k/1k runs: 5/5 completed, exactly 1,000 output tokens, no errors. - GSM8K-1319 and GPQA-Diamond: complete, with no API, HTTP, or connection errors. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add NPU and NPUGraph unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation (not required; no public API change). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [KDA] Route Kimi-Linear through native Cake kernels
signals.text: Depends on #34299 for the checkpoint-capable KDA serving surface and on FlashInfer [#4535](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4535) for the native `lower_bound=None` kernels. The incremental commits after #34299's head will narrow automatically when the dependency lands. ## Summary - Auto-select BF16 recurrent state and native Cake prefill/decode for Kimi-Linear-48B's D128 equal-head contract at TP-local H4/H8/H16/H32 (TP8/TP4/TP2/TP1). - Read prefill selection from the runner-scoped linear-attention dispatcher, preserving current server configuration ownership after the upstream backend refactor. - Feed packed projection Q/K/V, raw gate, and beta views directly to FlashInfer without `contiguous()` staging or state gather/scatter copies. - Preserve the native prefill route under breakable CUDA Graph padding by slicing only the live token prefix as storage-sharing row views; unpadded calls preserve exact tensor identity. - Keep admission fail-closed and emit structured per-layer route telemetry proving eligibility, native success, zero fallback/fatal outcomes, graph phase, and static zero-copy ownership. ## Validation - B200 and B300 each pass 85 focused unit tests, 12 GPU decode integration tests, and seven GPU prefill integration tests, including bounded rows, native H4/H8/H16/H32 unbounded routes, checkpoints, packed rows, graph padding, and exact-identity inputs. - The exact-stack FlashInfer matrix passes 93 source/API/JIT contracts, eight prefill GPU rows, and 30 decode/export tests on both architectures. - The final source passes current Black, Ruff, isort, Python compilation, and the repository lint workflow. ## Cold-L2 performance versus FLA Triton All rows use CUPTI GPU activity timing with L2 flushing. Ratios are `FLA / Cake`, so values above 1.0 mean Cake is faster. | Arch | Decode B1 | B4 | B8 | B16 | B32 | B64 | B128 | Geomean | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | B200 | 0.9932x | 0.9501x | 0.9911x | 1.0748x | 0.9899x | 0.9733x | 0.9188x | 0.9835x | | B300 | 0.9854x | 0.9200x | 0.9724x | 1.0571x | 0.9966x | 0.9778x | 0.9321x | 0.9765x | The selected decode topology is `1.0105x` faster than the prior Cake checkpoint on B200 and `1.0386x` faster on B300, reducing the FLA gap from 3.10%/6.12% to 1.68%/2.41%. FLA's multi-kernel prefill active-union/Cake speedups at T=512/1024/2048/4096/8192 are `1.4917x/1.4084x/1.3418x/1.3114x/1.2670x` on B200 and `1.4775x/1.4031x/1.3687x/1.3374x/1.2972x` on B300, for `1.3618x/1.3754x` geometric means. A separate local-H4 split-8/split-16 screen at B=1/4/8/16/32/64/128 found split-16 faster at every row on both targets, by `1.2118x/1.2050x` geometric means. The existing work-based selector therefore already chooses the faster topology throughout the new TP8/H4 route. The final same-stack local-H4 Cake-versus-FLA ratios at B=1/4/8/16/32/64/128 are `0.9927x/0.9648x/0.9526x/0.9748x/0.9451x/0.9955x/1.0617x` on B200 and `0.9688x/0.9626x/0.9638x/0.9797x/0.9649x/0.9716x/1.0647x` on B300, for `0.9832x/0.9817x` geometric means (Cake 1.71%/1.86% slower). Cake is 6.17%/6.47% faster at B128. This bounds the native TP8 kernel residual well below the full-model delta and rules out fallback or a wrong H4 topology. ## Kimi-Linear-48B serving The reference arm uses SGLang's Flash Linear Attention-derived `TritonKDAKernel` (FLA Triton). The one post-interface-change audit runs Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct at TP8/local-H4 on eight B200 GPUs. Both arms use 32 workload-shaped warmup requests followed by 64 measured requests at nominal 2,048 input / 256 output tokens, concurrency 32, seed 20260814, and cache flush. ### Accuracy and stop behavior Both arms use the same 200-example, five-shot GSM8K evaluation: temperature 0, 512 maximum tokens, 128 request threads, and stop token `163586`. | Metric | Cake | FLA Triton | Cake delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | GSM8K accuracy | 0.890 | 0.895 | -0.005 absolute | | Required accuracy | >0.88 | >0.88 | both pass | | Stop-token completions | 200/200 | 199/200 | — | | Length-capped completions | 0/200 | 1/200 | FLA response valid at 512-token cap | Every reported stop matches token `163586`; there are no mismatched stop tokens. ### End-to-end serving performance For throughput, positive Cake delta means speedup. For latency and memory, negative Cake delta is better. | Metric | Cake | FLA Triton | Cake/FLA result | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Completed requests | 64/64 | 64/64 | equal | | Total throughput | 25,490.40 token/s | 30,404.58 token/s | `0.8384x` (-16.16%) | | Input throughput | 22,330.18 token/s | 26,635.11 token/s | -16.16% | | Output throughput | 3,160.22 token/s | 3,769.46 token/s | -16.16% | | Request throughput | 22.480 req/s | 26.814 req/s | -16.16% | | Mean TTFT | 129.163 ms | 113.298 ms | +14.00% | | Median TTFT | 171.820 ms | 84.394 ms | +103.59% | | Mean TPOT | 7.491 ms | 6.023 ms | +24.38% | | Median TPOT | 6.904 ms | 6.254 ms | +10.39% | | Mean ITL | 7.566 ms | 6.028 ms | +25.51% | | Median ITL | 4.055 ms | 4.077 ms | -0.55% | | Peak memory, eight GPUs | 1,366,752 MiB | 1,388,080 MiB | -21,328 MiB (-1.54%) | | Peak individual GPU | 170,940 MiB | 173,606 MiB | -2,666 MiB (-1.54%) | There is no full-model throughput speedup in this TP8 run: Cake reaches `0.8384x` FLA throughput, or 16.16% lower, while saving 1.54% memory. This is reported separately from the native H4 kernel result above, where the cold-L2 decode gap is only 1.71% on B200; the larger serving delta is therefore not hidden as a kernel speedup. signals.title: [Perf] Restore the 16-token router GEMM threshold on SM10X
signals.text: ## Motivation #29470 dropped `max_router_gemm_tokens` from 16 to 4 on SM10X. That doesn't hold anymore: I re-ran its sweep and the JIT `dsv3_router_gemm` wins every `M` up to 12, ties 13-16. Likely #29783, which swapped the fallback it was measured against (`F.linear` → `linear_bf16_fp32`). Unverified. Speculative decoding never gets the fast path: the router sees `M = batch_size * num_draft_tokens`, so EAGLE 5/1/6 is at `M = 6` from concurrency 1. Plain decode keeps it to concurrency 4. So put it back to the kernel's compiled `1..16` range, the same bound `linear_with_fused_a_gemm` already uses. Literal revert of #29470. ## Speed Tests and Profiling 4x GB300, `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP4, `--quantization modelopt_fp4`. ### M sweep, current main Not an exact replication of #29470's: all 16 points instead of 8, and 8192/1024 instead of 1K/1K. No MTP, so router `M == concurrency`. WITH = JIT forced on, WITHOUT = cuBLAS forced on. | M | ITL WITH | ITL WITHOUT | ΔITL | tok/s WITH | tok/s WITHOUT | Δtok/s | winner | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---| | 1 | 6.63 | 6.85 | −3.21% | 144.13 | 140.08 | +2.89% | JIT | | 2 | 7.21 | 7.54 | −4.38% | 256.41 | 246.73 | +3.92% | JIT | | 3 | 8.18 | 8.51 | −3.88% | 332.53 | 321.75 | +3.35% | JIT | | 4 | 8.11 | 8.44 | −3.91% | 435.57 | 421.00 | +3.46% | JIT | | 5 | 9.28 | 9.53 | −2.62% | 470.70 | 461.76 | +1.94% | JIT | | 6 | 9.56 | 9.80 | −2.45% | 536.96 | 527.81 | +1.73% | JIT | | 7 | 9.87 | 10.09 | −2.18% | 599.41 | 588.15 | +1.91% | JIT | | 8 | 9.81 | 10.04 | −2.29% | 672.72 | 660.05 | +1.92% | JIT | | 9 | 10.81 | 10.94 | −1.19% | 684.09 | 679.03 | +0.75% | JIT | | 10 | 11.10 | 11.23 | −1.16% | 730.54 | 724.47 | +0.84% | JIT | | 11 | 11.40 | 11.51 | −0.96% | 773.95 | 767.62 | +0.82% | JIT | | 12 | 11.31 | 11.39 | −0.70% | 834.13 | 829.49 | +0.56% | JIT | | 13 | 12.20 | 12.18 | +0.16% | 837.63 | 839.08 | −0.17% | tie | | 14 | 12.47 | 12.42 | +0.40% | 872.36 | 875.12 | −0.32% | tie | | 15 | 12.67 | 12.63 | +0.32% | 909.12 | 911.54 | −0.27% | tie | | 16 | 12.57 | 12.55 | +0.16% | 960.27 | 961.61 | −0.14% | tie | Against what #29470 reported: | M | #29470, Jun 2026 | current main | |---:|:---|:---| | 1-4 | JIT +1.0 to 2.1% | JIT +2.9 to 3.9% | | 5 | **cuBLAS +1.8%** | **JIT +1.9%** | | 8 | **cuBLAS +1.7%** | **JIT +1.9%** | | 12 | **cuBLAS +1.7%** | **JIT +0.6%** | | 16 | **cuBLAS +3.4%** | tie | Each column is JIT against the fallback of its day (`F.linear` then, `linear_bf16_fp32` now), so this isn't a controlled A/B against their baseline. Every router call in a run sees the same `M`, so this grid derives any threshold `T`: `perf(T, M) = WITH(M) if M <= T else WITHOUT(M)`. `T = 16` wins or ties everywhere. ### E2E, speculative decoding ``` sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --tp-size 4 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 5 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 ``` ``` python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang \ --model nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts 8 \ --max-concurrency 1 \ --warmup-requests 64 \ --flush-cache ``` 19 runs over 7 server launches (9 before / 10 after): | metric | before (M=6 → cuBLAS) | after (M=6 → JIT) | Δ | |:---|---:|---:|---:| | Benchmark duration | 17.041 s | **16.681 s** | **−2.11%** | | Output token throughput | 480.76 tok/s | **491.13 tok/s** | **+2.16%** | | Mean E2E latency | 2127.7 ms | **2082.7 ms** | **−2.11%** | | Mean TPOT | 1.772 ms | **1.730 ms** | **−2.38%** | | Median ITL | 1.750 ms | **1.710 ms** | **−2.29%** | Ranges don't overlap: slowest run after (16.73 s) beats the fastest run before (16.93 s). ITL and TPOT had zero within-arm variance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31927191884](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927191884)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31927191623](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927191623)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [KV Cache] Use exact page demand for paged prefill eviction
signals.text: ## Motivation `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend()` overestimates the capacity needed before paged prefill allocation as: ```python extend_num_tokens + batch_size * page_size ``` This ignores free slots in each request's existing partial tail page and can evict reusable prefixes even when the allocation already fits. For example, with `page_size=64`, `prefix_len=63`, and `seq_len=64`, the one-token extend fits in the existing tail page and requires zero new pages. The current estimate still requests 65 token slots of eviction headroom. ## Modifications - Set the paged-prefill eviction target to `get_num_new_pages() * page_size`. - Add CPU regression tests for page boundaries, cached-prefix survival, and a mixed-batch capacity shortfall. ## Accuracy Tests Target regression: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_alloc_extend_eviction.py ``` ```text 3 passed, 15 subtests passed ``` The tests cover page sizes 16, 64, and 128, verify that a zero-new-page extend preserves an evictable `RadixCache` prefix, and check a mixed batch where the eviction shortfall drops from 353 tokens to the exact 32 tokens. Adjacent allocator regression: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_alloc_extend_eviction.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_alloc_extend_page_estimation.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_allocator.py \ -k 'not TestO3FusedAllocBind' ``` ```text 70 passed, 11 deselected, 15 subtests passed ``` `TestO3FusedAllocBind` was excluded locally because its unrelated Triton JIT tests require Python development headers that are not installed on the test host. ## Speed Tests and Profiling One additional CPU `get_num_new_pages()` call costs about 9-10 us per paged extend batch in the local microbenchmark (batch sizes 1-128). Its inputs are CPU tensors, so this does not introduce GPU synchronization. No general throughput improvement is claimed; the change only avoids unnecessary prefix eviction under page-level cache pressure. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing API or configuration change.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31891562985](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31891562985)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31891562818](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31891562818)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

zero vision parameters materialized - connectors: exact checkpoint coverage; video/audio conditioning relative L2 `0.00273` / `0.00321`, cosine `> 0.99995` - refiner: all 48 layers loaded; final output max abs error `0.0234375` against Diffusers - streaming pre/post-RoPE KV capture and history-prefix injection passed - resident vs layerwise outputs are bitwise identical for the refiner, text encoder, and both connector stacks <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31893100590](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893100590)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31893100482](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893100482)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Quantization] Fix GPTQ scheme attachment broken by LinearBase.scheme default
signals.text: ## Summary #29328 added a class-level `scheme = None` to `LinearBase`, turning GPTQ's `if not hasattr(layer, "scheme")` guard into a no-op — the scheme never gets built and every GPTQ checkpoint dies on load with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'create_weights'`. The probe becomes `layer.scheme is None`, which makes that default load-bearing, so it's declared on the other two bases a GPTQ method can be handed (`VocabParallelEmbedding` for a quantized `ParallelLMHead`, `FusedMoE` for gptq_marlin MoE) and `FusedMoE`'s two `hasattr` weight-loader reads flip with it — leaving those would set `method = None` for every unquantized and fp8 MoE layer on reload. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31927156951](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927156951)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31927156871](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927156871)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Native Pi0.5 SigLIP vision tower
signals.text: ## Summary - extract the existing native SigLIP implementation from Gemma3 into a shared encoder - replace Pi0.5's Hugging Face `PaliGemmaModel` vision tower and runtime attention monkey patch with the native SigLIP/PiGemma composition - preserve both Gemma3 TP packed-QKV weights and Pi0.5 non-TP Transformers checkpoint names - document that the Pi0.5 runtime neural network is fully native ## Why Pi0.5 constructed a Transformers PaliGemma model, deleted its language model, and monkey-patched every SigLIP attention layer after dtype materialization. This left a third-party `nn.Module` in the native runtime and made checkpoint layout, dtype handling, attention selection, and layerwise ownership harder to reason about. The shared native encoder now owns those semantics directly. Transformers remains only for configuration, output dataclasses, and tokenization. ## Validation - remote pre-commit: passed - remote Pi0.5 unit tests: `24 passed` - `lerobot/pi05_base` real checkpoint: strict load passed - old/new real-checkpoint vision features, first-layer prefix K/V, masks, and 2-step actions: bitwise equal, max absolute error `0` - old/new Gemma3 TP SigLIP state-dict and output parity: bitwise equal, max absolute error `0` - H100 single-image SigLIP forward, 50 repeats: median `5.075 ms -> 4.858 ms` (`-4.3%`) The public Python E2E preprocessor could not be run because `google/paligemma-3b-pt-224` requires gated access in the validation environment. The direct policy validation uses the same real checkpoint and covers vision encoding, prefix K/V generation, and action denoising without tokenizer access. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31895887526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31895887526)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31895901766](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31895901766)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 CUTLASS MoE
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion. This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in: ```bash --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 ``` The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged. Related work: - SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816 - FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738 ### FlashInfer version requirement This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP. The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI. The new option therefore requires both: - `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18` - `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change. GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431. ## Modifications ### Runtime selection and compatibility - Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`. - Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90. - Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior. - Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths. - Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI. - Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility. ### Weight preprocessing - Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing. - Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer. - Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2. - Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules. - Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range. - Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path. ### Kernel invocation Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API: 1. FC1 folded weight block scales 2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation 3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale 4. FC2 folded weight block scales 5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale. ### Tests and benchmark - Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with: - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales - EP rank with global expert IDs - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18 - Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare: - SGLang Marlin W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16 - FlashInfer Humming W4A8 - Update the server-argument documentation. ## Accuracy Tests The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed: ```bash python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v ``` ```text 18 passed, 1 skipped ``` The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \ --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` DeepSeek-V4 accuracy was evaluated using the same 200-example GSM8K setup as SGLang #24816. Both runs used the same TP=4 configuration, dataset, sampling parameters, and server options; only `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision` changed between `bf16` and `fp8`. ```bash PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang_dev/python \ python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --port 30000 \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 200 \ --api chat \ --max-tokens 1024 \ --num-threads 32 \ --temperature 0 \ --gsm8k-data-path /tmp/gsm8k-test.jsonl ``` | MoE precision | GSM8K score | Total latency | Output throughput | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | W4A16 (`bf16`) | 0.985 | 37.301 s | 611.809 token/s | | W4A8 (`fp8`) | 0.985 | 32.952 s | 683.574 token/s | W4A8 preserved the W4A16 GSM8K score while reducing evaluation latency by 11.7% and increasing output throughput by 11.7%. The score also matches the 0.985 W4A16 result reported in SGLang #24816. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The downstream benchmark uses the GPT-OSS-like shape from SGLang #24816: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, and top-k 6. Each FlashInfer path was fully autotuned, followed by 5 warmup iterations and 30 timed iterations. The remaining token shapes were run in parallel with one independent shape per H20 GPU; each W4A16/W4A8 pair ran on the same GPU. The benchmark can be reproduced with FlashInfer 0.6.18+: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python:/path/to/flashinfer \ FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py ``` Results on NVIDIA H20-3e: | Tokens | CUTLASS W4A16 median (min) | Humming W4A8 median (min) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 | 0.275 ms (0.272 ms) | 0.164 ms (0.162 ms) | 1.68x | | 16 | 0.842 ms (0.840 ms) | 0.463 ms (0.460 ms) | 1.82x | | 64 | 1.894 ms (1.892 ms) | 1.037 ms (1.019 ms) | 1.83x | | 256 | 2.410 ms (2.403 ms) | 1.478 ms (1.383 ms) | 1.63x | | 1024 | 3.912 ms (3.906 ms) | 2.093 ms (1.999 ms) | 1.87x | | 2048 | 6.973 ms (6.954 ms) | 3.394 ms (3.384 ms) | 2.05x | | 4096 | 13.013 ms (12.971 ms) | 6.295 ms (6.210 ms) | 2.07x | | 8192 | 25.624 ms (25.546 ms) | 12.308 ms (12.293 ms) | 2.08x | Humming W4A8 was faster at every measured token count, with speedups ranging from 1.63x to 2.08x. The gain reaches approximately 2.0x for token counts of 2048 and above. The GSM8K latency and throughput numbers above provide an end-to-end serving sanity check, but the kernel benchmark is the more controlled performance comparison because generated output lengths are not fixed. ## Scope and Limitations - The implementation is SM90-only. - It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path. - A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update is required before production enablement. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions. - [x] Update server-argument documentation. - [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18. - [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result. - [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31955085259](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955085259)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31955085154](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955085154)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(unified-cache): allow multiple concurrent load-back pins per node
signals.text: ## Motivation Under heavy device-eviction↔load-back cycling (small-VRAM GPUs with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, hybrid GDN/mamba models), the scheduler crashes with: ``` AssertionError: node 2498 pinned by load-back 2563, new anchor 2498 ``` at `UnifiedTreeCore.commit_load_back` (`unified_tree_core.py`). Hit repeatedly serving `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` + EAGLE + hicache ratio-12 on RTX 5090 (32GB) under a production-trace replay; 96GB GPUs never trip it (no deep evicted chains → no overlap). ## Root cause `UnifiedTreeNode.load_back_pending_id` is single-valued, but two live load-backs can legitimately pin the same node: 1. Request A load-backs anchored at a **descendant**; its Full-KV chain covers the evicted **ancestor** and pins it (`load_back_pending_id = A`). 2. Before A's ack, request B anchors **at that ancestor** to restore its **independently-evicted mamba state** (`mamba_component.build_hicache_transfers` pins `[node.id]`). 3. The single pin slot can't represent both live pins → assertion (`new anchor` == the node itself, matching the production message shape exactly). The overlap is semantically safe: both in-flight DMAs only **read** the shared host slots, and their writes target disjoint destinations (Full-KV pool vs mamba pool). Only the bookkeeping cannot represent it. ## Modifications - `load_back_pending_id: Optional[int]` → `load_back_pending_ids: set[int]`. - `commit_load_back` adds the anchor id (idempotent for a node sitting in both the Full and an aux transfer list of one anchor). - `finish_load_back` discards its anchor id along the root path; duplicate tracking updates once the last pin drains. - Reclaim guards (`_is_settled_full_host_duplicate`, `_can_reclaim_full_host_duplicate`) and the sanity check test set-emptiness; split inheritance copies the set. ## Test / repro `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_loadback_multipin.py` — a deterministic CPU repro built on the existing `UnifiedRadixCacheSuite` fixtures (FULL+MAMBA): backup → full evict → load-back anchored at the leaf (ack withheld) → load-back anchored at the pinned ancestor. - **Unpatched**: fails in 0.3s with the exact production assertion. - **Patched**: passes; pins drain to empty after both acks; `sanity_check` clean. - Full inherited FULL+MAMBA suite under the new class: 107 tests green. - Serving-level: the patched server sustains 400-span production-trace replays at hicache ratio-12 on RTX 5090 with zero assertions (previously crashed mid-run). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings as needed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31902335393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902335393)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31902335225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902335225)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [misc] Rename shared-read boundary to shared-read ends and fix wrapper delegation
signals.text: Follow-up to #34916. Three things: name the read-end concept after what it is, make wrapper backends answer for the child that actually reads, and cut the fence tests down to what they guard. ### `SharedReadBoundary` -> `SharedReadEnds` The values now say where they sit relative to the two init hooks, instead of leaving the reader to infer it: ```python PRE_REPLAY = auto() # After the init_forward_metadata_out_graph IN_REPLAY = auto() # After the init_forward_metadata_in_graph POST_REPLAY = auto() # Metadata snapshot not implemented UNKNOWN = auto() # not audited -> coarse whole-forward fence ``` `POST_REPLAY` is worth calling out: it is not a design state, it marks a backend whose metadata snapshot is incomplete. Naming it that way is what makes the remaining users of it auditable. Also `shared_read_boundary()` -> `shared_read_ends()`, `_resolve_shared_read_boundary` -> `_resolve_shared_read_ends`, and the local in the resolver -> `declared` (the backend's declaration, as distinct from the resolved point the function returns). ### Wrapper backends now delegate the declaration A wrapper drives one or more child backends but inherited the base declaration and answered for itself. Fixed for all four, via a new `SharedReadEnds.max_of` (the record must cover every child, so the latest end wins): | wrapper | | |---|---| | `HybridAttnBackend` | delegates to `_select_backend(mode)` | | `TboAttnBackend` | max over primary + children | | `HybridLinearAttnBackend` | max over `attn_backend_list` | | `MiniMaxHybridAttnBackend` | max over sparse + dense | This is a real fence bug wherever a wrapped child overrides the default. Concretely, `TboAttnBackend` wrapping `DeepseekV4AttnBackend`: the child declares `POST_REPLAY` for non-DSPARK target verify, the wrapper reported `IN_REPLAY`, so the scheduler was released while the child was still reading across graph segments. Behavior is otherwise unchanged -- children that inherit the default all report `IN_REPLAY`, so the aggregate matches what the wrapper returned before. ### Fence tests: 136 -> 80 lines Dropped the `execute()` harness (fake backend, `ShapeKey`, `PPProxyTensors`, `load_batch`, `device_module`) and the three cases built on it -- ~60 lines guarding six lines of `if` wiring. What is left tests the two methods directly: a five-row table over the resolver, and both branches of `_publish_read_done`. The backend stub is now `create_autospec(AttentionBackend, instance=True)` rather than a `SimpleNamespace`. A hand-rolled stub supplies whatever name the caller asks for, so a renamed method leaves a stale call site in the runner green in CI and broken at runtime; spec'd against the real ABC it fails in the test. Not covered anymore: that the pre-replay record lands before `backend.replay()`. That ordering assertion was the only thing needing the full harness. ### Not in this PR - The default stays `IN_REPLAY`. Moving a backend to `PRE_REPLAY` is a per-backend optimization worth one audit each, not a global flip. - `_resolve_shared_read_ends` still answers two questions (does this phase own the publish, and where do the reads end). Splitting the ownership predicate out is the next step. - The `IN_REPLAY -> PRE_REPLAY` fallback demotes to a point earlier than the declared end; `POST_REPLAY` is the sound direction. Left as a TODO in code -- it is only reachable under `--debug-cuda-graph` and on platforms without external-event support, where the barrier is off anyway. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31935886199](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935886199)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31935886026](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935886026)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] feat: load quantized H3 text encoder checkpoints
signals.text: ## Summary - detect serialized quantization metadata from an overridden native text-encoder checkpoint - opt MiniMax-H3's native Qwen3-VL language stack into checkpoint FP8 while keeping embeddings, normalization, and the vision tower in BF16 - use the generic component-path interface (`--component-paths.text_encoder`, with `--text-encoder-path` as an alias) and fail closed for encoder/format combinations that have not explicitly opted in - document the checkpoint-first workflow without adding text-encoder-specific online quantization flags ## Why MiniMax-H3 uses a large Qwen3-VL prompt encoder, and users commonly want to select a concrete pre-quantized checkpoint for that component. The native encoder loader previously did not resolve the checkpoint's quantization metadata, pass it into the language model, or run post-load processing for quantized linears. The component path is generic, but quantization contracts are not: VAE, image-encoder, and text-encoder checkpoints can use different layer types, scale layouts, and kernels. This change therefore keeps support capability-based instead of claiming blanket quantization support for every component. ## Validation - H100 serialized `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-FP8` load through the normal `sglang serve` download path - complete 5-second 1344×768 T2VA request with the serialized checkpoint and layerwise offload - serialized FP8 TP1/TP2 load and forward comparison - after rebasing onto current `main` and removing the online-only API: `23 passed` in the focused loader/admission suite - changed-files pre-commit passed on the remote checkout <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31935377715](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935377715)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31935377652](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935377652)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] Bound tokenizer-side GPU memory in Kimi GPU image preprocessing
signals.text: ## Motivation `_gpu_preprocess_images` (Kimi K2.5/K3) keeps every image's fp32 patch tensor alive in a list and ends with a request-wide `torch.cat`, so peak GPU memory in the tokenizer process is ≥2× the request's total patch bytes and unbounded in image count/resolution. On deployments running a high `--mem-fraction-static`, a large multi-image request OOMs device 0, and the caching allocator retains the peak permanently. ## Modifications - `_gpu_preprocess_images`: process size-groups in sub-batches capped by `SGLANG_MM_GPU_PREPROCESS_CHUNK_BYTES` (default 512 MB); return per-image tensors instead of a request-wide concat; optionally hand each image to a `per_image_sink` as it is produced. - `MMFeatureStreamSink` (K2.5/K3): hash each image and wrap it into the CUDA-IPC pool (or move it to host for non-IPC transports) at production time, so peak GPU usage is one sub-batch plus one image regardless of request size. - `get_new_expanded_mm_items`: split list-shaped bundled features by element and preserve production-time hashes (`PRECOMPUTED_FEATURE_HASHES_KEY`) instead of re-hashing wrapped features. `mimo_v2` has the same accumulate-and-concat pattern; can be ported in a follow-up. ## Accuracy Tests Outputs are bit-exact with the previous pipeline and hashes are unchanged (same bytes, same algorithm), so radix-cache keys are stable — asserted by `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_kimi_mm_preprocess_bounded.py` across size-groups, chunking, and K3 RGBA compositing. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test_peak_memory_bounded` (H100): unchunked peak ≥2× total patch bytes; new peak ≤4× chunk bytes, independent of image count. Kernels are unchanged; chunking only splits batched launches. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31923380287](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31923380287)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31923380236](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31923380236)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] fix: make MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache rebuild transactional
signals.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3 can rebuild AdaLN outputs from checkpoint weights on demand and memoize the resulting timestep plans across requests. Two cache bookkeeping paths could leave the cache inconsistent: 1. When a new request exceeded `max_plans`, the cache cleared all resident plans but rebuilt only the plans that had been missing before the clear. If the request also reused an existing plan, that plan disappeared from the slab and its later lookup failed during denoising. 2. A plan was added to the host-side `_slots` index before all checkpoint reads and projections completed. If rebuilding raised midway, a retry treated the incomplete plan as a cache hit, skipped rebuilding it, and then failed because its zero `plan_lengths` entry remained invisible to lookup. The cache also accepted non-positive plan capacities, which could create degenerate slabs and fail later with less actionable errors. ## Modifications - Rebuild every plan required by the current request after a capacity reset, including plans that were cache hits before the reset. - Validate the request's plan count and width before clearing resident cache metadata, so an invalid request does not destroy a usable cache. - Keep new slot assignments in a pending host-side map while checkpoint weights are read and projected. - Publish `_slots` only after every layer has been written and the corresponding `plan_lengths` entries have been activated. A failed rebuild therefore leaves the incomplete slots invisible and allows a later request to retry. - Reject non-positive `max_plans` and `max_plan_width` values at cache construction time. ## Accuracy Tests The change only updates cache admission and metadata publication. It does not change timestep embeddings, checkpoint reads, tensor-parallel sharding, GEMM shapes, collectives, or cached output tensors. - Forced the capacity-reset path with a request containing both a previously resident plan and a new plan. All plans required by the request remained available to lookup after rebuilding. - Checked 470,367,744 AdaLN output elements against resident `adaln_proj` projections at both TP1 and TP2: zero mismatches. - Compared online-rebuild and resident-weight end-to-end outputs at TP1 and TP2. For both cold and cached cases, the online-rebuild MP4 MD5 matched the corresponding resident-weight run. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This is a correctness-only cache bookkeeping change. The normal successful rebuild path performs the same checkpoint reads, projections, and collectives as before. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31926449143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31926449143)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31926448971](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31926448971)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Build Rust extensions on demand in source checkouts
signals.text: ## Motivation Source checkouts (editable installs) currently require the PyO3 extensions (`sglang.srt.grpc._core`, `sglang.srt.server._core`, `sglang.srt.multimodal._core`) to be prebuilt into the wheel: importing them from a plain checkout fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` (or, for `--grpc-port`, a hard `RuntimeError`). This adds an on-demand build path so a source checkout with a Rust toolchain just works. ## Modifications - New `sglang.srt.rust_extension.load_rust_extension()`: prefers a module bundled in the installed wheel, then a content-fingerprinted cache under `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/rust_extensions`, and finally builds the crate with `cargo build --release --locked`. Crates are discovered from the same `[package.metadata.sglang] python-module` manifest metadata that `setup.py` uses, so new crates need no registration. Concurrent builds are serialized with a file lock and artifacts are staged atomically. - New env `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=auto|never|force` controls the behavior. - The three existing import sites (`http_server.py` gRPC startup, `RustServer.launch`, inkling `image_processing_rust.py`) go through the loader. - `python/sglang/srt/server/__init__.py` makes the extension package importable in source checkouts. - `rust/Cargo.lock`: bump the dynamo crate family (dynamo-protocols 5.1.0→5.3.1, dynamo-parsers 7.0.1→7.1.1, dynamo-renderer 5.0.0→5.0.1, dynamo-tokenizers 1.7.0→1.8.0, plus their transitives) via targeted `cargo update --precise`; dynamo-protocols 5.3.1 adds the `token_id` field, which `chat_logprobs` now populates. - Unit tests for the loader in `test/registered/rust/test_rust_extension.py` (mock-based, no cargo invocation at test time). Note: the source change also touched a `test/registered/rust/test_cargo_workspace.py` (`cargo test --workspace` → `--locked`); that file was intentionally removed here by #34309, so that part is dropped rather than re-added. ## Test plan - `cargo check --locked -p sglang-server` passes with the updated lock. - `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server chat` — 15 passed, including the updated `chat_logprobs` test asserting `token_id`. - Loader logic validated directly against the checked-in workspace: crate discovery for all three crates (package/lib/features), bundled-import fast path, `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE` default, and build-context fingerprinting. - `python3 -m py_compile` on all changed Python files. - Not run: the full `test_rust_extension.py` via the CI harness (local venv has an unrelated `transformers`/`kernels` import breakage); CI will run it. No GPU/runtime serving test was run — the change is import-path plumbing only. ## Original commits - `6e7fcf6b3` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31938576707](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31938576707)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31938576537](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31938576537)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix world-size-one aliasing in MLP batch sync

signals.title: [Diffusion] Reuse SRT CLIP encoder blocks
signals.text: ## Summary - remove the duplicated CLIP embedding, attention, MLP, and encoder blocks from `multimodal_gen` - reuse the native SRT CLIP modules and tensor-parallel linear layers while keeping the diffusion output/loader wrappers - give the shared CLIP attention explicit text-causal vs. vision-bidirectional semantics - centralize encoder TP-group execution for all native text/image encoders and reused SRT modules - add a two-GPU tiny-SD3 end-to-end guard for encoder `fold` vs. `replicate` ## Why The two CLIP implementations had drifted in both behavior and maintenance: - padded CLIP text input dropped causal masking in the diffusion copy - SRT CLIP vision attention was accidentally causal - model blocks, TP loading, and mask handling were implemented twice Encoder folding also built and sharded a reused SRT encoder under the folding group, then restored the DiT TP group before forward. SRT layers that resolve their collective group at execution time could therefore run their folded weights with the wrong group. Model-specific group patches had started to grow around this behavior and did not protect every encoder entry point. `use_tensor_parallel_group` now switches MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP as one nested context and restores each previous value on exit. Native encoder roots bind the group used to build their shards through `EncoderTensorParallelMixin`, so construction, weight loading, and every public forward use the same group. The retained CLIP wrappers own only diffusion-specific output selection, pooling, and weight loading. The duplicated MMGen implementation is removed. ## Validation - H100, real `openai/clip-vit-base-patch32` BF16 weights: all 148 text and 151 vision parameters loaded - TP=1 parity after the fix: text (masked and unmasked) and post-norm vision outputs match Transformers exactly - TP=2: both ranks produce identical outputs; mean absolute difference vs. the replicated BF16 Transformers reference is `0.0141` - layerwise offload: text and vision encoder stacks are detected and two consecutive streamed runs match resident outputs exactly - H100 batch=4, 500 measured iterations: vision encoder median `1.814 ms -> 1.584 ms` (`-12.7%`) - tiny SD3 native e2e, identical 2-GPU Ulysses topology: encoder `fold` vs. `replicate` gives SSIM `0.994886`, PSNR `43.625576`, MAD `0.771159` - negative control on the pre-fix runtime gives SSIM `0.924886`, PSNR `30.782886`, MAD `5.275228`, and the new e2e fails as intended - exact final SHA `33a240aa067b5`: standalone fold suite `2 passed`; focused group/folding/SigLIP unit suite `40 passed` - full pre-commit range passed; no consistency GT or threshold was changed ## Correctness regressions fixed With the previous CLIP implementation and the same real weights: - padded text vs. Transformers: max absolute difference `31.375` - post-norm vision vs. Transformers: max absolute difference `10.5` Both are `0.0` after this change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31984970487](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31984970487)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31984970374](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31984970374)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Reuse SRT Qwen vision and text modules
signals.text: ## Motivation The multimodal generation Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3, and Qwen3-VL encoders duplicated pure modules already implemented in SRT. Maintaining both copies also left the MMGen paths without reusable SRT tensor-parallel projections, embeddings, activation kernels, and checkpoint loaders. ## Modifications - Reuse SRT Qwen vision patch embeddings, MLPs, patch mergers, RMSNorm, and tensor-parallel linear layers from MMGen. - Reuse SRT Qwen2.5 text projections, split `Qwen2_5_VLMLP`, HF-semantics `RMSNorm`, and `VocabParallelEmbedding`. - Reuse SRT `SiluAndMul` and `RMSNorm` in the native Qwen3 and Qwen3-VL text paths. - Extend SRT RMSNorm kernels to flatten and restore higher-rank activations when a residual is present. This is required by diffusion text encoders with `[batch, sequence, hidden]` states. - Keep the Qwen2.5 split gate/up execution order as `act(gate) * up`; this avoids a concatenation and preserves HF numerical behavior. - Use replicated SRT linears at TP=1 and explicit TP rank/size at TP>1, while retaining the existing replicated fallback when a dimension is not TP-divisible. - Share one MMGen packed-sequence attention adapter between Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL. It remains MMGen-owned because diffusion backend selection and segmented SDPA fallback differ from SRT serving's attention contract. - Reuse SRT MRoPE in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL text attention. Keep MMGen LocalAttention and Qwen3-VL quantized linears because their diffusion runtime and quantization contracts differ from SRT serving. - Map MiniMax-H3 checkpoint `.attn.qkv.` names to the native SRT `.attn.qkv_proj.` parameters. - Keep `model.visual.blocks` and language-model layer ownership unchanged so layerwise offload and FSDP selection continue to work. - Bind each native encoder root to the TP group used to construct and shard it. One nested context now switches MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP together for construction, loading, and forward, then restores their previous values independently. ## Accuracy and Integration Tests Latest validation on H100 at exact head `0844a9a3088f3`: - Focused Qwen, encoder-folding, and group-lifecycle unit tests: `55 passed`. - The new two-GPU no-download guard uses a real SRT `RowParallelLinear` with DiT TP=1 and folded encoder TP=2. Its output matches the complete unsharded linear reference, and MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP all restore to size 1 after forward (`1 passed`, 24.63s). - Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL SRT MRoPE versus Transformers: FP32 maximum absolute error `2.38e-7`; BF16 maximum absolute error `0.015625` (1-2 ULP), with mean absolute error between `1.8e-4` and `4.0e-4`. - Qwen2.5-VL/Qwen3-VL batched GQA layout, three-axis positions, Transformers v5 RoPE config, and attention wiring are covered by focused tests. The full native server/pipeline encoder `fold` versus `replicate` e2e guard is in #35004. On its pre-fix runtime negative control it fails with SSIM `0.924886` and MAD `5.275228`; after the shared group fix it passes with SSIM `0.994886` and MAD `0.771159`. No consistency GT or threshold was changed. Broader component and E2E validation at parent head `6e57d71d6efe2`: - Focused GPU unit/component suite: `26 passed`, plus 2 parameterized subtests. - Qwen2.5 TP=2 MLP matches the previous MMGen implementation exactly; TP=2 embedding output is exact. - Qwen2.5 full-GEMM comparison differs only by expected BF16 TP reduction order (`max_abs=3.81e-6`). - Real Z-Image Qwen3 text component: cosine similarity `0.999898`. - Real Qwen-Image server/API case: CLIP/SSIM `1.0`, infinite PSNR, zero pixel difference; `/v1/models` success and not-found paths passed. - Real MiniMax-H3 2-GPU video E2E: minimum CLIP `0.9953`, minimum SSIM `0.9687`, minimum PSNR `43.06`. - Existing Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL vision TP=1/TP=2, layerwise-offload, component-accuracy, and Qwen-Image-Edit E2E checks remain covered. ## Performance - Qwen2.5 split text MLP, real model size, H100: paired median ratio `0.9961` versus the previous MMGen implementation. - Qwen-Image E2E: `12697.67 ms` versus `12799.17 ms` baseline. - MiniMax-H3 2-GPU E2E: `47120.89 ms` versus `47538.57 ms` baseline. - Existing full vision-tower measurements remain 1.08x faster for Qwen2.5-VL and 1.19x faster for Qwen3-VL. These measurements show no observed regression; the E2E results are within or better than their checked-in baselines. ## Checklist - [x] Full pre-commit range passed. - [x] Focused unit and weight-transfer tests passed. - [x] Validate folded SRT collectives and TP-group restoration on two GPUs. - [x] Validate TP=1, TP=2, higher-rank residual RMSNorm, layerwise offload, component accuracy, and real server E2E. - [x] Validate Qwen-Image public image/model APIs. - [x] Public CLI and model compatibility are unchanged; no documentation update is required. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31958834919](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31958834919)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31958834804](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31958834804)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] Classify PIL decode-time failures as client errors (400)
signals.text: ## Motivation Image bytes that pass PIL's `open()`-time format sniffing can still fail during the eager `img.load()` in `_load_single_item`: - a PNG whose corruption sits **past the first IDAT chunk** raises `SyntaxError("broken PNG file")` — `Image.open` only parses up to the first IDAT, so sniffing succeeds; - a truncated file raises `OSError("image file is truncated")`. Neither type is in `CLIENT_MEDIA_EXCEPTIONS` (`UnidentifiedImageError` only covers open-time sniffing failures), so these requests return **500** instead of **400**. Observed in production: a client with a broken screenshot pipeline retried the same corrupt PNG repeatedly, each attempt logged as an internal server error. ## Modifications Add `OSError` and `SyntaxError` to `CLIENT_MEDIA_EXCEPTIONS`. The existing `ValueError`-preserving wrap layers already carry the classification to the serving layer's 400 mapping. Tests (`test_base_processor_bad_input.py`) lock both corruption shapes against a multi-IDAT PNG where `open()` succeeds and `load()` fails: - zeroed later chunk header → `SyntaxError` → `ValueError` - truncation → `OSError` → `ValueError` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31931370470](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31931370470)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31931370348](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31931370348)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix Qwen3 Coder stalls on large string tool arguments
signals.text: ## Motivation Qwen3 Coder emits tool calls in an XML-like format. The streaming parser currently buffers every parameter value until it sees `</parameter>`. For large string arguments such as generated source files, the model keeps producing tokens but OpenAI-compatible clients receive no argument deltas. Client-side inactivity watchdogs can therefore time out and retry a healthy generation. Credit to @ccq1: #25246 first identified this root cause and proposed incremental string emission. This PR reworks the fix on current `main` and preserves behavior added since that PR, especially complex JSON Schema type inference and nullable-string `null` conversion. Related: #27005. ## Modifications - Stream schema-inferred string parameters as JSON-escaped argument fragments while their XML parameter is still open. - After at most four characters of `null` disambiguation, retain only a possible split terminator suffix and one trailing newline instead of the full argument, keeping the parser buffer bounded for large values. - Keep non-string parameters on the existing complete-value conversion path, including `anyOf`/`oneOf` schemas. - Delay string quoting for at most four characters to distinguish a JSON `null` value from a string beginning with `null`, preserving existing nullable-string semantics. - Add regressions for pre-close deltas, JSON escaping, split closing tags, bounded 128 KiB streaming, typed parameters after a streamed string, and nullable strings. ## Accuracy Tests - All 19 parser-only `TestQwen3CoderDetector` tests pass locally (the `xgrammar` construction-only test was excluded because the macOS test host does not have that optional runtime dependency). - A focused parser suite passes 9/9 tests, including 40 randomized chunk-boundary reconstructions and 330 nullable-string boundary cases. - The existing streaming nullable-`anyOf` array test remains green, confirming that complex non-string schemas are not accidentally streamed as strings. - `black==26.1.0` and `ruff==0.15.1 --select=F401,F821,UP037` pass on both changed files. The parser output is unchanged after fragments are concatenated; only the timing of string argument deltas changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling In a local end-to-end DSH run, a 250-line file-writing argument produced 256 argument deltas with a maximum 287 ms inter-delta gap. The task remained active for more than 300 seconds and completed without the inactivity retry seen with the buffering parser. The unit test also streams 128 KiB through an open string parameter and asserts that the parser buffer never grows beyond the terminator length. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository-pinned Black version. - [x] Add unit tests for the parser regression and compatibility cases. - [x] Documentation is not needed; this changes internal streaming timing without changing the public format. - [x] Provide end-to-end timing and bounded-buffer results above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31932735293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31932735293)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31932735059](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31932735059)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(hicache): scope write-back load-back pins by component
signals.text: ## Problem In write-back mode, `UnifiedTreeNode.load_back_pending_id` is a node-wide, single-anchor guard for in-flight H→D DMA. However, residency and load-back decisions are component-scoped. A shared radix-tree node can independently hold Full, SWA, or Mamba data on Host or Device. Each request rebuilds transfers per component, so two requests with different anchors can legitimately load different components from the same node before the first DMA ACK arrives. A concrete sequence is: 1. Request A has a deep anchor. The shared node is in its Full prefix but outside its SWA window, so it loads `Full(node)` and stores anchor A in the node-wide pending field. 2. Before A's ACK, request B has a nearer anchor. Full is already represented as device-resident by A's commit, but SWA is still Host-only and falls inside B's window, so B loads `SWA(node)`. 3. The second commit checks the same node-wide field and rejects anchor B: ```text assert pending_anchor in (None, anchor_b) ``` The two operations read different component host pools and are safe to run independently, but the node-wide single-anchor state treats them as conflicting. ## Solution Scope write-back load-back pins to `(node, component, transfer)`: - add `ComponentData.load_back_pending_transfer_ids`; - allocate a unique transfer ID for each H→D operation; - use the transfer ID as the cache-controller ACK key; - pin only the component entries actually listed in each `PoolTransfer.nodes_to_load`; - clear only that transfer ID when its ACK completes; - allow different components, and multiple transfers, to remain independently pending on one node; - use only Full-component pending IDs to protect Full Host duplicate reclamation; - validate pending transfer IDs against live operations in `sanity_check()`. The existing node-wide field remains untouched for non-write-back behavior. This PR is intentionally separate from #34519, which limits node-wide pending behavior in write-through mode. ## L3 considerations Storage prefetch can create Host-side nodes or split an existing node before a later H→D ACK. The fix therefore also: - copies component pending transfer-ID sets when Full/SWA data is redistributed during node split; - keeps Full duplicate tracking deferred until the corresponding load-back ACK; - verifies the real file-storage path: L3 → Host insertion → H→D load-back → ACK cleanup → explicit sanity check. ## Tests Focused regressions cover: - different anchors loading Full and SWA from the same shared node; - multiple transfer IDs pending on the same component and cleared independently; - Full duplicate tracking after an L3-refilled Host copy is loaded back; - node split inheritance of Full/SWA pending transfer IDs. Validation: ```text 99 passed, 308 skipped ``` The selected suite includes all load-back tests, storage-prefetch corruption tests, L3 write/prefetch tests, and the new regressions. The explicit write-back file-L3 round-trip ran across Full and Full+SWA configurations with multiple page/window sizes: ```text 13 passed, 6 skipped ``` Each successful case performs L3 prefetch into a fresh tree, Host→Device load-back, ACK processing, KV-byte verification, and `sanity_check()`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31933353632](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933353632)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31933353414](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933353414)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
