signals.title: [AMD] Reuse DSV4 logits workspace for long contexts
signals.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 prefill calls the AITER C4 indexer with an FP32 logits tensor shaped `[total_tokens, max_seq_len]`. For long prompts, `max_seq_len` grows for every chunk, so allocating this tensor on every call leaves a sequence of differently sized blocks in the caching allocator. In DP8 testing, a 756K-token request exhausted device memory after about 376K processed tokens even though the persistent KV pools had enough capacity. ## Modifications - reuse one eager AITER logits workspace per device and CUDA stream - grow workspace capacity geometrically to the next power of two and return an exact shaped view - allocate graph-owned storage during CUDA graph capture instead of retaining an eager workspace - add CPU CI coverage for reuse, geometric growth, stream isolation, capture behavior, and invalid dimensions ## Accuracy Tests This changes workspace ownership only. The existing AITER kernel receives the same FP32 dtype, logical shape, and arguments. Patched 756K c1 and c8 requests completed with zero cache hits and zero retractions. - `test_dsv4_indexer_logits_workspace.py`: 3/3 pass - `test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py`: 7/7 pass - MI355X eager workspace smoke: pass ## Speed Tests and Profiling DeepSeek-V4-Pro, DP8/EP8/TP8, MI355X, original `mem_fraction_static=0.90`: | Input | Result | | --- | --- | | 756K, c1 | 142.350 s TTFT | | 756K, c8 | 221.501 s median TTFT, 222.085 s P99 | The unpatched run OOMed after about 376K processed tokens. Lowering `mem_fraction_static` to 0.75 only moved the failure to about 663K. The reusable workspace completed both c1 and c8 at the original 0.90 setting, preserving persistent KV capacity. A patched 128K control showed no TTFT regression. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Add focused unit tests and run neighboring DSV4 indexer tests. - [x] Documentation is not required for this internal workspace ownership change. - [x] Provide long-context validation and performance results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31934229974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934229974)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31934229857](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934229857)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(npu): split packed MTP HiCache transfers by pool
signals.text: ## Summary - split Ascend packed MTP HiCache transfers across the target and draft device pools - slice the packed host K/V buffer to the matching layer range for each device pool - keep CUDA's existing packed per-layer pointer path unchanged ## Root cause This is a follow-up to #32500 and #34560. It depends on #32500; #34560 is already merged into `main`. #34560 appends the NEXTN/MTP draft KV layers to the target host pool, so the host K/V layer dimension covers `target + draft`. With #32500, Ascend uses the fused `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` path for `page_first_direct`, but the transfer was invoked once with only the target device pool and the full packed host buffer. The target and draft device layers are separate pools, so the device and host layer ranges did not match and the draft KV was not transferred correctly. The CUDA path does not have this problem. It packs target and draft per-layer pointers into one pointer array, and the staged kernels dispatch each host layer through its corresponding device pointer. The Ascend fused operator accepts one contiguous device pool per invocation, so it must be called separately for the target and each draft pool. ## Changes On Ascend, `_npu_transfer_buffers` now walks the target and draft pools, obtains each pool's contiguous HiCache K/V buffers, slices the packed host K/V layer range, and issues one fused H2D or D2H transfer per pool. Ascend no longer attempts to build the CUDA-style packed pointer arrays. ## Validation - focused unit tests on latest `upstream/main`: `2 passed` - NPU packed MHA initialization does not require CUDA pointer arrays - target/draft H2D and D2H transfers use matching host-layer slices - pre-commit on all six files in the stacked diff: passed - Qwen3.6-27B, TP2, Ascend NPU, `page_size=128`, 4 prompts, input 3000/output 512 on latest `upstream/main` (`117edb499`): - NEXTN L2: 4/4 prompts hit 2944 device tokens - NEXTN Mooncake L3: 4/4 prompts hit 2944 storage tokens - L2/L3 replay output IDs were identical (`sha256=80bd5171ccc62c4a8a5c5d0753d31c82437561e89c0df1b12e0738d5b1a61695`) - L2/L3 weighted accept rate was identical at `63.6795%`; weighted accept length was identical at `2.9132` - NEXTN-disabled comparison on the fix stack: L2/L3 each hit 2944 tokens for 4/4 prompts and replay output IDs were identical (`sha256=b2f62b4a23240036f43ec5cceba736b81f06f57f4182e4c579146ec79d4dff34`) Cold generation and cache replay can diverge token-by-token, but the same behavior is present with the L1 radix cache. L2 and L3 replay are identical in both NEXTN modes, so Mooncake L3 does not introduce an additional state-restoration divergence.
signals.author: momaekar1

signals.title: [diffusion][Model] Support MAGI-2-preview
signals.text: ## Motivation Relate #35011 Adds native support for [MAGI-2-preview](https://huggingface.co/sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview), SandAI's 114B MoE model that generates a video and its synchronized stereo soundtrack in one denoising trajectory. About 6B parameters are active per token. Audio is not a second pass over finished video: video and audio latents share one packed sequence and one denoise loop. Text-to-video and image+text-to-video are both supported. The checkpoint ships two DiTs. A preview model denoises the clip, and a refiner then takes that result to 1920x1088; the words "preview" and "refiner" below always mean those two. Serving it today means standing up a second stack. The reference implementation launches under `torchrun`, depends on SandAI's own kernels ([MagiAttention](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiAttention), [MagiCompiler](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiCompiler), FlashAttention 3) and so ships as a [Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/sandai/magi-2-preview), and its checkpoint has no `model_index.json`. This PR builds it against SGLang's own layers so it is served like every other family in `sglang.multimodal_gen`. ## Modifications ### New code Four pieces the tree did not already have. Everything else goes through existing machinery. - **Multi-head MoE** (`runtime/layers/moe_multihead.py`). MAGI-2 routes 12 independent heads over 256 experts each, top-6, where the tree's MoE assumes one routing head. Viewing tokens as `[N * 12, 256]` instead of `[N, 12, 256]` makes it a standard MoE with `hidden_size=256` and `num_experts=3072`, so srt's Triton `fused_experts` runs unmodified. MAGI-2's activation, which it calls `swiglu7`, is a sigmoid-gated GELU approximation clamped to ±7 and maps onto that kernel's existing `gemm1_alpha` and `gemm1_clamp_limit`. - **Attention sinks** (`runtime/layers/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`). Both DiTs use one always-attended sink token per sequence, and the FlashAttention backend accepted no `sinks` argument, so those logits were dropped silently. Now plumbed through, along with `window_size`. - **Block-window local attention** (`runtime/layers/attention/magi2_block_grid_attention.py`). Every refiner layer restricts video-to-video attention to a radius-(2,2,2) ball on the 3-D latent block grid, which no `(left, right)` flash window can express, so it is carried as a `flex_attention` `BlockMask` built from tile occupancy rather than through `create_block_mask` and its dense intermediate. - **Multi-stream hyper-connections**, mHC (`runtime/models/dits/magi2_mhc.py`). The preview DiT's residual is 4 parallel streams of 3072 rather than one of 12288, mixed by a per-block matrix that Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization keeps doubly stochastic. ### Reused from the tree Both DiTs are wired to the existing optimizations rather than reimplementing them: - **Ulysses sequence parallelism** carries the packed sequence. Rows are sharded once per forward and gathered at the end, and pad rows from an uneven split get their own varlen segment so real tokens cannot attend to them. - **Expert parallelism** shards the MoE head axis with one all-to-all, through the same `ep_group` plumbing srt's MoE uses. - **Layerwise and CPU offload** via `LayerwiseOffloadableModuleMixin` and `layer_names`, so `--dit-layerwise-offload` and `--cpu-offload-components` work without model-specific code. - `AutoencoderKLWan` for the video VAE (which is what MAGI-2 ships), the UniPC scheduler, FSDP sharding through `_fsdp_shard_conditions`, and the `PipelineStage` / `Req` / `OutputBatch` contracts. ### Structure Eleven stages under `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/magi2/`. Two orderings are load-bearing and easy to break in review: Image encoding runs **before** text encoding, because each conditioning image needs a `<Figure N>` phrase present in the prompt; pooling that phrase's embedding runs **after**, because it needs the encoded prompt. A conditioning image is not the clip's first frame — it is VAE-encoded, parked past the clip on the rope time axis, and bound to the prompt through that pooled embedding. The denoise loop is model-owned rather than delegated to `DenoisingStage`, because video and audio carry separate guidance scales and separate multistep scheduler state, which the shared loop's single-latent contract cannot represent. Compile, residency and warmup still come from the base stage. ### Parallelism `--num-gpus` must divide every head axis, since a rank owns whole heads on all of them: 24 preview attention heads, 12 preview MoE heads, 32 refiner attention heads, 8 refiner GQA key/value heads. The refiner's 8 bind, so the two-stage tier admits 2 or 4 and preview-only admits 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12. All four axes are checked in `validate_server_args`, so a bad count fails at launch instead of inside a collective. 8 GPUs divides three axes but not the preview's 12 MoE heads. The reference handles that by padding the head axis to 16 and giving the spare ranks zero-weight experts; this port rejects the configuration instead, rather than waste two ranks of expert capacity. `--enable-cfg-parallel` is rejected — the denoise loop already runs both branches itself, so splitting CFG across ranks would double-apply the guidance. Expert parallelism is what lets the weights fit, not merely what makes them fast: the preview partition is 228 GB in BF16 and only its expert tensors shard, while the 6.7B refiner is replicated per rank. Below the divisibility rules, how many ranks a given card needs is a memory question — the offload flags above are the lever. ### Deliberate divergences from the reference Both are marked at the site in the code. **The refiner's residual accumulates in BF16, not FP32.** The reference promotes it at the first `down_proj` and holds FP32 through all 30 layers. Matching that roughly doubles the residual's footprint across 30 layers at the 1080p sequence length; BF16 accumulation is the cheaper of the two errors. The refiner's QK-norm likewise stores in BF16 while reducing in FP32, where the preview DiT can afford FP32 through the rotary. **Expert-parallel head padding is not implemented**, as described under Parallelism. ### Docs `docs/cookbook/diffusion/MAGI/MAGI-2.mdx` covers the quality tiers, the parallelism rules, offload recipes, and the stage timings below. Added to the compatibility matrix. ### Known limitations - Only 1920x1088 and 896x512 are accepted, rejected before denoising otherwise. 1088 rather than 1080 because the VAE stride forces multiples of 16. - 10-second clips only; the model was trained for one duration. - `--enable-torch-compile` does not work: inductor autotuning fails on the multi-head MoE GEMMs, asking more shared memory than sm90 has (`triton_mm Required: 262144, Hardware limit: 232448`), and then stalls. The refiner's flex-attention mask is compiled separately and does work. - `--tp-size` and `--ring-degree` are rejected, per the speed tests below. - FlashAttention only. Sinks and the packed varlen path exist nowhere else, so `sage_attn` is rejected rather than silently degraded. - The two-stage tier wants `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`. Its decode asks for one large block while both DiTs are resident, which otherwise tends to fail on fragmentation well into a run. A startup warning fires when it is unset. ## Accuracy Tests ### Side-by-side with the reference implementation Three pairs, each generated twice on the same box with the same weights, the same seed 42, and the same 1920x1088 two-stage tier — once by the reference implementation and once by this PR. The prompts are the reference repository's own long structured captions, used verbatim so nothing depends on prompt wording. **Pair 1, text-to-video.** An 8895-character caption describing a 10-second Japanese-anime-style sequence: a young girl walks from a dark, mist-filled forest into a bright clearing over the ocean, with one deliberate camera cut near the climax. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b734f741-c01f-43ac-bde9-8634b447fb1a - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05fccde8-111a-4162-91ba-4eb31f974b67 **Pair 2, image-to-video.** The same caption as pair 1, plus a still frame as the conditioning image. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fdab8b3-a4f4-4569-983f-5c9087891e51 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19f6148-4c93-4dca-8ef1-c3714fa4242d **Pair 3, image-to-video.** A 10931-character caption describing a stop-motion clay animation — a small clay figure searches a room for a lost red ball and finds it at his feet — plus its conditioning still. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9444c586-ebae-4daa-901a-bd7161e36858 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f8638fd-90cd-4ee1-b824-e3334f99d964 The two are not bit-identical and are not meant to be. The port runs SGLang's own attention, MoE and VAE paths rather than the reference's kernels, and it accumulates the refiner residual in BF16 where the reference uses FP32 — see Deliberate divergences. Frame statistics across the three pairs (contrast, shadow occupancy, spatial detail) land within a few percent of the reference, but they are weak evidence either way; the clips are the thing to look at. ### Prompt coverage Eight prompts in one process, all at 1920x1088 with joint audio, seed 42 — static and fast-moving subjects, interior and exterior, one non-English: - Calm mountain lake at sunrise, mist over still water — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bed79a0e-4a39-42da-a144-fe77765f3ffe - Busy night market in the rain, neon reflected in puddles — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed94afe5-4337-44ce-949a-78abc5f0ae20 - Cellist in an empty concert hall, dust in a shaft of light — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2abb3374-184d-4278-ac9a-0ebb6976df38 - Golden retriever bounding through deep snow, powder spraying — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/728e9d78-5577-4ec3-8eae-d524f9fc66bc - Timelapse of storm clouds over wheat fields — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a677bb13-efca-4aba-932e-ebfdf250e98e - 一位老人在清晨的公园里练太极，动作缓慢舒展 — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79e8bbc7-6970-4007-815b-0b4d0ab987d9 - Blacksmith hammering glowing steel, sparks arcing — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b39855-3163-48eb-af15-677dd499bf0b - Sea turtle gliding over a coral reef, sunlight rippling — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a876691-8373-423b-8ad1-c7096c1bec23 All eight ran without a restart. Every output verified h264 1920x1088 at 25 fps, 249 frames, AAC 44100 Hz stereo, 10.0s. The audio tracks its prompt rather than being generic ambience — the blacksmith clip is 66% silence between strikes, the lake clip is continuous and low-frequency. ### Unit tests 47 unit tests, no GPU required: the MoE router and expert layout, mHC normalization, rope construction and partial rotation, the coordinate builder, packed-sequence layout, the noise schedule the refiner restarts from, guidance arithmetic, the block-grid mask and the block order it must be applied in, sequence bucketing, and the expert-axis sharding predicate. They are flat files under `test/unit/`, so `_discover_unit_tests()` picks them up and they run in the existing suite with no CI change: ``` python3 sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py --suite unit ``` The full 1080p path needs four cards and about ten minutes per clip, so it is not in the suite. ## Speed Tests and Profiling All figures below are one machine's numbers — 4x H200 at `--ulysses-degree 4` with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` — and are meant as relative comparisons, not as sizing targets. **One 1080p clip, 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, text-to-video — 592s total:** text encoding 17.6s, preview denoise 452.8s, the preview-to-refiner handoff under 0.1s, refiner denoise 101.6s, decode 15.5s. Weight load is separate and paid once per process, about 5 minutes for both DiTs. Image-to-video costs more — the conditioning image adds 1680 patch tokens and the longer caption takes 24s to encode — and measures 741s. **Batch stability.** Eight clips of differing prompt length in one process gave refiner times of 101.6, 102.4, 101.0, 101.2, 100.8, 100.4, 101.8 and 103.6s. Flat, which is the property that matters for serving. Text encoding drops from 17.6s on the first clip to about 9s afterwards, as the memory-mapped encoder weights stay in the host page cache. **Tensor parallelism**, preview tier at 896x512, 20 steps, four ranks: pure Ulysses 124.5s; `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` 205.9s; `--tp-size 4` 608.1s, each using more memory per rank than the last. Neither DiT has a column- or row-parallel layer, so `--tp-size` shards no weights and only takes ranks away from Ulysses — those ranks stop sharding the sequence and duplicate full-length work. Rejected at startup rather than left as a footgun. **Sequence length.** The refiner's packed sequence is `video + audio + text + reference`, so its length follows the prompt, and its `flex_attention` mask is compiled per length with each graph retained. Six clips at 4 preview steps, where the first three share a prompt length: - rounding the sequence to a bucket: 100.8, 98.0, 99.4, 103.0, 102.3, 102.2s - using each length verbatim: 102.6, 100.8, 102.0, 174.1, 215.5s, then out of memory Two changes keep the graph count bounded. `Magi2RefinerDiT` rounds the sequence up to a multiple of 1024 rows before sharding, collapsing the whole 0-7000-token prompt range to eight lengths at under 0.4% padding. And `build_mask_mod` carries the valid-row length as a tensor rather than an int, because dynamo guards a captured int by **value** — as an int it recompiles per prompt length even once every tensor shape is identical, and nine distinct values trip the default `recompile_limit` of 8, after which flex_attention falls back to an eager path that materializes the full score matrix. As a tensor, nine values give one graph. `dynamic=True` is not an alternative: the rebuilt closure misses the guard either way and costs 26s per clip. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31935589148](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935589148)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31935589182](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935589182)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

The baseline file is tightened field-by-field, so historical stage minima and E2E values do not necessarily come from one coherent run. The apparent 35x Hunyuan3D delta exposed a coverage regression: PR #28781 made the case shape-only by injecting `paint_enable=false`. This PR removes that fixture override and restores the complete pipeline, its three paint-stage thresholds, and the paint-inclusive E2E threshold. The remaining four largest E2E deltas were investigated separately: | Case | Baseline delta | Attribution | | --- | ---: | --- | | `turbo_wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` | 4.69 s -> 0.96 s | The January baseline explicitly used no warmup and the old default offloaded every video component. The current H100 path warms the request shape and keeps the small model components resident. signals.title: [Scheduler] Add configurable decode interval after prefill
signals.text: [by Codex] ## Motivation With DP attention, each rank schedules attention work locally while all ranks still participate in the same MoE collective. A rank with repeated chunked-prefill continuation work can therefore keep winning SGLang's prefill-first scheduling decision and starve decode work on peer ranks. In the AgentX workload this left requests waiting while the actual decode batch remained small. The DP-attention MLP-sync all-gather already exposes whether any rank selected an EXTEND batch. Use that globally synchronized signal to enforce a rank-consistent decode interval after prefill. ## Modifications - Add `--prefill-decode-interval N`, defaulting to `0` (disabled, so existing behavior is unchanged). - After an EXTEND batch, defer new prefill scheduling for the next `N` scheduler rounds so the running batch can decode. - Under DP attention, arm the interval from the existing globally synchronized `is_extend_in_batch` flag. Under non-DP scheduling, use the local forward mode. - Validate non-negative values and add focused scheduler/server-argument unit tests. No AIPerf source change is required. The benchmark prototype used the existing per-session routing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This changes batch selection cadence only; it does not change model math or sampling. - Added unit coverage for disabled, non-DP, globally synchronized DP, and decode/non-rearm behavior. - Added server-argument validation coverage. - `python -m py_compile` passed for all modified Python/test files. - The focused pytest command could not collect on the development VM because its base Python environment does not include `torch`/`numpy`; the new tests are registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The equivalent scheduler prototype was evaluated with full 3,600-second DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 AgentX runs on 8x B200 using TP8/DP8/EP8, DP attention, MTP3, and an interval of 16: | Concurrency | Interactivity (tok/s/user) | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | Cache hit | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 56 | 30.75532 | 23,559.05865 | 95.945% | | 84 | 23.24221 | 26,110.24296 | 94.703% | The c84 run completed 7,096 profiled requests with zero request errors. These results validate the equivalent prototype on SGLang v0.5.17; this PR ports the behavior onto current `main` using the existing global DP EXTEND flag. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [Fix] Correct dense FP8 Marlin bias ordering
signals.text: ## Motivation Dense FP8 Marlin preparation permuted the bias into the Marlin tile layout. However, the dense wrapper does not pass bias into the Marlin GEMM; it adds bias after the kernel returns. The post-GEMM addition therefore requires the original logical output-channel order. The old behavior produces incorrect biased projections, including the Qwen2 QKV projection. ## Modifications - Keep dense FP8 Marlin bias in logical output-channel order. - Continue wrapping the loaded bias as a non-trainable parameter. - Add a CPU-only regression test in the source-mirrored marlin_utils_fp8 test module. This applies to all biased dense FP8 Marlin layers. Fused MoE bias handling is unchanged because it follows a separate kernel path. ## Accuracy Tests Added a CPU-only regression test that uses a non-uniform bias and verifies that Marlin preparation preserves its channel order. Local validation: - python3 -m py_compile passed for the changed source and test files. - git diff --check passed. - The unit test was not executed locally because the available Python environment does not include PyTorch or pytest; CPU CI will execute it. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The inference-time path is unchanged, and preparation removes an unnecessary bias permutation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit guidance. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests guidance. - [x] Documentation is not required for this internal correctness fix. - [x] Accuracy and speed impact are described above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31955054834](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955054834)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31955054569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955054569)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: retire the multi-engine accommodation in the runtime context
signals.text: A process holds at most one live config: the bags always describe the engine running now. Re-publish stays last-publish-wins, which is what lets a process rebuild an engine after shutting the previous one down. Drop preserve_config() and its per-leaf bag snapshot/restore helpers. They existed for a nested build that publishes a private ServerArgs copy; the draft build stopped doing that when per-runner values became constructor arguments, and no production caller is left. Drop the launcher entry from ROLE_NAMESPACE_SETS: no process publishes under that role. The multi-item scoring tests held two engines alive at once. The reference engine now runs its scoring calls first and shuts down before the engine under test boots; engine boots per class are unchanged, so the CI harness still sees the same GPU demand. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979513572](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979513572)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979513393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979513393)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: publish before a process reads configuration
signals.text: Five processes read config namespaces before they published. The launch path ran validation, port allocation and the subprocess launches ahead of its publish; the scheduler ran its process configuration first; the tokenizer manager read the parallel bag in a constructor that is the first publish in a tokenizer-worker process; the encode server's launch path read the DP size before the encoder it builds publishes; the detokenizer never published at all while reading resolution-written fields off the instance it was handed. Each publishes as early as its config is final -- for the launch path that is right after late resolution, which refuses a published instance. The two DSA seed predicates take no config argument: every caller was handing over the process config, and the fields they read are bag leaves. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979514149](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979514149)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979513991](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979513991)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: spec: size the speculative buffers from the bags, not the startup record
signals.text: Adaptive speculative decoding switches the step config at runtime through get_context().override, which moves the spec bag leaves and leaves the ServerArgs record on its startup values. Six sizing paths read the record: - allocation_sizing: the per-decode KV reserve, recomputed every decode batch, kept reserving for the startup step count after a switch - spec_utils.resolve_num_tokens_per_req: draft-extend capture widths were sized for the startup draft-token count while a different candidate state was being captured - spec_info.create_dummy_verify_input: the autotune forward inside the capture window built its dummy verify input at the startup tree shape - eagle_disaggregation: the prebuilt-batch draft-input state count - managers.utils.compute_num_reserved_tokens: the token budget the rust ingress enforces All of them read the spec bag now, and so do the two DSA seed predicates the disagg path calls. The config parameter goes away where every caller was handing over the process config anyway, which drops the disagg draft-input hand-off chain down to what it uses; the tests that drove those paths with stand-in objects publish a config. The exposure pins shrink by 16 (axis 1) and 6 (axis 2) pairs. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979516189](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979516189)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979516074](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979516074)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: the DP/EP topology reads come from the parallel bag
signals.text: dp_size, enable_dp_attention and ep_size are resolution outputs: --dwdp-size derives all three, so a raw record carries the pre-derivation values. Every reader of the five topology fields now reads the parallel config leaves. Two processes were reading configuration before they published: the scheduler ran configure_scheduler_process ahead of its publish, and the launch path published only once the tokenizer manager was built. Both publish at process entry now. The load-snapshot owner decision and the scheduler recv skipper take no config argument any more -- every caller was handing over the process config. Their tests publish a config instead of injecting a stand-in object. The exposure pin drops 39 pairs on axis 1 and 19 on axis 2. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979517957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979517957)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979517871](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979517871)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: the per-instance families read the bags
signals.text: The tokenizer manager, the detokenizer, the multimodal processors, the encode server and the HTTP entrypoint read resolved config off the instance they were handed. That was justified by several engines sharing one process; a process holds one live config, so they read the bags like every other consumer. The same goes for the launch paths, the sidecar and the Ray driver, and for the three single-reader decisions (the grammar-backend factory, the token-oracle install gate, the new-token ratio tracker). The parallel sizes are the exception that has to be spelled out: pp_size and its four siblings are read-through properties over the process groups, so a launch path -- which decides how many processes to spawn before joining any group -- must ask for the configured value. Functions lose the config parameter where every caller was handing over the process config: the EPD rejection guard, the hidden-state ceiling, the token-oracle gate. sarvam-moe stops caching the process config in a lazy slot and dispatches on the configured attention pair like the other dispatch sites. Two guards pin what only a server boot would otherwise catch: that no launch path reads a live-shadowed size, and that the bag accessors are never called as object members. The tests that drove these paths with stand-in objects publish a config instead. The reads that stay: the two gates deciding whether late resolution runs, the remote-instance seed check, and the NCCL environment setup. All three run before this process publishes, and each needs its own call on whether it is asking about raw input or about the effective value. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979519532](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979519532)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979519397](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979519397)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: /server_info overlaid the tokenizer's control-plane log (detected parsers, weight version, load format, the HiCache mirror) onto the serialized config, so the one endpoint whose job is to report what the operator asked for answered with a mix of that and what changed since. It reports the record. The facts that overlay carried keep their own endpoints: /get_weight_version and /model_info for the weight version, /hicache/storage-backend for the mirror. /model_info also reports the parsers in effect, which is where a resolved-from-the-chat-template value belongs. The crash dump keeps the overlay: a dump is asking what was running. is_no_spec_infer_or_topk_one is called only by the resolution pipeline, with a resolved view rather than the record. Naming its parameter after the record made it look like a supplied-instance reader, and the exposure census counted it as two pinned pairs it never was. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979520036](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979520036)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979520005](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979520005)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: one control-plane log for the process
signals.text: The tokenizer manager kept its own log of post-startup config changes with the same shape as the context's -- (source, fields) with provenance -- and read it back with a reverse scan on every output message. It records into the config bags now, so a process carries one log and one provenance format, and reading one field is an attribute read. config_leaf() is the read side of override(): callers holding a field name rather than a namespace no longer have to know which bag it lives in. model_path and served_model_name stay manager attributes. They answer the readback from there, and writing them to the bags would not reach the other processes that read them. The exposure census follows the wrapper: record_config_updates call sites are override sites now, and its resolver learned the loop-variable key shape the parser detection uses. Three parser pairs join the pinned surface -- the two launcher gates ask the record on purpose, and the grammar backend reads in a different process from the writer. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979522884](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979522884)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979522815](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979522815)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: **Not for merge.** This carries the whole series against `main` so CI runs over the finished state; the units merge through their own PRs. | # | PR | what it does | |---|---|---| | 1 | #35022 | retire the multi-engine accommodation (a process holds one live config) | | 2 | #35023 | five processes publish before they read configuration | | 3 | #35024 | **bug fix**: adaptive spec sized its buffers from the startup record | | 4 | #35025 | the DP/EP topology reads come from the parallel bag | | 5 | #35026 | the per-instance families read the bags | | 6 | #35027 | `/server_info` reports the record; the resolving view is named as one | | 7 | #35028 | one control-plane log per process | Why this is a series: `ServerArgs` is on its way to holding the user's raw input, with resolution output living in the config bags. Every reader that wants the effective value has to be on the bags before that, and the exposure ratchet counts what is left: **297 → 181 pairs on the supplied-instance surface, 75 → 45 on the post-publish override surface**. Two defects here only a real server boot reaches, and both now have a static guard so they cannot come back: * a bag accessor called as an object member (`x.get_disagg()`) — imports fine, unit tests pass, `/health` returns 500 and the server never becomes healthy; * a launch path reading `get_parallel().pp_size` — a read-through property over process groups, so it raises before distributed init. Validation: the CPU battery over 535 registered files, twice (main and this series), diffed name by name — no new failure. signals.title: Add bit-exact guard for extra_buffer_lazy
signals.text: ## Motivation `extra_buffer_lazy` has no bit-exact coverage today. It is a different code path rather than the same code under a flag: a request holds one ping-pong slot instead of two, and the second is allocated only on the forward that crosses a track boundary and freed again afterwards. The checkpoint therefore lands in a slot chosen per forward instead of one the request owns for its lifetime, and picking the wrong one restores another request's conv window. Admitted by revert-then-red rather than by adding a class that reads 0 either way. Reverting https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34184 (stale track rows corrupting conv checkpoints under the prefill graph) takes the new class's `test_prefill_cache_hit` to **5.56e-06** against a 1e-9 floor. The non-lazy class read 1.18e-05 in the same session, so read the pair as "both fire", not as the lazy one being weaker. Tracked in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34899. ## Accuracy Whole file, one B200, `thinkingmachines/Inkling@test`: ``` 7 passed in 655.52s TestUnifiedHybridBitExact 354s 3 cases, avg_kl_div=0.0 TestUnifiedHybridLazyBitExact 129s 3 cases, avg_kl_div=0.0 TestUnifiedHybridHiCacheBitExact 142s 1 case, avg_kl_div=0.0 ``` `est_time` goes 600 -> 790 from that measurement: the two pre-existing classes take 496s against the current 600, and the same ratio on 655s is 790. The new class adds only 129s because it reuses a warm model. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31955574489](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955574489)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31955574352](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955574352)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [JIT Kernel] Migrate causal_conv1d_fwd and causal_conv1d_update from AOT to JIT
signals.text: ## Motivation Move `causal_conv1d_fwd` / `causal_conv1d_update` off the prebuilt `sgl_kernel` wheel and onto the JIT kernel infra, keeping the in-place contract, the exported ops, and bit-level numerics. Both sit on the prefill/decode path of every short-conv hybrid model — LFM2 / LFM2-MoE, Mamba2, GDN. ## Modifications - Device kernels move into `kernels/jit/csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cuh` unchanged; only the host launchers switch to the tvm-ffi `TensorView` API. Strides stay `uint32_t` elements, as in the AOT `ConvParamsBase`. - The JIT build matches the wheel's arch split — `-use_fast_math` on SM 9.0, precise math elsewhere, per `load_utils.py`'s `compute_capability == 90` — so the SiLU epilogue emits the same bits. Math mode is part of the build key. - CUDA serving goes through the JIT registry behind a `torch.compile`-compatible custom op; everything else keeps Triton. The AOT ops stay exported for external users and for the differential test. - Only a JIT/CUDA spec is registered, since the AOT kernel was CUDA-only anyway — `csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cu` sits in the CUDA CMakeLists and nowhere else, and `common_extension_rocm.cc` never defined the ops. ROCm and MUSA were already landing on Triton through the old `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.causal_conv1d_update` probe; now they get there directly via `_HAS_CONV1D_KERNEL = is_cuda()`. Nothing changes on any device. - The AOT `cudaFuncSetAttribute` branch goes away behind a `static_assert`: every instantiation sits near 4 KB of shared memory, nowhere near the 48 KB it existed to raise. - `width` outside 2..4 now raises in prefill, where the AOT `if`/`else if` chain had no `else` and quietly did nothing. - `has_initial_state` gets a dtype check. The kernel reads it as `const bool*`, and `kDLBool` has no C++ trait, so it lands as a `CHECK_HOST` on the dtype code rather than a matcher clause. - Tests and benchmarks move to the registered kernel layout, and the superseded AOT-only test is gone. ## Accuracy Tests `pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py` | | H200 (SM90, fast-math) | GB300 (SM103, precise-math) | |---|---|---| | Total | 473 passed, 12 skipped | 473 passed, 12 skipped | | Bit-exact vs AOT (72 cases) | pass | pass | | Reference vs `F.conv1d` (393 cases) | pass | pass | Two machines because the kernel picks its math mode by arch, so each one compiles a different build. The 12 skips are the same deliberate guard on both: the circular-buffer reference can't arbitrate when `seqlen > state_len`, where `scatter_` hits duplicate indices. Behind those counts, the reference tests cover FP32/FP16/BF16 × widths 2–4 × seqlens 1–4096, varlen (per sequence) and non-varlen, both conv-state layouts, gathered slots. The differential is one config per dispatch path, narrowed from a ~900-config sweep that came back bit-identical to AOT throughout. On GB300 the SiLU epilogue — where a math-flag mismatch would show up — gives `max_abs_diff = 0.000e+00`. Also checked: `pad_slot_id` slots untouched, bad dtype / width / non-bool mask rejected, `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` bit-identical to eager, and `LiquidAI/LFM2-350M` serving end to end (GSM8K 200q = 0.325, H200). B200 is registered in `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/mamba/bench_causal_conv1d.py` — FP16/BF16, `dim` 2048–8192, prefill seqlens 128–8192 (4-sequence varlen batch), decode batch 1–256 with gathered slots. 24 configs each. | | prefill geomean | prefill range | prefill wins | decode geomean | decode range | decode wins | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | H200 (SM90) | **1.063x** | 1.022x – 1.122x | 24/24 | 1.001x | 0.995x – 1.015x | 14/24 | | GB300 (SM103) | **1.041x** | 1.015x – 1.062x | 24/24 | 1.000x | 0.987x – 1.013x | 10/24 (3 tied) | - Prefill wins every config on both machines. GB300 extremes: BF16 `(512, 2048)` 22.09 vs 22.41 us, BF16 `(2048, 8192)` 84.90 vs 90.16 us. - Decode is a wash, and those win counts are noise rather than a result: 23/24 configs on H200 and 20/24 on GB300 land within ±1% either way, three of them exact ties. The decode kernel is unchanged, so neither direction means anything. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing documentation change is required.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31951691285](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31951691285)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31951691178](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31951691178)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Llama4 NVFP4 checkpoint loading: fused expert scales and packed q/k permute
signals.text: ## Motivation Loading `nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-NVFP4` crashes during weight loading on current main. Repro on a DGX Spark (GB10, SM121) at tp=1: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-NVFP4 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 --tp-size 1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --context-length 8192 ``` It dies at the first expert scale with 0 of 14 shards loaded: ``` Multi-thread loading shards: 0% Completed | 0/14 File ".../srt/models/mllama4.py", line 902, in _handle_expert_scale_params param.data[expert_id] = loaded_weight RuntimeError: expand(CPUFloat8_e4m3fnType{[16, 512, 5120]}, size=[5120, 512]): the number of sizes provided (2) must be greater or equal to the number of dimensions in the tensor (3) ``` Fixing that alone gets you a second crash a bit later: ``` File ".../srt/models/mllama4.py", line 629, in permute w.view(n_heads, attn_in // n_heads // 2, 2, attn_out) RuntimeError: shape '[8, 64, 2, 5120]' is invalid for input of size 2621440 ``` Both come from the loader assuming unquantized HF layouts. ### Fused expert block scales This checkpoint stores the per-expert block scales fused into one 3D tensor under a name with no expert index. That matches how it stores the fused weights: ``` experts.down_proj_weight_scale: [16, 512, 5120] = [E, K/16, N] experts.gate_up_proj_weight_scale: [16, 320, 16384] = [E, K/16, 2N] ``` `_handle_expert_scale_params` only knows two cases. Either the name carries an expert index or the value is a per-tensor scalar to broadcast. A fused 3D tensor lands in the broadcast branch and gets assigned into a per-expert `[N, K/16]` slot. Hence the expand error. The param layout from `create_weights` in `modelopt_quant.py` is `[E, N, K/16]` so it is also transposed relative to the checkpoint. ### Packed q/k in the rotary permute `permute()` takes the trailing dim from `config.hidden_size`. NVFP4 weights arrive packed two values per byte so `k_proj.weight` is `[1024, 2560] uint8` rather than `[1024, 5120]`. The matching 2D q/k `weight_scale` is `[1024, 320]` for k and has the same row layout as the weight. It needs the same permutation. Permuting the weight alone does not crash. It silently misaligns every row's scale. ## Modifications All of it is in one file: `python/sglang/srt/models/mllama4.py`. - `_handle_expert_scale_params` now sends 3D scales through the FusedMoE `weight_loader` per expert with a transpose. That mirrors `_handle_expert_weight_params` right below it and uses the same `chunk(2)` gate/up split and the same shard ids. The scales end up sharded exactly the way the weights are. Both existing branches are untouched. - `permute()` in `permute_qk_weight_for_rotary` now takes the trailing dim from the tensor (`w.shape[-1]`) instead of `config.hidden_size`. The permutation only reorders rows so this is correct for packed and unpacked layouts alike. It now also covers 2D q/k `weight_scale`. 0-dim per-tensor scales are left alone. There are no import changes and nothing here branches on GPU architecture. This is not SM12x specific. SM121 is the only place I have tested it. I could not test tp>1 on a single GPU box. The 3D scale path goes through the same TP-aware `weight_loader` the weights already use. ## Accuracy Tests The scale permutation is the half of this that changes numbers instead of crashing, so it wants an accuracy check rather than a crash check. At the element level, skipping it pairs 88.8% of this checkpoint's `layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.weight_scale` with the wrong scale, with a mean relative error of 31.3% over the mismatched elements. End to end on a DGX Spark (GB10, SM121) at tp=1 with `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` and the patch applied to the in-container source. Loading is not enough to serve on SM12x, so the fix proposed in #34192 is applied on top in every row that runs at all: | build | gsm8k | invalid | |---|---|---| | main | does not load (dies at 0/14 shards) | | | this PR | 0.925 | 0.000 | | this PR with the `weight_scale` permutation left out | 0.485 | 0.000 | That is `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` at its defaults: 5-shot, 200 questions, greedy. The third row is why that half of the fix is there. Nothing crashes and no output is malformed. The answers are simply wrong. Loading itself goes from dying at 0/14 shards to a clean 198 s load of 65.9 GB of weights. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This only touches weight loading and the forward path is unchanged. ## Related - #34192 is the SM12x runtime assert you hit after this fix. Separate bug. Its repro uses `--load-format dummy` so it never exercises checkpoint loading and does not overlap with this PR. - #9526 and #12649 both previously identified these same two loading problems as part of larger changes (3 and 4 files that also reach into the fused MoE layer and modelopt quantization). Both were closed unmerged and #12649 explicitly as outdated. Neither fix ever landed. This PR is the loading-only subset and it was validated on hardware against the real checkpoint. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). `black` and `ruff` are clean on the changed file. There is no unit test yet because it needs a real NVFP4 checkpoint to be meaningful. I am happy to add a shape-level test for the 3D scale path if you want one. Docs are unchanged because this is not user facing. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31952815636](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31952815636)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31952815513](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31952815513)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(disaggregation): route equal-TP fragmented KV transfer through staging
signals.text: ## Problem Equal-TP (MHA/GQA) PD-disaggregated KV transfer collapses bandwidth when the decode-side KV cache becomes fragmented: each `(group, layer)` slice becomes a separate transfer entry, and per-entry device-memory (D2H) copy overhead dominates the transfer. - engine-level: 1 entry → 4792 MB/s; 4096 entries → 15.5 MB/s - end-to-end (200 concurrent long shared-prefix requests): 1.41 → 1.76 req/s (+25%), TPOT 23.03 → 13.80 ms (−40%) This is the root cause behind the bandwidth collapse reported in #5450 (which was auto-closed without a confirmed fix; the "larger page-size" workaround avoids, but does not fix, fragmentation). ## Root cause 1. `alloc_extend` allocates across non-contiguous free segments under pool pressure (decode-side radix cache reuse) → fragmented dst indices. 2. The equal-TP direct path (`send_kvcache`) emits one transfer entry per (group × layer), so fragmentation blows up the entry count. 3. Per-entry fixed cost × thousands of entries → bandwidth collapse. ## Fix Route equal-TP fragmented chunks through the existing staging path (local gather → 1 bulk RDMA → decode scatter), collapsing G×2L entries into 1. Gated behind `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER` and a new `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_MIN_GROUPS` (default 8); `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_ALWAYS` opts into staging for every equal-TP chunk. - `mooncake/conn.py`: equal-TP fragmentation branch + `_fragmented_groups` + `_ensure_equal_tp_staging_req` (on-demand STAGING_REQ) + bounded spin - `decode.py`: register gate widened to non-MLA equal-TP, excluding fake-transfer requests (warmup/health-check) to avoid a warmup hang - `utils.py`: poll demote gate switched to `is_staging_room` - `environ.py`: `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_MIN_GROUPS` / `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_ALWAYS` All changes are env-gated and default-off: behavior is unchanged unless staging is explicitly enabled. ## Validation - Warmup passes with `STAGING_BUFFER=1`, and with staging + decode radix cache on both MHA and GQA. - Fragmented workload (200 rooms shared-prefix): 1.41 → 1.76 req/s (+25%), TPOT 23.03 → 13.80 ms (−40%), 90/90 staging transfers succeeded, 0 failures. - Healthy path no regression (1.47 → 1.49 req/s, within noise). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31953598057](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31953598057)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31953597944](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31953597944)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Model] Add native SenseNova U1 multimodal generation and interleave serving
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds native SenseNova U1 support to main SGLang, including: - native language and multimodal-understanding execution; - native bounded flow matching for image generation; - OpenAI-compatible T2I and IT2I image APIs; - flow-prefill CUDA graph capture and replay; - scheduler-owned text-to-image-to-text interleave continuation; - deterministic, batch-size-invariant interleave image generation; - reusable official-HF versus native end-to-end benchmark tooling. The final cross-batch correctness fix is commit `581e47848d6791e5134c19ecd9763283fdd547b9`. It prevents the internal flow child from reusing parent KV generated under a concurrency-dependent text batch. The child remains scheduler-owned and request-isolated, but recomputes its flow conditioning with a Radix prefix match limit of zero. Parent decode state, parking, image attachment, re-encoding, and resumed decode remain unchanged. Hermes first-review hardening is commit `48b91296805e66f45c3a75ac4eaba6d40ed4a62a`. It adds bounded parsed-upload reads, request propagation, active-RID aborts, and strict numeric validation. The remaining receive-boundary hardening is commit `dafbc308ea8fb998ad2828a15beda31b783fe7d8`. It enforces the total edit multipart cap before Starlette materializes `UploadFile`, validates declared and observed body lengths, and fails closed on interrupted or malformed streams. This commit is pushed to `waltstephen/sensenova-u1-native-main`, which updates existing `sgl-project/sglang#35038`; no new PR was created. The warmed-performance completion is commit `7b23547014ec6387f7efdd27972729196fb2063d`. It adds bounded exact-text and flow caches, fixes decode-graph MRoPE staging, preserves multi-image flow-prefix identity, and passes the approved H100 BS1/8/16, T2I, and fixed-work first-image targets without changing the workload, context, parity, determinism, or safety gates. ## Architecture The native interleave lifecycle is owned by main SGLang: 1. A bounded exact-text segment decodes until the model emits ``. 2. The scheduler parks the parent request state without finalizing it. The segment's private exact-text KV is released rather than inserted into shared Radix state. 3. A scheduler-owned prefix child recomputes the committed text/image prefix under a content-derived extra key, then a bounded internal flow request is created with: - a per-parent batch-isolation key; - an explicit image seed; - the same token/image geometry and MRoPE time index as the parent; - a Radix match limited to the canonical prefix child, never the concurrency-dependent parent segment. 4. Native flow matching runs inside SRT. No HF modeling fallback or serial HTTP wrapper is used. 5. The generated float16 image is converted to native vision features and attached to the parent request. 6. The next bounded exact-text segment recomputes or reuses its private prefix cache with the new image-context span and resumes the same parent request. The canonical flow-conditioning prefix is independently keyed by token IDs and multimodal feature bytes, bounded in scheduler state, and reset per image turn. Public T2I/IT2I requests retain their own prefix caching and the 64-token flow-prefill CUDA graph path. Implementation commit sequence: - `0db493a02`: native language core - `17a12f5ae`: native multimodal understanding - `fdf95b93a`: native flow execution - `f5a84ebb1`: native image APIs - `530b9f010`: flow-prefill CUDA graph - `7b1aa9826`: scheduler-owned interleave continuation - `899e9da56`: reusable interleave benchmark - `581e47848`: cross-batch invariant flow conditioning and benchmark regression - `48b912968`: image upload, cancellation, disconnect, and validation hardening - `dafbc308e`: pre-parser multipart request-boundary hardening and ASGI tests - `7b2354701`: warmed text/T2I/interleave optimization and fail-closed exact-text admission ### Image request lifecycle Image generation and edit requests now preserve the HTTP request lifecycle: 1. The FastAPI `Request` object is passed to every tokenizer-manager prefix and flow request. 2. Each active prefix/flow RID is tracked. 3. Client disconnects are detected by the tokenizer manager. 4. Task cancellation, disconnect exceptions, and other stage failures explicitly call `abort_request(rid)` before unwinding. 5. The async generator is closed after each stage. A pure ASGI middleware runs before multipart parsing. The total edit request cap is `2 * media_url_max_file_size_mb + 64 KiB`, covering image, optional mask, and multipart/form overhead. It requires one valid `Content-Length`, rejects a declared over-limit body before reading, counts actual receive-stream bytes, rejects understated/overstated lengths, and fails closed on disconnects. Compressed edit bodies are rejected because expansion would bypass the raw receive cap. The parsed `UploadFile` reader remains as defense in depth, consumes at most one byte beyond the per-file cap, and closes image and mask. Explicit user values are never replaced by truthiness defaults: - `n=0` is rejected rather than treated as `1`; - `num_inference_steps=0` is rejected rather than treated as `2`; - `flow_shift=0.0` is rejected rather than treated as `1.0`; - negative, nonfinite, and configured upper-bound violations are rejected. ## Correctness Benchmark contract: - model: `SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Interleaved-bd39` - prompt: `Say 'Here is the image:' then generate an image of a red apple. After the image, write at least 100 words describing it.` - seed: `20260813` - image: 256x256 - flow steps: 2 - generated text budget: 64 tokens - real turn: 6 text tokens, ``, flow, re-encode, 58 continued-text tokens - concurrency levels: 1, 2, 4, 8 - repetitions: 1 warmup plus 5 measured batches per level Results: - real text-to-image-to-text turn: PASS - shared output contract: PASS - generated text budget: 64/64 for HF and native - HF repeat determinism: PASS - native repeat determinism: PASS - native contract batch-size invariance: PASS - native image batch-size invariance: PASS - mapped logical request invariance across BS1/2/4/8: PASS - native image SHA-256 at every batch size: `dcc1e46748949c4da76065a98ab172562fe3fd954bb72f346dc18393ade93d33` - HF/native pre-image text tokens: exact - HF/native post-image wording: not token-exact after re-encoding, but both satisfy the same output contract and text budget - HF/native image parity: 52.416960 dB PSNR, 0.999723 SSIM ### Cross-BS root cause and fix For the same prompt, seed, and logical request ordinal, the baseline BS4/BS8 trace showed: - initial latent: exact - image embeddings: exact - parent prefix KV: first divergence at transformer layer 1 - step-0 conditional hidden state and velocity: different - step-0 updated latent: different - step-1 latent and velocity: different - final image and re-encoded feature: different - continued greedy text token IDs: exact `cfg_scale=img_cfg_scale=1`, so no unconditioned branch is evaluated and CFG velocity equals conditional velocity. After canonical isolated conditioning, BS4 and BS8 are exact at every traced checkpoint, including the final image, re-encoded feature, and continued decode. ## End-to-End Interleave Performance Headline metric is total client-observed end-to-end wall time. HF concurrency uses simultaneous bounded clients queued behind one official `interleave_gen` model lock because the reference implementation mutates shared KV/current-index state. Native requests are issued simultaneously and use SGLang continuous batching with scheduler-owned parent/child lifecycle management. HF reference timing uses the official in-process `interleave_gen` call. Each HF request enters the bounded model lock, runs a CUDA-synchronized model call, then materializes the shared output contract by base64-encoding the image and JSON-encoding and decoding the response payload. This captures lock queueing, model execution, and equivalent client-side contract serialization, but it does not include a FastAPI server, socket transport, or HTTP framing. Native request wall is measured through the real `/generate` HTTP endpoint and includes request JSON serialization, FastAPI/tokenizer-manager dispatch, scheduler execution, response base64/JSON serialization, socket transfer, JSON parsing, and output-contract materialization. Model/server execution and HTTP/client overhead are reported separately. The headline wall comparison is therefore an official-HF in-process reference versus the native deployed HTTP path, not a claim that the two transport stacks are identical. All values below are measured. No missing batch size is estimated or extrapolated. | Concurrency | HF request median / P95 (s) | Native request median / P95 (s) | HF batch median / P95 (s) | Native batch median / P95 (s) | HF req/s | Native req/s | HF tokens/s | Native tokens/s | Batch wall speedup | Throughput speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 3.7785 / 3.8244 | 3.8811 / 3.9355 | 3.7796 / 3.8253 | 3.8821 / 3.9363 | 0.2641 | 0.2570 | 16.902 | 16.445 | 0.974x | 0.973x | | 2 | 5.7981 / 7.8267 | 4.2385 / 4.2690 | 7.6057 / 7.9047 | 4.2414 / 4.2667 | 0.2612 | 0.4714 | 16.717 | 30.167 | 1.793x | 1.805x | | 4 | 9.6068 / 15.3799 | 4.7805 / 4.8394 | 15.2746 / 15.7867 | 4.7869 / 4.8350 | 0.2606 | 0.8345 | 16.680 | 53.411 | 3.191x | 3.202x | | 8 | 17.4986 / 30.9200 | 6.0621 / 6.0948 | 30.9000 / 31.4323 | 6.0746 / 6.1032 | 0.2576 | 1.3158 | 16.487 | 84.211 | 5.087x | 5.108x | Peak GPU memory: - official HF: 34,842 to 35,792 MiB - native SGLang: 45,534 MiB Model execution and HTTP/client serialization timings are reported separately in the raw and summarized benchmark artifacts. ## T2I/IT2I CUDA Graph Spot Gate The existing public image parity and performance gate remains passed after the interleave fix. | Path | Native median model time (s) | Official HF median (s) | Speedup | HTTP wall median (s) | PSNR | SSIM | Max uint8 diff | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | T2I | 0.070879 | 0.161285 | 2.276x | 0.101458 | 51.4839 dB | 0.999658 | 6 | | IT2I | 0.046370 | 0.167753 | 3.618x | 0.092515 | 52.2700 dB | 0.999657 | 4 | Additional checks: - five measured repeats per path plus one warmup - T2I deterministic PNG SHA-256: `a36c7bd6501ab8e74068086c0f37a817d4fb3475ebed099cd88416ffdacd624d` - IT2I deterministic PNG SHA-256: `5f45aa47e8e255fc13d83110413c521ad2a5023d79d46087bb24e4a86572bd60` - IT2I cached prefix tokens: 550 - server log records `cuda graph: True` for measured 64-token flow batches - real multipart IT2I sends `Content-Length: 40435` and returns HTTP 200 - a chunked multipart request without `Content-Length` fails closed with 411 - live invalid-value probes return HTTP 400 for `n=0`, `num_inference_steps=0`, and `flow_shift=0.0` - an omitted generation `response_format` follows the protocol default `"url"` and returns a `data:image/png;base64,...` URI - GPU cleanup after validation: 1 MiB, 0% utilization, no live compute process ## Warmed Performance Acceptance Final H100 run: one warmup plus five measured repeats per gate, 4096 context, 8192 max total tokens, 16 max running requests, auto truncation disabled. | Gate | Required | Native result | Correctness | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Text BS1 | >=58.4513 tok/s, >=2.5049x | 58.4915 tok/s, 2.5066x | 32/32 exact | PASS | | Text BS8 | >=387.1545 tok/s, >=16.6321x | 387.3900 tok/s, 16.6422x | 8x32 exact | PASS | | Text BS16 | >=729.8184 tok/s, >=31.2222x | 734.9902 tok/s, 31.4435x | 16x32 exact | PASS | | T2I 256x256, 2 steps | <=0.050109s, >=3.2001x | 0.049367s, 3.2482x | deterministic; 48.0578 dB / 0.999247 | PASS | | Fixed-work first image | <=2.350700s, >=2.6785x | 2.296077s server, 2.298605s client, 2.7423x | boundary 125, post 1, deterministic | PASS | Additional acceptance: - exact BS1 graph capture followed by ordinary BS1/8/16 decode remains token exact, proving shared Radix and decode graph coexistence; - malformed exact-text budget and unknown-key requests return HTTP 400; - health remains HTTP 200 after the invalid probes; - final consolidated focused suite: 91 passed, 1 skipped; - final GPU cleanup: 1 MiB, 0% utilization, no live compute process. ## Limitations and Fail-Closed Modes Native interleave deliberately rejects or fails closed for: - overlap scheduling, until per-request lookahead rollback is supported; - speculative decoding; - disaggregated serving; - pipeline parallel size greater than 1; - HiSparse; - Mamba cache layouts; - sessions; - input embeddings or positional-embedding overrides; - logprob, sampling-mask, hidden-state, routed-expert, or indexer-top-k returns; - constrained JSON/regex/EBNF/structural-tag decoding; - context-window overflow after reserving generated image spans; - invalid or excessive image dimensions, pixel counts, flow-step counts, and image-turn counts. Existing request limits remain unchanged: - context length: 4096 - auto truncation: disabled - maximum interleave image turns: 8 - maximum flow steps: 64 - image size and pixel limits remain enforced - image API supports one output image and guidance scale 1 - image-edit masks remain unsupported and are rejected - each parsed edit image is bounded by `media_url_max_file_size_mb` - total edit multipart bytes are capped before parsing at twice the per-file cap plus a fixed 64 KiB multipart/form allowance - absent, duplicate, invalid, understated, or overstated `Content-Length`, interrupted streams, and compressed edit bodies fail closed Internal flow children remain independently batch-isolated and are not inserted into the shared Radix cache. Image response behavior: - generation requests that omit `response_format` inherit the generic protocol default `"url"`; because this integration has no hosted object store, the returned URL is a `data:image/png;base64,...` URI - generation requests with `response_format="b64_json"` return `b64_json` - edit multipart requests default to `response_format="b64_json"` - explicitly passing `response_format=None` to the internal adapter also uses `b64_json` ## Test Commands and Results ### Consolidated unit and graph regression ```bash PYTHONPATH=/mnt/afs/fanyijiat/sensenova_u1_sglang/python \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/models/test_neo_chat.py \ test/registered/unit/models/test_neo_chat_multimodal.py \ test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_sensenova_u1_images.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_sensenova_u1_interleave.py \ test/registered/unit/bench/test_sensenova_u1_interleave_benchmark.py \ test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_batch_info.py \ test/registered/unit/configs/test_model_config.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_cuda_graph_setup.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_prefill_cuda_graph_padding.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner_helpers.py ``` Result: `142 passed, 1 skipped, 6 subtests passed`. The native runtime work, cross-batch diagnosis, correctness fix, benchmark mapping, H100 reruns, parity checks, performance measurements, and regression evidence in this PR were completed by Argus before Hermes independent review. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31987531454](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31987531454) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31987531356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31987531356) ## 2026-08-17 exact-text isolation follow-up Final head `379ec33f59ead4b0bf68e88f1317b9ca0b723061` contains runtime fix `2cd5d43b6b9233253f11eb20762a3acad9716714` plus lint/CI-registration follow-up `379ec33f59ead4b0bf68e88f1317b9ca0b723061`. The continuation regressions are closed without weakening the accepted workload or thresholds: - exact-text requests never enter the shared prefill CUDA graph; - standalone exact text uses a per-request batch/Radix namespace, zero shared-prefix matching, and no shared Radix insertion; - interleave parents share only an isolated scheduler lane, preserving BS1 private exact execution while BS>1 uses ordinary continuous decode; per-request Radix namespaces remain distinct; - interleave turn seeds are normalized once and frozen in scheduler-owned state, including deterministic wrap at `2**63`; - flow prefix children explicitly recompute with a zero Radix match limit; - all new `test/registered` modules are registered in the CPU CI suite, and the repository's exact isort/ruff/Black/codespell/registry hooks pass. Final gates: - focused regression suite after runtime fix: `156 passed, 1 skipped`, plus `6` subtests; - focused regression suite after lint follow-up: `156 passed, 1 skipped`, plus `6` subtests; - repository pre-commit hooks on all 36 files changed by this PR: PASS; - GitHub `Lint` workflow on final head: PASS; - upstream GPU/extra suites remain policy-gated for this external-author PR until a maintainer applies `run-ci` / `run-ci-extra`; their aggregate red status is the explicit label gate, not a test failure; - live fail-closed probes: budget mismatch `400`, unknown exact parameter `400`, mixed exact/interleave mode `400`, valid exact request `200` with `cached_tokens=0`, health after probes `200`; - warmed H100 acceptance: BS1 `58.5402 tok/s` (`2.5087x`), BS8 `387.7611 tok/s` (`16.6582x`), BS16 `735.7258 tok/s` (`31.4749x`), all token-exact and exact-text Radix-isolated; - warmed T2I: `0.048384s`, `3.3142x`, deterministic, `48.0578 dB / 0.999247`; - warmed fixed-work first image: `2.294372s` server / `2.296602s` client, `2.7443x`, deterministic, `50.0555 dB / 0.999531`; - complete official-HF/native fixed-work BS1/2/4/8 matrix: PASS, 64/64 effective text tokens, real text-image-text turn at every level, native deterministic and logical-request invariant across all levels, image parity `47.1384 dB / 0.999063`; - native/HF batch-wall medians: BS1 `2.2122s / 3.7863s` (`1.712x`), BS2 `3.3966s / 7.6031s` (`2.238x`), BS4 `2.8222s / 15.1023s` (`5.351x`), BS8 `3.1784s / 30.7367s` (`9.671x`). signals.title: [AMD] Use HIP batched copies for HiCache write-back
signals.text: ## Motivation ROCm staged HiCache write-back currently submits one `hipMemcpyAsync` per page even though HIP 7.1+ provides `hipMemcpyBatchAsync`. This reduces CPU-side submission overhead for page-first D2H write-back while preserving the existing fallback on older runtimes or unsupported calls. ## Modifications - Dynamically resolve `hipMemcpyBatchAsync` on ROCm 7.1+. - Submit large page copies as one batch with null attributes, as required by the HIP API. - Retain per-page fallback for old runtimes, missing symbols, and unsupported calls. - Add a ROCm large-page correctness case that exceeds the existing 128 KiB batch threshold. ## Accuracy Tests MI355X, ROCm 7.2.26015: - `pytest -q -s test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py`: 13 passed. - `rocprofv3` confirms the large-page case issues `hipMemcpyBatchAsync`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Base-A / Candidate / Base-B on one idle MI355X, 16 MHA/MLA shapes, 8/32 layers, 1/4/16/64 pages, page size 256, 40 repetitions per shape: - Host submission latency: 3.27% lower geomean; all 16 shapes improved. - End-to-end synchronized D2H latency: +0.01% geomean (neutral, as expected because transferred bytes are unchanged). - Largest individual submission reduction: 7.01%. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add and run unit tests. - [x] Provide correctness and speed results. - [ ] Run repository CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31956151780](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31956151780)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31956151654](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31956151654)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
