signal.title: [PD] Preserve decode KV across retraction in HiCache
signal.text: ## Motivation PD decode retraction currently preserves KV in per-request CPU tensors. Reusing HiCache host pools avoids a second host-memory path and also lets speculative draft KV survive retraction. ## Modifications - Add explicit and inferred `cpu_tensor` / `host_pool` retraction backends behind `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup`. - Resolve the backend once the decode KV pool exists, since it cannot be decided in `ServerArgs.__post_init__`. The resolved value lands on the config bags via `get_context().override(...)`, and every reader goes through `get_disagg()` — `server_args` stays the pristine read-only record. - Make `--hicache-ratio` `Optional` and give it its default at that same point (`1.0` for host-pool retraction, `2.0` otherwise), so a decode server can size the host pool 1:1 with the device pool. The `hicache_ratio` reads in `hiradix_cache.py` and `hybrid_pool_assembler.py` move to `get_memory()` accordingly — that is the only reason those two files appear in the diff. - Reserve and validate HiCache capacity for compatible MHA and hybrid-SWA decode pools. - Back up, restore, and discard target plus speculative draft sidecar KV through the flattened L2 transfer path from #34793. - Force host-pool retraction in the PD EAGLE3 integration test and assert retracted requests retain speculative acceptance above the calibrated 1.3 gate. - Add a CUDA round-trip test that poisons both target and draft device KV before restoring them at different slots. ## Accuracy Tests Run on the current revision: - Python compilation for all changed files - All applicable pre-commit hooks on the changed files - The `_EXPOSED` / `_OVERRIDDEN_AND_READ` pin sets in `test_supplied_instance_exposure_ratchet.py` are unchanged by this PR, and the mutation / global-config-read ratchets stay at their zero baselines Run on an earlier revision of this branch, before the rebase onto post-#34793 main: - `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py` - `test_runtime_context_override.py` - `test_runtime_context_config_bags.py` The CUDA target/draft round-trip and the PD EAGLE3 integration test have not been executed locally (no GPU on the dev host). They are registered in CI. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. The new transfers execute only when decode requests are retracted; the steady-state decode path is unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit and integration tests. - [ ] Update documentation (no user-facing documentation change needed). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (GPU tests are delegated to CI; no steady-state performance change). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31984438697](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31984438697)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31984438611](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31984438611)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Enables KimiLinearForCausalLM (hybrid KDA linear-attention + MLA + MoE) to run on Intel XPU. ## Modifications - XPU has no tvm_ffi CUDA JIT kernel for KDA packed decode, so batched decode crashed. Set supports_packed_decode = ... and not is_xpu() so XPU uses the non-packed Triton decode() path (fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update) — the same fallback CPU/NPU already use - grouped-topk kernels (sgl_kernel topk_sigmoid on XPU) require fp32. signal.title: [Not for merge] config readers move to the bags (CI carrier for #35022-#35028)
signal.text: **Not for merge.** This carries the whole series against `main` so CI runs over the finished state; the units merge through their own PRs. | # | PR | what it does | |---|---|---| | 1 | #35022 | retire the multi-engine accommodation (a process holds one live config) | | 2 | #35023 | five processes publish before they read configuration | | 3 | #35024 | **bug fix**: adaptive spec sized its buffers from the startup record | | 4 | #35025 | the DP/EP topology reads come from the parallel bag | | 5 | #35026 | the per-instance families read the bags | | 6 | #35027 | `/server_info` reports the record; the resolving view is named as one | | 7 | #35028 | one control-plane log per process | Why this is a series: `ServerArgs` is on its way to holding the user's raw input, with resolution output living in the config bags. Every reader that wants the effective value has to be on the bags before that, and the exposure ratchet counts what is left: **297 → 181 pairs on the supplied-instance surface, 75 → 45 on the post-publish override surface**. Two defects here only a real server boot reaches, and both now have a static guard so they cannot come back: * a bag accessor called as an object member (`x.get_disagg()`) — imports fine, unit tests pass, `/health` returns 500 and the server never becomes healthy; * a launch path reading `get_parallel().pp_size` — a read-through property over process groups, so it raises before distributed init. Validation: the CPU battery over 535 registered files, twice (main and this series), diffed name by name — no new failure. Every commit passes the tests it touches on its own. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31979528227](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979528227)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979528205](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979528205)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] Reuse bit-exact modulation fast path for LTX-2.3
signal.text: ## Summary - reuse the existing self-verified bit-exact `_ltx2_modulate` fast path after the reference RMSNorm in `quality=lossless` - retain the fused RMSNorm + modulate path for request-scoped `quality=high` - keep the ordinary arithmetic expression visible to Inductor while compiling instead of routing compiled calls through an opaque custom op ## Why The lossless LTX-2.3 path already computes the reference RMSNorm and then launches separate broadcast scale/add operations. The shared modulation fast path preserves that RMSNorm result and its rounding while collapsing the two large pointwise launches. This is independent of enabling BCG for LTX-2.3. ## B300 validation In the 2026-08-14 full sweep from #21, the rebuilt lossless path kept the LTX-2.3 one-stage eager result within measurement noise of `torch.compile` (24.019 s versus 24.005 s denoise), while the two-stage presets remained faster than compile. These are end-to-end sweep results, not an isolated microbenchmark attribution. ## Tests - require `torch.equal` between the lossless fast path and the eager RMSNorm/modulate expression for both video and audio hidden sizes - verify that the compile path never calls the opaque modulation custom op - full pre-commit and CI registry validation pass on the rebased branch - Python syntax compilation passes - original combined isolated candidate: `a40940428`; this PR contains only the lossless modulation part and is rebuilt on current `main` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31933841193](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933841193)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31958334875](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31958334875)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Avoid materializing GDN QKV tensors during target verification
signal.text: ## Summary This PR removes redundant Q/K/V materialization from compatible GDN speculative target-verification paths. `causal_conv1d_update` already produces packed QKV. Previously, every GDN layer launched `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel` to copy that output into three contiguous tensors before Triton target verification. Triton accepts explicit token strides, so it can consume zero-copy `torch.split`/`view` tensors instead. The optimization is route-aware: - Triton and ReplaySSM target verification use strided Q/K/V views. - Prefill, FlashInfer, CuTeDSL, and other routes requiring contiguous inputs retain materialization. - Model arithmetic, recurrent-state updates, speculative acceptance, logits, and sampling are unchanged. This eliminates one memory-copy kernel launch per GDN layer on every compatible target-verification pass. ## Profile evidence Matched H200 CPU/GPU traces using Qwen3.5-4B, ReplaySSM, and NEXTN T=3: | Target-verification metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | QKV-split launches/pass | 24 | 0 | **-100%** | | QKV-split GPU time/pass | 56.946 us | 0 | **-56.946 us** | | CUDA-graph kernels | 452 | 428 | **-24** | | CUDA-graph span | 8,132.684 us | 8,040.898 us | **-91.786 us / -1.129%** | The graph-span reduction's approximate 95% interval was **79.732-103.841 us**. ## Standardized GSM8K benchmark 3 alternating baseline/QKV pairs ran on the same H200 with fresh servers, seed 0, empty prefix cache, and a 30-second cooldown. The benchmark used its defaults: 200 questions, five shots, 512 maximum output tokens, temperature 0, and parallelism 64. ### Pair 1 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,433.642 tok/s | 6,762.467 tok/s | **+5.111%** | | Latency | 5.379 s | 5.145 s | **-4.350%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.7374 ms | 9.4735 ms | **-2.710%** | ### Pair 2 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,202.258 tok/s | 6,366.221 tok/s | **+2.644%** | | Latency | 5.470 s | 5.401 s | **-1.261%** | | Engine TPOT | 10.2534 ms | 9.7761 ms | **-4.655%** | ### Pair 3 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,496.073 tok/s | 6,669.102 tok/s | **+2.664%** | | Latency | 5.270 s | 5.134 s | **-2.581%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.3372 ms | 9.4393 ms | **+1.093%** | ### Three-pair aggregate | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,377.324 tok/s | 6,599.263 tok/s | **+3.480%** | | Latency | 5.373 s | 5.227 s | **-2.723%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.7760 ms | 9.5630 ms | **-2.179%** | | Accuracy | 87.667% | 87.500% | -0.167 pp | ## Reproduction Server: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ PYTHONPATH=<sglang-source>/python \ sglang serve /path/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/ \ --port 30000 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --language-only \ --limit-mm-data-per-request '{"image":0,"video":0,"audio":0}' \ --context-length 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --linear-attn-decode-backend triton \ --random-seed 0 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \ --speculative-draft-model-path /path/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/ \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --enable-linear-replayssm-spec ``` Benchmark: ```bash python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --data-path /data/gsm8k/test.jsonl ``` Dataset SHA-256: ```text 3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14 ``` ## Validation - Exact target-verification output and recurrent-state parity. - ReplaySSM ring/fold parity and routing coverage. - Contiguous-input behavior retained for unsupported routes. - 31 affected H200 tests passed, covering 46 parameterized cases. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31970230867](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31970230867)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31970230734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31970230734)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: vedantjh2

signal.title: [AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support
signal.text: ## Motivation AMD gfx1250 is a new GPU architecture that differs substantially from the existing gfx95x and gfx942 targets SGLang already supports. Several components require gfx1250-specific paths due to architectural differences: - **No MFMA/WMMA FP4 scale instructions** (`V_WMMA_SCALE_F32_32X16X128_F4`): the existing CK/ASM `fused_moe` and fp4 dense GEMM paths produce garbage or crash. - **Triton `tl.dot(fp8, fp8)` miscompiles** for contraction dim ≥ 128 on gfx1250 (verified correct at K=64, broken at K≥128), requiring bf16 upcasting in the MLA attention Triton kernels. - **`llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.*` buffer instructions are absent** on RDNA4 (gfx12): the `quick_all_reduce` kernel would fail to compile. - **aiter CK-backed kernels (rope, QK RMSNorm, etc.) do not build** against the gfx1250 ROCm 7.15 image's composable_kernel. - **TileLang CK-backed buffer addressing does not compile** on gfx1250, blocking the Sinkhorn/MHC path. - **`num_stages > 1` Triton pipelines miscompile** on gfx1250, causing NaN in block-FP8 matmuls. - **ROCm SDK is pip-installed** (not at `/opt/rocm`) on this new image, requiring build and runtime path fixups for AITER, TileLang, MORI, and SGLang itself. This PR brings up gfx1250 support for DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B models with MXFP4/FP8 quantization. ## Modifications ### Infrastructure & Docker (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile`, `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, `python/pyproject_other.toml`) - Added a new `gfx1250-rocm7_15` Docker build stage starting from `ubuntu:24.04` with pip-installed ROCm 7.15 SDK, PyTorch 2.11, and Triton 3.7. Includes path and symlink workarounds for a pip-based (non-`/opt/rocm`) ROCm SDK. - Added `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` build-arg and made `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` configurable; per-arch `TRITON_COMMIT_DEFAULT` env vars. - Added gfx1250-specific AITER build path (`ENABLE_CK=0`, pip `--no-build-isolation`) and MORI build path using `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` for the ROCm SDK. - Added gfx1250-aware TileLang `ROCM_PATH` override during CMake build. - Updated Triton rebuild logic to preserve the installed version string (workaround for ROCm 7.15 / [rocm-systems#7643](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/issues/7643)). - Renamed `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` → `SGLANG_VERSION` to avoid leaking SGLang's nightly version into AITER's version. - Added `compressed-tensors==0.16.0` pin to `runtime_common` (supports torch ≥ 2.10) and dropped the old per-`srt_hip` `==0.15.0` pin. - CI install script: ROCm-version-aware AITER rebuild (`pip --no-build-isolation` for ROCm ≥ 7.15), MORI `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` fix, and MORI commit extraction validation. ### Core utility (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`) - Added `is_gfx1250_supported()` (cached) to detect AMD RDNA4 by `gcnArchName`. - Extended `mxfp_supported()` to include `"gfx1250"`. ### sgl-kernel (`sgl-kernel/setup_rocm.py`, `sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/quick_all_reduce_base.h`) - Added `gfx1250` to the allowed arch list in `setup_rocm.py`; gfx1250 shares the `E4M3` FP8 type and the 128KB dynamic smem budget with gfx950. - Guarded `llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.load/store.v4i32` declarations behind `#if !defined(__gfx1250__)`, providing stub no-ops for RDNA4 where those intrinsics don't exist. ### Attention kernels (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/`) - **`decode_attention.py`**: Do not downcast `q` to `fp8` before the QK dot; instead upcast K to `q`'s dtype (`bf16`) for the dot product, avoiding the gfx1250 fp8 dot bug at K≥128. Also keep softmax weights `p` in fp32 for the P·V accumulation (recovers GSM8K accuracy ~0.82 → ~0.92 on gfx1250 R1). - **`extend_attention.py`**: Same fp8 upcast fix and fp32 P·V fix for the prefill extend/unified kernels. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_decode.py`**: On gfx1250, dispatch DSv4 sparse decode attention to `aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_decode_sparse.pa_decode_sparse` (the triton path) instead of the custom Triton implementation. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_prefill.py`**: Disable the OPUS (gfx950 ASM) prefill path on gfx1250. ### MoE gate JIT kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/moe_fused_gate.cuh`) - Widened `__shfl_down_sync` mask from `0xFFFFFFFF` to a 64-bit `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFULL` on gfx1250 (which requires a 64-bit sync mask), while staying 32-bit on all other arches. ### Layernorm (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`) - On gfx1250, use aiter's Triton RMSNorm and `rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add` instead of the CK-backed aiter equivalents (which do not build). - Added pure-torch (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_torch`) and Triton (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_triton`) implementations of the Sinkhorn MHC kernel, dispatched on gfx1250 since TileLang's CK-backed addressing does not compile there. ### Quantization – FP8 (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`) - **`fp8_kernel.py`**: Added `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_gfx1250`, a gfx1250-specific block-FP8 matmul that: (1) upcasts fp8 operands to bf16 before `tl.dot`, (2) uses only `num_stages=1` (no SW pipelining), and (3) avoids modulo-wrap index tricks that miscompile on gfx1250. Selected automatically when `_is_gfx1250` is set. - **`fp8_utils.py`**: Force `_use_aiter = False` on gfx1250 (CK/MFMA-dependent aiter quant/GEMM kernels cannot run), directing gfx1250 to the pure-Triton block-FP8 path. Extended `triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` to accept pre-quantized `(input, input_scale)` from gfx1250's fused quant ops (skipping re-quantization). - **`fp8.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) instead of the gfx950 `shuffle_scale` (e8m0 layout) for FP8 MoE weight scales. Respect the `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` flag to select the triton a8w4 kernel shuffle layout. ### Quantization – MXFP4 Quark schemes (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/`) - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py`**: On gfx1250 with `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`, dequantize FP4 weights to bf16 at load time (since no dense fp4 GEMM is available) and run a plain bf16 linear forward. Includes a pure-Python MXFP4 e2m1 → bf16 dequantization LUT. - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) for W4A4 MoE weight scales (instead of `e8m0_shuffle`). Shuffle weights with the (16,16) aiter layout when `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` is set. - **`quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe.py`**: Added a dedicated gfx1250 W4A8 MoE path (`_use_gfx1250_w4a8`): bypasses the aiter CK/ASM fused_moe entirely; uses aiter's triton `moe_gemm_a8w4` kernel with a contraction-major, gate/up-interleaved, unshuffled weight layout. Weight preparation (`_process_weights_gfx1250`) and forward (`aiter_w4a8_gfx1250_forward` in new file `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py`) are implemented separately from the gfx950 path. ### New file: `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py` - Implements MXFP4 W4A8 GPT-OSS MoE forward for gfx1250 via `moe_gemm_a8w4`: routing, manual activation gather (in-kernel TDM gather disabled on gfx1250), static-FP8 downcast, two-GEMM (gate_up + down) execution with fused SwiGLU, and scatter back to token order. ### RoPE (`python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py`) - Fall back from aiter's CK rope kernels to SGLang's native rope on gfx1250 (aiter rope does not build on this arch). ### Communicator / fused quant (`python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py`) - On gfx1250, use `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` (triton, group_size=hidden_size = per-token) instead of aiter's CK `rmsnorm_quant` / `add_rmsnorm_quant` kernels. ### Sampler (`python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py`) - Disable aiter's greedy sample kernel on gfx1250 (not supported), falling back to `torch.argmax`. ### Capture mode (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/capture_mode.py`) - Disable `torch.compile` during CUDA graph capture on gfx1250 (compilation + capture together triggers issues on this arch). ### MLA attention (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py`, new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`) - On gfx1250 (`AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`), substitute the aiter `fused_qk_rmsnorm` (CK-backed, doesn't build) with a self-contained Triton RMSNorm or pure-torch fallback from the new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`. - Fixed the RoPE skip condition to check membership in `FORWARD_ABSORB_CORE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS` (not a string equality check), preventing an incorrect empty-K bug on non-aiter backends. ### DSv4 decoder layer (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_common/utils.py`, `amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`) - Extended all `_is_gfx95_supported` guards that gate MXFP4 fused quant, MQA q/k-norm, post-attention layernorm fused rmsnorm, and the fused MHC post/pre path to also include `_is_gfx1250_supported`. - On gfx1250, the fused MHC path is enabled by `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE` alone (no TileLang dependency), and the aiter Triton `try_fused_hc_post_pre` is used at all token batch sizes (no M-threshold cap, since there is no TileLang fallback). - gfx1250 does not skip the post-layernorm step after the Triton MHC kernel (since `norm_fused=False` for the aiter path). ### C4 attention indexer (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py`) - Added `_use_torch_fn` guard so the `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH` env var correctly prevents the 1D c4sl unsqueeze on gfx1250. ### Server args (`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`) - Track `_mem_fraction_static_set_by_user`: when the user explicitly sets `--mem-fraction-static`, skip the automatic 0.85 scaling for `aiter` backend with long contexts (instead, emit a warning so the user knows what is happening). ## Accuracy Tests Passed E2E accuracy tests of DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B. GPT-OSS-120B > AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8/ --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --prefill-attention-backend triton --decode-attention-backend aiter --max-running-requests 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-radix-cache --page-size 64 DSR1 > ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 SGLANG_MOE_SHUFFLE_GFX1250=1 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE SGLANG_AITER_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=0 SGLANG_INT4_WEIGHT=0 SGLANG_MOE_PADDING=1 SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1 SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=0 SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --attention-backend triton --max-running-requests 128 --kv-cache-dtype auto --page-size 64 DSv4-Flash > SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0 SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=0 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 --max-running-requests 256 --disable-radix-cache --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ## signal.author: akao-amd

signal.title: docs: fix Qwen3.8-27B mamba ratio calculator for speculative decoding
signal.text: The Qwen3.8-27B mamba ratio calculator (`docs/src/snippets/_qwen38_mamba_ratio_calculator.jsx`) was derived from the Kimi K3 one but lost four behaviours along the way, so it emitted the wrong `--mamba-full-memory-ratio` and `--max-mamba-cache-size` for **every** speculative configuration. The K3 sibling is correct on all four — this brings Qwen3.8 back in line with it. ### The four bugs **1. ReplaySSM ignored.** `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` moves the `D` intermediate SSM states off the per-request slot budget onto a fixed ring, so `D` is 0 even with spec on. The calculator counted `D=4`, emitting `r=2.08` where the truth is `1.04` — a 2x over-provision of the state pool, and the surplus comes straight out of KV. **2. DSPARK draft count.** DSPARK never emits `--speculative-num-draft-tokens`; its verify window is `--speculative-dspark-block-size` (gamma) + 1, auto-inferred from the draft checkpoint when omitted. `Number(null) || 4` therefore returned **4** where the truth is **6**, emitting `r=2.08` against `2.60` and under-provisioning. > 1 and 2 err in **opposite directions**, which is why no single spot-check surfaced them. **3. The pin double-counted D.** The engine divides the main state pool by `S` alone — `kv_cache_configurator.py`, `mamba_cap = max_mamba_cache_size // ratio` with `ratio = _calculate_mamba_ratio() = S` — and sizes the spec intermediate buffer separately from `D`. So the pin is `C * S`, not `C * (S + D)`. **4. `S` was hardcoded 5/4/3/1**, ignoring `SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_SKIP_DECODE_LOCK` (base 3 -> 2) and a disabled overlap scheduler / `--pp-size > 1` (ping-pong 2 -> 1). Replaced with the same expression the K3 calculator uses. `derive()` now takes `env`, matching K3's signature. ### Measured impact RTX 5090, NVFP4 W4A4 + fp8 KV, radix cache on, 8192 ISL / 1024 OSL, concurrency 1: | config | old r | correct r | effect | |---|---|---|---| | EAGLE (ReplaySSM) | 2.08 | **1.04** | KV pool 19,469 -> 11,992 tokens (**-38%**) | | DSPARK | 2.08 | **2.60** | under-provisions the state pool | | no-spec | 1.04 | 1.04 | unaffected | At bs=1 both still served with identical latency/throughput, so nothing published was broken at the documented operating point — but the KV loss bites at longer context or above concurrency 1. ### Verification The patched `derive()` reproduces the ratio actually used in each of the 10 servable RTX 5090 configurations (3 spec x 2 tiers x 2 state dtypes, minus 2 unachievable), where the old code was wrong for every speculative one. Also checked: `no_buffer` -> S=3, radix-off -> S=1, skip-lock and overlap-off each drop one slot, and an explicit `--speculative-dspark-block-size 7` -> D=8. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31982854811](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31982854811)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31982854471](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31982854471)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [sglang-miles] Upstream the restore_weights_before_load / process_weights_after_loading RPC infrastructure to main
signal.text: ## Context We're decomposing #25141 (K2.5 LoRA support) into focused PRs against \`main\`. Two pieces are tracked separately; the rest are landing as #28562 and #28564. While going through the diff against \`main\`, one hunk in \`model_runner.py\` from #25141 cannot land because the surrounding infrastructure it modifies doesn't exist on \`main\` yet. ## What's missing on \`main\` The \`PostProcessWeightsReqInput\` flow with the two flags ```python recv_req.restore_weights_before_load recv_req.post_process_quantization ``` and the corresponding pair of loops in \`ModelRunner.post_process_weights\` (or the equivalent location) that iterate \`self.model.named_modules()\` and call - \`quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading(module)\` when \`restore_weights_before_load\` is set, and - \`quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(module)\` when \`post_process_quantization\` is set. A quick \`git log -S \"restore_weights_before_loading\" origin/sglang-miles\` shows the symbol was introduced by > **5bd6c6bc4** [3/14] [sglang-miles] Support INT4 QAT for RL (#18565) — @yueming-yuan …as part of the larger sglang-miles weight-update series. ## The (small) follow-up hunk we want to land afterwards Once the loops exist on \`main\`, #25141's contribution is just a two-line skip of LoRA wrappers in each loop: ```python from sglang.srt.lora.layers import BaseLayerWithLoRA if recv_req.restore_weights_before_load: for _, module in self.model.named_modules(): if isinstance(module, BaseLayerWithLoRA): continue quant_method = getattr(module, \"quant_method\", None) if quant_method is not None and hasattr(quant_method, \"restore_weights_before_loading\"): quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading(module) ... if recv_req.post_process_quantization: for _, module in self.model.named_modules(): if isinstance(module, BaseLayerWithLoRA): continue quant_method = getattr(module, \"quant_method\", None) if quant_method is not None and hasattr(quant_method, \"process_weights_after_loading\"): quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(module) ``` LoRA wrappers forward \`quant_method\` for forward-path dispatch but don't own the packed params, so re-running quant post-processing on the wrapper double-processes or errors. The inner base FusedMoE / Linear is yielded separately by \`named_modules\` and gets its quant post-processing there. ## Ask Could you (or whoever owns the \`[N/14] [sglang-miles]\` series) carve the post-process-weights RPC plumbing out of #18565 into a \`main\`-targeted PR? It's: - the \`PostProcessWeightsReqInput\` field additions in \`managers/io_struct.py\`, - the dispatcher entry in \`managers/scheduler.py\` (or wherever \`PostProcessWeightsReqInput\` is routed), - the two \`named_modules\` loops in \`model_executor/model_runner.py\`, - the (likely existing) \`quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading\` shim on the relevant quant schemes. Once that lands we'll send a tiny follow-up with the two \`BaseLayerWithLoRA: continue\` lines and link back here. ## Why we can't just port it ourselves It touches several files that depend on the broader RL weight-update contract — \`PauseGenerationReqInput\`, \`UpdateWeightsFromTensorReqInput\`, etc. — and the right factoring there is something you've already worked through on sglang-miles. Re-doing it would risk diverging the two trees. cc @yueming-yuan @lifuhuang @jybsuper @Yan-Tan

signal.title: [DFlash] Infinite loop when using repetition_penalty — missing token accumulation and scaling penalties
signal.text: ## Summary The `repetition_penalty` sampling parameter is accepted by the API but completely ignored during inference. This occurs because `BatchedRepetitionPenalizer` is not implemented or registered in SGLang penaltylib orchestrator, causing the penalty to never be applied to logits. ## What Happens (User-facing symptoms) **Scenario A - Repetition loops in generation:** When setting `repetition_penalty > 1.0` (e.g., `1.15`) via the API, the model occasionally gets stuck in a repetition loop where it generates the same content indefinitely. The penalty has zero effect on the output distribution. **Scenario B - Silent parameter drop:** Users configure `repetition_penalty` expecting standard HuggingFace-style behavior (multiplicative logit adjustment), but the generation behaves identically to `repetition_penalty=1.0`. No warning or error is raised. ## Reproduction Steps This issue occurs with high probability (not truly sporadic). The following steps can reliably reproduce it: 1. Start an SGLang server with DFlash speculative decoding: ``` python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <your-model> --speculative-algo dflash --port 30000 ``` 2. Send a completion request with `repetition_penalty > 1.0` and a prompt that encourages repetition: ``` curl http://localhost:30000/generate -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text": "Please keep repeating this sentence: ", "temperature": 0.1, "top_p": 0.9, "max_new_tokens": 500, "repetition_penalty": 1.5, "stream": false}' ``` 3. Observe the logs showing `accept rate: 1.00` continuously, `#full token` keeps increasing, and the request never terminates normally. ## Observed Behavior (Logs) The following logs show a request stuck in a repetition loop with 100% accept rate and continuously increasing token count: ``` [2026-06-14 15:28:57] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 47360, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 290.40, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:28:58] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 47680, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 290.22, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:28:59] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 48000, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 290.38, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:00] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 48320, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 289.19, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:01] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 48640, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 289.10, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:02] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 48960, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 288.85, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:03] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 49280, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 289.00, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:05] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 49600, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 260.42, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:06] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 49920, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 287.98, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:07] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 50240, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 288.73, #queue-req: 0 ``` **Key observations:** - `accept rate: 1.00` (100%) - draft model predictions are fully accepted - `#full token` continuously increases (47360 to 50240+) - `#running-req: 1` - request never terminates - gen throughput remains stable (~290 token/s) - Model is stuck in a repetition loop despite `repetition_penalty` being set ## Root Cause Analysis ### Initial Finding In `sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py`, the `SamplingBatchInfo` class initializes the penalty orchestrator WITHOUT `BatchedRepetitionPenalizer`: ```python penalizer_orchestrator = penaltylib.BatchedPenalizerOrchestrator( vocab_size=vocab_size, batch=batch, penalizers={ penaltylib.BatchedFrequencyPenalizer, penaltylib.BatchedMinNewTokensPenalizer, penaltylib.BatchedPresencePenalizer, }, ) ``` `BatchedRepetitionPenalizer` is **missing** from the `penalizers` set. The `SamplingParams` class accepts and validates `repetition_penalty`, but since no penalizer implements it, the value is never read or applied during the `_apply_penalties()` phase. ### DFlash-Specific Root Cause (Updated) After deeper debugging, we identified the core issue specific to DFlash speculative decoding: **DFlash drafts multiple tokens per step (default 8), which conflicts with how `repetition_penalty` accumulates seen tokens via `scatter_`.** Detailed mechanism: 1. DFlash outputs `output_ids` with shape `(batch, K)` where K=8 (number of draft tokens), instead of the standard `(batch,)` single token per step. 2. `BatchedRepetitionPenalizer._cumulate_output_tokens` uses `scatter_` to accumulate penalty values into `cumulated_repetition_penalties` based on the output token IDs. 3. When `output_ids` is `(B, K)`, the `scatter_` operation maps multiple draft tokens into the same accumulation buffer. If multiple draft tokens within a single step share the same vocab index, the later write **overwrites** the earlier penalty value instead of properly accumulating it. 4. As a result, `repetition_penalty` cannot correctly track which tokens have already appeared, and fails to break the repetition loop. **Why this is a sporadic issue:** - The bug only manifests when the drafted tokens happen to include tokens that have already appeared in the generated sequence. - If all drafted tokens are new (no overlap with history), the `scatter_` overwrite problem does not surface. - This explains why the same request can sometimes succeed and sometimes get stuck in an infinite loop. ## Impact - Users cannot control repetition behavior via the standard `repetition_penalty` parameter. - Models prone to looping (especially under high temperature or long context) cannot be stabilized. - Breaks compatibility with HuggingFace `generation_config` and other frameworks that rely on this parameter. - Particularly problematic with speculative decoding (DFlash/Eagle) where repetition loops can cause infinite generation. ## Proposed Fix 1. Implement `BatchedRepetitionPenalizer` in `sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/repetition_penalty.py` following the HuggingFace formula: - If `logit > 0`: `logit /= repetition_penalty` - If `logit < 0`: `logit *= repetition_penalty` - If `logit == 0`: unchanged 2. Handle the `(B, K)` shape from DFlash by flattening `output_ids` before `scatter_` accumulation, ensuring each token penalty is properly accumulated rather than overwritten. 3. Register it in `penaltylib/__init__.py`. 4. Add `penaltylib.BatchedRepetitionPenalizer` to the `penalizers` set in `SamplingBatchInfo.__init__`. 5. Add unit tests to verify logit modification matches HF behavior. ## Next Steps Due to the sporadic nature of this bug, it is difficult to construct a stable reproduction case for automated testing. Our plan: 1. Apply the patch locally and validate it through extended real-world usage. 2. Monitor for a period to confirm the fix resolves the issue without introducing side effects. 3. Submit a formal PR upstream once stability is verified. ## Environment - **Model:** Qwen3.6-27B (FP8) - **Speculative Decoding:** DFlash (with Mamba hybrid layers) - **GPU:** RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96GB) - **Python Version:** 3.11 - **SGLang Version:** Both main branch and release versions tested - **Relevant Files:** - `sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py` - `sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/__init__.py` - `sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py`

signal.title: [Bug] MambaRadixCache.sanity_check() O(N) heap-walk runs on every idle scheduler tick — hangs server under sustained multi-stream load
signal.text: ## Environment - sglang 0.5.9 (also confirmed on 0.5.12 codebase by reading source) - Model: any `is_hybrid_ssm=True` model (Qwen3.5, Jamba, Zamba2, etc.) - Hardware: 16-card TP; reproducible on 1-card too - Trigger: 2+ concurrent `/v1/chat/completions` streams, growing context (5 k → 80 k tokens over 15 turns each) ## Symptom After 1–3 minutes of concurrent multi-stream load, **all scheduler TP ranks freeze**. Every rank spins at 99% CPU. In-flight requests never return. `pgrep`/`py-spy` shows all scheduler processes stuck in: ``` MambaRadixCache.sanity_check() └─ TreeNode.sanity_check() ← recursive heap walk └─ ... (depth × O(N) per call) ``` The function is called by `check_tree_cache` in `scheduler_runtime_checker_mixin.py`: ```python def check_tree_cache(self: Scheduler): if (self.is_hybrid_ssm and self.tree_cache.supports_mamba()): self.tree_cache.sanity_check() # <-- called every idle tick ``` `sanity_check` does a **full recursive walk of the entire radix tree** to verify invariants. With a grown 50 k-token cache after dozens of turns, this takes seconds per call. Since it is called on every scheduler idle tick, the scheduler never exits the check — it is continuously re-entered before completing. ## Root cause `self_check_during_idle` calls `check_tree_cache` on **every loop iteration** with no rate-limiting, no early exit, and no check that the previous invocation completed. For pure attention models the radix tree walk is O(N tokens) but fast (no mamba state bookkeeping); for `is_hybrid_ssm` models `sanity_check` additionally validates mamba state tensors per node, making it dramatically slower. ## Reproduction Minimal reproducer (2 concurrent streams, 15 turns each, context grows 5 k → 80 k): ```python import threading, json, urllib.request, time EP = "http://localhost:30000" SYSTEM = "You are an assistant.\n" + "context " * 5000 # ~5 k tokens TURNS = [{"role": "user", "content": f"Turn {i}: summarise the context."} for i in range(15)] def stream(tid): msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}] for turn in TURNS: msgs.append(turn) req = urllib.request.Request(f"{EP}/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps({"model": "...", "messages": msgs, "max_tokens": 120, "temperature": 0}).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) r = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90).read()) msgs.append(r["choices"][0]["message"]) threads = [threading.Thread(target=stream, args=(i,)) for i in range(2)] [t.start() for t in threads] [t.join() for t in threads] ``` Triggers the hang in < 2 minutes on a model served with `--reasoning-parser` (which sets `is_hybrid_ssm=True`). ## Fix proposal Option A (minimal / safe): guard `check_tree_cache` so it only runs at most once per N seconds: ```python _last_cache_check: float = 0.0 def check_tree_cache(self: Scheduler): if not (self.is_hybrid_ssm and self.tree_cache.supports_mamba()): return now = time.monotonic() if now - self._last_cache_check < 30.0: # at most every 30 s return self._last_cache_check = now self.tree_cache.sanity_check() ``` Option B (correct long-term): move `sanity_check` out of the hot scheduler loop entirely — call it only on explicit request (debug flag / admin endpoint) rather than on every idle tick. The check is debug-only and should never run in production. Option C (what we ship in our deployment): no-op `check_tree_cache` entirely. The radix cache continues to function correctly; the sanity check is a debug assertion, not a correctness requirement. ## Workaround Patching `check_tree_cache` to return immediately (no-op) eliminates the hang. The mamba radix cache stays active and correct — the walk is purely a debug assertion. ## Tested on 2-stream stress test (15 turns × 2 streams, context 5 k → 80 k, back-to-back for 5 minutes): | Config | Outcome | |---|---| | `check_tree_cache` unpatched | Hang after ~90 s, 100% CPU on all schedulers | | `check_tree_cache` no-op patched | 25/26 requests complete (1 rare TCP transient), server stays live for entire test duration |

signal.title: [Bug] HF3FS HiCache hits ZeroDivisionError with DeepSeek-V4 logical KV anchor
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Symptom DeepSeek-V4 HiCache uses a LogicalHostPool as the primary KV anchor. This pool only manages logical token indices and does not contain physical KV data. When hf3fs is selected as the HiCache storage backend, the backend calculates bytes_per_page=0 from this logical pool and later divides by it during initialization. Therefore, DeepSeek-V4 cannot start with HF3FS L3 storage. Starting sglang with DSV4 and HF3FS will encounter: ``` File "/path/to/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/storage_hf3fs.py", line 220, in __init__ self.num_pages = self.file_size // self.bytes_per_page ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero ``` The DeepSeek-V4 cookbook currently lists hf3fs as an available L3 backend, but I could not find a DSV4-specific HF3FS test or existing issue covering this problem. ### root cause DeepSeek-V4 creates a LogicalHostPool whose storage-related properties are: ``` self.kv_buffer = None self.size_per_token = 0 def get_ksize_per_token(self): return 0 ``` The storage factory calculates: ``` bytes_per_page = ( mem_pool_host.get_ksize_per_token() * mem_pool_host.page_size ) ``` Therefore, bytes_per_page is zero. `HiCacheHF3FS.__init__()` subsequently executes: ``` self.num_pages = self.file_size // self.bytes_per_page ``` This should result in: ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero ### Reproduction Setup HF3FS config json file according to doc https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/docs/deploy_sglang_3fs_multinode.md Start SGLang server like: ``` export --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 \ --served-model-name local-dsv4-flash \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-ratio 2 \ --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \ --hicache-io-backend direct \ --hicache-storage-backend hf3fs \ --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete ``` You will see ``` File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 527, in build_deepseek_v4_hicache_stack cache_controller = HybridCacheController( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py", line 205, in __init__ self.attach_storage_backend( File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py", line 225, in attach_storage_backend super().attach_storage_backend( File "/path/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py", line 475, in attach_storage_backend self.storage_backend = StorageBackendFactory.create_backend( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/backend_factory.py", line 94, in create_backend return cls._create_builtin_backend( signal.title: config: the per-instance families read the bags
signal.text: The tokenizer manager, the detokenizer, the multimodal processors, the encode server and the HTTP entrypoint read resolved config off the instance they were handed. That was justified by several engines sharing one process; a process holds one live config, so they read the bags like every other consumer. The same goes for the launch paths, the sidecar and the Ray driver, and for the three single-reader decisions (the grammar-backend factory, the token-oracle install gate, the new-token ratio tracker). The parallel sizes are the exception that has to be spelled out: pp_size and its four siblings are read-through properties over the process groups, so a launch path -- which decides how many processes to spawn before joining any group -- must ask for the configured value. Functions lose the config parameter where every caller was handing over the process config: the EPD rejection guard, the hidden-state ceiling, the token-oracle gate. sarvam-moe stops caching the process config in a lazy slot and dispatches on the configured attention pair like the other dispatch sites. Two guards pin what only a server boot would otherwise catch: that no launch path reads a live-shadowed size, and that the bag accessors are never called as object members. The tests that drove these paths with stand-in objects publish a config instead. The reads that stay: the two gates deciding whether late resolution runs, the remote-instance seed check, and the NCCL environment setup. All three run before this process publishes, and each needs its own call on whether it is asking about raw input or about the effective value. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979519532](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979519532)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979519397](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979519397)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: config: publish before a process reads configuration
signal.text: Five processes read config namespaces before they published. The launch path ran validation, port allocation and the subprocess launches ahead of its publish; the scheduler ran its process configuration first; the tokenizer manager read the parallel bag in a constructor that is the first publish in a tokenizer-worker process; the encode server's launch path read the DP size before the encoder it builds publishes; the detokenizer never published at all while reading resolution-written fields off the instance it was handed. Each publishes as early as its config is final -- for the launch path that is right after late resolution, which refuses a published instance. The two DSA seed predicates take no config argument: every caller was handing over the process config, and the fields they read are bag leaves. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979514149](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979514149)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979513991](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979513991)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: config: retire the multi-engine accommodation in the runtime context
signal.text: A process holds at most one live config: the bags always describe the engine running now. Re-publish stays last-publish-wins, which is what lets a process rebuild an engine after shutting the previous one down. Drop preserve_config() and its per-leaf bag snapshot/restore helpers. They existed for a nested build that publishes a private ServerArgs copy; the draft build stopped doing that when per-runner values became constructor arguments, and no production caller is left. Drop the launcher entry from ROLE_NAMESPACE_SETS: no process publishes under that role. The multi-item scoring tests held two engines alive at once. The reference engine now runs its scoring calls first and shuts down before the engine under test boots; engine boots per class are unchanged, so the CI harness still sees the same GPU demand. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979513572](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979513572)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979513393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979513393)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: spec: size the speculative buffers from the bags, not the startup record
signal.text: Adaptive speculative decoding switches the step config at runtime through get_context().override, which moves the spec bag leaves and leaves the ServerArgs record on its startup values. Six sizing paths read the record: - allocation_sizing: the per-decode KV reserve, recomputed every decode batch, kept reserving for the startup step count after a switch - spec_utils.resolve_num_tokens_per_req: draft-extend capture widths were sized for the startup draft-token count while a different candidate state was being captured - spec_info.create_dummy_verify_input: the autotune forward inside the capture window built its dummy verify input at the startup tree shape - eagle_disaggregation: the prebuilt-batch draft-input state count - managers.utils.compute_num_reserved_tokens: the token budget the rust ingress enforces All of them read the spec bag now, and so do the two DSA seed predicates the disagg path calls. The config parameter goes away where every caller was handing over the process config anyway, which drops the disagg draft-input hand-off chain down to what it uses; the tests that drove those paths with stand-in objects publish a config. The exposure pins shrink by 16 (axis 1) and 6 (axis 2) pairs. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31979516189](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979516189)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31979516074](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31979516074)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][CI] Add GPT-OSS perf benchmarks to the ROCm 7.2 nightly
signal.text:
## Motivation GPT-OSS is one of the models in the reported ROCm 7.2 + Triton 3.7 slowdown, and it has no throughput coverage on AMD — DeepSeek-V4 is the only affected model that does. ## Modifications Add one benchmark per architecture, each sweeping batch sizes 1/8/16/64 (plus a leading warmup) at ISL 4096 / OSL 512 through `bench_one_batch_server`: | Test | Hardware and precision | Models | |---|---|---| | `test_gpt_oss_perf_mi35x.py` | MI35x (gfx950) TP8, native MXFP4 + AITER | `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `openai/gpt-oss-120b` | | `test_gpt_oss_perf_amd.py` | MI30x (gfx942) TP8, bf16 conversions | `lmsys/gpt-oss-20b-bf16`, `lmsys/gpt-oss-120b-bf16` | Launch arguments match the corresponding accuracy tests, so a throughput change points at the serving stack rather than at a different recipe. The checkpoints differ per architecture for the same reason the accuracy tests already split them: MI30x does not serve the MXFP4 checkpoints natively, which is why the `lmsys/*-bf16` conversions exist. **Both run as a step on the GPT-OSS accuracy job that already serves the same models**, not as separate jobs: - MI30x → `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-rocm720` - MI35x → `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-rocm720` That avoids paying container setup and the weight cache a second time. Because no new jobs are created, the workflow diff is just the two added steps — no `job_select` options and no `check-all-jobs` dependencies change. Both steps also clear `github_summary.md` before running, matching the convention every other multi-step job here uses. Without that, the second step re-appends the first step's block to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Also lift the duplicated cost-free AMD markdown renderer into `generate_simple_markdown_report()` in `nightly_bench_utils.py`; both new tests use the same output schema as the existing AMD perf sweeps. The tests report benchmark data and fail on launch or benchmark errors. They intentionally carry no throughput thresholds: there is no nightly history yet from which to set defensible baselines. The numbers below are the first data points toward those baselines. DeepSeek-V4 gating is separate in [#34640](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34640). ## Validation run **[nightly-test-amd-rocm720 run 31850998638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31850998638) — success**, dispatched against this branch: ```bash gh workflow run nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml \ --ref cursor/amd-gpt-oss-kimi-k3-perf-tests-7e6c \ -f job_filter='nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-rocm720,nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-rocm720' \ -f continue_on_error=true ``` The filter selected exactly the two jobs this PR touches and skipped the other 45. All four steps passed, with each new perf step running after its existing accuracy step in the same job: | Job | Accuracy step | Perf step | |---|---|---| | `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-rocm720` | success, 11.7 min | success, 6.5 min | | `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-rocm720` | success, 18.4 min | success, 3.9 min | Re-validating the summary-clearing fix in [run 31936282742](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31936282742). ## Accuracy Tests No model or kernel changes; the new tests reuse existing serving recipes and add no accuracy assertions. Both GPT-OSS accuracy steps still pass in the validation run, unaffected by the added perf step. Static validation completed: - registered-test registry validation, and both suites resolve to exactly one file - workflow YAML parsing, duplicate job-name check, and no stale dispatch option or `check-all-jobs` dependency - Ruff, Black, isort, codespell ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured in the validation run above, at ISL 4096 / OSL 512, TP8. **Each architecture runs two different model sizes**, so every table below holds two independent sweeps — 20b and 120b — not one model measured twice. **MI35x (gfx950), MXFP4 — `openai/gpt-oss-20b`** | BS | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | ITL (ms) | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 1.14 | 463.69 | 2.16 | | 8 | 1.43 | 3148.30 | 2.54 | | 16 | 1.66 | 5793.03 | 2.76 | | 64 | 2.82 | 17393.64 | 3.68 | **MI35x (gfx950), MXFP4 — `openai/gpt-oss-120b`** | BS | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | ITL (ms) | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 1.65 | 319.90 | 3.13 | | 8 | 2.06 | 2177.35 | 3.67 | | 16 | 2.39 | 4040.90 | 3.96 | | 64 | 4.21 | 11661.29 | 5.49 | **MI30x (gfx942), bf16 — `lmsys/gpt-oss-20b-bf16`** | BS | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | ITL (ms) | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 1.61 | 328.27 | 3.05 | | 8 | 2.25 | 2119.96 | 3.77 | | 16 | 2.73 | 3889.67 | 4.11 | | 64 | 5.41 | 11078.14 | 5.78 | **MI30x (gfx942), bf16 — `lmsys/gpt-oss-120b-bf16`** | BS | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | ITL (ms) | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 2.29 | 230.71 | 4.33 | | 8 | 3.41 | 1393.54 | 5.74 | | 16 | 4.72 | 2165.65 | 7.39 | | 64 | 10.52 | 4837.02 | 13.23 | ### 20b vs 120b on the same hardware The two sweeps per architecture differ because the models differ — 120b has ~6x the parameters and ~1.4x the active parameters per token of 20b: | Architecture | 20b at BS 64 | 120b at BS 64 | 20b/120b | |---|---:|---:|---:| | MI35x (MXFP4) | 17393.64 tok/s | 11661.29 tok/s | 1.49x | | MI30x (bf16) | 11078.14 tok/s | 4837.02 tok/s | 2.29x | ### Cross-architecture note The MI35x and MI30x tables are also not comparable to each other: they differ in silicon *and* checkpoint precision, and the precision split is forced (MI30x cannot serve MXFP4 natively). Per-GPU weight footprint from the run's `Load weight end` lines: | Model | MI35x (MXFP4) | MI30x (bf16) | Extra traffic on MI30x | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 20b | 2.33 GB | 5.00 GB | 2.15x | | 120b | 11.52 GB | 27.40 GB | 2.38x | For 120b at BS 64 the MI35x/MI30x throughput ratio (2.41x) lands almost exactly on that weight-traffic ratio (2.38x), which is what bandwidth-bound decode should do. Each table gates its own architecture over time; neither is a regression against the other. ### Added nightly cost The sweeps are short because both models load and serve quickly: | Step | Measured | Added cost | |---|---:|---:| | MI30x perf step | 6.5 min | 0.87 GPU-h | | MI35x perf step | 3.9 min | 0.52 GPU-h | | **Total** | | **≈1.4 GPU-h/night** | Folding into the accuracy jobs rather than creating standalone jobs avoids repeating container setup and dependency install, which cost 9.0 min on MI30x and 6.0 min on MI35x in this run: standalone jobs would have made the same coverage ≈3.4 GPU-h/night. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

signal.title: [Fix] Select custom all-reduce v2 by topology capability
signal.text: ## Motivation This fixes a regression introduced by #32541. Before that PR, custom all-reduce v2 was enabled by default and eligible TP16 groups reached the topology and allocator capability check. The added TP2-8-specific multinode policy disabled `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2` for TP16 before capability detection, forcing an otherwise eligible configuration to fall back. ## Modifications - Remove the separate multinode flag and server-argument policy; `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2` remains the single enable and opt-out control. - Select cross-node v2 from the actual topology, VMM allocator capability, and architecture-tuned world sizes. - Let eligible custom all-reduce inputs run before symmetric-memory PyNccl; larger inputs still fall through. - Replace the server-argument policy tests with capability and dispatch tests. ## Original commits - `fb9411abe` ## Accuracy Tests No model math changes. - `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py` — 10 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No public speed benchmark was run. The change restores the eligible TP16 custom all-reduce v2 path and preserves fallback for unsupported topology or message sizes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Pre-commit passed for the changed files. The bare-pytest checker was run directly under Python 3.12 because its isolated hook interpreter cannot parse the `int | None` annotation used by the checker. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31978608777](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31978608777)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31978608691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31978608691)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] [GLM5] Skip DSA decode indexer when kv_len <= index_topk (dense k-only fast path)
signal.text: ## Summary - On GLM-5.2 DSA decode, when a request's `kv_len <= index_topk` the top-k selects **all** valid positions, so the indexer's logits GEMM + `paged_mqa_logits` + top-k selection is wasted work. Add a **k-only** fast path that skips the indexer, stores the K cache, and generates the identity index directly (`[0, 1, ..., kv_len-1, -1, ...]`), feeding the same sparse-MLA decode attention kernel. - **CUDA-graph "Design A" dual-graph:** capture a dense (k-only) and a sparse (full indexer) decode graph per batch-size bucket and dispatch on `max_kv_len` vs `index_topk` at replay. This is correct for mixed lengths — any request with `kv_len > index_topk` in the batch falls back to the sparse graph. - **Auto-enabled for DSA models, no env toggle.** Since DSA models expose `index_topk` in their HF config, the dual-graph is turned on automatically whenever `index_topk` is present (`dsa_dual_graph = dsa_index_topk is not None`); non-DSA models and other archs are unaffected. Eager decode takes the same fast path per-step when safe. (No `SGLANG_DSA_DECODE_*` / `SGLANG_KONLY_DEBUG` environment variables — an earlier revision gated this behind opt-in/debug flags; those were removed per review.) ## Changes | File | Change | | --- | --- | | layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py | k-only fast path (`_forward_cuda_k_only`): skip logits/top-k, store K cache; for MLA generate the identity index; extended to DECODE (eager + graph) | | model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py | Design A dual-graph: capture dense (k-only) + sparse decode graphs per bs bucket; host-dispatch on `max_kv_len` vs `index_topk`; auto-enabled for DSA models via `dsa_index_topk` | | model_executor/runner_utils/capture_mode.py | capture-time DSA variant flag (dense/sparse) read by the indexer skip branch | | model_executor/runner/shape_key.py | include the DSA decode variant in the cuda-graph shape key | ## Scope GLM-5.2 DSA decode on gfx950 (MI355X). Auto-enabled for DSA models; correct for mixed lengths (long context stays on the sparse indexer path). Other archs / hardware unaffected. ## Test plan **Accuracy (GSM8K, MI355X TP4, GLM-5.2-MXFP4):** | | Baseline | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | | GSM8K | 0.922 | 0.941 | Within margin of error. **Performance (MI355X TP4, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, docker `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260714`, tilelang DSA backend):** token throughput per GPU (tok/s/gpu, higher better) and median TPOT (ms, lower better), dense-decode OFF vs ON (this PR). Isolated effect — same build/backend, only this PR's commits added, everything else identical. Only **i1024 / o1024** is shown: this optimization applies when `kv_len <= index_topk` (2048). At i8192 every decode step has `kv_len > 2048`, so it stays on the sparse path and is unchanged. | Concurrency | TPUT off | TPUT PR | Δ TPUT | TPOT off | TPOT PR | Δ TPOT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | 71.8 | 75.5 | +5.2% | 13.28 | 12.62 | −5.0% | | 8 | 126.8 | 133.2 | +5.1% | 15.18 | 14.41 | −5.1% | | 16 | 196.9 | 205.1 | +4.2% | 19.46 | 18.67 | −4.1% | | 32 | 312.4 | 322.8 | +3.3% | 24.66 | 23.90 | −3.1% | | 64 | 468.9 | 480.3 | +2.4% | 32.88 | 32.14 | −2.3% | ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \ --tp 4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tool-call-parser glm47 \ --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 32}' \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \ --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --tokenizer-worker-num 8 \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion ``` Token throughput per GPU improves ~2.4–5.2% and TPOT drops ~2.3–5.1% at i1k, from skipping the wasted indexer when the sparse top-k would select all positions anyway. The gain is largest at low concurrency and converges to ~2.4% at conc 64. (Δ is the isolated dense-decode effect — same build/backend, feature off vs on — not a full-stack-vs-stock comparison.) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31978978932](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31978978932)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31978978765](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31978978765)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [HiCache] Buffer-only mode for HiCache host memory layer
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation There has been extensive discussion around making HiCache work better for small host-memory setups: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28614, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20535, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16909, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14056. Out of this, we've converged on the following design: use the L2 host-memory layer as a buffer. This decouples L2 from the complex tree management and the frequent, pressure-driven evictions it would otherwise incur, while still capturing the full benefit of IO latency hiding and maximizing cache hit rate through the larger L3 layer. signal.title: [KDA] Route Kimi-Linear through native Cake kernels
signal.text: Depends on #34299 for the checkpoint-capable KDA serving surface and on FlashInfer [#4535](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4535) for the native `lower_bound=None` kernels. The incremental commits after #34299's head will narrow automatically when the dependency lands. ## Summary - Auto-select BF16 recurrent state and native Cake prefill/decode for Kimi-Linear-48B's D128 equal-head contract at TP-local H4/H8/H16/H32 (TP8/TP4/TP2/TP1). - Read prefill selection from the runner-scoped linear-attention dispatcher, preserving current server configuration ownership after the upstream backend refactor. - Feed packed projection Q/K/V, raw gate, and beta views directly to FlashInfer without `contiguous()` staging or state gather/scatter copies. - Preserve the native prefill route under breakable CUDA Graph padding by slicing only the live token prefix as storage-sharing row views; unpadded calls preserve exact tensor identity. - Keep admission fail-closed and emit structured per-layer route telemetry proving eligibility, native success, zero fallback/fatal outcomes, graph phase, and static zero-copy ownership. ## Validation - B200 and B300 each pass 85 focused unit tests, 12 GPU decode integration tests, and seven GPU prefill integration tests, including bounded rows, native H4/H8/H16/H32 unbounded routes, checkpoints, packed rows, graph padding, and exact-identity inputs. - The exact-stack FlashInfer matrix passes 93 source/API/JIT contracts, eight prefill GPU rows, and 30 decode/export tests on both architectures. - The final source passes current Black, Ruff, isort, Python compilation, and the repository lint workflow. ## Cold-L2 performance versus FLA Triton All rows use CUPTI GPU activity timing with L2 flushing. Ratios are `FLA / Cake`, so values above 1.0 mean Cake is faster. | Arch | Decode B1 | B4 | B8 | B16 | B32 | B64 | B128 | Geomean | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | B200 | 0.9932x | 0.9501x | 0.9911x | 1.0748x | 0.9899x | 0.9733x | 0.9188x | 0.9835x | | B300 | 0.9854x | 0.9200x | 0.9724x | 1.0571x | 0.9966x | 0.9778x | 0.9321x | 0.9765x | The selected decode topology is `1.0105x` faster than the prior Cake checkpoint on B200 and `1.0386x` faster on B300, reducing the FLA gap from 3.10%/6.12% to 1.68%/2.41%. FLA's multi-kernel prefill active-union/Cake speedups at T=512/1024/2048/4096/8192 are `1.4917x/1.4084x/1.3418x/1.3114x/1.2670x` on B200 and `1.4775x/1.4031x/1.3687x/1.3374x/1.2972x` on B300, for `1.3618x/1.3754x` geometric means. A separate local-H4 split-8/split-16 screen at B=1/4/8/16/32/64/128 found split-16 faster at every row on both targets, by `1.2118x/1.2050x` geometric means. The existing work-based selector therefore already chooses the faster topology throughout the new TP8/H4 route. The final same-stack local-H4 Cake-versus-FLA ratios at B=1/4/8/16/32/64/128 are `0.9927x/0.9648x/0.9526x/0.9748x/0.9451x/0.9955x/1.0617x` on B200 and `0.9688x/0.9626x/0.9638x/0.9797x/0.9649x/0.9716x/1.0647x` on B300, for `0.9832x/0.9817x` geometric means (Cake 1.71%/1.86% slower). Cake is 6.17%/6.47% faster at B128. This bounds the native TP8 kernel residual well below the full-model delta and rules out fallback or a wrong H4 topology. ## Kimi-Linear-48B serving The reference arm uses SGLang's Flash Linear Attention-derived `TritonKDAKernel` (FLA Triton). The one post-interface-change audit runs Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct at TP8/local-H4 on eight B200 GPUs. Both arms use 32 workload-shaped warmup requests followed by 64 measured requests at nominal 2,048 input / 256 output tokens, concurrency 32, seed 20260814, and cache flush. ### Accuracy and stop behavior Both arms use the same 200-example, five-shot GSM8K evaluation: temperature 0, 512 maximum tokens, 128 request threads, and stop token `163586`. | Metric | Cake | FLA Triton | Cake delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | GSM8K accuracy | 0.890 | 0.895 | -0.005 absolute | | Required accuracy | >0.88 | >0.88 | both pass | | Stop-token completions | 200/200 | 199/200 | — | | Length-capped completions | 0/200 | 1/200 | FLA response valid at 512-token cap | Every reported stop matches token `163586`; there are no mismatched stop tokens. ### End-to-end serving performance For throughput, positive Cake delta means speedup. For latency and memory, negative Cake delta is better. | Metric | Cake | FLA Triton | Cake/FLA result | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Completed requests | 64/64 | 64/64 | equal | | Total throughput | 25,490.40 token/s | 30,404.58 token/s | `0.8384x` (-16.16%) | | Input throughput | 22,330.18 token/s | 26,635.11 token/s | -16.16% | | Output throughput | 3,160.22 token/s | 3,769.46 token/s | -16.16% | | Request throughput | 22.480 req/s | 26.814 req/s | -16.16% | | Mean TTFT | 129.163 ms | 113.298 ms | +14.00% | | Median TTFT | 171.820 ms | 84.394 ms | +103.59% | | Mean TPOT | 7.491 ms | 6.023 ms | +24.38% | | Median TPOT | 6.904 ms | 6.254 ms | +10.39% | | Mean ITL | 7.566 ms | 6.028 ms | +25.51% | | Median ITL | 4.055 ms | 4.077 ms | -0.55% | | Peak memory, eight GPUs | 1,366,752 MiB | 1,388,080 MiB | -21,328 MiB (-1.54%) | | Peak individual GPU | 170,940 MiB | 173,606 MiB | -2,666 MiB (-1.54%) | There is no full-model throughput speedup in this TP8 run: Cake reaches `0.8384x` FLA throughput, or 16.16% lower, while saving 1.54% memory. signal.title: Clean up environ.py: remove dead env vars, unify deprecation handling, move examples to a unit test
signal.text: ## Motivation `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` accumulated several kinds of clutter: deprecated descriptors nothing reads, four different mechanisms for warning about deprecated env vars, and ~80 lines of example functions at the bottom that were the module's only test coverage. ## Modifications **Remove dead descriptors** (verified no readers outside `environ.py`): - `SGLANG_CUTLASS_MOE` — only consumer was the deprecation shim `_cutlass_moe_env_override` (removed along with its pass invocation in `server_args.py` and its unit test). Setting the env now warns instead of silently flipping the backend; use `--moe-runner-backend=cutlass`. - `SGLANG_OPT_USE_COMPRESSOR_V2` — DSV4 compressor V2 is always used. - `SGLANG_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK` — duplicate polarity of `SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK`, which is the only variant the check reads. A registry entry keeps the old name working (inverted) with a warning. `SGLANG_DEEPEP_BF16_DISPATCH` and `DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT` were candidates but still have live readers (`unquant.py`, `ep_moe/layer.py`, the MTP draft-build scopes, a MUSA path; the latter is a vendor alias consumed by the Ascend DeepEP library), so they stay with clarified comments. **Unify deprecation handling.** The four mechanisms — `_print_deprecated_env` calls inside the misnamed `_convert_SGL_to_SGLANG`, the inline ms→s loop, the `SGL_`→`SGLANG_` prefix rewrite, and top-level `_warn_deprecated_env_to_cli_flag` calls — collapse into one declarative `_DEPRECATED_ENVS` registry (old name → optional replacement + optional value transform + optional note) processed once at import by `_handle_deprecated_envs()`, with a single warning format. **Bug fix (behavior change):** the old `SGL_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK` → `SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK` mapping copied the value without inverting the polarity, so `SGL_DISABLE...=1` *enabled* the check. The registry entry now inverts it. **Move examples to a real test.** The `examples()` family at the bottom only ran via `python environ.py` and was the sole coverage of `override`/`set(None)`/`clear`/`is_set` and the `__bool__` guard. Deleted, and ported (plus new registry tests) to `test/registered/unit/test_environ.py`, registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. **Import hygiene:** `debug_utils.cuda_coredump` (which self-gates on `SGLANG_CUDA_COREDUMP`) is now imported only when that flag is set, keeping the default import of this early-loaded, stdlib-only module free of package side effects. `staging_buffer.py` now reads `SGLANG_STAGING_USE_TORCH` through `envs` instead of raw `os.environ` (note: a raw `"0"` was previously truthy-parsed as *enabling* the torch fallback; it now correctly parses as false). Docs: dropped the `SGLANG_CUTLASS_MOE` and `SGLANG_ENABLE_GRPC` rows from the env-var reference. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/test_environ.py`) - [x] Update documentation as needed <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31977905155](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31977905155)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31977977069](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31977977069)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Spec] Resolve shared-read ends from the backend declaration alone
signal.text: The decode runner gated the shared-read-ends resolution on the forward mode before asking the backend. Both halves of that gate are now redundant: - `elif not forward_mode.is_decode()` -- the modes that reach this runner are `DECODE` / `TARGET_VERIFY` / `IDLE` / `DLLM_EXTEND` (plus `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2` from the multi-layer eagle draft-extend runner), and the base `shared_read_ends` already returns `UNKNOWN` for everything but decode and target verify. - the `is_last_shared_read_phase` check -- which runner owns the publish is already answered by `last_shared_read_runner`. For every algorithm whose last reading phase is not verify, the target runner is not the runner the scheduler reads, so its verify record is simply never picked up. `is_last_shared_read_phase` had no other caller, so it is deleted from both `SpeculativeAlgorithm` and `CustomSpecAlgo`. A plugin that needs a different owner overrides `last_shared_read_runner` on its worker instead. One behavior change: NGRAM's scheduler-read runner is the target runner and its verify is the step's only GPU forward, so it moves from the coarse whole-forward fence to the fine-grained read-done event. That is the intended fence for it -- the old predicate returned `is_draft_extend_v2()`, which NGRAM never runs. Stacks on #35057, which is what makes the verify record harmless for multi-layer eagle. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31976677067](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31976677067)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31976676905](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31976676905)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
