signal.title: [Bug][Diffusion] TeaCache CFG lifecycle double resets serial CFG and leaks state with CFG parallel
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug TeaCache's CFG state lifecycle currently depends on the previous value of `self.is_cfg_negative`, even though the current CFG branch is already available from `forward_batch.is_cfg_negative`. This reproduces as two related state-lifecycle bugs: 1. In normal serial CFG, TeaCache resets twice at denoising timestep 0. The positive branch resets correctly, but the following negative branch resets again before `self.is_cfg_negative` has been updated to the negative branch. This loses one forward's counter/state and shifts the TeaCache schedule. 2. With CFG parallel, a rank that owns only the negative branch does not reliably reset TeaCache at the beginning of subsequent requests. Cached modulated inputs, residuals, counters, and accumulated distances can therefore survive across generation requests. There is also a related accounting issue under CFG parallel: `TeaCacheParams.get_skip_boundaries()` doubles the boundaries whenever CFG is enabled. That is correct when one model instance executes both positive and negative forwards serially, but not when CFG parallel assigns one branch to each rank. I verified that the relevant logic is still present on current `main` at: `ace7314173c8221ecf5f213575302eab98f4e84f` The same TeaCache implementation is also present in both v0.5.16 and v0.5.17. ## Root cause `TeaCacheMixin._get_teacache_context()` obtains the current branch: ```python is_cfg_negative = forward_batch.is_cfg_negative ``` but performs request-start reset using the previous model state: ```python if current_timestep == 0 and not self.is_cfg_negative: self.reset_teacache_state() ``` Current source: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ace7314173c8221ecf5f213575302eab98f4e84f/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/cache/teacache.py Wan then updates the model-side branch state only after `_get_teacache_context()` returns: ```python ctx = self._get_teacache_context() ... self.is_cfg_negative = ctx.is_cfg_negative ``` Current source: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ace7314173c8221ecf5f213575302eab98f4e84f/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/wanvideo.py For serial CFG, the sequence is therefore: ```text positive timestep 0 self.is_cfg_negative == False reset positive forward completes cnt becomes 1 negative timestep 0 self.is_cfg_negative is still False when context is built reset again cnt becomes 0 self.is_cfg_negative is then changed to True ``` This appears to explain the existing observation in #24227. That PR reports that at denoising timestep 5 the positive branch sees `cnt=9` while the negative branch sees `cnt=10`, even though both branches should already be inside the same configured skip window. #24227 currently treats this as a boundary indexing problem. My reading is that the counter is one behind because the negative CFG call at timestep 0 reset the state a second time. For CFG parallel, `run_two_branch_cfg_parallel()` executes only the branch owned by the local CFG rank: ```python cfg_rank = get_classifier_free_guidance_rank() pred_t = _run(predict_fn, cfg_rank, policy.branches) ``` That creates a second failure mode on the negative rank: ```text request A, negative rank timestep 0 starts with self.is_cfg_negative=False reset happens ... request finishes with self.is_cfg_negative=True request B, same negative rank timestep 0 self.is_cfg_negative=True reset condition is false previous request state survives ``` Finally, TeaCache currently converts timestep boundaries into forward-call boundaries solely from `do_cfg`: ```python if do_cfg: start_skipping *= 2 end_skipping *= 2 ``` Current source: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ace7314173c8221ecf5f213575302eab98f4e84f/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/sample/teacache.py For serial CFG, two local forwards correspond to one diffusion timestep. For CFG parallel, each rank executes one local forward per timestep, so the doubling no longer represents the local execution topology. ### Reproduction This can be reproduced as a CPU-only state-machine test with no model weights or GPU. The script loads the TeaCache implementation directly from the checked out upstream source tree. ```bash python - <<'PY' import importlib.util import sys from pathlib import Path from types import SimpleNamespace import torch path = Path("python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/cache/teacache.py") name = "teacache_direct" spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path) mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) sys.modules[name] = mod spec.loader.exec_module(mod) class DummyTeaCache(mod.TeaCacheMixin): prefix = "wan" cache = DummyTeaCache() cache._init_teacache_state() params = SimpleNamespace( teacache_thresh=0.1, get_coefficients=lambda: [1.0], ) batch = SimpleNamespace( enable_teacache=True, teacache_params=params, num_inference_steps=50, do_classifier_free_guidance=True, is_cfg_negative=False, ) forward_context = SimpleNamespace( current_timestep=0, forward_batch=batch, ) fc_name = "sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers.forward_context" fc_mod = type(sys)(fc_name) fc_mod.get_forward_context = lambda: forward_context sys.modules[fc_name] = fc_mod print("=== Case 1: serial CFG timestep-0 double reset ===") cache._get_teacache_context() cache.cnt = 1 cache.is_cfg_negative = False print("after positive forward, cnt:", cache.cnt) batch.is_cfg_negative = True cache._get_teacache_context() print("before negative forward, cnt:", cache.cnt) print("expected cnt:", 1) print("double reset reproduced:", cache.cnt == 0) print() print("=== Case 2: CFG-parallel negative rank next-request reset ===") cache.cnt = 50 cache.is_cfg_negative = True cache.previous_modulated_input_negative = torch.tensor([123.0]) cache.previous_residual_negative = torch.tensor([456.0]) cache.accumulated_rel_l1_distance_negative = 7.0 batch.is_cfg_negative = True forward_context.current_timestep = 0 cache._get_teacache_context() print("cnt after next request starts:", cache.cnt) print( "previous negative input cleared:", cache.previous_modulated_input_negative is None, ) print( "previous negative residual cleared:", cache.previous_residual_negative is None, ) print( "negative accumulator:", cache.accumulated_rel_l1_distance_negative, ) print("expected cnt:", 0) print("expected negative state cleared: True") PY ``` Observed output on current upstream `main`: ```text === Case 1: serial CFG timestep-0 double reset === after positive forward, cnt: 1 before negative forward, cnt: 0 expected cnt: 1 double reset reproduced: True === Case 2: CFG-parallel negative rank next-request reset === cnt after next request starts: 50 previous negative input cleared: False previous negative residual cleared: False negative accumulator: 7.0 expected cnt: 0 expected negative state cleared: True ``` ## Expected behavior TeaCache request state should be fresh at the beginning of every generation regardless of whether CFG branches execute serially on one model instance or are distributed across CFG-parallel ranks. For models that maintain separate positive and negative cache state, each active branch should have well-defined request-start initialization independent of the previous value of a mutable branch flag. Skip-window semantics should also remain expressed in diffusion timesteps, or otherwise account for the actual local CFG execution topology, rather than assuming that `do_cfg=True` always means two local forwards per timestep. ## Related work #24227 reports the serial Wan TeaCache off-by-one symptom. I think the timestep-0 double reset above may be the underlying reason its counter is one forward behind. The arithmetic adjustment proposed there appears to compensate for the shifted counter but would not address CFG-parallel request isolation. #21613 is also relevant. Its move toward independent `TeaCacheState` objects and timestep-based boundaries looks directionally aligned with this issue. However, the current branch still initializes cache state only from the positive CFG timestep-0 call, so the CFG-parallel negative rank appears to need explicit lifecycle handling as well. I am happy to work on a focused fix and CPU regression tests. I would appreciate maintainer guidance on whether the preferred direction is a narrow lifecycle fix on the current implementation or to address this as part of #21613. ### Environment Current code inspected and reproduced against: ```text SGLang main commit: ace7314173c8221ecf5f213575302eab98f4e84f No model weights or accelerator are required for the minimal state-machine reproduction above. OS: Ubuntu Linux, aarch64 Python: 3.12.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 torch.cuda.is_available(): False The reproduction is intentionally CPU-only. The cache module was loaded directly from the checked-out upstream source with `importlib`, because this test exercises Python state transitions and does not require model weights, CUDA kernels, or a full SGLang server installation. ``` cc @DefTruth

signal.title: [Bug][Diffusion] Spectrum CFG parallel skips negative-branch initialization and can reuse forecaster state across requests
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug rum maintains independent state for positive and negative CFG branches on models such as Wan, but generation-start reset is owned exclusively by the positive CFG call: ```python if ctx.current_step == 0 and not ctx.is_cfg_negative: self.reset_spectrum_state(ctx.spectrum_params) ``` This works when both CFG branches execute serially on the same model instance. It does not hold with CFG parallel, where one rank executes only the positive branch and another rank executes only the negative branch. On the negative CFG rank I see two lifecycle problems by inspection and with the state-machine reproduction below: 1. The first request never calls `reset_spectrum_state()`. The negative branch's initial `spectrum_curr_ws_negative` therefore remains `None`, and `_get_spectrum_branch_state()` converts it to `0.0` instead of the configured `window_size`. 2. At end of generation, the counter/window state wraps but the branch forecaster is not cleared. Because the next request on the negative rank again has no positive timestep-0 call, the previous request's forecaster can remain visible to the new request. This is on current main at: `ace7314173c8221ecf5f213575302eab98f4e84f` Spectrum was merged after the v0.5.17 release line diverged, so v0.5.17 does not contain this feature. ### Root cause Spectrum explicitly supports separate CFG branch state: ```python self.spectrum_cnt_negative = 0 self.spectrum_curr_ws_negative = None self.spectrum_forecaster_negative = None ``` A full reset initializes that state correctly: ```python self.spectrum_curr_ws_negative = spectrum_params.window_size self.spectrum_forecaster_negative = None ``` But `begin_spectrum_step()` performs the reset only from the positive branch: ```python if ctx.current_step == 0 and not ctx.is_cfg_negative: self.reset_spectrum_state(ctx.spectrum_params) ``` Current source: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ace7314173c8221ecf5f213575302eab98f4e84f/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/cache/spectrum.py The code comment explains the assumption: the positive call resets both CFG branches so that a following serial negative call does not reset a second time. That is correct for serial CFG, but CFG parallel changes branch ownership. `run_two_branch_cfg_parallel()` chooses the local branch from the CFG rank: ```python cfg_rank = get_classifier_free_guidance_rank() pred_t = _run(predict_fn, cfg_rank, policy.branches) ``` Therefore the negative rank never executes the positive branch that owns Spectrum initialization. There is also an internal consistency clue in `SpectrumParams`: `get_total_forward_steps()` already knows that separate CFG branch counters see only `num_inference_steps` calls each, rather than `2 * num_inference_steps`. The lifecycle reset still assumes both branches execute on one model instance. At the end of a run `begin_spectrum_step()` wraps: ```python if cnt >= total_steps: cnt = 0 consecutive = 0 curr_ws = params.window_size ``` but this does not clear the active branch's forecaster. The nearby comment says the wrap prevents state from leaking when the module is reused, but forecaster state can remain live on a CFG-parallel negative rank. ### Reproduction This can be reproduced as a CPU-only state-machine test with no model weights or GPU. The script loads the Spectrum implementation directly from the checked out upstream source tree. ```bash python - <<'PY' import importlib.util import sys from pathlib import Path import torch path = Path("python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/cache/spectrum.py") name = "spectrum_direct" spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path) mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) sys.modules[name] = mod spec.loader.exec_module(mod) class DummySpectrum(mod.SpectrumMixin): prefix = "wan" class Params: window_size = 2.0 flex_window = 0.75 warmup_steps = 5 history_size = 20 m = 2 lam = 0.1 tau_num_steps = 50 taylor_order = 1 w = 1.0 params = Params() def negative_ctx(step=0, total_steps=50): return mod.SpectrumContext( current_step=step, num_inference_steps=total_steps, total_forward_steps=total_steps, do_cfg=True, is_cfg_negative=True, spectrum_params=params, debug=False, ) print("=== Case 1: CFG-parallel negative rank first-request initialization ===") model = DummySpectrum() model._init_spectrum_state() model._get_spectrum_context = lambda: negative_ctx(step=0, total_steps=50) print("before first negative step:") print(" curr_ws_negative:", model.spectrum_curr_ws_negative) print(" forecaster_negative:", model.spectrum_forecaster_negative) model.begin_spectrum_step() print("after first negative step:") print(" curr_ws_negative:", model.spectrum_curr_ws_negative) print(" cnt_negative:", model.spectrum_cnt_negative) print("expected starting window:", params.window_size) print( "first-request initialization bug reproduced:", model.spectrum_curr_ws_negative != params.window_size, ) print() print("=== Case 2: forecaster survives into next request ===") model = DummySpectrum() model._init_spectrum_state() ctx_a = negative_ctx(step=0, total_steps=1) model._get_spectrum_context = lambda: ctx_a assert model.begin_spectrum_step() model.spectrum_record_features(torch.ones(2, 3)) request_a_forecaster = model.spectrum_forecaster_negative print("after request A:") print(" cnt_negative:", model.spectrum_cnt_negative) print(" curr_ws_negative:", model.spectrum_curr_ws_negative) print(" forecaster exists:", request_a_forecaster is not None) ctx_b = negative_ctx(step=0, total_steps=1) model._get_spectrum_context = lambda: ctx_b model.begin_spectrum_step() print("at request B start:") print(" cnt_negative:", model.spectrum_cnt_negative) print( " same forecaster object:", model.spectrum_forecaster_negative is request_a_forecaster, ) print("expected fresh forecaster: False") print( "cross-request forecaster reuse reproduced:", model.spectrum_forecaster_negative is request_a_forecaster, ) PY ``` Observed output on current upstream `main`: ```text === Case 1: CFG-parallel negative rank first-request initialization === before first negative step: curr_ws_negative: None forecaster_negative: None after first negative step: curr_ws_negative: 0.0 cnt_negative: 1 expected starting window: 2.0 first-request initialization bug reproduced: True === Case 2: forecaster survives into next request === after request A: cnt_negative: 0 curr_ws_negative: 2.0 forecaster exists: True at request B start: cnt_negative: 0 same forecaster object: True expected fresh forecaster: False cross-request forecaster reuse reproduced: True ## Expected behavior A CFG-parallel rank should initialize the Spectrum state for the branch it owns at the beginning of every generation. For a new request on the negative rank: ```text negative counter = 0 negative window = configured window_size negative forecaster = None negative statistics = fresh ``` No feature history from a previous request should be visible to the next request. This should hold independently of whether positive and negative CFG branches are executed serially on one model instance or on different CFG-parallel ranks. ## Possible direction The current positive-branch-owned reset is useful for preventing a double reset in serial CFG, so simply removing the branch check would reintroduce that problem. A cleaner invariant may be to reset only the state for the branch executing at timestep 0, rather than having the positive branch reset both branches. For example, a branch-local reset would allow: ```text serial CFG: positive t0 -> reset positive state negative t0 -> reset negative state CFG parallel: positive rank t0 -> reset positive state negative rank t0 -> reset negative state ``` Another option would be explicit generation/request identity if that is already available at this layer. I am happy to implement whichever lifecycle model the maintainers prefer and add CPU-only regression coverage for serial CFG and CFG parallel. ## Version scope Spectrum was introduced by #31491 and is present on current `main`. I confirmed that v0.5.17 does not contain `runtime/cache/spectrum.py`, so this is a current-main/nightly bug rather than a v0.5.17 regression. ### Environment Current code inspected and reproduced against: ```text SGLang main commit: ace7314173c8221ecf5f213575302eab98f4e84f No model weights or accelerator are required for the minimal state-machine reproduction above. OS: Ubuntu Linux, aarch64 Python: 3.12.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 torch.cuda.is_available(): False The reproduction is intentionally CPU-only. The cache module was loaded directly from the checked-out upstream source with `importlib`, because this test exercises Python state transitions and does not require model weights, CUDA kernels, or a full SGLang server installation. ``` cc @DefTruth

signal.title: fix(logprobs): guard tolist on mixed token-ids/top logprobs batches (#34719)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #34719. When a request that asks for token-ids logprobs (`token_ids_logprob`) shares a batch with a request that does not, the scheduler process dies with: ``` AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'tolist' ``` One scoring client can take the whole server down. ## Root cause `get_token_ids_logprobs_raw` / `get_top_logprobs_raw` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/logprob_processor.py`) build per-request lists whose entries are **heterogeneous**: - a request that asked for the logprobs contributes a device **tensor** (`vals.append(row ...)`, e.g. L151/L172); - a co-batched request that did **not** contributes a bare **`[]`** (L144-145, L159-165). Both consumers in `batch_result_processor.py` — `move_logprobs_to_cpu` (prefill) and `_normalize_decode_outputs` (decode) — then call `.tolist()` unconditionally on every entry: ```python logits_output.next_token_token_ids_logprobs_val = [ v.tolist() for v in logits_output.next_token_token_ids_logprobs_val ] ``` The plain-`[]` entries have no `.tolist()`, so the whole batch crashes. When every request in the batch asks for the logprobs the entries are all tensors and the bug is hidden — it only surfaces on mixed batches. `next_token_top_logprobs_val` / `next_token_top_logprobs_idx` carry the identical latent pattern at both sites. ## Fix Guard each entry with `torch.is_tensor` before converting, matching the style already used for `embeddings` a few lines above (`[tensor.tolist() for tensor in embeddings]`). Tensor entries convert exactly as before; plain-list entries pass through unchanged — no behavior change for the all-requesting case. ## Verification Standalone reproduction of the comprehension confirms the old code raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'tolist'` on a mixed `[tensor, []]` list, while the guarded version returns `[[...], []]` and leaves the all-tensor case byte-identical. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31966715761](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31966715761)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31966715537](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31966715537)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [PD] Deferred decode-side KV release for aborts mid-transfer
signal.text: ## Motivation Aborting a decode request (long-ITL abort/timeout, `/abort_request`) while its prefill→decode KV transfer is still in flight frees the request's KV pages and req-pool slot **immediately**, but does **not** cancel the transfer. The next request can then be allocated those same pages and have them overwritten by the earlier, still-in-flight write — the next request silently holds the first request's KV, with no error raised anywhere. This is the race [@ShangmingCai anticipated in #27372](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27372) ("we could introduce deferred release of decode-side KVCache to fix this"), the open bug in #32564, and the reason the `ABORT_ACK` handler in `mooncake/conn.py` carries a `TODO(shangming)` for exactly this mechanism. It is also why an O(1) tail-pop free-slot change like #34876 is unsafe on the decode side today: LIFO reuse maximally shrinks the free→reuse window and maximizes the probability of hitting this race. This PR is the prerequisite that makes immediate slot reuse safe. ## What this does An **env-gated deferred-release path**. When off (default) there is **zero behavior/perf change** — every new branch is behind an `enable_deferred_*` guard, and the wire format / free path are byte-identical. When on, an aborted request's KV pages, req-slot and metadata buffer are **held** until the prefill proves its transfer drained, then released. **Prefill (`mooncake/conn.py`).** On an `ABORT` for an active room, mark the room `Failed` **first** (stops `add_transfer_request` from enqueuing new chunks), then register the ack target, and do **not** ack from the bootstrap thread. The single transfer worker that owns the room sends the `ABORT_ACK` — carrying its prefill rank — once the room's in-flight chunk has drained (at both the skip and completion sites, via `_maybe_ack_drained_abort`). Rooms already done/unknown ack immediately. **Decode (`decode.py` + `common/conn.py`).** On the `Failed` poll (for a decode-initiated abort), instead of releasing, move the request to a held list with a deadline. `resolve_deferred_releases()` (called early every scheduler step) releases a room once **every prefill rank the abort was sent to** has acked (`is_abort_release_safe`) or the timeout fires. The per-room ack tracker is armed in `abort_request` when the `ABORT` is sent, so acks that arrive during the next forward step are captured. ### Why it's correct - **Single-writer per room.** A room's chunks shard to one transfer queue served by exactly one worker thread (`session_port_sum % len(transfer_queues)`, one thread per queue), so a room's writes and its `_staging_outstanding` counter are single-writer. The ack is driven **entirely from that worker**, never the bootstrap thread, so it can't race an in-flight write. No new locks. - **Dummy-proof denominator.** The decode requires an ack from **each** prefill rank it notified (`len(bootstrap_infos)`), not `required_prefill_response_num`. Every notified rank acks exactly once — real ranks after their write drains, dummy/already-done ranks immediately — so reaching the count provably means no prefill can still be writing to those pages. Over/under-counting from dummy ranks (which would cause early release = corruption) is impossible. - **Timeout backstop.** If an ack never arrives (dead prefill rank, stuck send), the pages are force-released after the timeout — matching the ~30s mooncake transfer ceiling noted in #27372. ### Coverage / fallback (honest scope) The fast (ack-driven) release fires for the primary corruption scenario — an abort while the transfer is actively in flight on the notified ranks. Cases where a rank already concluded before the abort fall back to the timeout hold (safe, never an early release). This is a deliberately lighter alternative to the full lease/barrier rework in #32564; it reuses the existing `ABORT`/`ABORT_ACK` channel and changes only *when* the ack is sent and *when* decode releases. ## Env - `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE` (bool, default `False`) - `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE_TIMEOUT` (float seconds, default `30.0`) ## Tests `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_deferred_decode_kv_release.py`: - ack aggregation: release-safe only after all required ranks ack; duplicate-rank ack does not over-count; single-rank fast path; state cleared. - `resolve_deferred_releases`: holds until drained then releases exactly once (frees metadata idx, resets `bootstrap_room`, clears deferred state, nulls receiver); releases on timeout without ack; no-op when nothing deferred. ## Validation status ⚠️ **Draft — pending PD-cluster integration validation.** The unit-tested decode-side state machine and the correctness argument above are done, but I have not yet run this on a live prefill/decode Mooncake deployment (e.g. the 2P1D H200 setup #32564 used, with in-flight-donor-abort victim-reuse probes). Marking draft until that passes. ## Checklist - [x] Format with pre-commit (black/isort) - [x] Add unit tests - [ ] Provide accuracy/speed benchmark results (N/A — abort-path correctness change; no kernel/throughput impact when off) - [x] Code style Related: #27372, #32564, #34876 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Self-review hardening (2nd commit) An adversarial multi-agent review of the first commit surfaced and fixed several real issues: - **Corruption (prefill ordering):** mark the room `Failed` **before** registering the ack target — the reverse order let the worker drain + ACK while the room wasn't yet `Failed`, so a newly-enqueued chunk could still write to already-freed decode pages. - **Corruption (room-reuse pollution):** `bootstrap_room` is not globally unique; a stale/late ACK could satisfy a later request reusing the room and release it early. The ack tracker is now armed/reset per abort episode (in `abort_request` when the ABORT is sent) and drops acks for unregistered rooms. - **Functionality (ack timing):** arming the tracker at defer-time lost almost every ACK (a full forward step runs between `abort()` and deferral), degrading every fast release to a timeout. Now armed when the ABORT is sent. - **Leak/functional (resolve reachability):** `resolve_deferred_releases` now runs early and unconditionally (was behind the retraction early-return and the polling gate; and independent of `release_rids` in the PP path), so held slots still time out under memory pressure. - **Corruption/cascade (resolve):** commit the surviving set before releasing and isolate a failing `_do_release`, so one error can't double-free a metadata idx or brick the decode loop. - Only decode-initiated aborts are deferred (`abort_notified`); prefill-initiated failures release immediately. Added regression tests for reuse-pollution, ack-before-register drop, and release-exception isolation. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31966529943](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31966529943)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31966529628](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31966529628)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Pack device-pointer tables as uint64 to avoid 64-bit address overflow
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35047. Several kernels pass base addresses to the device in a side table and bitcast each entry back to a pointer (`tl.load(meta_ptr + i).to(tl.pointer_type(...))` in Triton, `reinterpret_cast` in the host-side `gemm_ar` op). Those tables were built with `dtype=torch.int64`, which cannot hold an address `>= 2**63`: `torch.tensor()` unpacks Python ints through `long long`, so the build raises ``` ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long ``` on the host, before any kernel is launched. Intel XPU (Level Zero / SYCL USM) device addresses have the top bit set, e.g. `0xffff85abd4e00000`, so every Mamba/GDN model hits this in conv-state scatter and `MambaPool` slot maintenance. CUDA/HIP VAs stay in the low canonical half, which is the only reason `int64` looks lossless there. ## Modifications - New `sglang.kernels.ops.memory.ptr_table.make_ptr_table(rows, device)`: builds the table as `uint64` (the only dtype that accepts a full 64-bit address) and `view`s it back to `int64`. `view` moves no bits, so kernels and C++ ops keep their existing signed element type — no kernel-side change, and `gemm_ar.cuh::set_bases`' `with_dtype<int64_t>()` check still holds. Companion columns (strides, element counts, block offsets) are non-negative, so their bits are unchanged too. - Route the three table builders through it: `_conv_multi_build_meta` (`mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`), `build_conv_slot_descriptor` (`mem_cache/mamba_slot_fused.py`), and `gemm_ar.init`'s `uc_bases`. ## Tests - `test/registered/kernels/ops/memory/test_ptr_table.py` (new, CPU suite): covers the full `[0, 2**64)` address range, and asserts both call sites' tables round-trip a spoofed top-bit-set `data_ptr()` while leaving companion columns identical to a real-address build. It spoofs the address because a backend whose VAs stay `< 2**47` can never catch this regression — the guard has to run on any runner. - `test/registered/layers/mamba/test_mamba_slot_fused.py` and `test/registered/unit/layers/test_mamba_state_scatter_triton.py` now select the accelerator via `get_device()` instead of hardcoding CUDA, and register on the XPU suite. Added coverage for `fused_conv_window_scatter_multi` (single-type, multi-type, and with the second/track index set), which had no test on any backend and is the kernel most exposed to the packing. Verified on 8x Intel Arc Pro B60 (torch 2.12.0+xpu): the new cases fail with the reported `ValueError` when `make_ptr_table` is reverted to `int64`, and all 15 pass with the fix (2 CUDA-only skips). `isort`/`black`/`ruff` and the repo's registered-test lint checks are clean. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31965816187](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31965816187)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31965815971](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31965815971)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] Triton device-pointer tables use int64 and overflow on Intel XPU USM addresses
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] Written in English. ### Describe the bug Several Triton kernels build a device-pointer table by packing `Tensor.data_ptr()` values into a `dtype=torch.int64` tensor. On Intel XPU, Level Zero / SYCL USM device addresses have the top bit set (`>= 2**63`), so the pointer is not representable as a signed `int64`. `torch.tensor()` unpacks Python ints through `long long`, so it raises on the host before the kernel is ever launched: ``` ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long ``` This is **not** a Triton or driver bug. The in-kernel bitcast `tl.load(meta_ptr + i).to(tl.pointer_type(...))` works correctly once the value reaches the device — I verified this on XPU with both `uint64` and two's-complement `int64` pointer tables. The defect is purely the host-side `int64` packing step. Same root cause as pytorch/pytorch#191458 (`uint64` overflow, "reproduced on CPU, CUDA, XPU", fixed by pytorch/pytorch#191604) and pytorch/pytorch#157728 (still open). CUDA and HIP device VAs stay in the low canonical half (`< 2**47`), so `int64` packing is accidentally lossless there and the bug is invisible on NVIDIA/AMD. **The repo is already inconsistent about the dtype.** These sites are correct today because they use `torch.uint64`: - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_lora_kernel.py:34` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:2021-2032` These sites use `torch.int64` and therefore break on XPU: - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/mamba/mamba_state_scatter_triton.py` — `_conv_multi_build_meta`, the multi-type conv-window scatter meta table - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/mamba_slot_fused.py:117` — `ConvSlotDescriptor.ptr` - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/kimi_k3/gemm_ar.py:131` — `uc_bases` (not XPU-reachable today, but the same pattern) In practice this is hit by any Mamba/GDN model on XPU: conv-state scatter on the speculative-decoding verify path, and `fused_clear_conv_slots` / `MambaPool` slot maintenance. **Why CI does not catch it.** `test/registered/unit/layers/test_mamba_state_scatter_triton.py` and `test/registered/layers/mamba/test_mamba_slot_fused.py` are gated on `@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), ...)` and hardcode `device = torch.device("cuda")`, so the pointer-table path never executes on a non-CUDA backend. ### Reproduction Minimal, no model download required. On an Intel XPU host: ```python import torch from sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.mamba_state_scatter_triton import _conv_multi_build_meta dev = "xpu" L, B, D, C = 2, 4, 3, 8 pairs = [] for elems in (128, 64): dst = torch.zeros((L, C, 1, elems), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev) src = torch.zeros((L, B, D, 1, elems), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev) pairs.append((dst, src)) print([hex(d.data_ptr()) for d, _ in pairs]) _conv_multi_build_meta(pairs, block_size=64) ``` Output: ``` ['0xffff85abd4e00000', '0xffff85abd4e02800'] # both >= 2**63 ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long ``` The second site fails the same way: ```python import torch from sglang.srt.mem_cache.mamba_slot_fused import build_conv_slot_descriptor t = [torch.randn((2, 16, 4, 8), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="xpu")] build_conv_slot_descriptor(t) # ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long ``` And the underlying `torch` behaviour, for reference: ``` value uint64 ctor int64 ctor uint64 setitem 9223372036854775807 OK OK OK 9223372036854775808 OK ValueError ValueError 18446744073709551615 OK ValueError ValueError ``` ### Proposed common fix Standardize pointer tables on unsigned construction, then bit-reinterpret when the kernel wants a signed index type. One line, no per-backend branch, identical behaviour on CUDA/HIP/XPU: ```python # Build unsigned: XPU USM addresses exceed int64 max. view() keeps the bits. meta = torch.tensor(rows, dtype=torch.uint64, device=device).view(torch.int64) ``` `.view(torch.int64)` is a pure bit reinterpret, so the two's-complement value it yields bitcasts back to the original address inside the kernel, and non-pointer columns (strides, element counts) are unaffected because they are all non-negative. No kernel-side change is needed. Verified on `torch 2.12.0+xpu`: pointer and stride columns round-trip exactly, and `fused_clear_conv_slots` now runs correctly on XPU (cleared slots zeroed, untouched slots preserved). Suggested scope: 1. Convert the three `int64` sites listed above. 2. Add a lint check or a shared `make_ptr_tensor()` helper so new pointer tables cannot regress to `int64`. 3. Relax the two Mamba tests off `torch.cuda.is_available()` to a device-agnostic fixture, so non-CUDA backends actually exercise the path. Happy to send the PR for (1) and (3). ### Prior art vLLM hit the identical bug in the identical subsystem and is standardizing on `torch.uint64`: - vllm-project/vllm#50552 — "[Bugfix][XPU] Fix Mamba state pointer overflow" - vllm-project/vllm#49532 (open) — "Some XPU USM device pointers have the top bit set (value >= 2**63)" - vllm-project/vllm#50834 (open RFC) — "Unify the Tensor Type for Device-Pointer Storage to `torch.uint64`", plus vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels#505 PyTorch side: pytorch/pytorch#191458 (fixed), pytorch/pytorch#157728 (open), pytorch/pytorch#159168. Related SGLang tracker: #24922 (Intel XPU enablement). ### Environment ``` Python : 3.12.13 / Linux-6.14.0-37-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.41 torch : 2.12.0+xpu XPU available : True XPU count : 8 XPU 0 : Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics driver : 1.14.36300+8 total mem : 22.7 GiB transformers : 5.12.1 sglang : 0.5.18.dev536+gf2c84de02 (main @ f2c84de022) ```

signal.title: [DSv4] Integrate TRT-LLM DSv4 Attention for SM100/103
signal.text: ## Motivation Integrates TRT-LLM attention kernel for DSv4 style attention (CSA, HCA). ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests ``` SGLANG_DSV4_ATTN_DECODE_BACKEND=flashmla/trtllm_gen \ python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --mem-fraction-static 0.88 --max-running-requests 32 ``` ### GSM8K Accuracy GSM8K V4-Pro flashmla: 0.965 GSM8K V4-Pro trtllm_gen: 0.985 ### GPQA (add --chat-template to above server command) ``` python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 21000 --eval-name gpqa \ --num-examples 198 --max-tokens 120000 --repeat 8 \ --thinking-mode deepseek-v3 ``` FlashMLA: Repeat: 8, mean: 0.885 Scores: ['0.889', '0.879', '0.889', '0.879', '0.869', '0.899', '0.904', '0.874'] TRTLLM: Repeat: 8, mean: 0.907 Scores: ['0.919', '0.904', '0.894', '0.904', '0.909', '0.919', '0.904', '0.904'] ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Unit Kernel Benchmarking (ran with private benchmarking repo): ``` # prefill (varlen), long contexts python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode prefill --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 1,2 --seq-lens 4096,16384,65536 --graph # decode, low/mid concurrency x long contexts python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode decode --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 1,4,16,64 --seq-lens 1024,4096,16384,65536,131072 --graph # decode, high concurrency python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode decode --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 128,256,512,1024 --seq-lens 256,1024,4096,16384 --graph ``` Prefill: ~1.2x faster Decode: ~1.45x faster The performance for TP > 1 scales better on trtllm-gen, since it seems the flashmla variant requires padding the head_dim to 64 or 128. I've attached some sample graphs showing the kernel perf comparison. ### E2E bench-serving ```bash python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 21000 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 128 \ --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 4 ``` flashmla: ``` Benchmark duration (s): 59.92 Total input tokens: 1048576 Input token throughput (tok/s): 17500.55 Mean E2E Latency (ms): 29950.67 Mean TTFT (ms): 19009.87 (median 19636.34) Mean TPOT (ms): 86.15 Median ITL (ms): 12.12 ``` trtllm_gen: ``` Benchmark duration (s): 60.09 Total input tokens: 1048576 Input token throughput (tok/s): 17448.78 Mean E2E Latency (ms): 30039.27 Mean TTFT (ms): 16808.71 (median 15734.66) Mean TPOT (ms): 104.18 Median ITL (ms): 13.11 ``` ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31906402816](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31906402816) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31906402709](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31906402709)

signal.title: [Bug]
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug **Describe the bug** When running SGLang with `--enable-dp-attention` and `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang` on AMD MI355X (ROCm v0.5.16), the server hangs indefinitely during prefill. No error or traceback is produced — the process simply stalls. The same hang was observed on v0.5.14 (not a regression). **Additional context** The hang does **not** occur without `--enable-dp-attention` — `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang` works fine in non-DP mode. This suggests the issue is in the tilelang collective path that gets activated under DP-Attention (likely a distributed collective op that never returns on ROCm). The tilelang maintainer is aware and suggested filing here. We also observed that a **disaggregated prefill/decode** setup (2 nodes, prefill with `--enable-dp-attention`, decode without) completed successfully using image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260729`. We checked the SGLang commit log between `20260728` and `20260729` and found no changes related to tilelang or DP-Attention, so the success is likely due to the disaggregated topology rather than an image fix. Our hypothesis is that in a combined prefill+decode server, the tilelang DP collective deadlocks because some DP ranks are occupied with decode operations when the prefill collective fires. In the disaggregated setup, the prefill node is exclusively dedicated to prefill — all 8 GPUs are always available for the collective, so it completes normally. This suggests the root cause may be in the **scheduling overlap between decode and the DP-Attention prefill collective** on a combined server, rather than in the tilelang collective primitive itself. Workaround: disable DP-Attention entirely. ### Reproduction **To reproduce** ```bash # Env vars required for DP-Attention on ROCm (from the dsv4 green config): export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 export SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1 export GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <glm5.2-fp4> \ --tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \ --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --trust-remote-code # Server starts fine, then hangs indefinitely on the first long-context prefill. # No error, no traceback — silent stall. ``` ### Environment **Environment** | | | |---|---| | SGLang image | `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260728` | | Hardware | AMD MI355X × 8 | | Model | GLM-5.2 MXFP4 | | TP / DP | `--tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention` | | KV cache dtype | `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` | | DSA prefill backend | `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang` (default) | | DSA decode backend | `--dsa-decode-backend tilelang` |

signal.title: [Diffusion] Reuse SRT Qwen vision and text modules
signal.text: ## Motivation The multimodal generation Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3, and Qwen3-VL encoders duplicated pure modules already implemented in SRT. Maintaining both copies also left the MMGen paths without reusable SRT tensor-parallel projections, embeddings, activation kernels, and checkpoint loaders. ## Modifications - Reuse SRT Qwen vision patch embeddings, MLPs, patch mergers, RMSNorm, and tensor-parallel linear layers from MMGen. - Reuse SRT Qwen2.5 text projections, split `Qwen2_5_VLMLP`, HF-semantics `RMSNorm`, and `VocabParallelEmbedding`. - Reuse SRT `SiluAndMul` and `RMSNorm` in the native Qwen3 and Qwen3-VL text paths. - Extend SRT RMSNorm kernels to flatten and restore higher-rank activations when a residual is present. This is required by diffusion text encoders with `[batch, sequence, hidden]` states. - Keep the Qwen2.5 split gate/up execution order as `act(gate) * up`; this avoids a concatenation and preserves HF numerical behavior. - Use replicated SRT linears at TP=1 and explicit TP rank/size at TP>1, while retaining the existing replicated fallback when a dimension is not TP-divisible. - Share one MMGen packed-sequence attention adapter between Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL. It remains MMGen-owned because diffusion backend selection and segmented SDPA fallback differ from SRT serving's attention contract. - Reuse SRT MRoPE in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL text attention. Keep MMGen LocalAttention and Qwen3-VL quantized linears because their diffusion runtime and quantization contracts differ from SRT serving. - Map MiniMax-H3 checkpoint `.attn.qkv.` names to the native SRT `.attn.qkv_proj.` parameters. - Keep `model.visual.blocks` and language-model layer ownership unchanged so layerwise offload and FSDP selection continue to work. - Bind each native encoder root to the TP group used to construct and shard it. One nested context now switches MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP together for construction, loading, and forward, then restores their previous values independently. ## Accuracy and Integration Tests Latest validation on H100 at exact head `0844a9a3088f3`: - Focused Qwen, encoder-folding, and group-lifecycle unit tests: `55 passed`. - The new two-GPU no-download guard uses a real SRT `RowParallelLinear` with DiT TP=1 and folded encoder TP=2. Its output matches the complete unsharded linear reference, and MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP all restore to size 1 after forward (`1 passed`, 24.63s). - Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL SRT MRoPE versus Transformers: FP32 maximum absolute error `2.38e-7`; BF16 maximum absolute error `0.015625` (1-2 ULP), with mean absolute error between `1.8e-4` and `4.0e-4`. - Qwen2.5-VL/Qwen3-VL batched GQA layout, three-axis positions, Transformers v5 RoPE config, and attention wiring are covered by focused tests. The full native server/pipeline encoder `fold` versus `replicate` e2e guard is in #35004. On its pre-fix runtime negative control it fails with SSIM `0.924886` and MAD `5.275228`; after the shared group fix it passes with SSIM `0.994886` and MAD `0.771159`. No consistency GT or threshold was changed. signal.title: fix(attention): convert flashinfer base-2 LSE to natural log in chunked-prefix MLA merge
signal.text: ## Motivation `FlashInferMhaChunkKVRunner.forward` feeds the per-layer LSE of MLA chunked-prefix attention into `sgl_kernel.merge_state_v2`. FlashInfer's `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper.forward_return_lse` returns the LSE in base 2 (`log2(sum(exp2(x)))`; this is flashinfer's documented internal convention, see flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2113). `merge_state_v2` computes the merge weights with the natural-log convention (`exp(lse)`). Feeding base-2 LSE into a base-e merge weights the two attention states incorrectly. Measured effect of the mismatch (unit-level, chunked-prefix merge of an extend state and a prefix-chunk state vs an fp32 torch-native single-pass reference): max |error| = 0.105 at prefix length 4096. After converting base-2 to natural log at the runner boundary: max |error| = 0.0005. Affected configurations: MLA models with the flashinfer attention backend, on extend batches that take the chunked-prefix path (`sum(extend_prefix_lens) >= SGLANG_CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_THRESHOLD`, default 8192, i.e. above one-shot chunk capacity). The models routed through this merge are the users of `DeepseekMHAForwardMixin` / `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA`: `deepseek_v2.py` (DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1/V3.1, and the DSA variant — `_chunked_prefix_attn_mha` merges with `merge_state_v2` on the DSA path too), `deepseek_nextn.py`, `bailing_moe_v3.py`, `glm4_moe_lite.py`, and `sarvam_moe.py`. `deepseek_v4.py` is not affected (own MQA/sparse attention stack; no LSE state merge). The FA3 backend path is not affected: FA3 returns natural-log LSE, and its `merge_state_v2` call sites in `flashattention_backend.py` are consistent. The fallback `merge_state_triton` is also natural-log (`tl.exp`/`tl.log`), so both merge implementations share the convention flashinfer violates. vLLM avoids this class of bug with explicit per-backend `lse_base_on_e` flags. Related: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4547 adds an opt-in `return_lse_base_on_e` to the ragged wrapper. When that lands, this conversion can be replaced by passing `return_lse_base_on_e=True` at the two wrapper call sites. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_mla_backend.py` (+7 lines): in `FlashInferMhaChunkKVRunner.forward`, when the call returns an LSE (`forward_batch.mha_return_lse` or `forward_batch.attn_attend_prefix_cache`), multiply the wrapper's LSE by `ln(2)` before returning, converting base-2 LSE to natural-log LSE for the downstream `merge_state_v2` merge. No other path is changed; non-chunked prefill and decode are untouched. ## Accuracy Tests Unit-level (standalone repro driving the actual cutlass ragged wrappers and `sgl_kernel.merge_state_v2` on an NVIDIA B300): - Full-sequence ragged call vs fp32 torch-native attention: 0.0003 max error. - Chunked merge with the raw base-2 LSE: 0.105 max error vs fp32 reference (prefix=4096). - Chunked merge with the natural-log conversion applied: 0.0005 max error vs fp32 reference. Serving-level, validated on the BailingMoeV3 hybrid MLA model against a Ling-3.0-tiny deployment (this stack predates the model's upstream availability; the model is not loadable on current main, so the serving validation ran on the pull/33561-based image with the identical patch): - Bit-exact temperature-0 outputs vs the unpatched reference server on short, 4k-token, and 6k-token prompts. - Prefix-carrying multi-turn batches produce coherent outputs; the residual delta vs the reference server (0.036-0.087 |dlogprob|) matches the reference path's own instance-to-instance noise floor. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The fix does not change which kernels run, only the merge arithmetic. On the hybrid model above, routing prefix-carrying prefill batches through this (now numerically correct) chunked path replaces the fa2 paged MLA kernel with the cutlass ragged FMHA: 231.7 ms to 34.9 ms of MLA kernel time per 16x8k-token prefill block (torch profiler). Default paths are unaffected. Figures (all from real runs; generation script available on request): ![merge error vs prefix length](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/advpropsys/flashinfer/pr-assets/fig1_merge_error_vs_prefix.png) ![LSE and merge weights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/advpropsys/flashinfer/pr-assets/fig2_lse_and_merge_weights.png) ![serving dlogprob](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/advpropsys/flashinfer/pr-assets/fig3_serving_dlogprob.png) ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (black 26.1.0 clean; ruff F401/F821/UP037 clean on the changed file) - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (No new sglang-side test added; the change is a 3-line numeric conversion verified by the external repro above. Happy to add one if reviewers want it in-tree.) - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable; no user-facing behavior change beyond the numerical fix.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (See above.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

signal.title: Stabilize GB300 nightly tests
signal.text: ## Summary Stabilize the dedicated GB300 nightly suite by: - pinning the PyTorch TCPStore/NCCL rendezvous port outside the runner's ephemeral client-port range; - splitting long-running model configurations into independently registered test files; - moving a TP1 deterministic Blackwell test from GB300 to the smaller B200 pool; and - recalibrating test estimates from observed CI elapsed times. ## Motivation Two independent failures were observed on the GB300 nightly runner. First, distributed server startup failed with `EADDRINUSE` while binding dynamically selected ports in the runner's `10240-65535` ephemeral range. Although jobs execute sequentially on this host, a recently closed client connection can still occupy an ephemeral port when the next TCPStore tries to bind it. Second, the combined Qwen3.5 FP8 test reached its 10,800-second per-file timeout while the final DP4 accuracy evaluation was still healthy and actively processing requests. The TP4 and DP4 configurations shared one file-level deadline, so time consumed by TP4 reduced the budget available to DP4. The combined Kimi K2.5 test showed the same structural risk, completing in 10,008 seconds under the same 10,800-second cap. ## Changes ### Use a stable GB300 rendezvous port Add `GB300_NCCL_PORT = "10000"` and pass it to every GB300 nightly server launch. Port 10000 is below the runner's documented ephemeral range and therefore avoids collisions with recently closed client connections. ### Isolate model configurations by file Split the multi-configuration GB300 tests so every server configuration receives its own timeout and failure result: - Qwen3.5 FP8: TP4+MTP and DP4+DPA+MTP; - Kimi K2.5 NVFP4: TP4+EAGLE3 and DP4+DPA+EAGLE3; and - DeepSeek V4 Pro FP4: low-latency, balanced, and high-throughput. The existing accuracy parameters, thresholds, model launch arguments, environments, and performance batches are preserved, except that Qwen TP intentionally uses batches `[1, 8]` to retain batch-size-8 TP coverage. DP performance remains batch `[16]`. All affected tests now inherit from `CustomTestCase` for consistent cleanup behavior. ### Move TP1 deterministic coverage to B200 Move `test_glm4_moe_lite_deterministic.py` from the four-GPU GB300 nightly pool to the four-GPU B200 nightly pool. The test is TP1 and exercises the same SM100 Blackwell backend paths, so it does not require the GB300 machine. ### Recalibrate estimates Use elapsed times reconstructed from the supplied GB300 logs and round upward for scheduling: | Test configuration | Observed elapsed | Registered estimate | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DeepSeek low-latency | 688s | 720s | | DeepSeek balanced | 597s | 600s | | DeepSeek high-throughput | 531s | 600s | | Kimi TP | 4,568s | 4,800s | | Kimi DP | 6,940s | 7,200s | | Qwen TP | 4,698s | 4,800s | | Qwen DP | >6,116s (timed out before completion) | 7,200s | | GLM deterministic | 312s | 360s | The scheduled runner still derives a larger execution timeout from each estimate using the standard proportional/additive slack. ## Validation - Scoped pre-commit checks passed for all changed Python files. - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. - All changed Python files AST-parse successfully. - Full CI registry collection and suite validation passed. - The final GB300 nightly suite contains eight enabled test files. - Two-way LPT partition estimates remain below the six-hour suite limit. No GB300 or B200 hardware tests were run locally. Execution on the actual nightly runners remains the material validation gap. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31960466335](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31960466335)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31960466276](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31960466276)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [HiCache] Dedup MLA KV cache in host memory across TP ranks
signal.text: ## Motivation In MLA models every TP rank holds an identical copy of the KV cache. HiCache currently backs each rank's copy up to host memory independently, so a TP=N deployment stores the same bytes N times and wastes `(N-1)/N` of the host pool. This PR keeps a single host copy on rank 0 and broadcasts pages back to the other ranks when they are loaded. ## Modifications - **Backup (D2H)** — only rank 0 performs the host transfer. The remaining ranks create an allocator-only host pool via `MLATokenToKVPoolHost(is_dummy=True)`: it tracks free slots so eviction/allocation bookkeeping stays consistent across ranks, but never reserves the actual host buffer. Non-rank-0 ranks skip the D2H copy and just ack. - **Load (H2D)** — rank 0 reads from host, then broadcasts the loaded GPU pages to the other ranks. Both the H2D copy and the broadcast are enqueued on `load_stream`, so stream ordering guarantees rank 0's H2D lands before the broadcast reads the KV buffer. The broadcast runs on a **dedicated NCCL group** (created via `create_custom_parallel_group`, kept off the model-forward collectives) and coalesces all layers of a token chunk into a single reused staging buffer, one broadcast per chunk. The existing per-layer load events fire when the stream drains, so the normal `loading_check` ack path finalizes the load — **no extra process and no polling**. - The dummy-pool gating in `HiRadixCache` and the broadcast gating in `HiCacheController` derive from the same TP rank/size condition (attention-TP-aware when DP attention is enabled), so the two never disagree on which ranks own real host memory. - The dedicated broadcast group is torn down in `HiRadixCache`'s shutdown path via `_destroy_mla_broadcast_group`. ## Scope / Limitations - CUDA only. - DSA pools are excluded — their per-rank indexer buffers are not identical across ranks and are not broadcast. - Draft/speculative KV pools are unsupported and explicitly rejected in `set_draft_kv_pool`. ## Accuracy Tests Needs a multi-GPU MLA run with TP>1. Not yet benchmarked — help validating on a multi-GPU box is welcome. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Host KV memory drops by `(tp_size-1)/tp_size`. Each H2D load adds one NCCL broadcast per token chunk, issued on the dedicated broadcast group and serialized after the H2D on `load_stream` (overlapped with scheduling via the normal load-event ack path). Not yet benchmarked. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31960372068](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31960372068)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31960371958](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31960371958)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DSA] Trim top-k v2 output modes and tighten its PDL waits
signal.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation The DeepSeek-V4 (DSA indexer) top-k v2 kernel carried an optional `raw_indices` output that no production caller ever requests: the c4 indexer routes to the v1 kernel whenever it needs raw indices, so the v2 argument was only ever exercised by a unit test. Everyone else still paid for it with a per-element `raw_out != nullptr` branch inside the page-table transform loop. While removing it, two PDL (programmatic dependent launch) details in the same kernel turned out to be leaving performance on the table or resting on a condition the caller was not told about. ## Modifications **Output modes.** `raw_indices` is gone; `page_tables` becomes optional instead. `None` selects a `TopKMode::INDICES` template that emits the selected positions straight into the output, so the transform pass -- and the 8 KB shared staging buffer it needs -- is compiled out rather than skipped at runtime. Passing a page table keeps the existing behaviour bit for bit. **Output buffer is no longer prefilled with -1.** Every path already writes all `topk` slots of every row: the collect pass fills `[0, above_count)`, `handle_tie` fills `[above_count, topk)` (padding included), and the trivial path fills everything. The per-layer fill kernel was dead work. **Level-3 PDL wait narrowed to the cluster path.** Only rows whose raw indices come from the persistent cluster kernel need that kernel to have retired. The register / streaming / trivial rows were waiting on it too, holding an SM slot until the long-running pool finished and serializing the short items behind it -- which is exactly the mix level 3 exists for. The wait now lives inside the cluster branch (block-uniform, so the following `__syncthreads()` is unaffected). **Small-batch kernel.** Dropped the redundant `PDLWaitPrimary` after `forward()` (`forward()` already waits internally) and added the missing `PDLTriggerSecondary` so dependents can be scheduled without waiting for the whole grid to drain. **PDL prefetch contract.** The kernel reads `seq_lens` and the plan metadata *before* its `griddepcontrol.wait`, which is only legal while neither is produced by the immediately preceding kernel in the stream (per CUDA: the launch trigger "provides no memory visibility guarantee itself"). Production satisfies this -- both are built during per-forward metadata prep -- but two call sites could quietly break it, so: - the DSA backend now asserts `lengths.dtype == torch.int32` instead of calling `.to(torch.int32)`, which would place a cast kernel exactly there; - the unit test no longer launches `plan_topk_v2` back to back with the transform. Also renamed `TopKMode::INDICE` to `INDICES`. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py` -- 234/234 pass on B200. The no-page-table mode is validated directly against `torch.topk` across every dispatch template and boundary (`test_topk_v2_output_indices`), and the paged mode is still validated by inverting the output through the page table (`test_topk_v2`, `test_topk_v2_ragged`), so both modes keep full coverage. ## Benchmarking and Profiling No kernel-algorithm change on the paged path, so throughput is unchanged for the common shapes. The wins are structural: one fewer fill kernel per layer, one fewer branch per output element in the transform loop, and short rows in a mixed-length long-context batch no longer sit blocked on the persistent cluster pool. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31958299936](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31958299936)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31958598209](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31958598209)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [SM120&90] Add CUDA fused Triton sparse-MLA prefill backend for DSA
signal.text: ## Motivation DSA prefill on CUDA has no fused Triton path, and the kernels it does dispatch to are a poor fit for the head count the model actually has after TP. `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` requires `num_heads % 64` on SM90 and `% 128` on SM100+, so `_forward_flashmla_sparse` zero-pads the head dim before calling it. GLM-5.1 at TP8 has **8 real heads**, so 7/8 of the tensor-core work on SM90 — 15/16 on SM100+ — is spent on padding, and the split form then writes `O(tokens x splits)` partials to HBM for a second kernel to merge. Neither cost is necessary at this size. The attention tile is small enough that one Triton program per query token, holding the online softmax in registers, beats a wide cooperative block, and it lets the head dim be padded into a 16-row MMA tile (8 -> 16) instead of into the grid (8 -> 128) — no partials, no merge. ## Modifications Adds `--dsa-prefill-backend triton_sparse_mla`, **default off**, plus two opt-in fast paths. Both are algebraic rewrites rather than approximations, and both are gated against an fp32 reference in the tests. ### `--dsa-triton-union {2,4}` In DSA prefill the indexer's scores drift slowly in `t`, so neighbouring query tokens select nearly the same KV rows. Measured on captured GLM-5.1 traces: | capture | valid rows/token | union of 2 tokens | union of 4 tokens | |---|---|---|---| | bs1 x 2048 | 1024 | 1.00x one token's set | 1.01x | | bs1 x 4096 | 1536 | 1.05x | 1.09x | | bs1 x 8192 | 1792 | 1.12x | 1.23x | | bs2 x 4096 | 1536 | 1.05x | 1.09x | | bs4 x 2048 | 1024 | 1.00x | 1.01x | One gather can therefore serve four tokens for ~1.1x the rows. `G` adjacent tokens share a single gathered index set, and a 32-row MMA tile then carries 4 tokens x 8 heads of *real* work instead of 8 real rows and 24 of padding. A per-row ownership bitmask restores each token's own softmax support, so the result is identical to the per-token path. One measurement note, because it is easy to get wrong: uniformly random indices have none of that structure and understate this path by about 2x. The benchmark added here builds indices as a calibrated random walk instead — token `t+1` is token `t` with ~2% of rows swapped, plus the `-1` padding real prefill has for `t < topk` — so the synthetic union sizes match the captured ones. On SM120 it reproduces the real-trace measurements within ~10%. ### `--dsa-triton-dense-prefix` A token whose top-k covers its entire causal prefix (`t + 1 <= topk`) is doing dense causal attention by definition. Those tokens take a zero-gather tiled path, behind an exact count/min/max guard that falls back to the sparse path whenever the selection is not exactly the prefix. ### Robustness The launcher steps the shared-memory tile down rather than propagating `OutOfResources` to the request: the tuned tile does not fit at 32 heads on SM120's 100 KB budget, and the union tile (`num_heads * G` rows) does not fit at 16 heads with `G=2`. A capability check rejects unsupported configurations at construction rather than mid-forward, and the union path degrades to the per-token path under CUDA-graph capture, where its scratch sizing cannot run. ### Files New kernel module (no environment variables); a dispatch branch, startup validator and option plumbing in `dsa_backend.py`; three server args; an SM120 allowlist widening that leaves the auto-selected default unchanged; and registration in the DSA variant matrix so `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py` exercises this backend too. ## Accuracy Tests **Kernel** — `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_triton_sparse_mla_prefill.py`, 10 cases against an fp32 reference: base path at three shapes, `-1`/ragged padding, union exactness on overlapping-but-unequal selections, dense-prefix identity, int32-vs-int64 gather addressing equivalence, determinism, and three launch-time regressions (32-head and 16-head-union shared-memory step-down, union scratch reuse across batch shapes past the epoch wrap). **Every timed point below is correctness-gated** against the same fp32 reference before it is timed — 5/5 shapes PASS on each architecture. Two independent model-level checks, at different tolerances, because they answer different questions. **(a) The kernel's own output tensor** — GLM-5.1 and GLM-5.2 configs, TP8 on SM90, `--load-format dummy` (fixed per-parameter seed, so both runs get identical weights) and a seeded prompt. Comparing the layer-0 prefill attention output — the tensor this backend actually computes — in fp64, against a control of the reference backend rerun against itself: | comparison | cosine | rel L2 | max abs | |---|---|---|---| | control: `flashmla_sparse` vs itself (rerun) | 0.9999999094 | 4.26e-04 | 3.05e-05 | | `triton_sparse_mla` | 0.9999997999 | 6.33e-04 | 6.10e-05 | | + `--dsa-triton-union 4` | 0.9999997168 | 7.53e-04 | 6.10e-05 | | + `--dsa-triton-dense-prefix` | 0.9999998000 | 6.32e-04 | 6.10e-05 | The delta is 1.5x the stack's own run-to-run noise — the same order, i.e. bf16 rounding between two correct kernels. This is the tight measurement: it reads the kernel's output directly, before 78 layers of MoE can amplify anything. GLM-5.2 reproduces these figures to the digit, which is expected rather than a second sample — the two configs share every attention dimension and the dummy weights are seeded per parameter by shape, so layer 0 sees the same tensors in both. **(b) What the model actually emits, on real weights** — GLM-5.2 (78 layers, FP8, TP8 on SM90), seeded prompt, next-token logits over the full 154880-wide vocabulary in fp64, again against a rerun control: | tokens | comparison | cosine | rel L2 | |---|---|---|---| | 2048 | control: `flashmla_sparse` vs itself | 0.9992698 | 7.70e-02 | | 2048 | `triton_sparse_mla` | 0.9995887 | 4.74e-02 | | 4096 | control: `flashmla_sparse` vs itself | 0.9988628 | 4.81e-02 | | 4096 | `triton_sparse_mla` | 0.9990866 | 5.97e-02 | | 8192 | control: `flashmla_sparse` vs itself | 0.9994673 | 3.53e-02 | | 8192 | `triton_sparse_mla` | 0.9993207 | 3.78e-02 | The tolerances here are three orders looser than in (a) — that is the MoE, not the kernel. What matters is the comparison to the control: our deviation from the reference is bracketed by the reference's deviation from itself, and is smaller than it at two of the three lengths. The control is doing real work — at 4096 the reference already disagrees with its own rerun on the argmax token, so this stack (256-expert MoE on FP8) is not bit-reproducible run to run and a greedy-token match is not a usable metric here. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Kernel-level numbers are on **real captured GLM-5.1 index sets** at five (batch, seqlen) points, not synthetic indices; times in ms, median of 15. End-to-end numbers are on real model weights. ### SM120 — kernel level, vs `flashinfer_sparse_mla` (the backend SM120 selects today) | capture | tokens | flashinfer | ours | ours+union4 | ours | +union4 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | bs1 x 2048 | 2048 | 1.240 | 0.990 | 0.499 | 1.25x | 2.48x | | bs1 x 4096 | 4096 | 3.474 | 2.878 | 1.329 | 1.21x | 2.61x | | bs1 x 8192 | 8192 | 7.989 | 6.667 | 3.673 | 1.20x | 2.18x | | bs2 x 4096 | 8192 | 6.999 | 5.782 | 2.871 | 1.21x | 2.44x | | bs4 x 2048 | 8192 | 5.028 | 4.020 | 1.865 | 1.25x | 2.70x | | **geomean** | | | | | **1.22x** | **2.47x** | ### SM90 — kernel level, vs `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` (padded 8 -> 64 heads, as the backend does) | capture | tokens | flashmla | ours | +union2 | +union4 | +dense | best | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | bs1 x 2048 | 2048 | 4.518 | 1.209 | 0.799 | 0.789 | 0.806 | 5.73x | | bs1 x 4096 | 4096 | 8.859 | 3.155 | 2.010 | 1.990 | 2.923 | 4.45x | | bs1 x 8192 | 8192 | 17.636 | 7.149 | 4.776 | 4.889 | 6.887 | 3.69x | | bs2 x 4096 | 8192 | 17.632 | 6.222 | 3.936 | 3.806 | 5.973 | 4.63x | | bs4 x 2048 | 8192 | 17.631 | 4.377 | 2.674 | 2.468 | 4.120 | 7.14x | | **geomean** | | | **3.12x** | **4.86x** | **4.97x** | 1.98x | **5.00x** | The spread is wide but monotone in the right variable: shorter requests favour this kernel most, because more of their rows are `-1` padding that the per-token early exit skips and the padded dense kernel does not. ### SM120 — end to end, GLM-5.1 (real weights), TP8, prefill latency | tokens | baseline | ours | ours+union4 | ours | +union4 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2048 | 0.764 s | 0.630 s | 0.592 s | 1.21x | 1.29x | | 4096 | 1.595 s | 1.279 s | 1.152 s | 1.25x | 1.38x | | 8192 | 3.274 s | 2.594 s | 2.346 s | 1.26x | **1.40x** | Dense-prefix at 8192 tokens: 2.586 s (1.27x) on its own; it does not stack on top of union (2.369 s, 1.38x), since union already amortises the same rows. Measurement basis: mainline's DSA indexer does not yet run on SM120 (DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits asserts `arch_major in (9, 10)`), so this ladder routes the shipped kernel module into an SM120 deployment's DSA prefill seam and compares against that deployment's own prefill path. Every run reports the number of invocations actually served by this kernel, so a silent no-op cannot be mistaken for a win. The kernel-level SM120 table above is the like-for-like comparison against an upstream backend. ### SM90 — end to end, 8-layer configs, TP8, prefill latency at 4096 tokens The small configs, kept because they cover both model generations side by side: | model | `flashmla_sparse` | `triton_sparse_mla` | + dense-prefix | |---|---|---|---| | GLM-5.1 | 128.35 ms | 81.73 ms (**1.57x**) | 80.62 ms (1.59x) | | GLM-5.2 | 126.24 / 123.82 ms | 77.83 ms (**1.61x**) | 75.18 ms (1.66x) | Two baseline runs are shown for GLM-5.2 to make the ~2% run-to-run spread visible; the ratios are against their mean. The same kernel serves both generations unchanged — GLM-5.2 has the same DSA shape (`kv_lora_rank` 512 + `qk_rope_head_dim` 64 = 576, `d_v` 512, topk 2048, 8 heads at TP8) and the same `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` architecture. Its layers are not uniform (`indexer_types` mixes `full` and `shared`), so the run counts kernel invocations to confirm coverage rather than infer it: 16 per rank for an 8-layer model over two prefills, i.e. every DSA layer. ### SM90 — end to end, GLM-5.2 (78 layers, real FP8 weights), TP8, prefill latency | tokens | `flashmla_sparse` | `triton_sparse_mla` | + union=4 | + dense-prefix | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2048 | 0.2212 s | 0.2231 s | 0.2218 s | 0.2243 s | | 4096 | 1.0633 s | 0.6090 s (**1.75x**) | **0.5214 s (2.04x)** | 0.5914 s (1.80x) | | 8192 | 2.0877 s | 1.2508 s (**1.67x**) | **1.0651 s (1.96x)** | 1.2299 s (1.70x) | The reference column is the mean of two independent runs that agreed to within 0.1% at every length, so the ratios are well outside run-to-run noise. Each measured shape is warmed in-process before it is timed: `bench_one_batch` warms up only at `input_len[0]`, so a plain multi-length sweep charges the first visit to each new shape with Triton JIT and allocator growth — which lands on this backend harder than on a precompiled CUDA kernel. **Short contexts are unchanged by design, not by accident.** At 2048 tokens the three configurations are identical because the kernel is never called: on SM90 and SM100, `dsa_backend.py` routes prefill to a dense MHA one-shot path when `max_kv_len <= SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD` (default 2048). Counting invocations confirms it — 312 calls per rank across the sweep, i.e. 78 layers x the 4 prefills that exceed the threshold, and zero for the rest. Every run in this PR reports that count, so a configuration that silently routed nothing cannot be mistaken for a result. A benchmark is included at `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_dsa_triton_sparse_mla_prefill.py`. Absolute numbers here are from SM90 and SM120 parts that are not CI runners, so the benchmark is written to make the *relative* comparison reproduce on `1-gpu-large`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests according to Run and add unit tests - [ ] Update documentation — there is no DSA-backend page to update; happy to add one if wanted - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31957622433](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31957622433)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31957622319](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31957622319)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
