signal.title: [Model] Support Ling-3.0-flash (BailingMoeV3)
signal.text: ## Motivation Day-0 support for [inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash) (`BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM`, `model_type=bailing_hybrid`): a hybrid MoE architecture interleaving KDA linear attention (with a safe-gate lower bound) and MLA, with MTP (NEXTN) and DSPARK speculative decoding support. ## Modifications - `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM` model (`bailing_hybrid` config): KDA + MLA hybrid layers, 512-expert MoE, and MTP (NEXTN). - DSPARK support for the KDA hybrid path: graph-folded draft proposal, fused KDA chain-verify kernel, and DSA token-to-KV pool sizing. - KDA safe gate propagation through the Triton decode/target-verify kernels and their call sites, matching fused verification. - `ling3` reasoning and tool-call parsers. - BF16, FP8, compressed-tensors INT4, and native MXFP4 checkpoint support on Hopper and Blackwell. - Exactness, fusion-gate, quantization, and parser tests. ## Validation All serving runs kept decode CUDA Graph enabled and used the default graph sizing. No run used `--disable-cuda-graph` or `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`. ### Quantized checkpoints Full GSM8K uses 1,319 questions. Performance uses 80 exact-length random requests at ISL/OSL 8192/1024 with concurrency 1 and 16; throughput includes input and output tokens per second per GPU. | GPU | format | GSM8K | stop rate | throughput/GPU (c1 / c16) | P50 TTFT ms (c1 / c16) | P50 TPOT ms (c1 / c16) | default graph range | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | H200 | INT4 | 95.30% | 100% | 1,159 / 7,184 | 205.96 / 1,891.74 | 3.68 / 8.16 | through batch 218 | | H200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 100% | 709 / 5,215 | 305.23 / 2,725.52 | 6.05 / 11.17 | through batch 227 | | B200 | INT4 | 96.74% | 99.70% | 482 / 1,344 | 641.41 / 6,202.62 | 8.72 / 48.01 | through batch 305 | | B200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 99.62% | 785 / 7,933 | 127.97 / 1,117.16 | 5.60 / 7.98 | through batch 314 | INT4 selects Marlin on H200 and the graph-compatible Triton WNA16 path on B200. MXFP4 routed experts use the native FlashInfer runner on both GPUs. The B200 MXFP4 checkpoint also contains block-FP8 dense/shared projections, which use the Triton FP8 GEMM backend to avoid an unsupported FlashInfer FP8 tactic without converting the routed experts. BF16 and FP8 were rerun on H200 and B200 after the quantization changes. All four combinations served with CUDA Graph enabled, completed generation, and passed the 20-example GSM8K regression gate with 100% stop rate. ### Speculative decoding Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x B200 TP4, `temperature=1.0 / top_p=0.95`, thinking on, full GSM8K, `max_tokens=8192`: | spec decoding | score | stop rate | error rate | |---|---:|---:|---:| | DSPARK | 96.66% | 99.77% | 0.00% | | MTP (NEXTN) | 96.44% | 99.62% | 0.00% | Non-stop finishes are long reasoning outputs reaching `max_tokens`, not repetition loops. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests and register them in CI. - [x] Validate serving correctness, stop rate, and accuracy on H200 and B200. - [x] Publish deployment recipes and benchmark results in #34363. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31956934564](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31956934564)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31956934369](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31956934369)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU] Add mxfp4-w4a4 MOE Quantization Support for NPU
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang already supports ModelSlim W4A4_MXFP4 quantization for dense linear layers on Ascend NPU, but the corresponding MoE path is still missing. As a result, MoE models whose expert weights are exported with the W4A4_MXFP4 scheme cannot be loaded and executed through the ModelSlim quantization backend. The Ascend MoE implementation has also been refactored into the modular AscendRunner architecture. Therefore, MXFP4 MoE support needs to integrate with the new per-weight-group quantization methods and runner flow instead of restoring the legacy fused MoE implementation. ## Modifications - Add a ModelSlim W4A4_MXFP4 MoE scheme and register it for MoE quantization detection. - Create w13 and w2 expert weights independently, following the existing ModelSlim MXFP4 checkpoint format:FP4 values stored in float8_e4m3fn containers. - UE8M0 block scales stored as uint8 with a block size of 32. - Add an Ascend MXFP4 MoE quantization method compatible with the refactored AscendRunner and GroupedMatmul interfaces. - Repack offline FP8-container weights into float4_e2m1fn_x2, convert them to the required NPU layout, and reshape block scales for grouped matmul. - Dynamically quantize BF16/FP16 activations to MXFP4 before both expert GMM operations. - Keep the dispatcher output in BF16, since the refactored Ascend dispatcher currently supports BF16 and INT8 outputs, and perform MXFP4 quantization inside the MoE method. - Treat MoE weight offsets as optional so offset-free schemes such as MXFP4 can use the common ModelSlim MoE runner. - Reuse the existing routing, activation, and finalization flow provided by the refactored Ascend MoE backend. - Leave the existing W4A4_MXFP4 linear implementation unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Tested with Qwen3-235B-A22B mxfp4 w4a4 weights. ``` metrics = run_eval(args) 100%|████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████| 1319/1319 [11:09<00:00, 1.97it/s] Accuracy: 0.938 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 669.312 s Output throughput: 263.397 token/s metrics={'accuracy': np.float64(0.9378316906747536), 'invalid': np.float64(0.0), 'latency': 669.312145670061, 'output_throughput': 263.39728203125276} metrics['accuracy']=np.float64(0.9378316906747536) ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - signal.title: [DFLASH] Remove FlashInfer and MRoPE host syncs
signal.text: ## Motivation DFlash speculative decoding with overlap scheduling still performs blocking CPU/GPU synchronization in four places: 1. FlashInfer planning for the draft worker's attention wrappers. 2. Calling `paged_kernel_lens.sum().item()` while preparing the draft worker's sliding-window attention metadata. 3. Uploading multimodal MRoPE deltas during target verification. 4. FlashInfer planning for the target worker's full-attention wrapper. These synchronizations force the CPU to wait for queued GPU work, preventing the CPU scheduler from staying ahead and introducing gaps before draft and target-verify execution. ## Modifications This PR addresses the synchronization points in three corresponding areas. The optimization is guarded by: ```bash export SGLANG_DFLASH_SYNC_FREE_DECODE=1 ``` The flag defaults to `False`. ### 1. Remove host synchronization from draft-worker FlashInfer planning The draft worker may use either a sliding-window wrapper together with a full-attention wrapper, or a single full-attention wrapper. Both layouts now use SGLang's sync-free FlashInfer prefill planning path during CUDA graph replay. During graph capture, the original FlashInfer `plan()` is still called once to initialize the wrapper's cached module. During replay, SGLang constructs the planning metadata from CPU-side request bookkeeping and calls `fast_prefill_plan()` instead of invoking the original blocking planning path. For sliding-window attention, the previous implementation also evaluated: ```python paged_kernel_lens.sum().item() ``` Because `paged_kernel_lens` is a CUDA tensor, `.item()` copies the scalar result to the host and waits for preceding GPU work. The optimized path computes the equivalent planning length from the existing CPU-side sequence-length metadata, removing this additional synchronization. This follows the approach introduced in [PR #32218](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32218). The CPU lengths are conservative planning bounds used only to select and partition the FlashInfer workload. The GPU `indptr` and `indices` remain the authoritative layout used for actual KV-cache access, so the attention computation is unchanged. Supported draft-worker layouts: | Attention layout | Optimization | | --- | --- | | Sliding-window + full attention | Both wrappers use sync-free planning | | Full attention only | The full-attention wrapper uses sync-free planning | | Unsupported layout | Falls back to the original FlashInfer planning path | ### 2. Avoid repeated MRoPE delta uploads during target verification For multimodal requests, the MRoPE delta is request-level metadata and remains unchanged across decode steps for the same request. Previously, target verification repeatedly stacked CPU tensors and copied the result to the GPU, introducing host-to-device transfer and synchronization overhead on every step. The optimized path creates a GPU-side MRoPE delta cache during prefill and reuses the cached tensor during subsequent DFlash target-verification steps. Cache entries are validated against the request metadata and device before reuse, and are recreated when the corresponding request state changes. This also supports batched requests: each request has its own cached delta, and the per-request tensors are stacked in the current batch order before use. ### 3. Remove host synchronization from target-worker FlashInfer planning The target worker's full-attention wrapper previously entered the original FlashInfer planning path during target verification. This PR applies the same sync-free planning mechanism used by the draft worker. The target wrapper uses CPU-side sequence-length metadata to construct the host planning inputs while retaining the exact GPU KV-cache layout for execution. Unsupported configurations, non-DFlash execution, and runs without `SGLANG_DFLASH_SYNC_FREE_DECODE=1` continue to use the existing implementation. ## Correctness The optimization changes only how FlashInfer planning metadata is constructed and when MRoPE deltas are transferred. It does not change attention computation or KV-cache addressing. The implementation preserves the following invariants: - CUDA graph capture initializes FlashInfer's cached module with the original `plan()` implementation. - CUDA graph replay uses CPU-side planning metadata without GPU-to-CPU scalar reads. - Host planning lengths are never smaller than the exact GPU KV lengths. - GPU `indptr` and `indices` remain authoritative for actual KV-cache access. - Unsupported layouts automatically fall back to the original code path. - The original behavior is preserved when the feature switch is disabled. ## Accuracy Tests Tested with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B and its DFlash draft model on 8x NVIDIA A800 GPUs (`TP=8`, `EP=8`, draft tokens `4`, DFlash block size `4`). Each multimodal request contained approximately 14k input tokens and three images: - Multimodal requests: **60/60 passed**. - Concurrent requests with `bs=2/4/8`: **14/14 passed**. - No plan metadata, host-bound, reconstructed indptr, or MRoPE value mismatch during development validation. - No scheduler exception, traceback, or CUDA error in the final service logs. Benchmark results before and after enabling the synchronization optimization: | Configuration | Math500 | GSM8K | MMBench_dev_en | MMStar | RealWorldQA | gRefCOCO | CountBench strict | MMLU-Redux | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Before sync optimization | 95.8 | 95.8 | 79.6 | 76.7 | 78.7 | 70.4 | 93.3 | 84.1 | | After sync optimization | 97.2 | 96.1 | 79.7 | 77.5 | 79.2 | 70.5 | 93.3 | 84.2 | No benchmark showed an accuracy regression. The optimization only changes how FlashInfer planning metadata is constructed and when MRoPE deltas are transferred; it does not change the attention computation. Unit tests on the latest `upstream/main`: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python3 \ test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_overlap_hostsync.py ``` Result: **10/10 passed** on an A800. ## Speed Tests and Profiling For the multimodal workload, TPOT decreased from **5.2 ms/token** to **4.5 ms/token**. | Metric | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | TPOT | 5.2 ms/token | 4.5 ms/token | MRoPE profiling: | Metric | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | MRoPE `cudaStreamSynchronize` calls | 13 | 0 | | MRoPE stream wait | 1200.4 us/step | 0 | | `forward_batch_init` | 1618.1 us/step | 555.5 us/step | With all three paths enabled, 39 speculative FlashInfer plans used the fast path (26 draft and 13 target). The remaining blocking plan was initialization or outside the speculative hot path. Before After ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31155288337](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31155288337) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31155288158](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31155288158)

signal.title: [Bug] Inkling MTP crashes during draft-extend CUDA graph capture
signal.text: ### Describe the bug Serving Inkling with MTP (multi-layer EAGLE) crashes at startup while capturing the draft-extend CUDA graph. `forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens` is `None` when the short-conv backend refreshes its track indices: ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape' speculative/multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:930 multi_step_fn layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:1007 init_forward_metadata_in_graph layers/attention/linear/inkling_sconv_backend.py:451 _refresh_track_conv_indices ``` The same configuration serves normally with CUDA graphs disabled (`--disable-cuda-graph --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`), reaching an accept length of 2.4-3.0, so it is specific to the capture path. ### Reproduction ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code \ --model-path thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4 --tp 8 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 --attention-backend fa4 --page-size 128 \ --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed \ --enable-torch-symm-mem --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.1 \ --enable-multimodal --reasoning-parser inkling --tool-call-parser inkling \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 8 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 9 --enable-multi-layer-eagle --speculative-use-rejection-sampling ``` All 8 ranks hit the same exception and the server never becomes ready. ### Environment sglang `4a6dc267`.

signal.title: [Apple Silicon] [MLX] Fuse MoE combine multiply-reduce into one Metal kernel
signal.text: <!-- PR body rewritten to .github/pull_request_template.md, fetched fresh from sgl-project/sglang main and followed verbatim (Motivation / Modifications / Accuracy Tests / Speed Tests and Profiling / Checklist / Review and Merge Process). Current head numbers only. Figures this run confirmed on hardware are marked [hardware verified, this run]; figures carried over from the original author's server level benchmark and not remeasured end to end are marked [author reported, not reverified end to end]; figures carried over from the prior founder review without a rerun this session are marked [prior review, not rerun this session]. --> ## Motivation The reference MoE combine, `(y * scores[..., None]).sum(axis=-2)`, runs a broadcast multiply and a reduction with a transient materialized between them. Fusing both into one Metal kernel saves a full read of `y`, the transient round trip, and one dispatch per MoE layer. This PR began as the kernel plus its verification suite. Review exposed a real coverage bug in the eligibility guard (rank 3 assumption against a rank 4 production call site), which the fix generalized. The performance question required measured serving numbers, which required an integration path. The abstraction ask captured the JIT declaration pattern this kernel now shares with `fused_swiglu.py`. A founder-level review of the abstraction and its test suite followed; this revision applies that review's fixes. ## Modifications **Guard generalization and bf16 scores** - SGLang never flattens batch and sequence upstream, so every real combine call site is rank 4 `y` with rank 3 `scores` (prefill `[1, L, 4, 2048]`, batched decode `[R, 1, 4, 2048]`). The original rank 3 guard would have fallen back on every real forward pass; caught in review. Both target models run bf16 activations, and the original `_SCORES_DTYPES` rejected bf16 scores. - The contract is now `scores.shape == y.shape[:-1]` with rank at least 3. Leading dims flatten into the kernel's row dimension before dispatch and the output reshapes back. bf16 scores are accepted. **Default off integration** - `SGLANG_MLX_FUSE_MOE_COMBINE = EnvBool(False)` in `environ.py`, plus `patch_moe_combine_with_fused`, a subclass swap on `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` and `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock`, gated in `_load_model` beside the existing SwiGLU patch. Per call eligibility stays inside `fused_combine`, which falls back inline, so patching never changes results. Merging changes nothing for any user; the flag flip is a separate, evidence backed decision. **`metal_jit` abstraction** - `hardware_backend/mlx/metal_jit.py`: kernel files declare source once via the `@metal_jit.kernel(...)` decorator on a `MetalJitOp` subclass. The base class owns a `can_fuse` to `dispatch_fused` or `dispatch_fallback` template with typed `NotFusable` routing. Compile failures degrade via a memoized guard mirroring `jit_kernel/moe_fused_gate.py`'s `can_use_moe_fused_gate` pattern (catch, log once, memoize, fall back) instead of crashing the forward pass. - `MetalJitKernel` still owns the per dtype key compile cache and warm dedupe underneath, unchanged in behavior. - Both kernels migrate as the first consumers. Name templates keep kernel names byte identical, so profiler labels and shader cache keys do not change; the SwiGLU warm set folds into `warm_once`. - Patch registration stays in `model_runner`. The env flags' one reader should remain the load path, and the patch functions encode `mlx_lm` model class knowledge, not Metal JIT knowledge. **`can_fuse` is now abstract, per review** - A founder-level review found `FusedGateQmvSiluMulKernel` was a live example of the risk in an optimistic base default: it inherited `can_fuse` returning `True` unconditionally instead of declaring its own eligibility, relying entirely on `dispatch_fused` raising `NotFusable` before any observable effect to stay safe. `MetalJitOp.can_fuse` now raises `NotImplementedError` (`metal_jit.py:123-125`, matching this codebase's existing abstract-method idiom of a bare `raise NotImplementedError`, used already by `dispatch_fused`/`dispatch_fallback` on the same class; no `abc.ABC` is used anywhere in this tree). The class docstring states the rule directly: every op declares its own predicate, the base declares none. - `FusedMoeCombineKernel.can_fuse` already had a real structural predicate (`fused_combine.py:100-112`); unchanged. - `FusedGateQmvSiluMulKernel.can_fuse` (new, `fused_swiglu.py:246-263`) delegates to the same `_check_eligibility` regime check `dispatch_fused`/`dispatch_fallback` already share, so all three stay in sync by construction. This does not change the op's observable behavior: for structurally ineligible inputs, `dispatch()` now short-circuits straight to `dispatch_fallback` instead of first attempting `dispatch_fused` (which raised the identical diagnostic anyway); for eligible inputs whose Metal compile fails, `can_fuse` cannot see that and the routing is unchanged. SwiGLU's asymmetry is preserved exactly: `dispatch_fallback` still always raises the diagnostic chain rather than computing, since its real fallback needs wrapper layer context the op does not receive; only its predicate became explicit. - Three `test_metal_jit.py` stub classes that exercised `dispatch_fused`/`dispatch_fallback` routing without overriding `can_fuse` (relying on the removed default) now declare an explicit `can_fuse` returning `True`, so they keep testing what they were written to test. **Tolerance test fix, per review** - The same review found the bf16 1 ULP, zero headroom bound in `test_fused_combine.py` could reach tens of thousands of "ULP" at production scale. Root cause, found this session: the huge values are a metric artifact, not a kernel regression. Near zero, fp16/bf16 use absolute (subnormal-adjacent) steps far finer than the ULP ceiling's relative-error assumption, and the two paths can even land on opposite sides of zero (e.g. `0.0` vs `-1e-7`), where the bit-pattern-distance metric's own documented same-sign assumption breaks down. `allclose(atol=tol)` already bounds these elements correctly. - Fix: the integer-ULP ceiling is now checked only on elements at or above a `1e-3` ground-truth-magnitude floor (`_ULP_FLOOR`, `test_fused_combine.py`), where the bit-pattern-distance metric is meaningful. A live 100-seed-per-shape sweep across every shape in `_SHAPES` plus the real production prefill shape `(1, 268, 4, 2048)` found max ULP at or above the floor was 0-1 in every case, for both dtypes; the ceilings (`_ROUNDED_MAX_ULP`) are now 3 for both fp16 and bf16, roughly 3x headroom over that observed max. The check is not deleted or loosened past what the evidence supports. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_fused_combine.py`: 102 of 102 matrix cases fire the fused path. fp16 and bf16 scores are bit exact against the fp32 reference; fp32 scores are asserted within narrowing tolerance and a floor-masked integer-ULP ceiling (see Modifications). **[hardware verified, this run]** the updated bound was demonstrated seed robust: `test_scores_fp32_correctly_rounded` and the production-shape case in `test_leading_dims_match_reference` were run across 7 shifted seed offsets (0 through 60000) on this hardware, all passing, with observed ULP at or above the floor staying in {0, 1} throughout. Patch idempotency on real, small dimension `mlx_lm` blocks is a no op with bit identical outputs. - `test_metal_jit.py`: cache identity, name formatting, warm dedupe, decorator validation, and the dispatch template's routing contract (fused, fallback, `NotFusable` propagation, now including `can_fuse` as a required override), including the compile failure memoization guard. - `test_fused_swiglu.py`: regime diagnostics through the wrapper, dtype membership fallback (not just dtype agreement), warm skip logging, warmup enumeration, and (new) the explicit `can_fuse` predicate. - **47 tests across the three files at head** (17 + 10 + 20, `pytest --collect-only`) **[hardware verified, this run]**. Unchanged from before this revision: the fixes changed test bodies and one helper signature, not test count. - **[hardware verified, this run]** Full suite: 45 passed, 2 skipped (opt-in, HF-checkpoint-gated, not a hardware skip), 0 failed, both before and after this revision's changes. - **[hardware verified, this run]** The three `NotFusable` safety sub claims from the prior review (forced Metal compile failure on an eligible input: no raise to caller, bit exact output, no partial/corrupted cache state) were re-run against the real `fused_combine()` entry point after the `can_fuse` change and still hold; the equivalent check on `FusedGateQmvSiluMulKernel`'s own compile-failure path (now gated by its own `can_fuse`) also holds. ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Original end to end measurement** [author reported, not reverified end to end], `mlx-community/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat-4bit` on a 24 GB Apple Silicon machine, interleaved on/off server launches, warmup discarded, temperature 0, medians with min and max: | config | decode bs=1 tok/s | per step ms | decode bs=4 tok/s | prefill L=268 tok/s | |---|---|---|---|---| | unfused | 131.02 [130.61, 131.67] | 7.632 | 201.20 [199.13, 203.11] | 758.4 [756.0, 815.8]\* | | fused | 131.80 [131.64, 132.11] | 7.587 | 203.56 [201.82, 205.55] | 818.2 [809.8, 820.1] | \* One unfused launch at 9.7 GB free excluded as memory pressure (732.7 tok/s). Decode bs=1 is +0.6 percent, decode bs=4 is +1.2 percent, prefill is +0.0 to +1.5 percent depending on which launches are compared. **Isolated op measurement, decode bs=1** [hardware verified, this run]: re-ran the fused-vs-fallback dispatch check on this hardware after the `can_fuse` change. `dispatch()` still routes through exactly one `metal_jit.get("fused_moe_combine", ...)` call on the fused path, output still bit exact against an independent reference, and the fused path still measures faster than the fallback (paired timing this run: +2.4%, a simpler protocol than the prior review's bootstrapped interleaved A/B, so not a direct comparison to the fuller table below). **Prior isolated op measurement** [prior review, not rerun this session], Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB, bootstrap 95 percent confidence interval: | shape | fused (us) | fallback (us) | speedup | 95% CI excludes zero | |---|---|---|---|---| | decode bs=1 | 17.87 | 18.80 | +9.6% | yes | | decode bs=4 | 18.39 | 19.54 | +7.4% | yes | | prefill L=268 | 34.83 | 190.94 | +82.2% | yes | The two end-to-end/isolated tables are not directly comparable: the isolated measurement strips out every other per token cost (attention, routing, the expert GEMMs, sampling, KV bookkeeping), so it upper bounds what the combine op itself could contribute, while the end-to-end measurement is what actually reaches a user after dilution by the rest of the forward pass. The `metal_jit` registry promotion and the `can_fuse` abstraction change are both same-process refactors with no dispatch-count or numerics change on the fused path, confirmed this run; neither table's numbers are affected by them. ## Known Limitations - `warmup_specs` declares each op's supported variant set and has no consumer yet. The working warm path (SwiGLU only; combine pays its first dispatch JIT cost today) warms instantiated shapes derived from the live model. `aot.py` reconciles the two in a follow up PR. - The patch time `can_fuse(switch_mlp)` free function in `fused_swiglu.py` is unrelated to `MetalJitOp.can_fuse`; a rename is follow up material. This is a naming collision only; both `FusedMoeCombineKernel` and `FusedGateQmvSiluMulKernel` now declare their own `MetalJitOp.can_fuse` explicitly (see Modifications), so the base class no longer has an optimistic default for a future op to silently inherit. - SwiGLU's `dispatch_fallback` intentionally raises rather than computes, since its real fallback needs wrapper layer context the op does not receive. Unifying that is follow up scope. - Nothing counts fallback occurrences on either op (no logging on `FusedMoeCombineKernel`'s fallback path, a once-per-process warning on SwiGLU's). This was flagged by review as a real but lower-leverage gap for this pass and is not addressed here. - The `register_mlx_ci` addition to `ci_register.py` this branch carries is now byte identical to what #30121 independently merged to `main`; a real merge auto-resolves it with no manual edit, confirmed this run (`git hash-object` matches on both sides). That conflict is outside what the prior review named and was not resolved unilaterally in this pass; it is reported here as the actual remaining blocker to a clean merge, and needs a codeowner call on how to reconcile the two files' content, not just their location. - Mergeable state at time of writing needs the `test_fused_swiglu.py` relocation above resolved before this branch can merge cleanly against current `main`; the `ci_register.py` duplication that previously blocked it is confirmed moot. <!-- pr-states block intentionally omitted here; it is auto injected by the repo's own tooling on the live PR, not authored content. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: Add bit-exact guard for extra_buffer_lazy
signal.text: ## Motivation `extra_buffer_lazy` has no bit-exact coverage today. It is a different code path rather than the same code under a flag: a request holds one ping-pong slot instead of two, and the second is allocated only on the forward that crosses a track boundary and freed again afterwards. The checkpoint therefore lands in a slot chosen per forward instead of one the request owns for its lifetime, and picking the wrong one restores another request's conv window. Admitted by revert-then-red rather than by adding a class that reads 0 either way. Reverting https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34184 (stale track rows corrupting conv checkpoints under the prefill graph) takes the new class's `test_prefill_cache_hit` to **5.56e-06** against a 1e-9 floor. The non-lazy class read 1.18e-05 in the same session, so read the pair as "both fire", not as the lazy one being weaker. Tracked in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34899. ## Accuracy Whole file, one B200, `thinkingmachines/Inkling@test`: ``` 7 passed in 655.52s TestUnifiedHybridBitExact 354s 3 cases, avg_kl_div=0.0 TestUnifiedHybridLazyBitExact 129s 3 cases, avg_kl_div=0.0 TestUnifiedHybridHiCacheBitExact 142s 1 case, avg_kl_div=0.0 ``` `est_time` goes 600 -> 790 from that measurement: the two pre-existing classes take 496s against the current 600, and the same ratio on 655s is 790. The new class adds only 129s because it reuses a warm model. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31955574489](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955574489)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31955574352](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955574352)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: ispobock

signal.title: [Diffusion] Fix H3 swap PEFT SwiGLU lora_B halves when loading FFN Lora
signal.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3 fuses SwiGLU `gate` / `up` into one `(28672, 5376)` matrix. The two official layouts store that fused tensor with opposite row order: - diffusers / LightX2V: `ff.net.0.proj` = `[up; gate]` - sglang native: `mlp.fc1` = `[gate; up]` Loading a LightX2V LoRA already renames `ff.net.0.proj` → `mlp.fc1`, but does not swap `lora_B` rows. Shapes match and nothing errors, so the FFN adapter is applied with the two halves reversed. Attention LoRA is unaffected. The two layouts are defined by the `forward` implementations: diffusers [`SwiGLU`](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/v0.37.0/src/diffusers/models/activations.py#L143-L146) (`ff.net.0.proj`): ```python hidden_states, gate = hidden_states.chunk(2, dim=-1) return hidden_states * self.activation(gate) # [up; gate] ``` sglang [`_silu_mul`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py#L271-L272) (`mlp.fc1`): ```python gate, up = hidden.chunk(2, dim=-1) return F.silu(gate) * up # [gate; up] ``` The MiniMax-H3 repo ships the same DiT twice, which confirms the row-order mismatch is in the official weights, not a sglang-only convention: - `FL2VA/transformer/` → `blocks.N.mlp.fc1.weight` (what sglang loads) - `transformer/` → `transformer_blocks.N.ff.net.0.proj.weight` (what LightX2V trains against) | tensor | as-is | after swapping the two 14336-row halves | |---|---|---| | fused FFN `fc1` / `ff.net.0.proj` (52 / 52 blocks) | 0 exact | **52 / 52 exact** | | `fc2` / `ff.net.2` | exact | n/a | They are the same model: native fused `qkv_proj` is bit-identical to diffusers `to_q/to_k/to_v` after the documented per-head `[q,k,v]` pack. LightX2V's own two exports of the same adapter repeat the same signature: | | as-is | swapped | |---|---|---| | `fc1` `lora_A` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a | | `fc1` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | 0 exact | **50 / 50 exact** | | `fc2` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a | `lora_A` lives on the input side, so it does not need a row swap. ## Modifications Swap the two 14336-row halves of `lora_B` only on the `ff.net.0.proj.lora_B` → `mlp.fc1.lora_B` path in `load_lora_adapter`. Leave `lora_A` and `fc2` unchanged. Native fused `mlp.fc1` keys and other models' `ff.net.0.proj` (e.g. Flux) do not match both sides of the guard, so they are not rewritten. ## Accuracy Tests Prompt: `A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves.` Config: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA + `lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo` (`minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_4step_v0.1.safetensors`), 1344×768 / 5 s, `seed=1101`, `lora_scale=0.0625`, `flow_shift=12`, `audio_flow_shift=3`, one H200. Same LoRA, 4-step and 8-step, before vs after this change. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37ee7943-0d37-462a-96c3-fc2be88fca26 Before the fix the fur is smeared; after the fix hair, face, and eyes resolve. Audio RMS also rises (4-step 0.0063 → 0.0097, 8-step 0.0067 → 0.0129). Latency and peak memory are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31880164198](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880164198)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31880164099](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880164099)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: zhihengy

signal.title: [Feature] Bit-exact correctness coverage for Unified Radix Cache
signal.text: ## Motivation Cache correctness is difficult to verify from model output alone. A corrupted KV block or recurrent-state checkpoint can still produce fluent text, and the resulting numerical drift can remain far below the tolerance used by accuracy and KL tests. These failures have shipped because the existing signals are approximate. Bit-exact logprob consistency turns one of these approximate signals into a correctness oracle. `kl_test_utils` evaluates the same token through prefill and decode. If both paths are batch-invariant and compute the same function, they must produce identical logprobs. Once that baseline is established, the contract for every cache-reuse path becomes: > **Any nonzero KL is a KV/state reuse bug.** This is stronger than threshold-based testing. It does not ask whether the error is large enough to matter to a benchmark. It asks whether restoring cached state is exactly equivalent to recomputing it. Bugs that previously sat below a model-specific noise floor become unambiguous regressions. Examples: - Incorrect reused state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34184, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29792 ## Foundation Bit-exactness depends on the model and execution path. Deterministic inference can remove batch-dependent kernel and communication behavior, but it cannot make two mathematically different algorithms identical. For example, Qwen3-Next uses different GDN kernels for prefill and decode, and retains a nonzero numerical floor. Inkling provides the combination needed for continuous gating. Its prefill and decode paths compute the same function, so under deterministic inference its prefill-versus-decode KL is exactly `0`. A shrunken checkpoint runs on one GPU. The model also contains `FULL`, `SWA`, and `MAMBA` cache components, so one test process exercises full KV, sliding-window, and recurrent-state reuse together. The resulting foundation has four layers: 1. deterministic execution makes repeated computation batch-invariant; 2. logprob consistency establishes an exact prefill/decode baseline; 3. cache tests apply that baseline to each state restoration path; 4. revert-then-red validation proves that each regression guard can detect the defect it claims to cover. Supporting work: - Inkling deterministic execution: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33417, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34159 - Workflow tools: [KL consistency test skill](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/.claude/skills/kl-consistency-test), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34169 - Real-weight consistency coverage: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34168, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34356 - Per-commit guards: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34607 - Calibration and follow-up validation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34405, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653 ## Roadmap The remaining work is coverage, not a new testing method. Every feature that can save, move, or restore model state introduces a distinct correctness boundary and needs its own exact-KL test class. - [x] Base cache path - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer` - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer_lazy` - [x] HiCache multi-turn - [ ] Speculative decoding - [ ] MTP - [ ] DSpark / DFlash @alphabetc1 - Support return_logprob - [ ] Unified memory

signal.title: [Fix] Correct dense FP8 Marlin bias ordering
signal.text: ## Motivation Dense FP8 Marlin preparation permuted the bias into the Marlin tile layout. However, the dense wrapper does not pass bias into the Marlin GEMM; it adds bias after the kernel returns. The post-GEMM addition therefore requires the original logical output-channel order. The old behavior produces incorrect biased projections, including the Qwen2 QKV projection. ## Modifications - Keep dense FP8 Marlin bias in logical output-channel order. - Continue wrapping the loaded bias as a non-trainable parameter. - Add a CPU-only regression test in the source-mirrored marlin_utils_fp8 test module. This applies to all biased dense FP8 Marlin layers. Fused MoE bias handling is unchanged because it follows a separate kernel path. ## Accuracy Tests Added a CPU-only regression test that uses a non-uniform bias and verifies that Marlin preparation preserves its channel order. Local validation: - python3 -m py_compile passed for the changed source and test files. - git diff --check passed. - The unit test was not executed locally because the available Python environment does not include PyTorch or pytest; CPU CI will execute it. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The inference-time path is unchanged, and preparation removes an unnecessary bias permutation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit guidance. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests guidance. - [x] Documentation is not required for this internal correctness fix. - [x] Accuracy and speed impact are described above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31955054834](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955054834)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31955054569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955054569)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 CUTLASS MoE
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion. This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in: ```bash --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 ``` The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged. Related work: - SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816 - FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738 ### FlashInfer version requirement This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP. The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI. The new option therefore requires both: - `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18` - `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change. GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431. ## Modifications ### Runtime selection and compatibility - Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`. - Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90. - Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior. - Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths. - Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI. - Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility. ### Weight preprocessing - Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing. - Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer. - Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2. - Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules. - Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range. - Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path. ### Kernel invocation Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API: 1. FC1 folded weight block scales 2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation 3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale 4. FC2 folded weight block scales 5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale. ### Tests and benchmark - Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with: - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales - EP rank with global expert IDs - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18 - Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare: - SGLang Marlin W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16 - FlashInfer Humming W4A8 - Update the server-argument documentation. ## Accuracy Tests The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed: ```bash python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v ``` ```text 18 passed, 1 skipped ``` The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \ --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` DeepSeek-V4 accuracy was evaluated using the same 200-example GSM8K setup as SGLang #24816. Both runs used the same TP=4 configuration, dataset, sampling parameters, and server options; only `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision` changed between `bf16` and `fp8`. ```bash PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang_dev/python \ python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --port 30000 \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 200 \ --api chat \ --max-tokens 1024 \ --num-threads 32 \ --temperature 0 \ --gsm8k-data-path /tmp/gsm8k-test.jsonl ``` | MoE precision | GSM8K score | Total latency | Output throughput | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | W4A16 (`bf16`) | 0.985 | 37.301 s | 611.809 token/s | | W4A8 (`fp8`) | 0.985 | 32.952 s | 683.574 token/s | W4A8 preserved the W4A16 GSM8K score while reducing evaluation latency by 11.7% and increasing output throughput by 11.7%. The score also matches the 0.985 W4A16 result reported in SGLang #24816. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The downstream benchmark uses the GPT-OSS-like shape from SGLang #24816: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, and top-k 6. Each FlashInfer path was fully autotuned, followed by 5 warmup iterations and 30 timed iterations. The remaining token shapes were run in parallel with one independent shape per H20 GPU; each W4A16/W4A8 pair ran on the same GPU. The benchmark can be reproduced with FlashInfer 0.6.18+: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python:/path/to/flashinfer \ FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py ``` Results on NVIDIA H20-3e: | Tokens | CUTLASS W4A16 median (min) | Humming W4A8 median (min) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 | 0.275 ms (0.272 ms) | 0.164 ms (0.162 ms) | 1.68x | | 16 | 0.842 ms (0.840 ms) | 0.463 ms (0.460 ms) | 1.82x | | 64 | 1.894 ms (1.892 ms) | 1.037 ms (1.019 ms) | 1.83x | | 256 | 2.410 ms (2.403 ms) | 1.478 ms (1.383 ms) | 1.63x | | 1024 | 3.912 ms (3.906 ms) | 2.093 ms (1.999 ms) | 1.87x | | 2048 | 6.973 ms (6.954 ms) | 3.394 ms (3.384 ms) | 2.05x | | 4096 | 13.013 ms (12.971 ms) | 6.295 ms (6.210 ms) | 2.07x | | 8192 | 25.624 ms (25.546 ms) | 12.308 ms (12.293 ms) | 2.08x | Humming W4A8 was faster at every measured token count, with speedups ranging from 1.63x to 2.08x. The gain reaches approximately 2.0x for token counts of 2048 and above. The GSM8K latency and throughput numbers above provide an end-to-end serving sanity check, but the kernel benchmark is the more controlled performance comparison because generated output lengths are not fixed. ## Scope and Limitations - The implementation is SM90-only. - It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path. - A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update is required before production enablement. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions. - [x] Update server-argument documentation. - [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18. - [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result. - [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31955085259](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955085259)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31955085154](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955085154)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [JIT Kernel] Migrate causal_conv1d_fwd and causal_conv1d_update from AOT to JIT
signal.text: ## Motivation Move `causal_conv1d_fwd` / `causal_conv1d_update` off the prebuilt `sgl_kernel` wheel and onto the JIT kernel infra, keeping the in-place contract, the exported ops, and bit-level numerics. Both sit on the prefill/decode path of every short-conv hybrid model — LFM2 / LFM2-MoE, Mamba2, GDN. ## Modifications - Device kernels move into `kernels/jit/csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cuh` unchanged; only the host launchers switch to the tvm-ffi `TensorView` API. Strides stay `uint32_t` elements, as in the AOT `ConvParamsBase`. - The JIT build matches the wheel's arch split — `-use_fast_math` on SM 9.0, precise math elsewhere, per `load_utils.py`'s `compute_capability == 90` — so the SiLU epilogue emits the same bits. Math mode is part of the build key. - CUDA serving goes through the JIT registry behind a `torch.compile`-compatible custom op; everything else keeps Triton. The AOT ops stay exported for external users and for the differential test. - Only a JIT/CUDA spec is registered, since the AOT kernel was CUDA-only anyway — `csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cu` sits in the CUDA CMakeLists and nowhere else, and `common_extension_rocm.cc` never defined the ops. ROCm and MUSA were already landing on Triton through the old `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.causal_conv1d_update` probe; now they get there directly via `_HAS_CONV1D_KERNEL = is_cuda()`. Nothing changes on any device. - The AOT `cudaFuncSetAttribute` branch goes away behind a `static_assert`: every instantiation sits near 4 KB of shared memory, nowhere near the 48 KB it existed to raise. - `width` outside 2..4 now raises in prefill, where the AOT `if`/`else if` chain had no `else` and quietly did nothing. - `has_initial_state` gets a dtype check. The kernel reads it as `const bool*`, and `kDLBool` has no C++ trait, so it lands as a `CHECK_HOST` on the dtype code rather than a matcher clause. - Tests and benchmarks move to the registered kernel layout, and the superseded AOT-only test is gone. ## Accuracy Tests `pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py` | | H200 (SM90, fast-math) | GB300 (SM103, precise-math) | |---|---|---| | Total | 473 passed, 12 skipped | 473 passed, 12 skipped | | Bit-exact vs AOT (72 cases) | pass | pass | | Reference vs `F.conv1d` (393 cases) | pass | pass | Two machines because the kernel picks its math mode by arch, so each one compiles a different build. The 12 skips are the same deliberate guard on both: the circular-buffer reference can't arbitrate when `seqlen > state_len`, where `scatter_` hits duplicate indices. Behind those counts, the reference tests cover FP32/FP16/BF16 × widths 2–4 × seqlens 1–4096, varlen (per sequence) and non-varlen, both conv-state layouts, gathered slots. The differential is one config per dispatch path, narrowed from a ~900-config sweep that came back bit-identical to AOT throughout. On GB300 the SiLU epilogue — where a math-flag mismatch would show up — gives `max_abs_diff = 0.000e+00`. Also checked: `pad_slot_id` slots untouched, bad dtype / width / non-bool mask rejected, `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` bit-identical to eager, and `LiquidAI/LFM2-350M` serving end to end (GSM8K 200q = 0.325, H200). B200 is registered in `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/mamba/bench_causal_conv1d.py` — FP16/BF16, `dim` 2048–8192, prefill seqlens 128–8192 (4-sequence varlen batch), decode batch 1–256 with gathered slots. 24 configs each. | | prefill geomean | prefill range | prefill wins | decode geomean | decode range | decode wins | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | H200 (SM90) | **1.063x** | 1.022x – 1.122x | 24/24 | 1.001x | 0.995x – 1.015x | 14/24 | | GB300 (SM103) | **1.041x** | 1.015x – 1.062x | 24/24 | 1.000x | 0.987x – 1.013x | 10/24 (3 tied) | - Prefill wins every config on both machines. GB300 extremes: BF16 `(512, 2048)` 22.09 vs 22.41 us, BF16 `(2048, 8192)` 84.90 vs 90.16 us. - Decode is a wash, and those win counts are noise rather than a result: 23/24 configs on H200 and 20/24 on GB300 land within ±1% either way, three of them exact ties. The decode kernel is unchanged, so neither direction means anything. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing documentation change is required.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Support decode radix cache on DeepSeek-V4 (hybrid-SWA, SWA-tail prealloc)
signal.text: ## Motivation `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` is unconditionally rejected for **every** hybrid-SWA model in `build_kv_cache`: ``` ValueError: --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache is incompatible with sliding window attention (SWA) models ``` But `disaggregation/decode.py` already implements a full **SWA-tail-prealloc decode-radix path** (`DecodeTransferQueue._uses_swa_tail_prealloc` → `_swa_tail_len` / `alloc_extend_swa_tail`) for pools whose allocator exposes `alloc_extend_swa_tail` with `page_size > 1` (e.g. `SWAKVPool` / `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool`): decode receives the full KV for full-attention layers and only the sliding-window tail for SWA layers, which is compatible with the prefix-match-and-lock allocation path. The blanket guard is stale — even `server_args` help documents decode radix as incompatible only with `--enable-hisparse`, speculative decoding, and the fake transfer backend, **not SWA**. As a result, decode-side prefix reuse is unavailable on DeepSeek-V4 and other SWA-tail-capable models, forcing redundant KV transfers. ## Modifications 1. **`mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.build_kv_cache`** — only reject SWA models whose allocator lacks the SWA-tail-prealloc capability (`hasattr(allocator, "alloc_extend_swa_tail") and page_size > 1`). Mamba/SSM stays rejected. 2. **`mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.UnifiedRadixCache.cache_unfinished_req`** — fix a fatal assert on hybrid-SWA decode radix. `match_prefix()` gates device indices on **all** components, so the SWA validator collapses `device_indices` to length 0 at the first out-of-window tombstone for a long prefix whose full-attention KV is entirely device-resident (`new_prefix_len=<full>, len(new_indices)=0`). Re-point the still-generating request onto the ungated **FULL-component** indices via a read-only walk of the just-inserted path, and protect the deepest full node from eviction. SWA reuse stays correctly window-gated everywhere else. ## Validation Tested on **DeepSeek-V4** (hybrid-SWA, `page_size=256`, `--attention-backend dsv4`) in a 1P1D PD-disaggregated (mori backend) agentic sweep on MI355X: - The startup guard clears; no `cache_unfinished_req` assert fires. - Decode server serves with **~93–96% decode-side prefix-cache hit** and **0 request errors** over the full profiling window. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Provide a description and validation for this change. - [ ] (Maintainers) Run/extend CI for the decode-radix + SWA path. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31953756304](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31953756304)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31953756227](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31953756227)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [VLM] Reuse Kimi-K3 embeddings before normal-serving preprocessing
signal.text: ## Summary This PR is now limited to **ordinary serving**. EPD reuse is split into #35033; metrics and the agentic benchmark harness are split into #35034. - acquires per-image embedding-cache leases on the request final DP route before processor dispatch - omits a feature only when every required TP rank has pinned the same full feature identity - transfers lease ownership to the admitted request; consume, cancel, abort, flush, timeout, and one internal cold-path retry release pins safely - lets repeated Kimi-K3 images skip processor work, feature transport, and ViT in ordinary serving - keeps CPU, CUDA IPC, and CUDA VMM paths compatible; a featureless hit does not allocate an IPC/VMM proxy or a new fixed HBM pool - uses typed processor contracts rather than model-name branches or dynamic attribute probing - adds the canonical VLM preprocessing-cache guide, API examples, model-support guidance, server arguments, and a concise K3 Cookbook reference ## Correctness boundary False hits fail closed under the default configuration: - media identity covers the exact bytes plus modality, processor configuration, backend, and per-image preprocess options - the artifact identity is bound to the processor-output hash; the compact embedding key only selects a candidate and the full feature identity must still match - K3 namespaces Radix prefix KV by ordered full feature identities, so legacy 30-bit pad-sentinel collisions cannot share language-model KV - mutable paths and URLs are re-read and re-hashed; same path with changed bytes misses - partial TP hits, expired leases, and lost leases fall back once to the feature-carrying cold path - feature-hash disagreement clears the stale processor artifact and rejects reuse - caller-provided legacy `mm_hashes` cannot redirect artifact, lease, embedding-cache, or Radix identity `--trust-mm-content-hashes` is the explicit exception: a trusted hot hit can skip reading the media source, so correctness is delegated to the caller. Without it, SGLang reads the actual media bytes, verifies a supplied SHA-256 digest, and rejects mismatches. ## Normal-serving performance Full real-weight Kimi-K3 (1.56 TB), 2 nodes × 4 NVIDIA GB300, TP8, commit `25eae3c909d7`. Each cell is the median of 3 runs over 32 conversations × 8 turns. The same seeded random image set (512²–2048²) is resent on every turn. Both sides use the same 4096 MiB lazy embedding-cache cap and automatic CUDA VMM/FABRIC feature transport; the A/B switch is K3 auto versus `--mm-preprocess-cache-size-mb 0`. Four random images, concurrency 32, 16 output tokens: | Request rate | Output tok/s off → on | Median TTFT off → on | Median E2E off → on | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 53.29 → 100.14 (+87.9%) | 5846 → 1122 ms (-80.8%) | 6364 → 1479 ms (-76.8%) | | 4 | 53.83 → 109.46 (+103.3%) | 6128 → 1148 ms (-81.3%) | 6721 → 1482 ms (-78.0%) | | 8 | 55.53 → 107.57 (+93.7%) | 5830 → 1174 ms (-79.9%) | 6294 → 1502 ms (-76.1%) | | inf | 54.33 → 106.05 (+95.2%) | 5973 → 1133 ms (-81.0%) | 6366 → 1479 ms (-76.8%) | The saturated A/B was repeated on the same nodes: duration fell from 75.39 s to 38.62 s, and median hot-turn TTFT fell from 5956 to 1147 ms. Across 896 hot images, processor calls, feature transport, and ViT forwards were all skipped. Aggregate preprocess-stage time fell from 194.28 s to 24.56 s (-87.4%). The CPU cache held 128 entries / 62,692 bytes with no eviction. Peak HBM was 257,304 MiB cache-on versus 265,202 MiB cache-off; this feature adds no fixed HBM reservation. These numbers establish the cache A/B, not best absolute production throughput: both sides pinned Marlin because the environment automatic TRT-LLM Gen SiTU path hung after one run. ## Validation - changed Python files compile; changed-file pre-commit, registered-test validation, and documentation checks pass - focused tests cover media mutation, cross-input-form identity, processor/backend/config changes, tensor/PIL metadata, duplicates, reordering, partial hits, single-flight, lease pin/timeout/cancel/flush, partial TP hits, retry, and Radix/pad collisions - full-real-weight 2-node GB300 validation passed 11 ordinary-serving identity cases with zero request errors and matching cold/hot prompt/output tokens, finish reasons, and usage - local macOS pytest collection is blocked by an older Transformers package (`transformers.image_processing_backends` is unavailable); the new Linux CI head runs the focused unit suite ## Stack 1. #34398 — media identity, API, bounded LRU, and single-flight infrastructure 2. #34404 — typed K3 per-image artifacts 3. this PR — ordinary-serving scheduler lease and embedding reuse 4. #35033 — EPD early reuse (draft) 5. #35034 — metrics and agentic benchmark coverage (draft) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31952160111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31952160111)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31952159866](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31952159866)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: mickqian

signal.title: [diffusion] fix: make MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache rebuild transactional
signal.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3 can rebuild AdaLN outputs from checkpoint weights on demand and memoize the resulting timestep plans across requests. Two cache bookkeeping paths could leave the cache inconsistent: 1. When a new request exceeded `max_plans`, the cache cleared all resident plans but rebuilt only the plans that had been missing before the clear. If the request also reused an existing plan, that plan disappeared from the slab and its later lookup failed during denoising. 2. A plan was added to the host-side `_slots` index before all checkpoint reads and projections completed. If rebuilding raised midway, a retry treated the incomplete plan as a cache hit, skipped rebuilding it, and then failed because its zero `plan_lengths` entry remained invisible to lookup. The cache also accepted non-positive plan capacities, which could create degenerate slabs and fail later with less actionable errors. ## Modifications - Rebuild every plan required by the current request after a capacity reset, including plans that were cache hits before the reset. - Validate the request's plan count and width before clearing resident cache metadata, so an invalid request does not destroy a usable cache. - Keep new slot assignments in a pending host-side map while checkpoint weights are read and projected. - Publish `_slots` only after every layer has been written and the corresponding `plan_lengths` entries have been activated. A failed rebuild therefore leaves the incomplete slots invisible and allows a later request to retry. - Reject non-positive `max_plans` and `max_plan_width` values at cache construction time. ## Accuracy Tests The change only updates cache admission and metadata publication. It does not change timestep embeddings, checkpoint reads, tensor-parallel sharding, GEMM shapes, collectives, or cached output tensors. - Forced the capacity-reset path with a request containing both a previously resident plan and a new plan. All plans required by the request remained available to lookup after rebuilding. - Checked 470,367,744 AdaLN output elements against resident `adaln_proj` projections at both TP1 and TP2: zero mismatches. - Compared online-rebuild and resident-weight end-to-end outputs at TP1 and TP2. For both cold and cached cases, the online-rebuild MP4 MD5 matched the corresponding resident-weight run. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This is a correctness-only cache bookkeeping change. The normal successful rebuild path performs the same checkpoint reads, projections, and collectives as before. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31926449143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31926449143)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31926448971](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31926448971)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: reset batch_is_full after prefill-only filter_batch
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #22518 - **Bug**: Embedding/reward models (prefill-only) permanently deadlock after processing one full batch. When requests fill `max_running_requests`, `batch_is_full` is set to `True`. For prefill-only models, completed requests are removed via `filter_batch()` on `running_batch` (line 2306-2307), but `batch_is_full` is never reset. This causes `get_new_batch_prefill()` to return `None` forever (line 2401), blocking all subsequent requests. - **Fix**: After `filter_batch()` for prefill-only batches, reset `batch_is_full = False` when the batch size decreases. This mirrors the existing pattern at lines 2286-2287 that already does this for the `last_batch` filter path. - **Test**: Added unit tests covering the deadlock scenario (all requests finish), partial filtering, and non-prefill-only batch behavior. ## Changes - `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: 3-line fix in `get_next_batch_to_run()` — record batch size before `filter_batch()`, reset `batch_is_full` if size decreased - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_embedding_batch_full.py`: New unit test file with 4 test cases ## Reproduction (from issue) ```bash sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \ --is-embedding --max-running-requests 2 --port 8234 # This request sends 3 inputs but max-running-requests=2, triggers deadlock: curl http://127.0.0.1:8234/v1/embeddings \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B","input":["a","b","c"]}' ``` ## Test plan - [ ] Unit tests pass (`pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_embedding_batch_full.py`) - [ ] Verify with embedding model that requests above `max_running_requests` no longer hang - [ ] Verify normal (decode) model behavior is unaffected 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.text: ## Summary Replace SHA256 with xxhash64 for radix cache block hashing in `hash_page()` and `get_hash_str()`. xxhash64 is ~7.7x faster than SHA256 for non-cryptographic hash operations. The radix cache hashing is called on every KV cache store/remove operation, making this a meaningful hot-path optimization. ## Changes - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py`: Replace `hashlib.sha256()` with `xxhash.xxh64()` in `RadixKey.hash_page()` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/utils.py`: Replace `hashlib.sha256()` with `xxhash.xxh64()` in `get_hash_str()` - `python/pyproject.toml`: Add `xxhash>=3.0.0` dependency ## Test plan - [ ] Existing radix cache unit tests pass - [ ] KV cache store/evict operations work correctly with new hash - [ ] Benchmark shows meaningful improvement in cache operations 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: fix(security): harden SafeUnpickler with exact-name allowlist for generic modules
signal.text: ## Motivation [CVE-2026-15969](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-359v-m36h-r94v) is an unauthenticated RCE via `/load_lora_adapter_from_tensors`: `SafeUnpickler.find_class()` used prefix allowlists + a deny-list, so reflective chains (`builtins.__import__` + `getattr`, `operator.attrgetter` + `pickletools.sys`, `sglang.srt.utils.common.dynamic_import`, `io_struct._maybe_unwrap_pickle(PickleWrapper(evil))`) all reach `os.system()` despite the deny-list. A rejected malicious payload also crashed the scheduler loop (DoS). ## Related work [#30423](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30423) (fixes [#30165](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30165)) targets the same root cause by extending the deny-list. As a blocklist it is inherently incomplete — we confirmed on a patched build that the `dynamic_import` and `io_struct` nested-pickle chains still execute. This PR takes the allowlist direction and closes those remaining bypasses. ## Modifications - `common.py`: exact-name allowlist for generic modules (drop `builtins.`/`operator.`/`pickletools.` prefix trust); drop all `sglang.srt.*` prefix trust, keep an exact `(module, symbol)` allowlist for `FlattenedTensorBucket`/`FlattenedTensorMetadata`/`LocalSerializedTensor`; deny `torch.load`/`hub.load`/`cpp_extension.load*`/`jit.load`; add `deserialize_tensor_payload` (safetensors preferred, hardened-pickle fallback). - `http_server_engine.py`: HTTP client sends base64 safetensors. - `tp_worker.py`: deserialize via `deserialize_tensor_payload`; normalize safetensors `dict` to `(name, tensor)` pairs. - `scheduler.py`/`weight_updater.py`: try/except around deserialization (rejected payloads no longer crash the server). - `http_server.py`: `@auth_level(ADMIN_OPTIONAL)` on `/load_lora_adapter_from_tensors`, matching the other admin LoRA endpoints. - `test_safe_unpickler.py`: tests for the original chain, operator/pickletools, dynamic_import, io_struct nested-pickle, torch.load denial, safetensors round-trip, benign round-trips. ## Accuracy / Speed Tests Not applicable. signal.title: O(1) slot allocation in DecodeReqToTokenPool.alloc()
signal.text: ## Motivation `DecodeReqToTokenPool.alloc()` (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py`) has the same free-slot bookkeeping shape as `ReqToTokenPool.alloc()` (fixed in [#32208](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32208)), and the same drawback: it selects free request-slots from the **head** of `self.free_slots` and rebuilds the list from the remainder (`self.free_slots = self.free_slots[need_size:]`). CPython slicing always allocates a new list and copies the surviving `PyObject*` pointers, so this line is O(len(free_slots)) — proportional to how many free slots *remain*, not to how many are being allocated (`need_size`). This pool is decode-side-specific to PD disaggregation: unlike plain `ReqToTokenPool`, it also carries slots for requests that are pre-allocated or mid-transfer from the prefill side (`_alloc_size = size + pre_alloc_size + 1`), so at steady state under high concurrency `free_slots` is not just pool-sized but *larger* than the running-request cap, and stays long precisely in the regime PD disaggregation is meant to help (high concurrency headroom, trickle admission per scheduler step). `alloc()` runs once per scheduler step that admits new decode-side requests, on the single-threaded scheduler process that gates GPU dispatch — so this is wasted allocation-dominated CPU cost on every scheduler iteration, worse than the non-PD case because `pre_alloc_size` inflates the pool further. `free()` is already O(1) amortized (`self.free_slots.append(...)`) and is unaffected. ## Modifications - Pop from the **tail** of `free_slots` instead of the head (`select_index = self.free_slots[-need_size:]; del self.free_slots[-need_size:]`), which only touches the `need_size` removed elements — O(need_size) instead of O(len(free_slots)). - Allocation order has no semantic meaning (`req_pool_idx` is an opaque row index into `req_to_token`/`req_generation`; `req_generation` already tracks reuse separately), so this is a pure performance change, not a behavior change. - Added an explicit `need_size == 0` guard: `free_slots[-0:]` is the *entire* list, not `[]` (`-0 == 0`), so the naive tail-pop would silently drain/return the whole free pool whenever every request in a batch is reusing its slot (e.g. a chunked-prefill continuation batch on the decode side). The guard makes `select_index = []` in that case — same footgun and same fix as `ReqToTokenPool.alloc()`. - No change to `free()`, `available_size()`, `clear()`, `write()`, or the public `free_slots` attribute's type/semantics. - Scoped to `DecodeReqToTokenPool` only. It does not subclass `ReqToTokenPool` (it duplicates `alloc`/`free`/`clear` because of the pre-allocation semantics described above), so the `#32208` fix did not already cover it; `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool` inherits from `HybridReqToTokenPool` separately and is unaffected either way. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This is a pure Python-level bookkeeping change to which integer index is handed out from an interchangeable free-slot pool; it does not touch KV cache contents, tensor values, or model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Added `benchmark/scheduler/bench_decode_req_pool_alloc.py`, comparing the old head-pop implementation against the new tail-pop `pool.alloc()` across a sweep of pool sizes (256–16384) and free-slot ratios (10%/50%/90%), independent of batch size. Steady-state result (pool=16384, ~90% free / 14745 free slots, trickle admission batch of 1-4 — the regime a large `--max-running-requests` with PD pre-allocation headroom actually hits): ``` cell old mean old p50 old p99 new mean new p50 new p99 speedup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- pool=16384 free=14745 batch=1 28515 24625 56917 344 250 3707 82.9x pool=16384 free=14745 batch=4 28746 24833 59412 335 250 3374 85.8x ``` Full sweep (256–16384, 10/50/90% free, batch 1 and 4) shows the same monotonic trend as the non-PD fix: speedup grows with pool size and free ratio (1.1x at pool=256/free=10% up to ~86x at pool=16384/free=90%), because the old cost is dominated by `len(free_slots)`, not `need_size`. This is a scheduler-CPU-dispatch-overhead fix, not a GPU-kernel or network-transfer change, so no end-to-end `bench_serving.py` throughput/TTFT numbers are attached — the effect is real but only becomes visible relative to GPU compute / KV-transfer latency at very high concurrency on the decode side. ## Testing Added `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_decode_req_to_token_pool_alloc.py`: ``` test_alloc_exhausts_pool_then_returns_none ... ok test_alloc_free_alloc_roundtrip_no_duplicates ... ok test_alloc_with_all_reqs_reusing_is_noop_on_free_slots ... ok Ran 3 tests in 0.006s OK ``` `test_alloc_with_all_reqs_reusing_is_noop_on_free_slots` is the regression test for the `-0` slicing footgun — confirmed it fails (`available_size()` incorrectly drops from 4 to 0) against a naive tail-pop fix without the `need_size == 0` guard, and passes against the real fix. Confirmed all three tests pass unmodified against the pre-fix head-pop implementation too (it was correct, just slow), so the suite is purely a behavior-preservation + footgun guard, not a change-detector for the performance fix itself. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31834880961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31834880961)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31834880676](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31834880676)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
