signal.title: [Scheduler] Add configurable decode interval after prefill
signal.text: [by Codex] ## Motivation With DP attention, each rank schedules attention work locally while all ranks still participate in the same MoE collective. A rank with repeated chunked-prefill continuation work can therefore keep winning SGLang's prefill-first scheduling decision and starve decode work on peer ranks. In the AgentX workload this left requests waiting while the actual decode batch remained small. The DP-attention MLP-sync all-gather already exposes whether any rank selected an EXTEND batch. Use that globally synchronized signal to enforce a rank-consistent decode interval after prefill. ## Modifications - Add `--prefill-decode-interval N`, defaulting to `0` (disabled, so existing behavior is unchanged). - After an EXTEND batch, defer new prefill scheduling for the next `N` scheduler rounds so the running batch can decode. - Under DP attention, arm the interval from the existing globally synchronized `is_extend_in_batch` flag. Under non-DP scheduling, use the local forward mode. - Validate non-negative values and add focused scheduler/server-argument unit tests. No AIPerf source change is required. The benchmark prototype used the existing per-session routing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This changes batch selection cadence only; it does not change model math or sampling. - Added unit coverage for disabled, non-DP, globally synchronized DP, and decode/non-rearm behavior. - Added server-argument validation coverage. - `python -m py_compile` passed for all modified Python/test files. - The focused pytest command could not collect on the development VM because its base Python environment does not include `torch`/`numpy`; the new tests are registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The equivalent scheduler prototype was evaluated with full 3,600-second DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 AgentX runs on 8x B200 using TP8/DP8/EP8, DP attention, MTP3, and an interval of 16: | Concurrency | Interactivity (tok/s/user) | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | Cache hit | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 56 | 30.75532 | 23,559.05865 | 95.945% | | 84 | 23.24221 | 26,110.24296 | 94.703% | The c84 run completed 7,096 profiled requests with zero request errors. These results validate the equivalent prototype on SGLang v0.5.17; this PR ports the behavior onto current `main` using the existing global DP EXTEND flag. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signal.title: Add distributed exact prompt Top-N logprobs
signal.text: # Add distributed exact prompt Top-N logprobs ## Summary Extend the distributed prompt-logprob path to `top_logprobs_num > 0` without gathering the full prompt vocabulary logits. Before this PR: ```text TP-local logits [rows, vocab / TP] | +-- full-vocab AllGather --> [rows, vocab] | +-- global Top-N +-- normalize selected values ``` With this PR: ```text TP-local logits [rows, vocab / TP] | +-- local Top-N --> [rows, N] values + global token IDs | | | +-- compact AllGather --> global Top-N | +-- distributed row MAX / exp-SUM ----------------> normalize ``` Each TP rank selects local Top-N over valid vocabulary columns, exchanges only fp32 logits and absolute token IDs for those candidates, and selects global Top-N locally. Candidate values use the existing distributed row normalizer. The full-vocabulary gather remains only for sampled rows, where the sampler requires it. Response assembly preserves chunked prefill and heterogeneous per-request `k`, including zero. Target-token and explicit token-ID results continue to use the owner-sharded path. ## Performance evidence Controlled TP4 GLM-5.2 on 4x GB200, one output token, concurrency one, prompt Top-5, and nine explicit token probes. Every fresh server received one full-workload warmup followed by five measured requests in A-B-B-A order (N=10 per path). | Input | Gathered median E2E | Distributed median E2E | E2E time saved | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4K | 0.959 s | 0.497 s | 0.462 s (48.2%) | 1.93x | | 8K | 1.698 s | 0.895 s | 0.803 s (47.3%) | 1.90x | | 16K | 3.554 s | 1.646 s | 1.908 s (53.7%) | 2.16x | Across 4K, 8K, and 16K, the distributed path saves 0.462, 0.803, and 1.908 seconds of client-observed whole-request E2E time at the median. Both paths contain high samples, so median is the primary statistic and raw per-leg samples are retained. The GPU-only logprob interval was not separately instrumented. All measured responses returned the expected prompt Top-N shape: 4,096 rows and 20,475 valid entries at 4K, 8,192 and 40,955 at 8K, and 16,384 and 81,915 at 16K. Stable early-row Top-5 IDs matched the gathered path, with values within `4.8e-7`; target and explicit-token scores agreed within `9.6e-7`. Later rows of the long random GLM-5.2 DSA workload remain nondeterministic on the unchanged server, so focused deterministic tests are the correctness reference. ## Caveats - The optimization applies only to the safe contiguous TP-vocabulary layout established by #34402. Existing fallback behavior remains for unsupported layouts and escape-hatch configurations. - For non-tied rows, Top-N values and IDs match the full-vocabulary result. Returned scores are exact and rank-descending, and IDs are distinct. At an Nth-score tie across shards, all strictly higher-scoring IDs are returned; remaining equal-cutoff IDs are valid alternatives, so their membership and relative order are not promised to match one monolithic `torch.topk` call. The separately returned target-token logprob remains exact. ## Stacked on This change is stacked on #34402 (`ead2bf163`, `Add distributed exact input logprobs`). It uses that PR's owner-sharded target-token lookup, explicit-ID lookup, and distributed row normalizer. ## Other tests CPU Gloo TP=2 coverage validates: - padded vocabulary exclusion; - a forced winner from a different TP rank; - `k=7`, `k=0`, and `k=3` in one chunked batch; - explicit IDs that are local, remote, and an empty-ID request; - sampled-row gathering and chunk stitching. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=99 PYTHONPATH=python python -m unittest discover \ -s test/registered/unit/layers -p test_logprob_fast_input.py -v ``` Result: 7 CPU tests passed; 7 existing CUDA-only tests skipped. The focused CUDA run subsequently passed all 14 tests. `py_compile` and `git diff --check` also pass. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31936547819](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31936547819)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31936547791](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31936547791)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Perf] Restore the 16-token router GEMM threshold on SM10X
signal.text: ## Motivation #29470 dropped `max_router_gemm_tokens` from 16 to 4 on SM10X. That doesn't hold anymore: I re-ran its sweep and the JIT `dsv3_router_gemm` wins every `M` up to 12, ties 13-16. Likely #29783, which swapped the fallback it was measured against (`F.linear` → `linear_bf16_fp32`). Unverified. Speculative decoding never gets the fast path: the router sees `M = batch_size * num_draft_tokens`, so EAGLE 5/1/6 is at `M = 6` from concurrency 1. Plain decode keeps it to concurrency 4. So put it back to the kernel's compiled `1..16` range, the same bound `linear_with_fused_a_gemm` already uses. Literal revert of #29470. ## Speed Tests and Profiling 4x GB300, `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP4, `--quantization modelopt_fp4`. ### M sweep, current main Not an exact replication of #29470's: all 16 points instead of 8, and 8192/1024 instead of 1K/1K. No MTP, so router `M == concurrency`. WITH = JIT forced on, WITHOUT = cuBLAS forced on. | M | ITL WITH | ITL WITHOUT | ΔITL | tok/s WITH | tok/s WITHOUT | Δtok/s | winner | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---| | 1 | 6.63 | 6.85 | −3.21% | 144.13 | 140.08 | +2.89% | JIT | | 2 | 7.21 | 7.54 | −4.38% | 256.41 | 246.73 | +3.92% | JIT | | 3 | 8.18 | 8.51 | −3.88% | 332.53 | 321.75 | +3.35% | JIT | | 4 | 8.11 | 8.44 | −3.91% | 435.57 | 421.00 | +3.46% | JIT | | 5 | 9.28 | 9.53 | −2.62% | 470.70 | 461.76 | +1.94% | JIT | | 6 | 9.56 | 9.80 | −2.45% | 536.96 | 527.81 | +1.73% | JIT | | 7 | 9.87 | 10.09 | −2.18% | 599.41 | 588.15 | +1.91% | JIT | | 8 | 9.81 | 10.04 | −2.29% | 672.72 | 660.05 | +1.92% | JIT | | 9 | 10.81 | 10.94 | −1.19% | 684.09 | 679.03 | +0.75% | JIT | | 10 | 11.10 | 11.23 | −1.16% | 730.54 | 724.47 | +0.84% | JIT | | 11 | 11.40 | 11.51 | −0.96% | 773.95 | 767.62 | +0.82% | JIT | | 12 | 11.31 | 11.39 | −0.70% | 834.13 | 829.49 | +0.56% | JIT | | 13 | 12.20 | 12.18 | +0.16% | 837.63 | 839.08 | −0.17% | tie | | 14 | 12.47 | 12.42 | +0.40% | 872.36 | 875.12 | −0.32% | tie | | 15 | 12.67 | 12.63 | +0.32% | 909.12 | 911.54 | −0.27% | tie | | 16 | 12.57 | 12.55 | +0.16% | 960.27 | 961.61 | −0.14% | tie | Against what #29470 reported: | M | #29470, Jun 2026 | current main | |---:|:---|:---| | 1-4 | JIT +1.0 to 2.1% | JIT +2.9 to 3.9% | | 5 | **cuBLAS +1.8%** | **JIT +1.9%** | | 8 | **cuBLAS +1.7%** | **JIT +1.9%** | | 12 | **cuBLAS +1.7%** | **JIT +0.6%** | | 16 | **cuBLAS +3.4%** | tie | Each column is JIT against the fallback of its day (`F.linear` then, `linear_bf16_fp32` now), so this isn't a controlled A/B against their baseline. Every router call in a run sees the same `M`, so this grid derives any threshold `T`: `perf(T, M) = WITH(M) if M <= T else WITHOUT(M)`. `T = 16` wins or ties everywhere. ### E2E, speculative decoding ``` sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --tp-size 4 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 5 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 ``` ``` python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang \ --model nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts 8 \ --max-concurrency 1 \ --warmup-requests 64 \ --flush-cache ``` 19 runs over 7 server launches (9 before / 10 after): | metric | before (M=6 → cuBLAS) | after (M=6 → JIT) | Δ | |:---|---:|---:|---:| | Benchmark duration | 17.041 s | **16.681 s** | **−2.11%** | | Output token throughput | 480.76 tok/s | **491.13 tok/s** | **+2.16%** | | Mean E2E latency | 2127.7 ms | **2082.7 ms** | **−2.11%** | | Mean TPOT | 1.772 ms | **1.730 ms** | **−2.38%** | | Median ITL | 1.750 ms | **1.710 ms** | **−2.29%** | Ranges don't overlap: slowest run after (16.73 s) beats the fastest run before (16.93 s). signal.title: Prevent Qwen3.5 MTP draft from inheriting GPTQ quantization
signal.text: ## Motivation On RTX Pro 6000 with Qwen3.5 speculative NEXTN serving, using the model from [Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4), I launched the server with: ```bash SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE=float16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path ~/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4/ \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --quantization moe_wna16 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \ --speculative-draft-model-path ~/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4/ \ --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph \ --max-running-requests 1 \ --dtype float16 ``` Before the fix, the draft path still inherited the target checkpoint quantization: ```text Load weight end. elapsed=4.86 s, type=Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP, quant=gptq, bits=4 ``` So `--speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant` was not taking effect for the Qwen3.5 MTP draft model, and the draft path could still inherit GPTQ quantization instead of staying unquantized. This can hurt MTP quality directly. On GSM8K with speculative MTP enabled at `steps=3`, the expected accept length is around 3.5, but with this bug the observed accept length drops below 3, which means the draft model is losing a large part of its speculative benefit. ## Modifications - Preserve explicit draft quantization intent through `ServerArgs` / `ModelConfig`. - Prevent draft-model quantization auto-detection when `--speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant` is explicitly set. - Add a Qwen3.5 MTP runtime fallback to avoid inheriting target checkpoint quantization. - Add a regression test to verify the draft config stays unquantized instead of falling back to the target model quantization. ## Accuracy Tests - Reproduced the issue on RTX Pro 6000 with Qwen3.5. - Verified from logs that the draft model loaded as `quant=gptq, bits=4` before the fix. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Not run. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31672997539](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31672997539)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31672997420](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31672997420)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(npu): split packed MTP HiCache transfers by pool
signal.text: ## Summary - split Ascend packed MTP HiCache transfers across the target and draft device pools - slice the packed host K/V buffer to the matching layer range for each device pool - keep CUDA's existing packed per-layer pointer path unchanged ## Root cause This is a follow-up to #32500 and #34560. It depends on #32500; #34560 is already merged into `main`. #34560 appends the NEXTN/MTP draft KV layers to the target host pool, so the host K/V layer dimension covers `target + draft`. With #32500, Ascend uses the fused `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` path for `page_first_direct`, but the transfer was invoked once with only the target device pool and the full packed host buffer. The target and draft device layers are separate pools, so the device and host layer ranges did not match and the draft KV was not transferred correctly. The CUDA path does not have this problem. It packs target and draft per-layer pointers into one pointer array, and the staged kernels dispatch each host layer through its corresponding device pointer. The Ascend fused operator accepts one contiguous device pool per invocation, so it must be called separately for the target and each draft pool. ## Changes On Ascend, `_npu_transfer_buffers` now walks the target and draft pools, obtains each pool's contiguous HiCache K/V buffers, slices the packed host K/V layer range, and issues one fused H2D or D2H transfer per pool. Ascend no longer attempts to build the CUDA-style packed pointer arrays. ## Validation - focused unit tests on latest `upstream/main`: `2 passed` - NPU packed MHA initialization does not require CUDA pointer arrays - target/draft H2D and D2H transfers use matching host-layer slices - pre-commit on all six files in the stacked diff: passed - Qwen3.6-27B, TP2, Ascend NPU, `page_size=128`, 4 prompts, input 3000/output 512 on latest `upstream/main` (`117edb499`): - NEXTN L2: 4/4 prompts hit 2944 device tokens - NEXTN Mooncake L3: 4/4 prompts hit 2944 storage tokens - L2/L3 replay output IDs were identical (`sha256=80bd5171ccc62c4a8a5c5d0753d31c82437561e89c0df1b12e0738d5b1a61695`) - L2/L3 weighted accept rate was identical at `63.6795%`; weighted accept length was identical at `2.9132` - NEXTN-disabled comparison on the fix stack: L2/L3 each hit 2944 tokens for 4/4 prompts and replay output IDs were identical (`sha256=b2f62b4a23240036f43ec5cceba736b81f06f57f4182e4c579146ec79d4dff34`) Cold generation and cache replay can diverge token-by-token, but the same behavior is present with the L1 radix cache. L2 and L3 replay are identical in both NEXTN modes, so Mooncake L3 does not introduce an additional state-restoration divergence.

signal.text:
# Support LingBot-Video MoE: image-to-video, text-to-image, refiner, and prompt rewriting ## Motivation The initial LingBot-Video MoE 30B-A3B port covered text-to-video. The released checkpoint also ships refiner weights and supports image-to-video and text-to-image, so a deployment today exercises only part of what the model can do. This PR closes that gap. Related issue: #32336 Upstream PR: #32341 ## Design One pipeline serves every task. `task_type` becomes `TI2V`, which makes the input image optional, so the request decides: `image_path` gives image-to-video, omitting it gives text-to-video, `num_frames=1` gives a still. The checkpoint leaves little choice here — `model_index.json` declares a single pipeline class and the registry resolves a single config, so a second class would be unreachable without an extra CLI flag on every image-to-video request. Conditioning uses the frame twice: as visual context for the Qwen3-VL encoder, and as a clean latent pinned to the head of the diffusion latent and rewritten after every scheduler step. The DiT forward signature is untouched. The refiner is the one part behind an explicit `--pipeline-class-name LingBotVideoRefinerPipeline`, since doubling resident DiT weights is a deployment decision rather than a per-request one. It loads from the checkpoint's `refiner/` subfolder by redirecting only the weight path, so the component keeps its `transformer_2` identity and still resolves the transformer loader. Its second pass rebuilds text conditioning without vision tokens because the refiner DiT has no image-conditioning path, drives both posterior samples and the noise draw from one seeded generator, and rejects single-frame requests. Prompt rewriting runs as a stage against an externally served vision language model over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, rather than pulling another 27B model into the diffusion worker. Set `rewriter_url` and free-text prompts get expanded and mapped to JSON in two turns; structured captions pass through untouched, and leaving the URL unset skips the stage. ## Verification Checked against the reference diffusers implementation on the same hardware, checkpoint, seed, and parameters. Cross-GPU comparison is not meaningful for this model — identical code and seed on an H100 and a 5090 produce visibly different motion — so every comparison below is same-hardware. ### Prompts and inputs The DiT consumes a structured JSON caption rather than a plain sentence, so the prompt below is the caption itself. Every run in this section uses seed 42 and the same caption for its task, so a reviewer can reproduce any clip from the served model. ```bash sglang serve --model-path robbyant/lingbot-video-moe-30b-a3b --num-gpus 1 ```

Every sglang number is the second or later run of that task on a resident server, so autotune is warm; for scale, a cold first request costs 0.890 s/step against a warm 0.700 for T2V on H100. sglang numbers are per-stage wall time from the server log. Reference numbers come from its own denoising-loop timer and exclude text encoding and VAE decode. Base pass, 320x192, 121 frames: | Runtime | Hardware | s/step | Denoise | Decode | Text encode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sglang T2V | H100 80GB | 0.700 | 28.0 s | 0.96 s | 0.13 s | | sglang TI2V | H100 80GB | 0.705 | 28.2 s | 0.96 s | 0.19 s | | reference T2V | H100 80GB | 0.95 | 38 s | -- | -- | | reference TI2V | H100 80GB | 0.95 | 38 s | -- | -- | | sglang T2V | 5090 32GB, dit layerwise offload | 2.122 | 84.9 s | 0.96 s | 0.12 s | | sglang TI2V | 5090 32GB, dit layerwise offload | 2.122 | 84.9 s | 0.97 s | 0.19 s | Text to image, 832x480, single frame: | Runtime | Hardware | s/step | Denoise | Decode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sglang | H100 80GB | 0.198 | 7.9 s | 0.06 s | | reference | H100 80GB | 0.30 | 12 s | -- | | sglang | 5090 32GB, dit layerwise offload | 2.122 | 84.9 s | 0.22 s | Across 16 requests all three tasks land on the same 2.122 s/step on the 5090, because layerwise offload streams the whole DiT from host memory every step and the loop is bound by that transfer rather than by sequence length: a single 832x480 frame carries 1560 tokens against 7440 for the 121-frame clip and still costs the same. On H100 without offload the three tasks separate as expected, 0.700 / 0.705 / 0.198. Refiner, 49 frames, 8 refiner steps, t_thresh 0.85, sigma tail 2: | Runtime | Hardware | Refiner res | Base denoise | Upscale | Refine s/step | Refine total | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sglang | H100 80GB, offload | 1920x1088 | 87.2 s | 5.8 s | 20.18 | 163.2 s | | sglang | 5090 32GB, offload | 640x384 | 86.5 s | 1.2 s | 2.17 | 17.6 s | | reference | H100 80GB, 8-way FSDP | 1920x1088 | 121 s | -- | -- | 210 s | Both sglang refiner rows keep layerwise offload on so the two DiTs share one card, which is why their base denoise sits near the 5090 figure rather than the 28 s an H100 reaches without offload. Refiner cost then tracks the refiner resolution rather than the hardware: 1920x1088 is 8.5x the pixels of 640x384 and costs 9.3x per step. Image conditioning, condition frame preprocessing plus a single-frame VAE encode: | Hardware | Resolution | Time | | --- | --- | --- | | H100 80GB | 320x192 | 0.30 s | | 5090 32GB | 320x192 | 0.02 s to 0.06 s | | 5090 32GB | 832x480 | 0.22 s | --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31935743822](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935743822) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31935743723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935743723)

signal.title: [diffusion][Model] Support MAGI-2-preview
signal.text: ## Motivation Relate #35011 Adds native support for [MAGI-2-preview](https://huggingface.co/sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview), SandAI's 114B MoE model that generates a video and its synchronized stereo soundtrack in one denoising trajectory. About 6B parameters are active per token. Audio is not a second pass over finished video: video and audio latents share one packed sequence and one denoise loop. Text-to-video and image+text-to-video are both supported. The checkpoint ships two DiTs. A preview model denoises the clip, and a refiner then takes that result to 1920x1088; the words "preview" and "refiner" below always mean those two. Serving it today means standing up a second stack. The reference implementation launches under `torchrun`, depends on SandAI's own kernels ([MagiAttention](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiAttention), [MagiCompiler](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiCompiler), FlashAttention 3) and so ships as a [Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/sandai/magi-2-preview), and its checkpoint has no `model_index.json`. This PR builds it against SGLang's own layers so it is served like every other family in `sglang.multimodal_gen`. ## Modifications ### New code Four pieces the tree did not already have. Everything else goes through existing machinery. - **Multi-head MoE** (`runtime/layers/moe_multihead.py`). MAGI-2 routes 12 independent heads over 256 experts each, top-6, where the tree's MoE assumes one routing head. Viewing tokens as `[N * 12, 256]` instead of `[N, 12, 256]` makes it a standard MoE with `hidden_size=256` and `num_experts=3072`, so srt's Triton `fused_experts` runs unmodified. MAGI-2's activation, which it calls `swiglu7`, is a sigmoid-gated GELU approximation clamped to ±7 and maps onto that kernel's existing `gemm1_alpha` and `gemm1_clamp_limit`. - **Attention sinks** (`runtime/layers/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`). Both DiTs use one always-attended sink token per sequence, and the FlashAttention backend accepted no `sinks` argument, so those logits were dropped silently. Now plumbed through, along with `window_size`. - **Block-window local attention** (`runtime/layers/attention/magi2_block_grid_attention.py`). Every refiner layer restricts video-to-video attention to a radius-(2,2,2) ball on the 3-D latent block grid, which no `(left, right)` flash window can express, so it is carried as a `flex_attention` `BlockMask` built from tile occupancy rather than through `create_block_mask` and its dense intermediate. - **Multi-stream hyper-connections**, mHC (`runtime/models/dits/magi2_mhc.py`). The preview DiT's residual is 4 parallel streams of 3072 rather than one of 12288, mixed by a per-block matrix that Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization keeps doubly stochastic. ### Reused from the tree Both DiTs are wired to the existing optimizations rather than reimplementing them: - **Ulysses sequence parallelism** carries the packed sequence. Rows are sharded once per forward and gathered at the end, and pad rows from an uneven split get their own varlen segment so real tokens cannot attend to them. - **Expert parallelism** shards the MoE head axis with one all-to-all, through the same `ep_group` plumbing srt's MoE uses. - **Layerwise and CPU offload** via `LayerwiseOffloadableModuleMixin` and `layer_names`, so `--dit-layerwise-offload` and `--cpu-offload-components` work without model-specific code. - `AutoencoderKLWan` for the video VAE (which is what MAGI-2 ships), the UniPC scheduler, FSDP sharding through `_fsdp_shard_conditions`, and the `PipelineStage` / `Req` / `OutputBatch` contracts. ### Structure Eleven stages under `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/magi2/`. Two orderings are load-bearing and easy to break in review: Image encoding runs **before** text encoding, because each conditioning image needs a `<Figure N>` phrase present in the prompt; pooling that phrase's embedding runs **after**, because it needs the encoded prompt. A conditioning image is not the clip's first frame — it is VAE-encoded, parked past the clip on the rope time axis, and bound to the prompt through that pooled embedding. The denoise loop is model-owned rather than delegated to `DenoisingStage`, because video and audio carry separate guidance scales and separate multistep scheduler state, which the shared loop's single-latent contract cannot represent. Compile, residency and warmup still come from the base stage. ### Parallelism `--num-gpus` must divide every head axis, since a rank owns whole heads on all of them: 24 preview attention heads, 12 preview MoE heads, 32 refiner attention heads, 8 refiner GQA key/value heads. The refiner's 8 bind, so the two-stage tier admits 2 or 4 and preview-only admits 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12. All four axes are checked in `validate_server_args`, so a bad count fails at launch instead of inside a collective. 8 GPUs divides three axes but not the preview's 12 MoE heads. The reference handles that by padding the head axis to 16 and giving the spare ranks zero-weight experts; this port rejects the configuration instead, rather than waste two ranks of expert capacity. `--enable-cfg-parallel` is rejected — the denoise loop already runs both branches itself, so splitting CFG across ranks would double-apply the guidance. Expert parallelism is what lets the weights fit, not merely what makes them fast: the preview partition is 228 GB in BF16 and only its expert tensors shard, while the 6.7B refiner is replicated per rank. Below the divisibility rules, how many ranks a given card needs is a memory question — the offload flags above are the lever. ### Deliberate divergences from the reference Both are marked at the site in the code. **The refiner's residual accumulates in BF16, not FP32.** The reference promotes it at the first `down_proj` and holds FP32 through all 30 layers. Matching that roughly doubles the residual's footprint across 30 layers at the 1080p sequence length; BF16 accumulation is the cheaper of the two errors. The refiner's QK-norm likewise stores in BF16 while reducing in FP32, where the preview DiT can afford FP32 through the rotary. **Expert-parallel head padding is not implemented**, as described under Parallelism. ### Docs `docs/cookbook/diffusion/MAGI/MAGI-2.mdx` covers the quality tiers, the parallelism rules, offload recipes, and the stage timings below. Added to the compatibility matrix. ### Known limitations - Only 1920x1088 and 896x512 are accepted, rejected before denoising otherwise. 1088 rather than 1080 because the VAE stride forces multiples of 16. - 10-second clips only; the model was trained for one duration. - `--enable-torch-compile` does not work: inductor autotuning fails on the multi-head MoE GEMMs, asking more shared memory than sm90 has (`triton_mm Required: 262144, Hardware limit: 232448`), and then stalls. The refiner's flex-attention mask is compiled separately and does work. - `--tp-size` and `--ring-degree` are rejected, per the speed tests below. - FlashAttention only. Sinks and the packed varlen path exist nowhere else, so `sage_attn` is rejected rather than silently degraded. - The two-stage tier wants `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`. Its decode asks for one large block while both DiTs are resident, which otherwise tends to fail on fragmentation well into a run. A startup warning fires when it is unset. ## Accuracy Tests ### Side-by-side with the reference implementation Three pairs, each generated twice on the same box with the same weights, the same seed 42, and the same 1920x1088 two-stage tier — once by the reference implementation and once by this PR. The prompts are the reference repository's own long structured captions, used verbatim so nothing depends on prompt wording. **Pair 1, text-to-video.** An 8895-character caption describing a 10-second Japanese-anime-style sequence: a young girl walks from a dark, mist-filled forest into a bright clearing over the ocean, with one deliberate camera cut near the climax. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b734f741-c01f-43ac-bde9-8634b447fb1a - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05fccde8-111a-4162-91ba-4eb31f974b67 **Pair 2, image-to-video.** The same caption as pair 1, plus a still frame as the conditioning image. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fdab8b3-a4f4-4569-983f-5c9087891e51 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19f6148-4c93-4dca-8ef1-c3714fa4242d **Pair 3, image-to-video.** A 10931-character caption describing a stop-motion clay animation — a small clay figure searches a room for a lost red ball and finds it at his feet — plus its conditioning still. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9444c586-ebae-4daa-901a-bd7161e36858 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f8638fd-90cd-4ee1-b824-e3334f99d964 The two are not bit-identical and are not meant to be. The port runs SGLang's own attention, MoE and VAE paths rather than the reference's kernels, and it accumulates the refiner residual in BF16 where the reference uses FP32 — see Deliberate divergences. Frame statistics across the three pairs (contrast, shadow occupancy, spatial detail) land within a few percent of the reference, but they are weak evidence either way; the clips are the thing to look at. ### Prompt coverage Eight prompts in one process, all at 1920x1088 with joint audio, seed 42 — static and fast-moving subjects, interior and exterior, one non-English: - Calm mountain lake at sunrise, mist over still water — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bed79a0e-4a39-42da-a144-fe77765f3ffe - Busy night market in the rain, neon reflected in puddles — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed94afe5-4337-44ce-949a-78abc5f0ae20 - Cellist in an empty concert hall, dust in a shaft of light — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2abb3374-184d-4278-ac9a-0ebb6976df38 - Golden retriever bounding through deep snow, powder spraying — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/728e9d78-5577-4ec3-8eae-d524f9fc66bc - Timelapse of storm clouds over wheat fields — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a677bb13-efca-4aba-932e-ebfdf250e98e - 一位老人在清晨的公园里练太极，动作缓慢舒展 — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79e8bbc7-6970-4007-815b-0b4d0ab987d9 - Blacksmith hammering glowing steel, sparks arcing — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b39855-3163-48eb-af15-677dd499bf0b - Sea turtle gliding over a coral reef, sunlight rippling — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a876691-8373-423b-8ad1-c7096c1bec23 All eight ran without a restart. Every output verified h264 1920x1088 at 25 fps, 249 frames, AAC 44100 Hz stereo, 10.0s. The audio tracks its prompt rather than being generic ambience — the blacksmith clip is 66% silence between strikes, the lake clip is continuous and low-frequency. ### Unit tests 47 unit tests, no GPU required: the MoE router and expert layout, mHC normalization, rope construction and partial rotation, the coordinate builder, packed-sequence layout, the noise schedule the refiner restarts from, guidance arithmetic, the block-grid mask and the block order it must be applied in, sequence bucketing, and the expert-axis sharding predicate. They are flat files under `test/unit/`, so `_discover_unit_tests()` picks them up and they run in the existing suite with no CI change: ``` python3 sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py --suite unit ``` The full 1080p path needs four cards and about ten minutes per clip, so it is not in the suite. ## Speed Tests and Profiling All figures below are one machine's numbers — 4x H200 at `--ulysses-degree 4` with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` — and are meant as relative comparisons, not as sizing targets. **One 1080p clip, 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, text-to-video — 592s total:** text encoding 17.6s, preview denoise 452.8s, the preview-to-refiner handoff under 0.1s, refiner denoise 101.6s, decode 15.5s. Weight load is separate and paid once per process, about 5 minutes for both DiTs. Image-to-video costs more — the conditioning image adds 1680 patch tokens and the longer caption takes 24s to encode — and measures 741s. **Batch stability.** Eight clips of differing prompt length in one process gave refiner times of 101.6, 102.4, 101.0, 101.2, 100.8, 100.4, 101.8 and 103.6s. Flat, which is the property that matters for serving. Text encoding drops from 17.6s on the first clip to about 9s afterwards, as the memory-mapped encoder weights stay in the host page cache. **Tensor parallelism**, preview tier at 896x512, 20 steps, four ranks: pure Ulysses 124.5s; `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` 205.9s; `--tp-size 4` 608.1s, each using more memory per rank than the last. Neither DiT has a column- or row-parallel layer, so `--tp-size` shards no weights and only takes ranks away from Ulysses — those ranks stop sharding the sequence and duplicate full-length work. Rejected at startup rather than left as a footgun. **Sequence length.** The refiner's packed sequence is `video + audio + text + reference`, so its length follows the prompt, and its `flex_attention` mask is compiled per length with each graph retained. Six clips at 4 preview steps, where the first three share a prompt length: - rounding the sequence to a bucket: 100.8, 98.0, 99.4, 103.0, 102.3, 102.2s - using each length verbatim: 102.6, 100.8, 102.0, 174.1, 215.5s, then out of memory Two changes keep the graph count bounded. `Magi2RefinerDiT` rounds the sequence up to a multiple of 1024 rows before sharding, collapsing the whole 0-7000-token prompt range to eight lengths at under 0.4% padding. And `build_mask_mod` carries the valid-row length as a tensor rather than an int, because dynamo guards a captured int by **value** — as an int it recompiles per prompt length even once every tensor shape is identical, and nine distinct values trip the default `recompile_limit` of 8, after which flex_attention falls back to an eager path that materializes the full score matrix. As a tensor, nine values give one graph. `dynamic=True` is not an alternative: the rebuilt closure misses the guard either way and costs 26s per clip. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31935589148](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935589148)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31935589182](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31935589182)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(dsv4): support --dsa-topk-backend flashinfer with fused top-k
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation @humansand **Scope: DeepSeek V4 FlashInfer top-k backend support.** This PR makes `--dsa-topk-backend flashinfer` usable for the DeepSeek V4 indexer. It uses FlashInfer's fused compact-page transform when `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=true` and preserves the existing unfused FlashInfer path when the flag is disabled. The packed PAGED-row prerequisite was merged in [#33006](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33006). DeepSeek V4 adds a compact page table where one page-table entry represents 64 score positions. FlashInfer [#4315](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4315) added the required `page_size`, caller-owned output, raw-index output, and padded-stride support. > **Dependency:** validation below uses FlashInfer [nightly-v0.6.18-20260816](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/nightly-v0.6.18-20260816), which contains #4315. SGLang still needs to bump its FlashInfer dependency and runtime minimum to the first containing stable release before relying on this API from published packages. ## Modifications - Add a fused DeepSeek V4 FlashInfer helper that calls `top_k_page_table_transform` with: - padded-stride score rows without a contiguous materialization; - the compact page table with `page_size=64`; - graph-safe deterministic and tie-break settings; - caller-owned translated and optional raw-index output buffers. - Preserve the existing unfused `flashinfer.top_k` plus vectorized page translation path and select it when `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=false`. - Plan and copy SGL top-k-v2 metadata only when that backend is eligible; FlashInfer and Torch no longer create an unused SGL plan. - Apply the FlashInfer version check uniformly when FlashInfer is selected as either an attention backend or the DSA top-k backend. - Update `bench_topk.py` to benchmark `page_size={1,64}` as a Cartesian axis with a preallocated output while keeping the focused CI value at `K=512`. The expanded performance grid below uses a source-unchanged runtime-axis wrapper. Page size 64 matches the compact CUDA DSA layout; page size 1 is the noncompact baseline. - Extend existing CPU and CUDA-graph tests across fused/unfused routing, `K={512,1024}`, optional raw output, padded score strides, replayed inputs, short rows, and raw/translated alignment. Tests validate only model-visible prefixes rather than imposing a full-tail sentinel contract. ## Accuracy Tests Final validation used SGLang `798019b5dcf815371b4986b84117ad56eff092ae` on one NVIDIA B200: - **Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20260813-273d978b` (`sha256:5e012cc3cfe06fd7718bab6f7b8183fad56df28a6b934058edb4d59afc42d440`; amd64 image `sha256:3983b61256623ab0eecb8af2ca6b38a5fa4ffd0546f66087c46f07a10f3d619d`). - **GPU/runtime:** NVIDIA B200 183,359 MiB; driver 580.126.09; CUDA 13.0.88. - **Python stack:** Python 3.12.3; PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`; `sglang-kernel==0.4.6.post1`; Triton 3.7.1. - **FlashInfer:** release `nightly-v0.6.18-20260816`, tag commit `f4043ef18c92f38e0c70da76ca40b26d36318eed`; `flashinfer-python==0.6.18.dev20260816`; `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.18.dev20260816`; `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.18.dev20260816+cu129`. The image's original FlashInfer 0.6.17 JIT artifact exported the old 12-argument transform and caused the first fused test attempt to fail when the nightly Python wrapper supplied 14 arguments. The final results below use an isolated virtual environment with matching nightly packages. The nightly `+cu129` AOT `topk.so` could not load on this CUDA-13 image because it depends on `libcudart.so.12`; FlashInfer fell back to a local JIT build against CUDA 13.0. Compilation is outside the test's CUDA-graph replay and benchmark timing. Install and test commands: ```bash python3 -m venv --system-site-packages /hai-workspace/sglang-pr33237-bench-venv /hai-workspace/sglang-pr33237-bench-venv/bin/python -m pip install \ --no-cache-dir --upgrade --no-deps \ https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/download/nightly-v0.6.18-20260816/flashinfer_python-0.6.18.dev20260816-py3-none-any.whl \ https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/download/nightly-v0.6.18-20260816/flashinfer_cubin-0.6.18.dev20260816-py3-none-any.whl /hai-workspace/sglang-pr33237-bench-venv/bin/python -m pip install \ --no-cache-dir --upgrade --no-deps \ 'https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/download/nightly-v0.6.18-20260816/flashinfer_jit_cache-0.6.18.dev20260816%2Bcu129-cp39-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl' export PYTHONPATH=/hai-workspace/sglang-pr33237-benchmark/python export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 unset FLASHINFER_TOPK_ALGO SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK /hai-workspace/sglang-pr33237-bench-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py /hai-workspace/sglang-pr33237-bench-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_indexer.py \ -k dsv4_flashinfer_compact_topk_cuda_graph ``` Raw summaries: ```text ......... [100%] 9 passed, 15 warnings, 16 subtests passed in 6.69s . [100%] 1 passed, 12 deselected, 15 warnings, 8 subtests passed in 7.90s ``` The GPU Cartesian product covers `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK={false,true} × K={512,1024} × raw_output={false,true}`. No DeepSeek V4 model-serving accuracy run was performed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Single-GPU operator microbenchmark at SGLang `798019b5dcf815371b4986b84117ad56eff092ae` in the same B200 environment used above: - **Workload:** FP32 random score rows, full uniform lengths, identity page tables, and caller-owned int32 translated-output buffers. Exact Cartesian grid: `K={512,1024,2048} × seq_len={8192,65536,131072} × batch_size={4,8,16,32,64} × page_size={1,64}`. Providers: SGL JIT-v1, SGL JIT-v2, FlashInfer, and PyTorch. JIT-v1 is unavailable at `K=2048` by design. - **Invocation:** the committed benchmark keeps its focused CI value `K=512`. A source-unchanged inline wrapper accepts the four requested axes as command-line arguments and replaces the benchmark's runtime configuration before calling `Benchmark.run()`; the provider list is asserted unchanged. - **Page-table layouts:** page size 64 matches DeepSeek V4's compact C4 transform and the shared SGL JIT-v2 representation. Page size 1 matches the current generic DSA/GLM-5 FlashInfer path, which expands its underlying 64-token KV pages into one table entry per token. - **Timing:** 50 warmups; CUDA-graph replay measured with CUDA events; read inputs rotated and L2 flushed between timed replays; 1,000 requested operator iterations; median microseconds reported. Compilation, JIT-v2 planning, output initialization/allocation, Python/host dispatch, and serving are excluded. - **Repetition:** three independent complete sweeps on the same B200. All 330 timed cells per sweep had a cross-sweep max-minus-min span below 0.41% of their median. - **Backend settings:** `FLASHINFER_TOPK_ALGO` unset (automatic); `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK` unset. The benchmark directly calls the fused FlashInfer API, so this is not a fused-versus-unfused comparison. The tested FlashInfer nightly predates the open CUB TopK PR, so these are not CUB-backend results. Each process emitted the already-documented AOT-to-JIT fallback warning; compilation remained outside timing. signal.title: [KV Cache] Use exact page demand for paged prefill eviction
signal.text: ## Motivation `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend()` overestimates the capacity needed before paged prefill allocation as: ```python extend_num_tokens + batch_size * page_size ``` This ignores free slots in each request's existing partial tail page and can evict reusable prefixes even when the allocation already fits. For example, with `page_size=64`, `prefix_len=63`, and `seq_len=64`, the one-token extend fits in the existing tail page and requires zero new pages. The current estimate still requests 65 token slots of eviction headroom. ## Modifications - Set the paged-prefill eviction target to `get_num_new_pages() * page_size`. - Add CPU regression tests for page boundaries, cached-prefix survival, and a mixed-batch capacity shortfall. ## Accuracy Tests Target regression: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_alloc_extend_eviction.py ``` ```text 3 passed, 15 subtests passed ``` The tests cover page sizes 16, 64, and 128, verify that a zero-new-page extend preserves an evictable `RadixCache` prefix, and check a mixed batch where the eviction shortfall drops from 353 tokens to the exact 32 tokens. Adjacent allocator regression: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_alloc_extend_eviction.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_alloc_extend_page_estimation.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_allocator.py \ -k 'not TestO3FusedAllocBind' ``` ```text 70 passed, 11 deselected, 15 subtests passed ``` `TestO3FusedAllocBind` was excluded locally because its unrelated Triton JIT tests require Python development headers that are not installed on the test host. ## Speed Tests and Profiling One additional CPU `get_num_new_pages()` call costs about 9-10 us per paged extend batch in the local microbenchmark (batch sizes 1-128). Its inputs are CPU tensors, so this does not introduce GPU synchronization. No general throughput improvement is claimed; the change only avoids unnecessary prefix eviction under page-level cache pressure. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing API or configuration change.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31891562985](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31891562985)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31891562818](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31891562818)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion][Model] Support MAGI-2-preview
signal.text: ## Support MAGI-2-preview (joint audio-video generation) [MAGI-2-preview](https://huggingface.co/sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview) is SandAI's 114B MoE diffusion model ([announcement](https://sand.ai/blog/magi-2-preview)). It generates a video and its synchronized stereo soundtrack in one denoising trajectory — the video and audio latents share a single packed sequence — and supports text-to-video and image+text-to-video, at 896x512 or two-stage 1920x1088. Running it today means a separate deployment: the reference implementation launches under `torchrun` and depends on SandAI's own kernel stack, so it ships as a [Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/sandai/magi-2-preview) and cannot be served alongside the model families sglang-diffusion already covers. I would like to add native support for it and to keep it maintained afterwards.

signal.title: [Quantization] Fix GPTQ scheme attachment broken by LinearBase.scheme default
signal.text: ## Summary #29328 added a class-level `scheme = None` to `LinearBase`, turning GPTQ's `if not hasattr(layer, "scheme")` guard into a no-op — the scheme never gets built and every GPTQ checkpoint dies on load with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'create_weights'`. The probe becomes `layer.scheme is None`, which makes that default load-bearing, so it's declared on the other two bases a GPTQ method can be handed (`VocabParallelEmbedding` for a quantized `ParallelLMHead`, `FusedMoE` for gptq_marlin MoE) and `FusedMoE`'s two `hasattr` weight-loader reads flip with it — leaving those would set `method = None` for every unquantized and fp8 MoE layer on reload. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31927156951](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927156951)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31927156871](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927156871)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Speed up MiniMax-H3 VAE decode on 2×H100
signal.text: ## Summary - preserve the existing model-aware `auto` residency thresholds and `memory` mode's layerwise VAE default - make the measured MiniMax-H3 2×H100 CI recipe explicitly select `vae=resident` - tighten the H3 H100 performance baseline to the measured resident-VAE latency - keep canonical and legacy VAE placement overrides compatible and document the placement semantics ## Why - MiniMax-H3 VAE residency adds about 4.8 GiB/GPU, much less than full DiT and encoder residency, so it offers high performance return when that headroom exists. - Layerwise VAE offload repeats decoder transfers for every temporal chunk and spatial tile; residency reduces H3 decode latency from 14.72s to 2.15–2.22s (about 6.8×). - This remains an explicit H3 recipe choice rather than a global default because residency is not numerically interchangeable for every video VAE path; model-aware `auto` thresholds and the conservative `memory` default remain unchanged. ## H3 2×H100 measurement Same 1344×768, 4-second, 7-eval request, two steady-state runs per configuration: | Placement | Denoise | Decode | Pipeline E2E | Peak / GPU | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | DiT + encoder + VAE layerwise | 16.58s | 14.72s | 32.23s | 22.44 GiB | | DiT + encoder layerwise; VAE resident | 16.55s | 2.15–2.22s | 19.63–19.76s | 27.24 GiB | | Full resident | 13.99s | 2.16s | 19.01s | 69.18 GiB | All six generated MP4 files had the same SHA-256 (`f9ae69f5b08314ce5631978d83e4ed9a0a60ebc0286ff29c451941efe9da6faa`). VAE residency is therefore bit-exact for this path and reduces decode latency by about 6.8×, with about 4.8 GiB/GPU additional memory. Full residency provides only about 3% more E2E improvement while using about 42 GiB/GPU more than the selected recipe. A batched-tile experiment was also bit-exact but slower (2.35–2.43s decode), so it is not included. ## Validation - pre-commit hooks - extend server-args coverage for the `memory` VAE default and explicit canonical/legacy overrides - real 2×H100 H3 A/B through the normal `sglang serve` model-loading path <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31928950202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31928950202)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31928950135](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31928950135)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: refactor(hicache): flatten L2 transfer execution
signal.text: **Resolve device↔host work into flat `L2Transfer` commands so the executor and host-pool group no longer recursively dispatch pool transfers, without changing cache behavior.** ### Boundary ```python class L2Transfer(NamedTuple): host_pool: Any device_pool: Any host_indices: torch.Tensor device_indices: torch.Tensor layer_mapper: Optional[Callable[[int], Optional[int]]] = None is_draft: bool = False L2TransferEngine(io_backend).submit_device_to_host( transfers: list[L2Transfer], ) -> TransferCompletion L2TransferEngine(io_backend).submit_host_to_device( transfers: list[L2Transfer], *, layer_num: int, start_event=None, on_layer_done=None, ) -> TransferCompletion ``` ### Ownership - Controllers: allocation, queues, acknowledgements, layer mapping, and `PoolTransfer` resolution. - Engine: execute already-resolved device↔host commands and retain index tensors on its streams. - Host pools: move bytes for one concrete pool. - Storage/L3 and tree lifecycle: unchanged. ### Result - One flat execution boundary for base and hybrid caches. - No nested transfer dispatch in `L2TransferEngine` or `HostPoolGroup`. - Existing concatenated per-pool index tensors continue to feed the same C++/JIT kernels. ### Validation - 2,124 tests run: 1,092 passed, 1,032 skipped, 0 failures. - Compileall, diff check, and all applicable pre-commit hooks pass. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31927917622](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927917622)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31927917545](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927917545)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Validate MiniMax-H3 quality=high on B300
signal.text: ## 0x0. What this PR does Video generation does not need distillation, a different solver, or model surgery to get fast. Keep the weights and the math untouched, be rigorous about *computing less*, and MiniMax-H3 goes from 41.19 s to 11.16 s for a 5-second 1344x768 clip with audio on 8x B300 — with the quality argument written down, gated, and byte-reproducible. Concretely, this PR: - admits the strict 8x B300 TP1/Ulysses8 deployment for MiniMax-H3 request-scoped `quality="high"` - gives each validated deployment its own audited Cache-DiT schedule: 4xH200 keeps the conservative `(4, 0.04, 1)`; **8xB300 ships `(4, 0.08, 3)`**, selected by a parameter sweep on the sglang-native prompt set and gated on LPIPS plus a consecutive-frame temporal review - makes Sol-Attn dense guard steps use the platform-selected FlashAttention implementation (FA4 on Blackwell) and preserves packed-document boundaries on sparse steps - lets the common BCG fail-closed path run before H3 arms Cache-DiT input preservation - documents the protocol, limitations, results, and comparison figure in the cookbook ![MiniMax-H3 B300 quality and latency comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16f604256169b1e9889a3ab4f297883f3f84c15d/docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/assets/minimax-h3-b300-quality-high.png) ## 0x1. Results first Hardware: 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (SM103). Workload: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA T2VA, 1344x768, 124 frames @24 fps, 50 sigma points, video/audio flow shifts 12/3, sglang-native prompts (cookbook example + two benchmark presets), seeds 0/1/2. Latency is the median of three requests after one warmup. This air-cooled node sits on its 1100 W power cap and its sustained-clock regime drifts intraday (~20% on step time), so only same-session ratios are comparable — every row below was measured back-to-back in one session: | Arm | Median latency | Speedup vs Diffusers | LPIPS mean / max vs SGLang lossless | Decision | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Diffusers BF16 dense + Ulysses8 | 41.19 s | 1.00x | 0.347 / 0.465 | baseline | | SGLang lossless | 23.03 s | 1.79x | 0.000 / 0.000 | exact default | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.04, 1) | 16.45 s | 2.50x | 0.101 / 0.129 | superseded on B300 | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.08, 3) | **11.16 s** | **3.69x** | 0.293 / 0.399 | **admitted** | The admitted path is 2.06x faster than SGLang lossless, and its LPIPS distance (0.293 / 0.399) sits below the distance that already separates the two reference implementations from each other (0.347 / 0.465). Side-by-side frames match the lossless output in content, staging, and lighting on all three prompts. ## 0x2. Where the speedup comes from The 0.08 residual threshold works as an adaptive brake: it sleeps on easy content and forces full computation the moment the trajectory drifts, leaving 21 of 49 full video-tower steps on this prompt set. The conservative 0.04 is too sensitive here (33 full steps on the same prompt, 16.45 s). The consecutive-cache cap barely binds at this threshold — cap 1 at the same threshold is strictly slower at equal quality (11.60 s, LPIPS 0.289 / 0.401) — so cap 3 is used. The schedule is deterministic: fresh server launches on the real `quality="high"` code path reproduce the audited sweep outputs byte-for-byte (md5-verified on all three prompts), so the quality gate transfers exactly to the shipped code. Measured on top of the admitted schedule but not enabled here: SubBlock sparse attention (#34148) composes with Cache-DiT and reaches 10.37 s, and passed a 6/6 production-style serving validation on six unseen prompts. Its blk64 kernel needed two separate fixes, both now proposed upstream in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4533 (open, not merged): a deterministic SM103 scheduling hang, and an intermittent CTA wedge — roughly 1 request in 25 — that turned out to be a named-barrier id collision in the kernel's correction warpgroup. With both applied, 100 consecutive requests ran clean and per-request output md5s became deterministic. That last result revises this arm's quality numbers rather than confirming them: the pre-fix kernel silently produced a differing output on roughly one request in six, so the LPIPS figures behind the 10.37 s arm were measured on a nondeterministic kernel and need re-taking before sparse can default. Latency is unaffected. NVFP4 was evaluated and rejected (LPIPS 0.53+ under the same-seed gate even MLP-only, for at most 6% latency). ## 0x3. Sweep and rejected candidates Every line below was measured, not guessed: - threshold 0.04 with cap 1 (the H200 schedule): 33 full steps, 16.45 s — superseded - wider thresholds: 0.24 never triggers the brake and reaches LPIPS max 0.596 — rejected - cache cap 4: LPIPS max 0.53+ — rejected - warmup 3: no end-to-end win, quality drops — rejected - cached audio tower: audio drift leaks into the video tower through the dual-tower bridge — rejected - TaylorSeer order 1: no measurable gain — rejected - `--minimax-h3-adaln-online` with Cache-DiT: corrupted outputs — disqualified - generic Sol-Attn on SM103: slower than dense cuDNN-SDPA — rejected - FA4 attention backend: 4-15% slower per kernel than cuDNN-SDPA at H3 shapes, end-to-end tie — not adopted ## 0x4. Quality protocol Two gates, both must pass. Gate one: frame-aligned LPIPS (AlexNet) at 1 fps against the bit-exact SGLang lossless output — LPIPS measures same-seed trajectory drift, not absolute quality, so the yardstick is stated explicitly: the two reference implementations already sit 0.347 / 0.465 apart, and drift below that line is treated as insignificant. Gate two: human review of consecutive 4 fps frames against a temporal-artifact taxonomy (flicker, coherence, boundaries, mosaic/static regions, ghosting, broken motion, major blur). ## 0x5. Reproducibility and validation - benchmark source rebased onto `41cd5a718`; Diffusers baseline `bb56997d4`, BF16 eager dense, lossless ContextParallel Ulysses8 only - `PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_admission.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sol_attn_backend.py` -> `25 passed, 1 skipped` on the current head - pre-commit hooks pass on every changed file - fresh-launch byte-exact smoke on 8x B300: three prompts, md5 match against the audited sweep outputs, no environment overrides ## 0x6. Risk and rollback The high-quality admission stays fail-closed to the exact B300 device name/capability, topology, task, shape, schedule, flow shifts, eager mode, and native dense attention. The per-deployment schedule map only distinguishes between already-admitted profiles; H200 behavior is unchanged. Removing the B300 deployment branch restores the previous H200-only admission without touching the lossless default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31934159311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934159311)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31934158406](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31934158406)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Avoid padded Q for unified DSV4 prefill
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 TP prefill currently allocates a decode-oriented 64-head padded Q tensor, then passes the local-head slice to the unified-KV attention backend. At TP=8 that slice has 16 heads and is noncontiguous, so the OPUS wrapper materializes it with `q.contiguous()` before launching the kernel. The 64-head layout is useful for the FlashMLA sparse decode specialization, but unified-KV extend/prefill does not require it. ## Modifications - evaluate the unified-KV gate once per `MQALayer.forward` call - skip TP head padding for unified-KV extend modes and write Q directly in contiguous local-head layout - retain the existing 64-head padded layout for decode - retain existing behavior for non-unified backends - add real `MQALayer.forward` control-flow tests for unified prefill, decode, fallback, multi-stream, and prefill-CP routing ## Accuracy Tests The focused test runs through the real `MQALayer.forward` control flow and verifies: - unified EXTEND, MIXED, TARGET_VERIFY, and SPLIT_PREFILL use contiguous local-head Q - unified DECODE retains 64-head padding - non-unified modes retain the previous layout - HIP multi-stream and prefill-CP paths preserve the intended decision Result: `4 tests passed` in the official ROCm MI355X image after rebasing onto current `main`. Static validation also passed: Ruff (`F401,F821,UP037`), `py_compile`, registered-test validation, and `git diff --check`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling At the production sparse-prefill shape, the OPUS wrapper-to-kernel delta was 43.5-44.7 us per call across three runs. That delta includes wrapper dispatch and argument handling, so it is an upper bound on the removable contiguous-copy cost, not a model-level or TTFT result. ## Model E2E (MI355X, TP8 / DP1) The branch was rebased onto current `main` (`ab9e7abad`; parent `c87a2ced1`) and tested in the pinned ROCm image on 8 x MI355X. Both arms used unified-KV DSV4 attention, TP8/DP1, chunked prefill 8,192, OSL=1, distinct uncached token sequences, one warmup, and repeated scored requests. - 8K: baseline median **318.23 ms**, candidate **315.29 ms** (**0.93%** improvement); all five output tokens matched. - 64K first sandwich: baseline median **2,790.31 ms**, candidate **2,771.56 ms** (**0.68%** improvement); all five output tokens matched. Candidate had one server-side **11.90 s** outlier, so the five-sample P90/mean regressed despite the steady-state median gain. - 64K candidate follow-up: ten fresh uncached prompts, median **2,772.25 ms**, P90 **2,782.55 ms**, range **2,765.25-2,808.13 ms**, zero retractions; the outlier did not reproduce. - 64K A2/B with the same ten fresh prompt indices: baseline median/P90/mean **2,793.65 / 2,795.65 / 2,793.33 ms**; candidate **2,772.25 / 2,782.55 / 2,775.21 ms**, improving **0.77% / 0.47% / 0.65%**. All ten output tokens matched; neither arm had an outlier above 2x its median. - Baseline A1 -> A2 drift on the original five prompt indices was **0.30%** at the median (A2 slower), below the candidate's steady-state improvement. The result is a small steady-state E2E win, not the larger wrapper-level upper bound. The isolated 11.90 s event is retained as a tail-risk observation; it did not reproduce in either ten-request arm and is not attributed to this Q-layout change. ## Checklist - [x] Add focused unit tests - [x] Preserve decode and non-unified behavior - [x] Provide accuracy and operator profiling evidence - [x] Complete model E2E and graph-capture validation - [ ] Documentation update (not needed for this internal layout change) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31890497031](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890497031)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31890496542](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890496542)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Preserve MXFP4 Triton weights in sharded state
signal.text: ## Summary - keep Triton-swizzled MXFP4 expert weights and scales registered on the layer - serialize non-contiguous postprocessed tensors through contiguous CPU snapshots - keep wrapper-backed runtime tensors out of CPU/offload-group parameter remapping - add CPU regressions for a fresh-layer sharded round trip and the offloader guard ## Root cause The Triton MXFP4 post-load path moved the swizzled `w13` and `w2` weight wrappers onto the quantization method and deleted the registered layer parameters. `ShardedStateLoader.save_model` only exports `model.state_dict()`, so those runtime weights were omitted. On reload, SGLang postprocesses freshly initialized placeholders before it builds the expected state dict. The missing weights therefore disappeared from both the checkpoint and the expected-key set, and loading silently succeeded with placeholder runtime weights. The swizzled scales held by `PrecisionConfig` had the same stale-storage problem even though the original scale parameters remained registered. This change rebinds all four Triton runtime tensors (two weights and two scales) to their existing registered `Parameter` objects. The module state and kernel wrappers then share the same backing storage, so sharded-load copies update the tensors actually consumed by the kernels. Parameter identity and weight-loader attributes are preserved. The Hopper swizzle can produce non-contiguous runtime tensors. Safetensors rejects those tensors, so the exporter materializes contiguous CPU snapshots at the save boundary without changing the live runtime layout. ## CPU offload compatibility Triton wrappers live outside the module parameter mapping temporarily installed by `functional_call`. The four wrapper-backed Parameters are therefore marked to remain on device, and both offloader implementations honor that marker. This preserves the previous effective behavior of the hidden Triton tensors while allowing them to remain registered for serialization. Fixes #34448 ## Validation - focused CPU regression with import-only stubs for unavailable GPU dependencies: `2 tests`, `OK` - creates source and zero-initialized destination layers through the real MXFP4 `create_weights` - runs the real MXFP4 post-load method with only the Triton layout conversion mocked - saves through the real `ShardedStateLoader`, reloads every safetensors entry into the fresh destination state, and verifies both weights and scales consumed by the runtime wrappers - verifies wrapper-backed Parameters are excluded from CPU offload - the same sharded round-trip regression against current `upstream/main@b3bffef70a` fails as expected because `w13_weight` is absent after postprocessing - `python3 scripts/ci/check_registered_tests.py` - Black (`--check`) on all four changed files - isort (`--check-only`) on the new test - Ruff (`F401`, `F821`, `UP037`) on all four changed files - `git diff --check` - `python3 -m py_compile test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_mxfp4_sharded_state.py` The CPU tests are registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. - reporter validation on the original GH200, TP=2 reproduction: the sharded export increased from the broken `4.0G` result to `14G`, resolving the reported missing-weight export symptom ([result](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34558#issuecomment-5293077326)) A full save-reload logits comparison has not yet been reported. Project CI is still pending. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31922959478](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31922959478)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31922959274](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31922959274)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(hicache): scope write-back load-back pins by component
signal.text: ## Problem In write-back mode, `UnifiedTreeNode.load_back_pending_id` is a node-wide, single-anchor guard for in-flight H→D DMA. However, residency and load-back decisions are component-scoped. A shared radix-tree node can independently hold Full, SWA, or Mamba data on Host or Device. Each request rebuilds transfers per component, so two requests with different anchors can legitimately load different components from the same node before the first DMA ACK arrives. A concrete sequence is: 1. Request A has a deep anchor. The shared node is in its Full prefix but outside its SWA window, so it loads `Full(node)` and stores anchor A in the node-wide pending field. 2. Before A's ACK, request B has a nearer anchor. Full is already represented as device-resident by A's commit, but SWA is still Host-only and falls inside B's window, so B loads `SWA(node)`. 3. The second commit checks the same node-wide field and rejects anchor B: ```text assert pending_anchor in (None, anchor_b) ``` The two operations read different component host pools and are safe to run independently, but the node-wide single-anchor state treats them as conflicting. ## Solution Scope write-back load-back pins to `(node, component, transfer)`: - add `ComponentData.load_back_pending_transfer_ids`; - allocate a unique transfer ID for each H→D operation; - use the transfer ID as the cache-controller ACK key; - pin only the component entries actually listed in each `PoolTransfer.nodes_to_load`; - clear only that transfer ID when its ACK completes; - allow different components, and multiple transfers, to remain independently pending on one node; - use only Full-component pending IDs to protect Full Host duplicate reclamation; - validate pending transfer IDs against live operations in `sanity_check()`. The existing node-wide field remains untouched for non-write-back behavior. This PR is intentionally separate from #34519, which limits node-wide pending behavior in write-through mode. ## L3 considerations Storage prefetch can create Host-side nodes or split an existing node before a later H→D ACK. The fix therefore also: - copies component pending transfer-ID sets when Full/SWA data is redistributed during node split; - keeps Full duplicate tracking deferred until the corresponding load-back ACK; - verifies the real file-storage path: L3 → Host insertion → H→D load-back → ACK cleanup → explicit sanity check. ## Tests Focused regressions cover: - different anchors loading Full and SWA from the same shared node; - multiple transfer IDs pending on the same component and cleared independently; - Full duplicate tracking after an L3-refilled Host copy is loaded back; - node split inheritance of Full/SWA pending transfer IDs. Validation: ```text 99 passed, 308 skipped ``` The selected suite includes all load-back tests, storage-prefetch corruption tests, L3 write/prefetch tests, and the new regressions. The explicit write-back file-L3 round-trip ran across Full and Full+SWA configurations with multiple page/window sizes: ```text 13 passed, 6 skipped ``` Each successful case performs L3 prefetch into a fresh tree, Host→Device load-back, ACK processing, KV-byte verification, and `sanity_check()`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31933353632](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933353632)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31933353414](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31933353414)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] W4A8 MoE kernel for NVFP4 models on non-Blackwell GPUs (SM90)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ### Background NVFP4 quantized models like **GLM-5 (744B)** and **DeepSeek V3.2 (671B)** are becoming increasingly popular. On Blackwell GPUs with native FP4 hardware support, these models run great. However, on non-Blackwell GPUs like H20 (SM90), SGLang falls back to the **Marlin W4A16 path** — dequantizing FP4 weights to BF16 and using BF16 tensor cores. We've been running GLM-5-NVFP4 on 8×H20 (141GB HBM3, SM90) and did extensive benchmarking and kernel-level profiling. The results suggest there's a significant opportunity to improve decode performance on these GPUs. ### Current Performance: NVFP4 (W4A16) vs FP8 on 8×H20 **Decode (DP Attention, MTP enabled):** | Concurrency | NVFP4 (Marlin W4A16) | FP8 | Gap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 58.6 tok/s | 63.6 tok/s | FP8 9% faster | | 64 | 963 tok/s | 1,228 tok/s | FP8 28% faster | **Prefill:** | | NVFP4 | FP8 | Gap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Peak (32 conc) | 5,300 tok/s | 10,500 tok/s | FP8 ~2× faster | We initially expected NVFP4 decode to be faster than FP8 since FP4 weights are half the size (decode is conventionally considered bandwidth-bound). However, **FP8 is faster across the board**. ### Root Cause: Marlin Kernel Efficiency Our profiling shows the Marlin W4A16 kernel has very low memory bandwidth utilization on MoE workloads: - **Theoretical** (bandwidth-limited): NVFP4 should read ~100MB per layer (8 activated experts), taking ~28μs at 4TB/s. FP8 reads ~200MB, taking ~52μs. NVFP4 should be ~1.8× faster. - **Actual**: Marlin takes ~117μs/layer (24% bandwidth utilization), FP8 Triton takes ~72μs/layer (72% utilization). FP8 ends up **1.6× faster**. Meanwhile, FP8 Triton's fused_moe_kernel achieves much higher efficiency with a simpler pipeline (direct FP8 loads, post-MMA scaling, FP8 tensor cores). ### Why This Matters NVFP4 has a key advantage over FP8 for serving: **much smaller weight footprint → more KV cache space**. On our 8×H20 setup with DP Attention, NVFP4 weights leave ~37GB/GPU for KV cache vs ~17GB/GPU for FP8, enabling significantly more concurrent requests. A W4A8 kernel would let non-Blackwell deployments benefit from both the memory advantage and competitive compute performance. Models that would benefit: any NVFP4 quantized MoE model on SM90 GPUs (H20, H100, H200, etc.), including GLM-5 and DeepSeek V3.2. ### Environment - GPUs: 8× NVIDIA H20 (SM90, 141GB HBM3) - Model: GLM-5-NVFP4 (744B MoE, 256 experts, top-8) - SGLang with DP Attention (tp=8, dp=8) - MTP/EAGLE speculative decoding enabled ### Related resources _No response_
